title: State to halve stake in ABN Amro to 10.5 percent
lead: The Dutch State will further reduce its stake in ABN Amro to 10.5 percent, from the current 20.7 percent. That is reported by <entity id="org:rwt-stichting-administratie-kantoor-financiele-instellingen-nlfi">NLFI</entity>, the foundation that manages the government's stakes in financial institutions on behalf of the State.

title: If Boud Slings had dropped by, the hanging lamp disappeared from the room
Griekspoor loses to Zverev, who rises to number 1 in the ATP ranking
lead: The rise of tennis player Tallon Griekspoor has come to an end against German Alexander Zverev. After his tournament win in Brussels, Griekspoor was eliminated on Thursday after two sets in the round of 16 of the ATP tournament in Vienna: 4-6 5-7. Through his victory, Zverev has virtually risen to first place in the world rankings. When the list is officially updated on Monday, he will overtake the injured Italian Jannik Sinner.

title: Cap on student loan interest scrapped, former students end up paying more
lead: Former students will probably end up paying more than 2.5 percent interest on their student loans in the long term. In the coalition agreement, D66, VVD and CDA had promised to set this limit on the interest. But according to education minister <entity id="person:rianne-letschert">Rianne Letschert</entity>, that costs too much money. Student organisations are angry and feel students are being used as 'money donkeys'.

title: Region gets priority for new infrastructure: road widening in Groningen yes, RandstadRail expansion no
Cabinet wants to cut 25,000 full-time jobs in the public sector: 'For every two civil servants, there will soon be only one workplace'
Jessica (38) was killed by her boyfriend: prosecution demands 12 years in prison and tbs with coercion against Coen K.
lead: No 'tbs light', but a long prison sentence, followed by mandatory treatment in a tbs clinic with no end date. That is the sentence the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> is demanding against Coen K. after the brutal manslaughter of Jessica Brants.

title: Tina de Bruin slips into the shoes of Orgel Joke, Jan Smit meets a smitten and naughty fan
lead: Brief updates from the stars on social media: we devour them. In the Showbytes column, the showbiz editorial team scours the web for you for the craziest, most beautiful and most striking posts from well-known Dutch people and celebrities. This article will be updated throughout the day.

title: Another 21 municipalities under supervision for housing too few asylum seekers
lead: The government has placed 21 municipalities under supervision because they are housing too few asylum seekers. In the coming period they must make clear how they will still comply with the Distribution Act. If they do not, the government can override a municipality and decide that an asylum reception centre will be set up there.

title: Husband filmed sex with hidden spycam in alarm clock radio: "Smeared dog poop in her hair"
lead: After 27 years of marriage, a woman from Rotterdam has filed a complaint against her ex-husband R. B. (61). He allegedly stalked her, threatened her and smeared dog poop on her, but also raped her. Recordings made by a spycam in an alarm clock radio are on B.'s phone. "Nothing was ever done against her will," says B.

title: The climate movement must meet voters where they are
lead: Opinion Imogen Learmonth: 'If the increased public concern is to lead to a renewed political mandate, then the climate movement must tell new stories'

title: Western leaders condemn Houthi attack on Riyadh airport: 'Spiral of violence'
lead: Several Western leaders have expressed their support for Saudi Arabia following the attack by Houthi rebels on Riyadh airport. Foreign minister <entity id="person:tom-berendsen">Tom Berendsen</entity> condemns the attack, for example. EU chief Ursula von der Leyen speaks of a "spiral of violence from Iranian allies".

title: Housing supply in the private rental sector continues to shrink: 22,000 rental homes sold
lead: For the second year in a row, the private rental sector has shrunk, the <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek</entity> (CBS) reports. During 2025 some 22,000 homes disappeared from this sector, leaving 1.16 million private rental homes at the start of 2026. The decline in 2025 was considerably higher than in 2024, when just over 3,000 homes left the sector.

title: Setback for cabinet: farmers' organisations dissatisfied after talks on nitrogen
lead: The two farmers' organisations with which agriculture minister <entity id="person:jaimi-van-essen">Jaimi van Essen</entity> is holding talks on nitrogen policy left home dissatisfied on Thursday after a meeting. The cabinet would not meet all of their desired adjustments.

title: FBI also says North Korea is behind billion-dollar hack of crypto exchange Binance
Spanish media: police start investigation into death of footballer
lead: The Spanish <entity id="org:politie">nationale politie</entity> has launched an investigation into goalkeeper Jesús Owono following the death of footballer Jesús de Miguel. Spanish media report this. The CD Tenerife striker died on Tuesday in hospital after he collided heavily with goalkeeper Owono in the final stages of a match against FC Andorra on Monday.

title: Across the border: British councils take action against dinosaurs and garden fountain
lead: A roaring dinosaur, a splashing garden fountain or a neighbour who stares at you for long periods. In England and Wales such irritations can lead to municipal enforcement. According to a British civil rights organisation, councils regularly go too far in doing so.

title: Man sentenced to eleven years in prison for strangling partner after acquittal
lead: The Amsterdam Court of Appeal on Thursday sentenced the 48-year-old Robert L. to eleven years in prison for strangling his life partner in 2016. The Amsterdam District Court had previously acquitted the man due to lack of evidence.

title: What the cup upsets by Excelsior '31 and Genemuiden earned the amateur clubs
lead: A cup upset is one for the history books, but it is also good for the bank accounts of amateur clubs. Excelsior '31 from Rijssen can add a nice sum after its win on Tuesday against ADO Den Haag in the first round of the Eurojackpot KNVB Beker. On Wednesday three more amateur clubs won.

title: Lieke Anna doesn't know what to do with her mother's statement, the next morning things go wrong
lead: Zeeland photographer and filmmaker Lieke Anna Haertjens (38) made a film about her mother, who suffered a brain haemorrhage in 2020. She survived, but their lives changed drastically. "I have already lost a very large part of my mother, while she is still here."

title: Israel: Shit, the wrong voters have won
lead: Israel has a problem with its democracy. Yes, of course, that problem too, but there is one more: elections have been held and the wrong people have won seats. 19 to be exact. The final election results give Netanyahu 53 seats and the established opposition under Gadi Eisenkot 48. The two Arab parties, Ra'am and […] Read more posts on Sargasso

title: 'On the metro you see everyone checking the share price': Taiwan is obsessed with investing
First-time buyers miss out due to depleted loan funds at municipalities
lead: The number of applications for starter loans is growing, partly due to rising house prices. Some first-time buyers are in for surprises and are missing out on purchases.

title: From 'ghost town' to square full of ADO fans and Mobile Unit deployment: how the disturbances unfolded in The Hague
lead: To the relief of shopkeepers, looting and vandalism did not occur on Saturday in the centre of The Hague. Still, there is enough to be upset about: around 15:00 the mood turned grim nonetheless, the ME had to intervene, and the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> made 34 arrests. The vast majority of those arrested are minors.

title: Asylum applications and follow-on migrants decline
lead: The number of first asylum applications in the Netherlands fell by 13 percent in the third quarter of 2026 compared with the same period a year earlier. That is what the <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek</entity> (CBS) reports, based on figures from the <entity id="org:immigratie-en-naturalisatiedienst">Immigratie- en Naturalisatiedienst</entity> (IND). Almost 5900 people applied for asylum in the Netherlands for the first time.

title: Cabinet wants to require hybrid heat pump from 2029 for homeowners, exception for 2 groups of homes
lead: From 2029, it will become mandatory for many homeowners to switch to a smart hybrid heat pump when replacing their central heating boiler. A regular gas-fired central heating boiler will no longer comply, writes minister <entity id="person:elanor-boekholt-osullivan">Elanor Boekholt-O’Sullivan</entity> (<entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-vro">Volkshuisvesting en Ruimtelijke Ordening</entity>) in a letter to the House of Representatives.

title: SCP: citizens feel left behind mainly in housing and politics
lead: A home that goes to someone else, politicians who mainly listen to influential groups: a considerable minority of the Dutch feel they are at the back of the line. Especially in housing and political representation this rankles, according to research by the Netherlands Institute for Social Research (SCP). And a large part of the population believes the government itself is responsible for this.

title: Shortly before the end, Hitler's Berghof finally got its turn
Ahold Delhaize takes over Tesco's activities in the Czech Republic and Slovakia
lead: The Dutch-Belgian supermarket chain is paying approximately €1,2 mrd for the acquisition and is also taking over lease obligations of €500 mln.

title: 'Very good that the Jetten cabinet is not going along with the nonsense about left and right'
lead: In the podcast Praat mee met AD, we discuss a statement every day. Today it is this one: enough talk, the cabinet must choose now, either left or right.

title: Solution sought for 500 million euro gap: coalition leaders meet Saturday for a tricky puzzle
lead: This weekend the prime minister, deputy prime ministers, and the minister and <entity id="pos:staatssecretaris-van-financien">staatssecretaris van Financiën</entity> want to jointly determine a route to secure a majority for their tax plan. First, the coalition parties must agree on the content and on cooperation with the opposition. After that, work will be done on a 'total deal'.

title: Many old Dutch folk songs feature women being murdered and raped: Rosa (27) had a problem with that. 'In our version, the girl in "Meisje loos" becomes the captain'
Cabinet wants to make refusing to return a criminal offence: prison sentence possible
lead: Foreigners who are not allowed to stay in the Netherlands and actively frustrate their return may soon face a prison sentence. The Cabinet presents a bill today that makes actively obstructing deportation a criminal offence. At the same time, the <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-orgaan-opvang-asielzoekers">COA</entity> again warns about overcrowded reception locations.

title: Mother of grave desecration victim: 'This burden will never go away'
lead: Four women are suspected of desecrating graves at a cemetery in Leusden on 11 September 2021. According to the suspicion, they held a 'paranormal session' at children's graves, during which they reportedly asked questions of the deceased and clamped glowing balls between the letters of several graves.

title: The month of October In Pictures
lead: Thousands of photos from around the world flow into our picture archives every day. From horrifying current events to serene landscapes, from breaking news to seemingly small moments. What do you choose when everything happens at once? Where do you put the emphasis and which images stay with you? Every month the NRC photo desk selects the photos that made the greatest impression.

title: Nick Schilder pays tribute to late manager during Nationale lichtjesavond: 'Such a collective moment offers comfort'
lead: When Nick Schilder takes the stage in Amersfoort on Sunday evening for his contribution to the Nationale lichtjesavond , he will do so without his guitar. The singer from Volendam steps out of his comfort zone and sits down at the piano to perform the song he wrote after the death of his manager and mentor.

title: Reader reactions: If only Trump were a toddler!
Late blow for Bayern as former PSV player sends Dortmund to a draw in entertaining top clash
lead: Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund shared the points in Der Klassiker: 2-2. Substitute Fábio Silva equalised in the 89th minute. Freshly crowned Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane played a negative lead role with a missed penalty.

title: Off to the boomer checkout? Certainly not. Many young people would rather not run the risk that someone says something to them
lead: Just making small talk on the train, at the supermarket or at the fishmonger? Always do it. It makes the other person happier and less lonely. But there is yet another, unexpected, reason to make small talk, Japke-d. Bouma heard from a 'happiness psychologist'. Read it here!

title: Ameland shipping route stays open under cabinet plan only through 'daily dredging'
lead: A project to improve the connection to and from Ameland is one of the 29 infrastructure projects that <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> is scrapping. A shipping channel that repeatedly silts up has for years required intensive maintenance and caused delays on the shipping route.

lead: Özcan Akyol writes three times a week about what occupies him.

title: Adyen shares fall sharply after margin expectations are lowered
lead: The payments company is dropping a medium-term profitability target to 'remain flexible'. Earlier it had aimed for an EBITDA margin of 55%.

lead: Do you know how many subscriptions you have? A monthly package of coffee pods, tights or perfume on the doormat is no longer an exception. "We underestimate how many subscriptions we have and what that does to our wallet."

title: Chaotic NSC congress: part of the hall walks out during Mona Keijzer's speech, board steps down in the afternoon
lead: That it would not be a hosanna mood at the congress of the ailing NSC on Saturday was already clear, but then the arrival of speaker Mona Keijzer also became a point of contention. The hall became considerably emptier as soon as she stepped onto the stage. "I am looking for sensible conservative people."

lead: Welcome to this liveblog! My name is Hein Nooijens and I will guide you through the draw for round 2 of the KNVB Cup. Have fun!

title: Naar verwachting stijgt het aantal wereldwijde luchtvaartpassagiers volgend jaar, ondanks hoge tarieven, becijferde ING
lead: Naar verwachting zal het aantal wereldwijde luchtvaartpassagiers volgend jaar stijgen, ook al blijven de ticketprijzen hoog, volgens een rapport van ING.

title: Arcadis shares start moving again on orange sneakers
lead: The share of the engineering consultancy rose on Wednesday after well-received quarterly figures. Now it is wait-and-see whether Arcadis can continue the increase in revenue and profit.

title: Explosion with three dead in Rotterdam: Jalal O. acquitted
lead: The court in Rotterdam has acquitted Jalal O. of involvement in a serious explosion on the Schammenkamp in Rotterdam-Zuid. Three people, including a cousin of the suspect, died in the blast in early 2024.

title: Frans Duijts after heart attack: 'I will never be quite the old one again'
lead: Frans Duijts has suffered serious damage to his heart from the heart attack he had last week. He had to be resuscitated several times. "I've had fifteen shocks in total," the 47-year-old singer tells Story.

title: Prime Minister Burnham (UK): possibly apologies for slavery, but no reparations
lead: Prime Minister Burnham is open to offering an apology for Britain's history of slavery, but calls reparations "not the right answer" in an open letter in The Guardian. His letter has been received with moderately positive reactions.

title: KLM crew in disbelief: Lufthansa employee electrocuted in pool of five-star hotel in India
lead: A crew member of the German airline Lufthansa died on Friday evening in the pool of a five-star hotel in the Indian city of Bangalore. That happened after the pool came under electric current, KLM writes in an internal communication. Crew members of the Dutch airline were staying at the hotel at the time of the incident.

title: A pleasant encounter as an antidote in this confusing world
Verstappen cannot make a mark even with undamaged car in last practice, McLaren surprises Ferrari
lead: A complaining Max Verstappen did not get beyond fifth fastest in the final free practice session before qualifying. The Dutchman fell well short in a session in which teammate Isack Hadjar was also completely dissatisfied with the car. Lando Norris set the fastest time by a minimal margin.

title: From Germany to Argentina: how the foreign press covers Rob Jetten's baby
lead: Prime Minister Rob Jetten and his partner Nicolás Keenan are expecting a baby. The news made headlines not only in the Dutch media but was also widely picked up abroad. The German newspaper Bild writes: 'It sounds like the plot of a saccharine novel.'

title: Djokovic eliminated by Struff at ATP tournament in Basel
lead: Novak Djokovic was eliminated on Thursday evening in the round of 16 of the ATP tournament in Basel by Jan-Lennard Struff. The Serbian 24-time Grand Slam winner lost to the German in three sets: 7-6 (4) 5-7 6-7 (5).

title: Willem de Kooning: the American giant next to Rembrandt
lead: Editor Agnès Hoogendijk walked through the Rijksmuseum one Saturday afternoon and was immediately impressed by the American giant Willem de Kooning.

title: Murdered Hajar sent 'worrying messages' to family on day of disappearance
lead: The 29-year-old Hajar, who was killed earlier this month, sent worrying messages to her family on the day she went missing, in which she asked for help. Yet that day it was not decided to classify the disappearance as "urgent", the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> reported on Thursday.

title: Cabinet plan to protect children online: 'They are running unacceptable risks'
lead: More needs to be done for the online safety of children. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> has therefore presented a renewed strategy with a broad package of measures. It includes, among other things, stricter rules against cyberbullying and addictive app designs.

title: Selma Blair apologises for alleged violent incident on plane
lead: Selma Blair has apologised after appearing in court over an alleged violent incident on board an airplane. In a video on social media, the actress spoke publicly about the events for the first time.

title: Reshuffling infrastructure projects does not solve the structural problem

Preservation and safety are the priority in the choices made. A large number of infrastructure projects are being paused to save costs. That was announced by minister <entity id="person:vincent-karremans">Vincent Karremans</entity> (VVD) […]

title: Traffic fines too high? Dutch people want harsher penalties for dangerous driving
lead: A majority of the Dutch think traffic fines in our country are too high. Yet that criticism does not mean people are fundamentally opposed to high fines: there is in fact a lot of support for (even) higher fines for dangerous offences, and for repeat offenders. That is shown by research by the RTL Nieuwspanel among more than 17,000 participants.

title: Veilig Thuis vraagt 70 miljoen euro terwijl meldingen van huiselijk geweld toenemen
lead: Mensen die vermoedens van kindermishandeling of huiselijk geweld melden, wachten gemiddeld 2 maanden op landelijk huiselijk geweld...

This organisation, founded by former prime minister Dries van Agt, says it is committed to a just policy regarding Palestine and Israel.

lead: After the massive fights during Halloween Fright Nights, the question arises: could Walibi have prevented this? Permits, house rules and conversations with those involved show that the amusement park in fact took all kinds of measures to counter disturbances. Yet it went disastrously wrong.

title: Six of 38 people on board rubber boat with migrants are minors
lead: Of the group of 38 migrants who were brought ashore yesterday morning from a rubber boat off the coast of Zeeland, six were minors. The Marechaussee reports this. The children have been taken to the registration center in Ter Apel.

lead: The agenda of judges is overfull. With penalty orders, the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> can reduce that pressure, but criticism is now being voiced about how they are used. That is unjustified.

title: Government wants to strengthen parents' educational knowledge
lead: This week minister <entity id="person:mirjam-sterk">Mirjam Sterk</entity> for Long-term Care and Sport and state secretary <entity id="person:judith-tielen">Judith Tielen</entity> of Education and Emancipation launched the initiative 'Team Ouders'. The aim is to start a conversation about better supporting parents. All kinds of dialogues and activities on parenthood and upbringing are being organised, including in municipalities.

lead: Chip companies were once again in demand with investors and helped the Nasdaq to a daily gain of 1.2%.

title: Irresistible Romana Vrede makes 'Een Groter Verhaal' the show of the year
lead: Een Groter Verhaal moves for an hour and a half on the boundary between cabaret and theatre, in a magnificent monologue by Romana Vrede about the exploitation of people, animals and the earth. Commissioner of the King: 'Municipalities must house more status holders, otherwise the province will step in'
lead: Municipalities must house status holders more quickly. That is the call from the Commissioner of the King in <entity id="org:provincie-zuid-holland">Zuid-Holland</entity>, <entity id="person:wouter-kolff">Wouter Kolff</entity>. Municipalities have a legal duty when it comes to designating housing for status holders. Provinces supervise and can ultimately intervene themselves. "Make sure you tackle it as a municipality. lead: He already misses it, says Peter van Hooijdonk. For decades his family was in the fireworks trade. "Whole families came every December with many generations." That is gone now. Bangs there will still be, but different: "I am joining in challenging the compensation, which is too low."

title: Immediate nationwide mandatory housing of poultry after three bird flu outbreaks
lead: Poultry farmers must keep their chickens indoors immediately to limit the spread of bird flu as much as possible, the ministry of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-landbouw-visserij-voedselzekerheid-en-natuur">Landbouw, Visserij, Voedselzekerheid en Natuur</entity> announced on Wednesday. The decision follows three outbreaks of the disease in a short time.

title: Videoland may take over Viaplay: 'For subscribers, nothing changes at this moment'
lead: Videoland may take over Viaplay. The Authority for Consumers & Markets (<entity id="org:zbo-autoriteit-consument-en-markt">ACM</entity>) has granted permission to the streamer, which is part of DPG Media. The ACM does not expect any adverse consequences of the takeover for viewers, the purchase of sports rights or the sale of advertising space, the ACM announced.

title: Construction seeks 73,000 workers, competes with Defence
lead: The Dutch construction sector needs some 73,000 new employees over the next three years. That is what the Economic Institute for Construction (EIB) calculates. The construction industry has been struggling with staff shortages for years, while the Netherlands wants to build many homes, expand the power grid, renovate infrastructure and make it more sustainable.

JA21, BBB and SGP have demands that are unacceptable to the coalition, yet they are coming to talk anyway
lead: In exchange for support for the Tax Plan, JA21, BBB and SGP want substantial changes on nitrogen, asylum and medical-ethical issues. These are demands that until now have been unacceptable to the three coalition parties.

title: Rotterdam council member must retract statements about entrepreneur
lead: Rotterdam council member Kevin van Eikeren (PRO) must correct his statements about entrepreneur and amusement park owner Wim Beelen online. That is the outcome on Tuesday of a summary proceeding that Beelen had initiated. Within 72 hours, the council member must post a correction on his Instagram and LinkedIn channels.

lead: He used to deliberately walk around a street just to see her one more time. Despite the major setbacks that followed, Utrecht residents Pieter (90) and Pauline (88) Bouthoorn are still inseparable seventy years later. They share the secret of their freshly minted platinum marriage.

title: Gambling Authority imposes record fine of 37 million on illegal gambling provider: payment was possible with crypto
lead: The Gambling Authority (Ksa) has imposed a record fine on the company EOD Code SRL for offering illegal online gambling in the Netherlands. Through various websites, people in the Netherlands could gamble without any checks. It is the highest fine the regulator has ever issued for this kind of illegal offering.

title: Demand for AI chips explodes: ASMI and NXP report record revenues
lead: The Dutch chip stocks ASMI and NXP are doing very well. The revenue of chip machine maker ASMI was never this high in the third quarter, thanks to strong demand for AI. Chip producer NXP is also growing through investments in AI and the construction of data centres.

title: Cabinet tightens screen use advice, phones in lockers for the entire school day
lead: The cabinet wants primary and secondary schools to ban the use of mobile phones throughout the entire school from 1 January 2027. Pupils may then no longer use their phones during break, in the assembly hall or on the schoolyard. Currently, at many schools, pupils are only not allowed to bring their phones into the classroom. This is one of the proposals from the so-called 'Strategy letter on online children's rights', in which, under the leadership of <entity id="person:willemijn-aerdts">staatssecretaris Aerdts</entity> (Digital Economy), various ministries have set out new and existing rules to better protect children online. The cabinet is not responsible for the phone use of pupils at Dutch schools, but can give an urgent recommendation. That also happened in 2024, when the Ministry of Education made national agreements with primary schools on limiting phones during lessons. The cabinet wants the tightened advice to take effect from 1 January 2027 at secondary schools and in primary education. Scrolling The cabinet, like many parents and other institutions, is concerned about the increasing online use of Dutch children and young people. At school, children are distracted and can concentrate less well. At home, parents find it difficult, for example, to curb their children's hours of scrolling. Because of addictive algorithms and automatically playing videos, it proves very hard to put the phone away, and daily screen times of around 5 to 6 hours are not unusual. Experts have long warned about the negative consequences of excessive screen use, such as sleep problems, short-sightedness and depression. Furthermore, it is unclear exactly what young people watch, and there is little insight into cyberbullying or other unpleasant matters. Unwanted contact Several ministries have for some time been working on various plans to offer young people sufficient protection against everything that can be viewed online. Today, State Secretary Aerdts presents a strategy for a "safe and healthy online world for children", with around forty arrangements, of which, according to her, fifteen are new. "Online, on social media or in video games, children quickly lose sight and run unacceptable risks", said the State Secretary. "Think of addictive algorithms, harmful images and unwanted contact." Work has been underway for some time on a number of measures from the Strategy letter, because they require a long-term effort. The European Commission has recently made a proposal for an age limit on social media. The European Commission considers 13 years, the Dutch cabinet 15 years. Other proposals include, for example, banning addictive techniques such as algorithms in the design of digital services at European level. A reliable age verification system must also be developed, in which the privacy of young people is well protected. Child labour The cabinet is also working on stricter rules for buy now, pay later services, such as the deferred payment service Klarna. The cabinet is also continuing to develop tightened rules for vlog families and kidfluencers. Online content of children under 15 will be seen as child labour and can be fined as such. The cabinet is also commissioning research into Netflix, YouTube, Roblox, Fortnite, ChatGPT, Instagram, Snapchat and TikTok to "gain better insight into how digital services affect the experience, development and choices of children who use digital services". The most concrete measure, banning phones in and around schools, must, according to the cabinet, therefore take effect in three months. <entity id="person:judith-tielen">Staatssecretaris Tielen</entity> of Education is now going to make agreements on this with the education sector.

title: Introducing a capital gains tax in 2028 becomes a race against the clock
lead: <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">Minister Heinen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity> promised <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> last week that he would do everything possible to introduce the new capital gains tax as early as 2028. It will be a race against the clock, and those involved are wondering whether it will all work out. On Friday <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> sent the bill needed to make the new system possible to the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity> for advice. Many MPs asked whether that advice would arrive in time for the next parliamentary debate on the subject, on 12 October. Heinen was optimistic on Thursday: "We are asking everyone for a maximum stretch, but then 2028 is achievable." He did acknowledge the risk that it will become 2029. A swift introduction of the new wealth tax is politically important to Heinen. It was an important commitment to right-wing opposition parties such as JA21 and the SGP. On request, the Raad van State says it will certainly not meet the deadline of 12 October. "We have only seven days left, impossible," a spokesperson states. The advice will arrive at the earliest on 19 October, and possibly not until the 26th. That makes it even tighter for the House to handle the law in time. Fraud lurking The banks say on request that they have too little time to adapt their IT systems. As a result, it will not be possible to have their customers' data pre-filled when those customers file their tax returns in 2028. The banks had already warned about this, but <entity id="person:eelco-eerenberg">staatssecretaris Eerenberg</entity> of Financiën suggested last week that there would be a solution. According to him, many banks have recently spoken out in favour of the new capital gains tax. "So I think we may also ask: now you must also help your clients make that possible." The Nederlandse Vereniging van Banken does not recognise that. "We have never expressed a preference for taxation of capital gains or capital accrual." A meeting with the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity> will soon take place to see what is possible as long as the pre-filled returns are not available, a spokesperson says. If banks and asset managers cannot supply the data, the Belastingdienst cannot check whether citizens have filled in their returns correctly. And then fraud lurks. For people who fill in their returns in good faith, it is questionable whether they can find the information themselves. Not all banks can supply the data directly to their customers. In any case, it makes filling in the return more complicated. Officials at Financiën already warned about this in an advice: "This places an additional burden on the 'doing capacity' of citizens." Even if the above problems are solved, it will be a real challenge for the Belastingdienst to carry out the system change by 2028. The service is also busy with adjustments to its computer systems, because a mandatory disability insurance for self-employed people arrives in 2030. If both adjustments have to be carried out at the same time, the introduction of that insurance will probably be delayed by a year, officials warned. Last week the cabinet made a new proposal for an accelerated transition to a capital gains tax, as a replacement for the current capital accrual tax. The VVD came under great pressure from its base, because investors object to paying tax on 'paper profit', that is, tax on shares that have not yet been sold and have only become more valuable on paper. Paying on sale But if citizens only start paying once the shares are sold, billions of euros in tax revenue will temporarily come in less. The cabinet wanted to fill that gap by also making smaller savers and investors pay capital gains tax, but there was no majority for that in the House of Representatives. Remarkably, the proposal sent to the Raad van State still contains that funding, which the House rejected. Meanwhile the cabinet is looking for alternatives, in consultation with opposition parties. That means further adjustments to box 3 are coming, also for next year. If the legislation does not get through the House of Representatives and the <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">Eerste Kamer</entity> this year, the current system will remain in force for at least another year. Each year of delay costs the treasury 3.5 billion euros in lost revenue. Eerste Kamer This evening Heinen and Eerenberg will provide text and explanation in the Eerste Kamer. The senators have repeatedly postponed votes on the box 3 plans at the request of the cabinet. And now there is urgency. Senator Crone of Pro is indignant about this course of events: "This is a major system change. We must handle it carefully, including by hearing experts." His colleague Griffioen of government party D66 urges the cabinet to make good use of the short time left: "The cabinet is responsible for getting this right, so do not dawdle and come up with good proposals."

title: Cabinet wants to link public transport and other transport in the region
lead: The cabinet wants to counter the erosion of public transport in the region by linking public transport and other types of transport, such as pupil transport, with each other. Trials with self-driving buses must also come. <entity id="person:annet-bertram">Staatssecretaris Bertram</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-infrastructuur-en-waterstaat">Infrastructuur en Waterstaat</entity> writes in two letters to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> that she is very concerned about accessibility in the region. She wants to look at whether, "with the available resources", hospitals and cultural institutions, for example, can also become more accessible. She points out that besides regular public transport there are already all kinds of alternatives, such as regional taxis, on-demand buses, neighbourhood buses and shared cars. However, these still largely operate alongside each other. For example, you see buses driving one after another to the same place, one time for pupil transport and another time for WMO transport for people who cannot travel independently by public transport. As far as she is concerned, much more efficient cooperation is possible. 'Fine-meshed network' Bertram envisions a "fine-meshed network of public transport", in which an important role is reserved for a mobility centre where all requests come in and "characteristics of all travellers" are known, so that "the available vehicles" can be deployed optimally. The state secretary also wants to conduct three trials with self-driving buses. Since last year one such bus already runs in Rotterdam, carrying people from a metro station to the airport. The state secretary fears a downward spiral when it comes to accessibility outside cities. Fewer older people can reach a hospital within three quarters of an hour, she notes. The ANP reported this week that 1100 bus stops have disappeared in the past six years, mainly in Drenthe and Groningen. Stalling "The current system is starting to stall", Bertram concludes. Transport operators are struggling with driver shortages, while buses outside peak hours often run empty. On Prinsjesdag the cabinet announced that it will set aside 300 million euros annually to improve regional accessibility. Later this month the minister will announce how she plans to spend this money.

title: Former head of German intelligence arrested for espionage
lead: The former head of the German intelligence service BND, August Hanning, has been arrested. According to German media, Hanning is suspected of espionage, high treason and disclosing state secrets, among other things. The German public prosecution service has confirmed his arrest. Hanning headed the Bundesnachrichtendienst (BND) from 1998 to 2005. He is alleged to have purchased, among other things, secret information from a BND employee up until 2022. He is said to have used this information to draw up a security analysis for a foreign intelligence service. It is not known which country, but according to German media it would not be Russia. He is also said to have shared internal information with a foreign agent. House search The 80-year-old Hanning was arrested at his home this morning. The former employee, who held a senior position at the service, has also been arrested. The man was previously an important right-hand man of Hanning and worked for the BND until spring. The authorities came onto the case after they conducted a house search at Hanning's home in September last year in connection with a kidnapping case. In the investigation into that case, a tip came in that information may have been leaked from the BND. Hanning may also have been involved in the kidnapping itself, although he has always denied this. During the house search, agents found highly sensitive information originating from the BND. The secret documents dated from the recent past, so Hanning should never have possessed them. According to sources, Hanning is said to have received around 2,000 documents, which reportedly included reports on Iran's nuclear programme and the Russian army. Key positions Throughout his career, Hanning held key positions in German security services for many years. After his period at the BND, he was responsible for security as state secretary at <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity>, after which he went into the business sector. In recent years Hanning has worked as a consultant in the security and business world, among other things. He did so in places all over the world. German media report that he has good connections with Russia and China and their government authorities.

title: Measles outbreak in New York and Pennsylvania largest since the 1990s
lead: Measles is spreading rapidly in the American states of New York and Pennsylvania. New York has even declared a state of emergency, after more than a hundred people have already been infected this week. Because of the state of emergency, care workers can intervene faster and may, for example, test and distribute vaccines more quickly. In Pennsylvania, the number of registered measles cases this year has passed the thousand mark. This makes it one of the largest outbreaks since the early 1990s. Nearly two hundred patients have been admitted to hospital and five people have died. Health experts link such outbreaks to the falling vaccination rate in the US. Large outbreaks have also been reported since the beginning of last year in other states, such as Texas, Utah and South Carolina. What is measles? Measles is a highly contagious infectious disease caused by a virus. A measles infection usually runs a mild course, but serious complications can occur and the patient can die from it. According to WHO figures, around 95,000 people worldwide died of measles in 2024, mainly children under the age of 5. Measles can be recognised by a sudden high fever, red eyes, coughing, a cold and red spots on the skin that often feel rough. In the Netherlands, more than five hundred people got measles last year, mainly children at primary schools where few pupils were vaccinated. In the Netherlands there is a shot against measles, the MMR vaccine. Along with Pennsylvania and New York, Ohio is also dealing with a serious measles outbreak: more than 200 infections have already been confirmed there this year. As in Pennsylvania, some of the hardest-hit areas in Ohio are home to strictly Christian Amish communities, where the vaccination rate is generally lower. According to the American health agency CDC, the US is experiencing its worst measles outbreak nationwide since 1991, with nearly 4,000 cases in total so far. About twenty percent of these are children under the age of five. In the past two years, eight people have died of complications related to measles. That is more deaths than in the thirty years before that combined. Deaths In February 2025, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. was appointed Minister of Health in the Trump <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> administration. For years he was one of the loudest vaccine critics in the US. For example, shortly after taking office he dismissed all the experts on the vaccine advisory committee and partly replaced them with vaccine sceptics. After several deaths from measles, he somewhat softened his positions on the disease. For instance, he stated that the MMR vaccine is the most effective way to prevent the spread of the disease. But the consequences of his criticism are already becoming visible. The vaccination rate is now already below the 95 percent needed to contain the spread of measles. As a result, infection figures are rising rapidly in several states. In November, international health officials will meet to determine whether the US and Mexico have lost their status as measles-free countries. A country must go twelve months without cases of the disease to be declared measles-free. Disinformation about vaccines and problems with access to healthcare also cause some parents not to have themselves or their children vaccinated. Salmonella Alongside measles outbreaks, the US is also struggling with a number of foodborne diseases. For example, this year nearly 13,000 Americans developed diarrhoea and other stomach and abdominal complaints from eating lettuce contaminated with the intestinal parasite. The American Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has since traced the contamination to a Mexican farm. American media report that food products in the US are increasingly being recalled due to contamination by bacteria, viruses or parasites. This concerns eggs, chicken or meat, among other things. According to various media, this development is caused by budget cuts and staff leaving the FDA and the US Department of Agriculture, which puts food inspections under pressure. The American health service CDC is currently investigating 33 outbreaks of food-related diseases, including salmonella, E. coli and listeria.

title: Drone attack on ships off Bulgarian coast, prime minister holds emergency meeting
lead: A ship has sunk off the coast of Bulgaria in the Black Sea after a drone attack. A fire broke out on another ship, Bulgarian President Iotova confirms in a statement. According to Prime Minister Radev, the crew of the sunken ship is missing. It is not clear how many people are involved. A search operation has been launched for them. Eighteen crew members have been rescued from the burning ship. Some have been taken to hospital in Varna, on Bulgaria's east coast. Local media report that one of them has serious burns, and another is reportedly injured in the head. Several others have minor injuries. Cargo ships. According to media sources, these are cargo ships. The sunken ship, named Alfa Watan, sailed under the flag of Togo. It is not known what cargo the ship was carrying. The ship where the fire broke out, named Able, sailed under the flag of Palau. That ship is known to have been carrying grain. The attack took place at around 03.00 local time, about 112 kilometres from the coast, still within Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone. That country is a member of NATO. After the incident, both ships sent out distress signals. Bulgarian Prime Minister Radev held an emergency meeting with the relevant ministries and security services. It is not yet clear whether this was an attack with drones in the air, sea drones, or both. Reference to war between Russia and Ukraine. It is not yet clear who is behind the drone attack. However, in a televised statement, the Bulgarian prime minister referred to the Russian war in Ukraine. Reuters news agency, citing a source in maritime security, writes that initial analyses of the attack point to it likely being a Russian attack. "If this war does not end in time, the risk of a global conflict grows," said Prime Minister Radev. "We see that the war is escalating: all rules of international law are being violated and civilian ships are being attacked at sea. This is completely unacceptable." Russia has not yet responded to the incident. Fire on Turkish ship. The attack follows shortly after a fire on a ship in the Black Sea yesterday, outside the territorial waters of Romania. Two people died in that incident, and eleven crew members could be rescued. The Romanian Ministry of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> says it is not yet known what caused that fire. Ukrainian President Zelensky accuses Russia of a drone attack on a Turkish ship carrying maize. Since the start of the war between Ukraine and Russia four years ago, several European countries have had to deal with Russian drones violating their airspace, as well as with mines in the Black Sea on important trade and energy routes.

title: 'Swimming lessons for children with disabilities need to be more accessible'
lead: For children with a disability, swimming lessons are not always a given, especially when their parents have money worries. Municipal income support for these parents falls short, says the Mulier Institute, which carried out research on the subject. Swimming lessons for children with a disability are often more expensive than regular swimming lessons. The research shows that children benefit from smaller groups of four or two pupils and sometimes even one-on-one lessons. "That is so they have fewer distractions from other children and get more attention from their teacher," explains researcher Mirjam Stuij of the Mulier Institute. A swimming instructor also needs to know how to handle a child with a disability. These two factors make adapted swimming lessons more expensive. "That is difficult for parents, but also for swimming instructors." Existing schemes fall short Municipalities already offer schemes and allowances, but these are sometimes unclear and differ from municipality to municipality. Parents run into several issues when applying, Stuij explains. "For example, the allowance they receive does not cover the cost of the swimming lessons." There are also parents who formally have too high an income, but who, because of high care costs or other high costs due to the child's disability, still have money worries. They therefore do not qualify. Thirdly, the institute sees that applying for schemes can demand a lot from parents. This is because information from the municipality is unclear or because parents do not know where to turn. Fewer or no certificates Stuij stresses that parents consider a swimming certificate of great importance. "If my child falls into a ditch, I want them to be able to save themselves. I think we can all picture that very well in the Netherlands." Figures from the <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">CBS</entity> show that 14 percent of children living in poverty have a disability, compared with 8 percent of children not living in poverty. Figures from Mulier also show that children with a disability obtain a swimming certificate at a later age, fewer certificates, or no swimming certificate at all. Clarity and flexibility The institute advises municipalities to map out how things are arranged for them, what the municipality reimburses and for whom. "Because we know that varies enormously," says Stuij. The research leads to a number of recommendations for local governments. For example, good information provision for parents should be established and the application process should be made as clear as possible. The institute calls for more flexibility in income support. For example, a standard allowance that can be increased if the costs for a child are higher, Stuij explains. The institute also advises appointing a fixed point of contact for parents. "Someone who can help them with the application and, for example, with finding suitable swimming lessons."

title: Event organisers in Breda send urgent letter about higher permit costs
lead: Eighteen event organisations in Breda, such as Breda Jazz, Ploegendienst and carnival activities, have together sent an urgent letter to the city council. They demand more transparency about the announced price increases for event permits, writes Omroep Brabant . From 2027 the municipality will increase the costs of an event permit. For example, the cost of a permit for large events, such as the big carnival parade, will rise from 17.000 euro to nearly 37.000 euro. For smaller events, the rate will double from 4900 to just over 10.000 euro. 'It is not going to work' The organisations fear that the higher costs will be the downfall of some events. Stichting Kielegat, a volunteer organisation for carnival activities in the city, says it cannot afford the price increase. "I see no possibility of raising that amount extra within a year. It is simply not going to work", said chairman Rutger Westenburg after the announcement. The Breda Jazz Festival attracts around 250.000 visitors each year. Even so, the price increase also shocked chairwoman Hanneke Griffioen. "It is a substantial amount, so you blink and then think: am I reading this correctly?" She therefore wants to sit down with the municipality. "Because this is not a normal price increase." The municipality says the higher costs are necessary because for many years Breda has only passed on around twenty percent of the costs related to permit applications. "We have tried to keep the increase limited, but unfortunately... Everything is getting more expensive", said the responsible alderman Arjen van Drunen. According to Van Drunen, even after the increase the full costs are still not covered. Transparency Among the signatories of the letter are volunteer organisations, but also commercial organisers. Koninklijke Horeca Nederland Breda and organised hospitality entrepreneurs have also joined. "We above all want transparency with all these organisations about how these permit fees have been built up", says Johan de Vos of Koninklijke Horeca Nederland Breda. "We want to see what the justification is. That this is a broadly supported demand is clear from all the organisations that have backed this letter." The organisers demand access to the full calculation behind the new rates. They want to know how many official hours are charged, which hourly rates are passed on, and whether costs for enforcement, public order and traffic measures have been included in the rates. Afterwards they want to discuss with the municipality which part of the costs organisers should pay. According to them, it should be clear which costs really belong to the permit and which belong to the municipality's normal tasks. "The mere fact that certain work takes place around events does not automatically mean that these costs can be recovered from the individual organiser through event fees", they write. The event organisations also want to examine whether the permit process can be made cheaper.

title: Heavy art book with work by Dalí stolen from French museum
lead: One of the most expensive and heaviest books in the world has been stolen from a museum in France. The cover of the artwork Apocalypse, made by Salvador Dalí alone, weighs 150 kilos. It is a mystery how the thieves got the extremely heavy book out of the building. The public prosecutor has started an investigation into the theft in the municipality of Issoire, about a hundred kilometres west of Lyon. The police have not released details about the art theft in the night from Sunday to Monday. It is unclear whether there are suspects. 'Murder of heritage' The owner of the artwork calls the theft an attack on the French cultural sector. "France has been murdered last night. French heritage has been murdered", Christian Karoutzos said yesterday evening to French media. The Apocalypse was made between 1958 and 1961 and weighs about 210 kilos in total. Fourteen of the most renowned artists of that time contributed to the project. The famous Spanish painter Dalí made the bronze cover. Dalí was one of the best-known artists of the last century. He painted surrealist works and was an eccentric person. He wore a distinctive thin moustache, with the tips curled upwards. The moustache is "the most serious part of my personality", Dalí once said jokingly in an interview.

title: Cat-theft ring in Vietnam busted: 'Thousands of animals stolen'
lead: The Vietnamese <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> has dismantled a network responsible for the theft of thousands of cats in Ho Chi Minh City. Twelve men are suspected of stealing and reselling the animals, presumably for consumption, state media report. The main suspect is 39-year-old Luu Thanh Binh, who is the suspected gang leader. According to the police investigation, Binh bought live cats and stored them at a location in the city before reselling them. Several people worked under him, who in turn recruited others to steal cats in different parts of the city. The network consisted of small groups, each with its own area. At night, the groups went through residential neighbourhoods on motorbikes in search of cats. They made their own cat traps. According to the suspects, each group stole four to ten cats per night. 50 cats rescued In July, the police raided the Dong Thanh district. 50 cats were rescued during the raid. Dozens of cat traps, scales, mobile phones, motorbikes, clippers and cash were also seized. Of the 50 rescued cats, thirteen have since been reunited with their owners, while the search for the other owners continues. During questioning, the suspects reportedly admitted to having stolen a total of 2,700 cats. It is not known exactly how long the gang was active. During an earlier raid in June, 400 cats were rescued. The animals were locked up in 45 cages. During that raid, more than 80 dead cats were also found, which were being kept cold with ice. Nine people were arrested. Eating cats and dogs Eating cats and dogs is not illegal in Vietnam, provided sellers hold the proper licences. The police emphasise that knowingly buying illegal meat is punishable, as is trading in stolen animals. There are no official figures on the local consumption of dogs and cats, but resistance to it has been growing in Vietnam in recent years. Particularly among young people and pet owners, writes animal welfare organisation Humane World for Animals. They point to the cruelty and animal abuse involved in the illegal catching, trade, storage and transport of the animals. But there is also increasing opposition because cats and dogs are increasingly seen as companion animals and not as food.

title: Online trade in 'blackmail packages' of women, Belgium and Netherlands investigate
lead: <entity id="person:david-van-weel">Minister Van Weel</entity> (VVD) of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-justitie-en-veiligheid">Justitie en Veiligheid</entity> will ask the Dutch <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> to offer help to the Belgian police, who are investigating the trade in nude photos of women on the so-called darkweb. He said this in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>, where he was asked questions about the case, which RTL reported. Nude photos and private data of hundreds of Belgian and Dutch women are being traded on the hidden part of the internet, RTL reported. Ready-made packages with intimate photos, social media profiles and contact details are offered on a site that has been active since 2023. Women can be harassed and blackmailed with them. For one euro per victim, access to private data and photos is provided. The 'packages' are sold to several people at once. The website offers, for a payment of 250 euros, to remove the data from the platform, but it is unclear whether this actually happens. 'Perverse practices' There is great revulsion across the House. Minister Van Weel spoke of appalling practices of a "perversity you do not often see". He also expressed his sympathy with the victims. One of the victims is a 31-year-old woman from Limburg who told her story to RTL. She had panic attacks when she heard she was on the site. Fifteen years later her photos still keep appearing. Van Weel called her story shocking and believes she is doing fantastic work, including by removing the shame felt by victims. MPs want justice to act firmly, if necessary at European level. "This concerns organised sexual violence", says VVD MP Becker. "These are not incidents, but a business model", says Pro MP Mutluer. The House wants the site to go offline as soon as possible. Parties also want the Dutch <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> to be involved in the case quickly. 'Investigation difficult' What is happening here is punishable, but investigating it will not be easy, says Van Weel. "It is technically not simple to find out who is behind it on the darkweb, where the server is, how a site can go offline". Van Weel says he "cannot take the darkweb offline with a bill tomorrow". According to him there are ways to take sites offline, but "first very specific technical investigations are needed, and we will certainly commit to those". The Belgian police have announced an investigation and Van Weel will ask the Dutch police to "consult the Antwerp police and see how we can help". The Dutch Openbaar Ministerie is not yet conducting an investigation into the case, a spokesperson told the NOS, but the OM does not rule out joining a later international joint investigation. "Given the facts and the number of potential Dutch victims, it would make sense if a request for help comes from Belgium; then we are also willing to help." Can you check whether your data has been leaked? For anyone worried after this news about whether her data or photos can be found on the darkweb, there is unfortunately no satisfactory answer: there is currently no simple way to search for that, says a spokesperson for the knowledge centre Offlimits to the NOS. "We do not advise people to search the darkweb themselves for their name or images. As far as we know there is no public and safe way to check that yourself on the darkweb." Moreover, she warns: "You don't know what you will encounter there. Other illegal or very shocking material can also be found in such environments. You also have no control over what appears on a page. Moreover, searching yourself gives no certainty whether you are or are not on the website. If you don't find your name, that does not automatically mean you are not in the database. And conversely, a namesake can of course cause confusion. It may also disrupt a police investigation." Her tip is: "Do you have concerns or concrete indications that your images or data have been shared, for example because someone is contacting or threatening you with them? Then get in touch with Offlimits or the police. We can look together at what is going on and which steps you can take."

title: Adults predominantly positive about LGBTI people, well-being of some groups 'concerning'
lead: Broadly speaking, the views of adult Dutch people on, for example, homosexuality are unchanged compared with two years ago. There are, however, large differences between the individual LGBTI+ groups. Moreover, the well-being of the groups varies greatly. This emerges from the biennial Lhbtiqa+monitor by Movisie, Panteia and Ipsos I&O. In September, another study revealed that acceptance of homosexuality among young people has declined over the past four years. That study was conducted among young people between the ages of 12 and 16. Who is this study about? The Lhbtiqa+monitor is a study carried out every two years on behalf of <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>. The abbreviation stands for the groups the study is about: lesbian, homosexual, bisexual, transgender, intersex, queer, asexual and non-binary persons. Not only their living situation is addressed. Every two years the researchers also ask about Dutch people's views on these groups. Although homosexuality is still predominantly viewed positively (84 percent), a slight shift is visible. Compared with two years ago, slightly more respondents think 'neutrally' about this group instead of 'positively'. The share of respondents who judge homosexuality negatively has remained stable (4 percent). Views on other groups have also remained broadly the same when compared with two years ago. The fact that little has changed in general is considered concerning by researcher Karijn van den Berg of Movisie. "Views on, for example, homosexuality are generally positive, but that applies much less to intersex, transgender and non-binary persons," the researcher said. When you zoom in on groups, changes are indeed visible. For instance, 65 percent of those surveyed found sex between two men "not disgusting" in 2024, while that number has now fallen to 60 percent. Moreover, more than a quarter of respondents have "difficulty with" kissing in public, mainly when it concerns two men. Two years ago that applied to about a fifth of Dutch people. Gender or sexual identity as a 'fashion phenomenon' The study also shows that being transgender, non-binary and bisexual is relatively often seen as a fashion phenomenon by those surveyed. That concerns the researchers. They also find it concerning that many respondents do not want a relationship with transgender, non-binary, bisexual, asexual or intersex persons. Another conclusion of the researchers is the limited knowledge about asexual, non-binary and intersex persons. Many questions about these groups are not answered by the respondents. They often indicate not knowing the answer or never having thought about it. "This finding shows that the knowledge about and understanding, or recognition, of these groups of persons in Dutch society is still fairly limited," the report states. The researchers did not only look at Dutch people's views on the individual LGBTI+ groups. They also mapped the well-being of those groups themselves. There too the differences between the groups are large, the report shows. Well-being of LGBTI+ persons Where the living situation of homosexual persons is generally comparable to that of heterosexuals, that of intersex, transgender and non-binary persons can be called concerning, the report states. For instance, they more often deal with depression, suicidal thoughts, financial problems and discrimination, a survey among these groups shows. Researcher Van den Berg calls these large differences in well-being between the studied groups "very striking". "We see a real gap between, for example, homosexual and transgender people, both in terms of acceptance and in terms of well-being." The researchers make a number of recommendations to the cabinet. For instance, they advise education and information about sexual and gender diversity. They also recommend paying attention to online hate and disinformation about LGBTI+ persons in lessons about media literacy. Attention to the studied groups in vocational training programmes in care and welfare and more room for inclusive policy in government are other recommendations. The groups the study is about Lesbian persons: women who are attracted to women. Homosexual persons: men who are attracted to men. Bi+ persons: persons who are attracted to more than one gender. Transgender persons: people whose gender identity does not (fully) correspond with the sex assigned at birth. Non-binary persons: people who identify as non-binary, feel at home with a gender identity outside the (binary) categories of man and woman. Intersex persons: are born with a body that does not correspond with the image most people have of man or woman. Queer persons: people who cannot find themselves in the usual, fixed (binary) frameworks and boxes for gender and/or sexual orientation, or reject these frameworks. Asexual persons: people who experience no or little sexual attraction to other persons.

title: IND must work through 140,000 Ukrainian applications, asylum system under further pressure
lead: The asylum applications of over 140,000 Ukrainians that have been put on the shelf must still be reviewed and assessed. This follows from a ruling of the European Court of Justice. Among administrators it is beginning to filter through that this could have major consequences for the pressure on the asylum chain, according to those involved. <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> also admits that it has a problem. Ukrainians who came to the Netherlands because of the war fell under the Temporary Protection Directive. This EU-devised rule allows displaced persons to receive temporary protection. The Netherlands arranged it so that if you wanted that protection, you also had to submit an asylum application. That application was then automatically suspended. And parking asylum applications is not allowed, the European court ruled last week. "We have long chosen not to handle applications from Ukrainians in the Netherlands, because they already received protection," says responsible minister Van den Brink of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-am">Asiel en Migratie</entity>. "Also because it was a very large number. The court now clearly says: it must be done," the minister said. Extra pressure on the asylum chain. Asylum lawyer Wil Eikelboom: "In hindsight it was not such a good idea to link temporary protection to submitting an asylum application. Quite awkward." In other countries no asylum application was automatically filed when someone fell under the Temporary Protection Directive. "The Netherlands really is an exception there," says Ricky van Oers, university lecturer in Sociology of Law and Migration Law at Radboud University. All applications from Ukrainians must therefore now be handled. "The question is how the IND is going to do this, they actually have no capacity for it at all," says Eikelboom. The minister admits that this ruling of the court will "certainly add extra pressure" to the asylum system. "At the same time the court also offers room," the minister states, hoping this way to make his problem manageable. He interprets the ruling so that he does not have to handle the applications of all Ukrainians immediately. Van den Brink first wants to handle the asylum applications of people who are arriving now, and at the same time the more than fifty thousand people who were already on the waiting list, and only then give priority to this group of Ukrainians. In short: yes, the asylum applications of the Ukrainians must be handled, but the minister wants to wait with most of them for now. According to university lecturer in migration law Van Oers there are indeed nuances to the ruling of the European Court. "Because it concerns so many applications, the Netherlands may be able to handle the procedures in phases. They can also decide to give priority to certain groups, for example families." But the question is how much room the minister's approach will actually provide, because all of this will certainly mean extra work. 'Permanent temporariness' The advantage of that directive for Ukrainians was, for example, that they could work here immediately, unlike asylum seekers. It also temporarily grants the right to shelter, medical care and education for children. But that also brings uncertainty. "Ukrainians live here in permanent temporariness," says Van Oers. "Because of that temporary protection there is continually little prospect of building a life. While in fact there is an asylum application pending. Such an asylum status gives more certainty." The temporary protection of Ukrainians runs until March 2028. It is still unclear whether it will be extended afterwards. According to Vluchtelingenwerk the ruling of the European Court of Justice has probably not yet reached many Ukrainians. "But it undoubtedly leads to more unrest and uncertainty. Return to Ukraine is currently not a realistic option." Vluchtelingenwerk wants a sustainable plan for Ukrainians in the Netherlands. "With a fast and careful assessment of their residence permits, so that these people, who have already experienced a great deal, know where they stand." The highest administrative judge in the Netherlands must now assess the European ruling. Afterwards it will become clear what its significance is in practice. According to lawyers, the Netherlands cannot simply ignore the ruling in any case.

title: Podcast De Dag: what makes the French schoolchildren's protests ever bigger
lead: The French secondary school protest is growing, more violent and more political. Today, during a national protest day, certainly tens of thousands, according to the union even hundreds of thousands of people took to the streets in solidarity with French students. The protest erupted two weeks ago, at the start of the school year. It concerns a shortage of teachers, deficient timetables and materials. And inequality: schools in the banlieues are hit much harder than schools elsewhere. Listening? You can listen to this episode of De Dag via NPO Luister and all other podcast apps. Like it? Then don't forget to subscribe. In the podcast De Dag, Dutch students Raoul and Felix, who study in France, tell what they see happening around them and what moves their fellow students. Niek Pas is a France expert at the UvA and also previously taught in France. According to him, we must also view the protests in light of the upcoming presidential elections. Politicians are jumping on the unrest and pointing fingers at each other about the causes of the poor state of education. Respond? Email dedag@nos.nl Presentation and editing: Elisabeth Steinz Editorial: Max Smedes and Wouter Sloekers Final editing: Judith van de Hulsbeek

title: Free ice cream action gets out of hand, police step in
lead: An action in which an ice cream parlour handed out free ice creams in Almere got out of hand yesterday. The many young people present became so unruly that, on police advice, the shop had to close its doors. "We wanted to do something good for the neighbourhood and this is what we get," the owner told Omroep Flevoland . The free ice cream action reached many young people. On TikTok the announcement was viewed more than 130,000 times. According to the entrepreneur, the first hour went without problems, but the atmosphere changed after that. Sent away According to the owner there was pushing and pulling, and young people harassed staff. "We almost had to work as bodyguards instead of as ordinary staff." Eventually the police were called. According to the entrepreneur, several vehicles arrived on the scene and officers went into the shop with a police dog. A police spokesperson says the young people were sent away but that no one was arrested. The owner is disappointed. "We wanted to bring people together and organise something fun. But of course our staff need to be able to work safely."

title: French prime minister: no lessons at French schools in the coming days, talking with each other
lead: There will be no lessons at all lycées throughout France for the next three days. That is what French prime minister Lecornu has said. The reason is the large-scale school student protests of the past weeks. Lycées are the upper secondary schools, for students from about 15 years of age. The prime minister wants, together with the minister of Education, to give a political answer to the protests. He hopes that schools and students will enter into dialogue with each other in the coming days. It is not clear whether schools will respond to this or whether schools want to keep lessons going. Lecornu calls the protests "real" and believes that students must be listened to. He also named a number of points of attention on which the government can work, such as the state of the school buildings. Protests today too. Today too tens of thousands of people took to the streets in French cities. It was the largest day of action since the protests began last month. Hundreds of schools were closed again. In the meantime, trade unions and parents have also rallied behind the protests. According to the ministry of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity>, at least 250,000 people are out today. One of the trade unions speaks of 450,000 demonstrators, even before the large demonstration in Paris began. Tens of thousands of people are also expected there during a march. In several places along the route the mood is grim. Pupils and students demand more money for education. They are furious about the poor state of the school buildings and the teacher shortage. In several cities the police used tear gas. In Strasbourg, Lyon and Rennes among others, demonstrators set fires and threw objects at the police. According to prime minister Lecornu, 85 teachers and 215 pupils were injured in the protests of the past days. He calls it "the heaviest toll that education staff has suffered in decades". 715 police officers were also injured in the protests.

title: Once again large protests and violence in France, what is behind it?
lead: It has been unrest in France for a few weeks now. What began as a small-scale protest at a secondary school outside Paris has grown into a national popular movement, which university students have also joined. At the same time, hooligans or rioters are abusing the demonstrations. Where does this unrest come from? Whereas in recent days it was still about hundreds of schools, demonstrators today blocked 1800 secondary schools. According to the ministry of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity>, at least 250,000 people took to the streets, from Rennes and Toulouse to Paris, to further increase pressure on the French government. Education and teachers' unions are also taking part. The demonstrators want an end to a series of problems in French education, such as the poor condition of school buildings. The police are cracking down hard: last week 5000 people were arrested, 87 percent of whom were minors. On 17 September, pupils in a suburb of Paris decided to block the entrance to their secondary school. They wanted to take a stand against overcrowded classes and long school days. The pupils were not alone; they received support from teachers who voiced their concerns about the shortage of staff and materials, and the high workload. French secondary school pupils are required to have more lesson hours than their peers in many other European countries. "I leave home at half past six in the morning and when I get back it's seven in the evening. I see my teachers more often than my family. That is not normal", says a pupil from Val-de-Marne to local media. Vulnerable neighbourhoods In addition, many French secondary schools struggle with a shortage of basic facilities such as tables and chairs. Due to a lack of air conditioning, temperatures in classrooms rise sharply during heatwaves, while in winter it can be bitterly cold. Pupils point to deferred maintenance, which leads to leaking roofs, cockroaches and rat infestations, as in Saint-Denis. According to activists, these problems are often most severe at schools in socioeconomically vulnerable neighbourhoods. Parcoursup, the platform through which pupils apply for further education, is also under fire. Sometimes pupils have to wait months until they know whether they will be admitted to their chosen course of study. According to many of them, the system causes uncertainty and extra stress about their future. Police violence The first demonstration was still fairly peaceful, with a few rubbish bins set on fire. But images spread rapidly via social media and protests spread to other cities outside Paris. The movement received almost immediate support from the radical left party La France Insoumise (LFI), which has a strong following among young people. That support is electorally significant, as some of the pupils will be allowed to vote in the French presidential election for the first time next year. Right-wing politicians accuse the party of fuelling and politicising the protest. For example, the LFI mayor of Saint-Denis, Bally Bagayoko, said that violence "is legitimate in some cases". These words, which according to Bagayoko were taken out of context, caused much uproar. Centre-right presidential candidate Bruno Retailleau asked whether LFI should not be banned. LFI leader Mélenchon, on the other hand, argues that his party only supports the movement and does not organise it. He wants the demonstrations to remain non-violent and points to what he describes as the police's "brutality". According to him, officers frequently used tear gas and batons to disperse demonstrators. Yesterday, in the French city of Lens, a 15-year-old pupil lost his hand after picking up a stun grenade that had been thrown by riot police. Nearly 200 pupils and teachers have since been injured. Despite the disorder, the demonstrators are continuing. So today at least 250,000 people took to the streets. According to one of the unions, there were even 450,000. On Sunday, Prime Minister Lecornu wrote a letter in which he promises to come up with concrete commitments for pupils this week, including making school buildings better able to withstand the effects of climate change. In addition, 1,2 billion euros extra is being allocated to education in the budget, which still has to be approved by parliament. He also announced that no lessons will be given at secondary schools up to and including Friday, in the hope that schools and pupils will then enter into dialogue with each other. But the fear is that the genie is already out of the bottle and that the protest movement could grow into a much broader popular movement. This is also because there is a lot of frustration in France about high fuel prices. The Yellow Vests movement, which largely paralysed France in 2018, has announced it will return to the streets on 17 October.

title: Dispute over box 3: coalition divided over paper gifts
