title: Voices from besieged Taiz in Yemen: 'Our city is gasping for breath'
lead: The Yemeni city of Taiz is completely surrounded by Houthi rebels. All access roads have been closed, and people and goods cannot enter or leave the city. Because of its strategic location, the country's third city has for years been an asset for the warring parties. Once again it is an important front in the recently flared-up war between the Houthis and the Yemeni government army. The United Nations and international aid organisations cannot reach the city and last week sounded the alarm. Four residents of the city describe the steadily worsening situation below. Ghada Nabil, works for an aid organisation: "My city has turned into an open-air prison. Residents are deprived of all basic necessities. There is constant danger. A systematic policy of starvation and isolation prevails here. The situation has deteriorated very quickly. It is no longer just the limited freedom of movement. The entry of food, drinking water and fuel into the city is being systematically blocked. The fighting is getting closer. I hear the sound of random shelling of residential neighbourhoods and civilians alongside the roar of explosions, mortar fire, the rattle of machine guns and the buzzing of drones. These sounds constantly remind us that we live in the middle of an active front line. I am afraid the world will forget us, while Taiz sinks into a humanitarian disaster. Crushed under the weight of this siege and the deafening international silence." Latifa Abdullah, accountant: "Our city is gasping for breath. We want to live, but we have to weigh every step we take carefully. It feels as if we have been completely cut off from the rest of the world. People who could afford it fled the city before the siege. Those who had nowhere to go stayed, rooted in their homes, their land and their memories of better times. Only at home do I feel safe. Together with my children and my family, far away from the stress on the street. I wonder what the future holds for our children, given the current state of education and the overall worsening situation. My hope is that a solution will come and the roads to Taiz will open again. My dream is that our children will know peace and safety and can experience the normal life they deserve, far removed from the fear, oppression and exhaustion we are going through now." Khaled Naggar, university professor: "Universities and schools are closed, a great challenge for our students. This war quickly led to the collapse of our infrastructure. Waste lies everywhere on the streets. Because of the fighting it is not being collected, because they cannot reach the rubbish dumps. The amount of waste on the streets affects the health of residents. Diseases are spreading quickly. We are worried about basic necessities. The flour supply is running out. There was panic and people tried to stock up as much as possible. Flour, sugar and oil were hoarded in large quantities. That means those products are now barely to be found on the market. If you do find them, they are unaffordable. I expect it to get worse quickly in the coming days if the roads do not open for food. And the petrol crisis is also growing. There is no diesel for the water pumps, so water supplies are running out. The lack of diesel is causing major problems in the hospitals. Many hospitals will have to close their emergency departments and other wards. They need help to prevent patients from dying unnecessarily." Weam Adnan, human rights activist: "There is hardly any traffic on the streets, because nowhere is safe. If you go out onto the street, you can be hit by a sniper or a bombardment. It is not only soldiers who are fighting; homes of ordinary civilians and hospitals have all been attacked by the Houthis. We hear the fighting every day and are starting to distinguish between the different types of weapons that hit the neighbourhoods. My greatest concern is that the Houthis are getting closer and closer to the city. They are not welcome here. My dream is that this war ends with the elimination of the Houthis. We want peace and want to begin reconstruction. We hope that the criminals will be punished for all their crimes in Taiz, because currently all kinds of war crimes can take place with impunity."

title: Afghans washed ashore on Texel were smuggled by convicted criminal
lead: The two Afghan men whose body parts washed ashore on Texel in 2023 were smuggled to the United Kingdom by an extensive people smuggling network led by criminal Idriss Ghazi Kareem. That is according to research by NH and Zembla. Kareem was sentenced at the end of last year in Paris to fifteen years' imprisonment for people smuggling, which he even managed to organise from prison. According to the judge he earned hundreds of thousands of euros a year from this. Shoe with foot On 6 October 2023 a shoe with a foot in it and a lower body were found on the beach of Texel. For a long time it remained unclear whose the washed-up body parts were. Police detective Fetze Venema spent 2.5 years on the identification. Together with the Red Cross he traced relatives of the missing men in Afghanistan for DNA research. Only this summer did it become clear that they were two Afghan refugees: Samiullah (20) and Ahmad Jan (27). On the night of 12 August 2023 the men boarded a rubber boat together with 66 others just north of Calais. The boat was not suitable for the crossing to England and so did not reach the coast. On open water the engine failed and after an explosion the boat tore. Sixty migrants survived, eight others did not. Of those eight, six were pulled from the water. Samiullah and Ahmad Jan went missing. Their remains washed ashore on Texel two months later. After this boat disaster, French justice tracked an extensive people smuggling network, led by Kareem. He arranged boats and other materials needed for migrant crossings of the Channel. Victims of escape attempts This year at least 26 people have died crossing the Channel in rubber boats, including two children. The actual number is probably higher because people are still missing. In 2025 there were 29 dead and missing, in 2024 83, in 2023 17. That ringleaders of such smuggling networks come from the Netherlands is, according to the Royal Netherlands Marechaussee, not unusual. Our country plays an important role in the trade: "It concerns the import, transit and storage of ship supplies that are transported to the French coast. There they are used to get migrants across to Great Britain." From intercepted conversations the Dutch <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> concludes that the traders themselves know the materials are not suitable for this. "For us that is an aggravating circumstance", says public prosecutor Petra Hoekstra. "They think the money outweighs a human life. And that means they knowingly put people on floating coffins." What do you think of the NOS app and website? What do we do well? What could be better? We are curious to hear your opinion. Complete the survey via this link .

title: Police take webshops selling dangerous fake pills offline, linked to three deaths
lead: The police have taken thirty websites offline where illegal medicines and drugs were sold. Three suspects who are said to be behind these sites were arrested this week. The police also hold them responsible for the webshop Slaappillen.net and link their sites to at least three deaths. The police suspect that the suspects simply continued selling, for example, sedatives, sleeping pills and painkillers, after Slaappillen.net was shut down last year. That happened after a woman from Voorburg died after ordering the strong painkiller oxycodone there. The fake pills contained nitazenes, a dangerous synthetic substance that carries a high risk of overdose. New webshops The suspects now arrested, according to the police, ensured that the sale of illegal medicines continued unabated via other sites. Customers of Slaapmiddelen.net were sometimes even directly invited to them. Whenever the government had websites taken offline, new variants appeared. According to the police, the three suspects played an essential role in setting up and running ever new webshops. Dangerous counterfeit medicines, possibly including contaminated oxycodone, were also sold there. Servers This time the police not only took the webshops offline but also seized the servers on which the sites ran. In this way the police hope to prevent new points of sale from being quickly set up again. "We have brought down all the technology behind the websites", says Ron van Brussel, responsible at the National Unit Investigation and Interventions for tackling serious organised crime. "This makes it harder to make a comeback." Prescription The suspects are a 35-year-old man from Kwintsheul, a 39-year-old man from Rotterdam and a 66-year-old man from The Hague. They are suspected of offering, selling and supplying illegal medicines, which led to the death of three people. The medication they are said to have sold is only available in the Netherlands on doctor's prescription and through a pharmacy. The webshops taken offline targeted the Dutch market, but sometimes also German or French customers. "The customers are often vulnerable people who need sleeping or sedative medicines that they cannot get through regular channels", Van Brussel says. "They then go looking online. Then you don't really know what you're buying." The precise composition of the medicines is often unknown, so users run serious health risks. The police call on people to report themselves if they know someone who has become seriously ill or even died after using pills ordered online. Relatives pleased Besides the arrests there were also several searches this week. The police seized, among other things, crypto wallets of the suspects. Various storage sites of illegal medicines have also already been found in recent times. Next week two men will appear before the judge who are said to have played a subordinate role in the organisation behind Slaappillen.net. The police are therefore now a step further in the investigation into the main responsible persons. Further arrests are not ruled out. Relatives of one of the victims of the fake oxycodone pills from Slaappillen.net respond with pleasure. "Congratulations to the police that there is finally progress in the search for the organisation behind the website that proved fatal to our daughter", they say. Trade not over Alongside the investigation into the group behind Slaapmiddelen.net and the replacement sites, the case against the webshop Funcaps is also still ongoing. That too sold counterfeit medicines and designer drugs on a large scale. The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> links more than twenty deaths to substances sold through Funcaps. The owners are still in custody. Although the police think that crucial players from the group around Slaapmiddelen.net have now also been arrested, the trade in illegal medicines is certainly not over. "There are several criminal groups keeping these kinds of sites online", says Van Brussel.

title: Fire in Delft city centre under control
lead: A fire broke out in the Delft city centre this morning. The fire is now under control. As far as is known, no one was injured. The fire broke out around 06:15 in a building on Kerkstraat, close to the Nieuwe Kerk. The flames spread quickly, and the fire brigade turned out with many personnel and vehicles to fight the blaze. "This concerns the old centre of Delft. That is very vulnerable. We would rather have too much material than too little", a fire brigade spokesperson told Omroep West . Because there was a risk the fire would spread to other buildings, ten homes were evacuated as a precaution. People who were troubled by the smoke were advised to close windows and doors and to switch off the mechanical ventilation. People taken in at a café Some fifteen to twenty people have been taken in at a nearby café. It is not yet clear when they can return home. "Everyone was initially taken in at the construction depot. That was cold. I then opened up my business", says the pub owner. "I woke up and live nearby. So I went to look. It turned out an emergency location was needed. So I made my business available." Although the fire is under control, the risk of it spreading to other buildings has not yet passed, the fire brigade says. Parts of the affected building are being demolished to check whether there are still any hotspots. Nothing is yet known about the cause of the fire. "So we also do not yet know whether the fire started inside or outside the building. The fire was first seen at the rear", the fire brigade said.

title: Florida officer finds dead man and moves into his house, caught after expensive renovation
lead: In the US state of Florida, a 35-year-old police officer has been arrested after taking on the identity of a dead man. In July 2022 the officer had responded in the city of Lauderhill to a report to check on the welfare of a person. On arrival it turned out that 71-year-old Dennis West had died. The officer reported this, and the medical examiner then determined that West had died of natural causes, and so the matter seemed closed. The officer, Brian Louis Sguros, however presented himself to the medical examiner as a close friend of the deceased and said that West had no family members left. He would therefore handle the death himself. Using the police database, the officer looked up the man's date of birth, social security number and other details, and in August 2022 Sguros finally moved into West's house. So as not to arouse suspicion with the local authorities, he simply paid the property tax and energy bills in the name of the deceased. New front door and windows He also forged West's signature to obtain a permit to renovate the house. A contractor who came in 2024 to replace the front door and some windows remembers his meeting with Sguros, according to American media reporting on the basis of the police report. The officer told the contractor that West was "not available". That the man had been dead for years was not mentioned. A year later, in 2025, the officer attempted to put the property permanently in his own name and contacted the local <entity id="org:zbo-dienst-voor-het-kadaster-en-de-openbare-registers">kadaster</entity> for this purpose. In the end it did not get that far: the fraud came to light when the heirs of the deceased man were traced by a property firm that wanted to buy the house. Renovation of more than 2 tons After that company bought the house, staff were surprised to find Sguros in the house. Confronted with the situation, he handed over the house keys, although he also started a civil case to recover the renovation costs of 214,000 dollars. The lawsuit that followed, however, raised so many questions that the authorities started a criminal investigation into Sguros. He is now suspected of fraud, identity misuse and unlawfully taking possession of the home. His defence is that he moved into the house to prevent it from being squatted. The Miami Herald reports that the officer has been placed on leave without pay. Yesterday the judge set the bail at 25,000 dollars. After paying it, he left the prison running and wearing two face masks. A local TV station has the footage:

title: Number of women in top positions lags behind: 'Only in 2044 will one third be women'
lead: "I had hoped that we would have reached the goal by now with which I started the list twenty years ago", sighs Mijntje Lückerath-Rovers. As professor of Corporate Governance, she has been compiling the Dutch ranking for 20 years on the representation of women and men in top positions: the Female Board Index. When she started the list in 2006, she set the goal that a third of supervisory directors and a third of executive directors would be women. Meanwhile, the number of female executive directors at the 81 listed companies in the Netherlands has risen to 18 percent. But Professor Lückerath-Rovers sees no acceleration in new appointments. The number of female supervisory directors is above a third. For those supervisors a statutory limit has been introduced; for executive directors that is not the case. Mixed picture According to Lückerath-Rovers, this year's list gives a mixed picture. "On the one hand there has been an increase in the share of female supervisory directors for a number of years, but on the other hand the increase in the number of female executive directors remains disappointing." At the current trend, a third of executive directors would only be women in 2044. There are now 21 companies with at least a third women on both the management board and the supervisory board, up from seventeen companies last year. In addition, at four companies (PostNL, Triodos, Fastned and Hydratec) both the management and supervisory seats are split fifty-fifty between men and women. At ABN Amro both boards have a majority of women. When the professor started the list, only 2 percent of executive directors and 8 percent of supervisory directors were women. Those percentages have now grown considerably to 18 and 44 percent respectively. Statutory quota: how does it work? Since 1 January 2022 a statutory quota applies to the supervisory board of listed companies. At least a third must be women and a third men. This year 71 of the 81 companies in the Female Board Index meet this standard. The ten companies below this limit are mainly smaller listed firms. Falling below a third does not automatically mean that a company is breaking the law. There is currently no statutory quota for the management board. For her research, Lückerath-Rovers has ranked all listed companies in the Netherlands since 2008. After each publication, the professor noticed that public debate on this flared up. And that companies made changes. "For example, I noticed that companies at the bottom of the list appointed more women the following year". Although after 20 years it is a good moment for Mijntje Lückerath-Rovers to pass the baton of the Female Board Index to someone else, she remains involved. "The importance of women at the helm must be continually emphasised. Companies should be ashamed if they have a top that consists only of men." According to the professor, staff also have a role to play. "Employees must continue to speak out for more women in executive positions." 'Missing opportunities' State Secretary <entity id="person:judith-tielen">Judith Tielen</entity> of Emancipation feels that the number of women in top positions is not growing fast enough. "Since the introduction of the statutory quota the number of women in top positions has been rising, and that is good. But it is slow. Especially when you look at the number of executive directors, it really is not fast enough. Organisations are missing opportunities." Next year she will evaluate the statutory quota. Tielen: "I am also going to talk with companies, organisations and women about what is needed to make more progress on the number of women at the top and in the management layers below that."

title: Government pages back online after PHP vulnerability, no data leaked or stolen so far
lead: The last websites of the Dutch government that were still unreachable overnight following yesterday's major PHP vulnerability are now back online. The sites Meld Misdaad Anoniem and Overheid.nl are accessible again, as are several judiciary websites and the website of the <entity id="org:rijksinstituut-voor-volksgezondheid-en-milieu">Rijksinstituut voor Volksgezondheid en Milieu</entity> (RIVM). NotuBiz is also back online. That is a service with which municipalities, provinces and water boards publish official notices. "After thorough testing, all systems are up and running again," says a spokesperson. Many personal and smaller business websites are still unreachable, because hosting providers have temporarily shut them off as a precaution, pending the update. Hosting providers are companies that provide storage space and internet connections for customers, so that they do not have to do so themselves. Update After the vulnerability was made public yesterday morning by the foundation that manages the programming language, many business and government sites worldwide went offline. After the foundation distributed a security update, most services came back online over the course of the evening and night. Nevertheless, some government services remained unreachable until this morning, as a precaution. No cases are yet known in the Netherlands in which data has actually been leaked or stolen as a result of the PHP problems, a spokesperson for the <entity id="org:zbo-autoriteit-persoonsgegevens">Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens</entity> (AP) reports. Organisations are legally required to report to this supervisory authority if there is a possible data breach involving personal data.

title: Police get help from military police to tackle nuisance in Ter Apel
lead: Police in Ter Apel are getting help from the Royal Military Police to tackle the problems in the village, RTV Noord reports. A group of migrants, mainly 'veiligelanders', is causing a lot of nuisance in the Groningen village. According to <entity id="person:jaap-velema">burgemeester Velema</entity>, it involves shoplifting and arguments, among other things. "We are dealing with a very high number of shoplifting incidents", he tells RTV Noord. On average it goes wrong twenty times a week. There are also, according to the mayor, regular incidents on and around the grounds of the reception centre, such as stabbings. The nuisance has now become so great that the <entity id="org:gemeente-westerwolde">gemeente Westerwolde</entity> has asked for extra deployment of the military police. Talks with the asylum minister Last month the mayor announced that the ministry would come up with new measures to tackle the nuisance in Ter Apel. A good month later, too little of that has come about, Velema said last night in the council. The mayor has a meeting this evening with minister Van den Brink of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-am">Asiel en Migratie</entity>. The asylum organisation <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-orgaan-opvang-asielzoekers">COA</entity> is also present. Velema wants to make clear in that meeting that the agreements to reduce the nuisance must also be kept. "I hope results will be achieved in the coming weeks. Actually, this nuisance should never have arisen at all", says the mayor. The military police will in any case help the police in Ter Apel in the coming months. Between 2022 and 2024 military police also stepped in in Ter Apel. "It is regrettable that this is necessary", says a COA spokesperson to RTV Noord. The ministry has not yet responded. Reception centre overcrowded The reception centre in Ter Apel has been overcrowded for months. Two weeks ago twenty asylum seekers were forced to sleep outside on the grass in the rain, because there were too few reception places. Last summer asylum seekers repeatedly tried to enter a residential care centre looking for a place to sleep. The care home has since hired security. "These are things we have not had before, and that is why we are contacting the minister", says Velema.

title: Record fine of 37 million euros for illegal gambling provider
lead: The <entity id="org:zbo-kansspelautoriteit">Kansspelautoriteit</entity> (Ksa) has imposed a record fine of 37 million euros on a gambling company. It concerns the illegal gambling company EOD Code SRL, registered in Costa Rica. The company offers gambling on all kinds of websites in our country without a licence, such as Instantcasino and Skyhills. The regulator had already established in 2024 that the company was in breach. EOD Code was then warned that it could receive a fine for the misconduct. The Ksa's first investigation focused on Instantcasino, but it later turned out that at least eleven other illegal gambling sites were active. The sites lacked visible age verification, and visitors could pay with crypto and anonymous payment methods. As a result, the company has now received a fine based on an estimate of the revenue it generated. "We have several instruments we can deploy, and we are deploying all of them, including imposing a fine," says the KSa. The regulator often sees that these kinds of parties, which operate from abroad, do not pay the fine. No response EOD Code was repeatedly given the opportunity to respond to the Kansspelautoriteit, but no response came, the regulator reports. To block access to the illegal sites, it has other options as well. For example, the Ksa works with hosting providers and payment service providers to block access to gambling sites.

title: Ukrainians who lost everything demand compensation from Russia via the Netherlands
lead: "I want nothing at all from Russia, but they destroyed my house. And they have to pay for that." Oleksandr Tereshchenko regularly wipes the tears from his cheeks as he describes how he lost his home in the Russian invasion of Ukraine. "I am not a soldier. My house was not a military base." Tereshchenko is one of many Ukrainians demanding compensation from Russia for the damage they have suffered from the violence in their country. Courts in their own country mostly rule in their favour, but the Russian authorities pay no attention to this. That is why various Ukrainian citizens and companies are now trying to pursue it through a Dutch court, as several ongoing lawsuits show. Chance in the Netherlands The aggrieved parties choose the Netherlands for various reasons. Tereshchenko does so out of hope, he explains: "Because of the history and the case over the shooting down of flight MH17. If there is a chance anywhere, it is in the Netherlands, the capital of global justice", he refers to the International Criminal Court in The Hague. Tereshchenko and his family lived in Horenka. This small sleepy town north of Kyiv turned into a war zone in February 2022, when Russian troops tried to take the nearby airfield before the attack on Kyiv. "Our apartment was hit by tanks, rockets, everything", says Tereshchenko. "We had to flee to the cellar. When it became quiet for a while, we crept outside. Nothing was left of our apartment." Tereshchenko, a lawyer in his own country, is realistic about his chances at the Dutch court: "I give myself a 0.1 percent chance, but I am trying anyway. If it succeeds, more people who have lost their homes to Russian violence may get something back." 'Alter ego' There is also another reason why Ukrainians try to fight out their lawsuits against Russia in the Netherlands. A lot of Russian money is still present in the Netherlands, for example from Dutch subsidiaries of gas giant Gazprom. The <entity id="org:hoge-raad">Hoge Raad</entity> ruled this year that Gazprom, as a state company, may be regarded as an 'alter ego' of the Russian state. For that reason, a claim against Russia via Gazprom may now be handled by a Dutch court. For example that of Farm Syu Zhnyva. This Ukrainian agricultural company had grain silos in the regions of Zaporizhzhia and Kherson. Those silos were partly looted "by Russian-speaking persons in Russian military uniforms", according to an interim ruling of the The Hague Court of Appeal from June. The rest of the grain has spoiled. Because of the disaster, Syu Zhnyva has now gone bankrupt. In Ukraine a court had ruled that the grain company is entitled to 75 million euros in damages. But because Gazprom does not pay, assets of Gazprom in the Netherlands were attached in 2024. Difficult, not unique Enforcing compensation from a State through the courts is not unique. However, it is difficult to sue a State, emphasises Mathijs ten Wolde, professor of international private law at the University of Groningen: "Certainly in another country." Ten Wolde points to Article 431 of the Dutch Code of Civil Procedure. It states that rulings of foreign courts cannot be enforced here. For this reason, Russia also disregards compensation awarded by Ukrainian courts. Exceptions are made for rulings in countries where the justice system meets international standards, Ten Wolde says: "If the procedures have been carefully followed, if a defendant has had sufficient opportunity to defend themselves and it does not conflict with public order." Money in the Netherlands If that is the case, a resident or company from Ukraine has a chance to recover the damage through a Dutch court. For example by having assets attached of the many Russian holdings that are here, including those of Dutch subsidiaries of Russian companies. Legal experts the NOS spoke with call the ongoing lawsuits very interesting, also because this is legally uncharted territory. However, they emphasise that this could become a matter of a long haul. The NOS asked the lawyer of Gazprom Nederland for a response to the ongoing lawsuits. The lawyer says that, due to the duty of confidentiality, they cannot respond on the substance. Claims commission in the Netherlands Late last year, the Netherlands announced it wants to become the host country for a special commission where Ukrainians can claim their war damage suffered during the Russian invasion. At that time, more than 80,000 damage claims had already been registered. This claims commission is not yet operational, according to the <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">ministerie van Buitenlandse Zaken</entity>. That can only happen when at least 25 states that have signed the founding treaty also ratify the treaty. In addition, these countries must guarantee at least half of the required total budget of 7.4 million euros. For now, ten countries, including the Netherlands, and the European Union have ratified the treaty for the claims commission. The ministry of Foreign Affairs expects that by mid-2027 the remaining sixteen countries will have signed.

title: Cabinet promise to cap student loan interest under pressure: plan turns out to be far too expensive
lead: Capping the interest rate on student loans at a maximum of 2.5 percent is risky and expensive. That is what <entity id="person:rianne-letschert">minister Letschert</entity> of Education (D66) writes to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. The minister "baalt ervan", but concludes that the plan is many times more expensive than thought. The coalition had reserved 40 million for it, but it will cost at least four times as much. That would have consequences for the rest of the education budget and the treasury. Letschert wants to discuss the problem with the Chamber soon, she writes. Amount could quickly rise Many students borrow money from the government so they can pay for their study time. Most have to repay that borrowed amount after their studies, and they pay interest on it. For a long time that interest was 0 percent, but in recent years the percentage has been rising. As a result, the amount that (former) students have to repay can quickly increase. For this reason D66, VVD and CDA agreed in the coalition agreement to introduce an interest cap of 2.5 percent. They reserved 40 million euros for this. Interest already above 2.5 percent The discussion about capping interest at 2.5 percent has become topical again in recent weeks. At the beginning of October the interest on student loans rose again, for hundreds of thousands of students even by one percentage point, to 3.28 percent. As a result, the interest is now higher for many (former) students than the coalition parties consider desirable. Letschert says she understands students' concerns, but says that the money now reserved for the maximum interest is not enough to work out the plans. Interest rises have regularly led to protests in recent years: That the plan for an interest cap poses a major risk to the government's treasury has been known at the ministry for years. In 2023, then education minister Dijkgraaf warned that an interest cap could 'drain' the Ministry of Education entirely. This is how it works: to pay out the student loans, the government itself also has to take out loans. If the interest on that loan rises sharply, the ministry has to cover the difference itself. That can quickly add up to tens of millions of euros per year. Moreover, students with an interest cap are likely to borrow much more than they need. For the money they thereby free up, they get a much higher savings rate at the bank or elsewhere. The ministry can reduce this risk by introducing the interest cap only for the current generation of students. However, according to the Ministry of Education this is difficult to implement, because <entity id="org:dienst-uitvoering-onderwijs">DUO</entity> would then have to distinguish between different generations of students. How many (former) students pay interest on student loans? According to the <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek</entity>, there are currently just over a million former students with student debt. There are also 400,000 people who are studying now and have student debt. The total student debt is currently around 28 billion euros. 145,000 people have student debt of more than 50,000 euros. Despite the earlier warnings, the current coalition parties nevertheless included the plan for an interest cap in their agreement. Student organisations want the coalition to keep that promise. They call on students to sign a petition. The anger is especially strong among former students who studied under the loan system. Then minister Bussemaker said, when that loan system was introduced, that students should not have to fear debt. Now the consequences of that high loan turn out to be greater for them than expected. The interest on student loans is always much lower than on other (commercial) loans. The repayment rules are also flexible: anyone with little or no income does not have to repay. Students can also temporarily pause repayment.

title: Signals at National Cyber Security Centre of misuse of PHP flaw
lead: The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) has received signals that the major flaw in the PHP programming language has now been misused. "We see attempts to exploit the vulnerabilities and we are receiving the first signals that this is successfully happening," says a spokesperson. Earlier, the NCSC said it did not yet see such signals. The NCSC advises companies to update systems quickly. "Attempts to exploit the flaw have been circulating since yesterday. We are in contact with all kinds of organisations at home and abroad, and through that channel we are receiving signals that exploitation is taking place." The NCSC does not want to say exactly what the concrete signals entail. The agency is conducting research, but that may take months. Protected At the same time, many websites have now been protected, research by NOS shows. At least 113.000 Dutch websites have demonstrably installed a newer version of PHP. As a result, those websites are no longer vulnerable to the flaw. However, around 145.000 Dutch websites may still be vulnerable. That cannot be said with certainty from a distance. These concern sites that run an old PHP version but which may nonetheless be protected through another route. Many problems The flaw in the PHP programming language, which many websites are built with, led to many problems yesterday. For example, the RTL Nieuws website went offline, as did a number of government sites. Municipalities using the Notubiz meeting system also could not log in, nor could accountants working with Exact software. This happened as a precaution, to prevent hackers from exploiting the flaw. At that moment there were no patches available yet, digital patches with which server administrators can protect their websites. Shortly before 16.00 the solution became available, after which many websites came back online in the course of the afternoon and evening.

title: No free bike bus on the Afsluitdijk in winter due to lack of passengers
lead: The free shuttle bus that lets people transport their bicycles across the Afsluitdijk will temporarily stop running on 1 November. In recent winters the service was barely used, which is why <entity id="org:rijkswaterstaat">Rijkswaterstaat</entity> has decided to save the money. For years it has not been possible to cycle along the 32-kilometer-long flood barrier. In 2019 the bike path was closed due to the reinforcement of the dike and the renewal of locks and pumps. The path has been largely open again since 2024, but cycling all the way to the other side is still not possible. To still get there by bicycle, people could use the free shuttle bus. Empty trips back and forth But in winter the bus often runs back and forth empty, says a spokesperson for Rijkswaterstaat to Omrop Fryslân . On average, fewer than thirty people per month used the bus, compared with 3,000 people per month in summer. "We drove back and forth empty quite a few days last year. That is a waste of money." From 1 March travelers can use the bus again. Later in the year cycling across the Afsluitdijk should be fully possible again: temporary bicycle bridges will be installed. These are likely to be put into use in the third quarter of 2027. Cheaper bicycle bridge The choice to install those temporary bicycle bridges is based on finances. Running the bike bus during the works would cost 14 million euros. Earlier this year, at the request of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>, <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> examined whether there might be a cheaper solution. That turned out to be the case: building temporary bicycle bridges. According to calculations, that would cost around 5 million euros.

title: Hajar (29) sent 'disturbing messages to an acquaintance' on the day she went missing
lead: The 29-year-old woman from Amsterdam who was found dead last week had sent "disturbing messages to an acquaintance" on the day of her disappearance. Hajar did so on Sunday morning 4 October, on the same day her parents contacted officers, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> reports. The police will not say what exactly she sent. De Telegraaf says it has seen WhatsApp messages in which Hajar sent "Help me. Now. He is killing me" to a family member. The police say Hajar had been away for longer periods before, but always came back. That weekend too she left with a suitcase, but she never returned. The police say Hajar sent the messages in the morning. Afterwards family members had no contact with her, after which they contacted officers in the evening, according to the police. It is not clear why that did not happen right away. Urgent a day later "Based on all the facts and circumstances known at that time, the disappearance was assessed as not urgent at that time", says the police. For privacy reasons nothing further is said about this. On Monday evening, a day later, the disappearance was nevertheless made urgent, because there was still no contact with Hajar. "That assessment is made by a judicial officer", says the police. "That happens based on facts and circumstances surrounding the disappearance, such as the behaviour and personal circumstances of the missing person, the statements of the reporter and other relevant information." Family members did not give permission that day to publish her photo, according to the police. Detectives did try to find her in several ways, the police say, for example by locating her phone. A property in the Amsterdam neighbourhood Buitenveldert was searched that night, but the woman and her phone were not found there. Suspect arrested Her body was eventually found on 16 October, in a suitcase in the water at the Amsteldijk. In connection with her death, a 23-year-old man has been arrested. He has Somali nationality and has lived in the Netherlands since he was six. This Abdi A. has a residence permit for an indefinite period and at the time of his arrest had no fixed residence. The man was arrested on Tuesday in the North Holland village of Spierdijk after he assaulted his foster father with a hammer. He will be brought before the investigating judge tomorrow, who will decide whether he remains in custody.

title: Residents of the Euromast have for months been hearing an 'irritating whistling tone', cause unknown
lead: A 'loud echo', 'constant rustling' or an 'irritating beep': residents around the Euromast in <entity id="org:gemeente-rotterdam">Rotterdam</entity> have been complaining for months about noise nuisance from the tower. The Rijnmond Environmental Service (DCMR) is investigating the cause, but so far there is no answer. "You really hear the sound all the time," says resident Sasha to Rijnmond. "Since June we haven't been sleeping. You wake up from it so many times." Since June, hundreds of reports have come in to the Rijnmond Environmental Service (DCMR), the municipality of Rotterdam and the Euromast itself. This week alone there were at least 75. The sound seems to depend on weather conditions such as the wind, the complaints show. No loose cables DCMR started an investigation. At first it was thought the sound was caused by loose cables. The Euromast had been closed since January for a major renovation; possibly something came loose as a result. A contractor therefore tightened several cables. But that did not help: in July the Euromast reopened and the work was finished, but the irritating sound was not. This is what the sound is like: Now that it is autumn, the sound has become worse, says Sasha. She thinks that is due to the wind. "It's no longer an irritating whistling tone, but really a loud screech. I turn the TV up louder in the evening so I don't have to hear it." Upper part DCMR has meanwhile established that the sound comes from the upper part of the tower. But the cause is still unclear. The investigation is complex, because according to the environmental service the sound is not constantly audible. A specialised engineering firm has meanwhile been brought in to help search for the source of the sound. At the same time, DCMR cannot rule out that some reports have a different cause and that the Euromast is not the only source of the reported noise nuisance.

title: Embassy in Cairo closes after nine days of protests against the Netherlands
lead: The Dutch embassy in the Egyptian capital Cairo is closed for the time being. The closure was decided after demonstrations against the Netherlands took place for the ninth day in a row, the embassy announced on Facebook. Each demonstration required the embassy to be evacuated for safety reasons. Protesters are demonstrating against the arrest of Ahmed Nasser by the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. Nasser is the deputy head of the 'Union of Egyptian Youth Abroad' and a mouthpiece of the government. He was arrested on 10 October and his pretrial detention has been extended by 14 days. The demonstrations at the Dutch embassy do not appear to have arisen spontaneously. Whereas demonstrations almost never take place in Egypt under the repressive government, demonstrators have now been dropped off by bus at the embassy every day in the Zamalek district. That is an island in the Nile where many embassies are located and where a large police presence is present. One day after Nasser's arrest, the Egyptian foreign minister asked his Dutch counterpart Berendsen in a phone call for Nasser's release and for clarification about his arrest. Although both ministers publicly stated after that conversation that they wished to continue the good relationship, the demonstrations at the embassy continued. Padlock at embassy in The Hague: Nasser was reportedly arrested in the Netherlands for threatening the activist Anas Habib. Habib became known last summer when he locked the gate of the Egyptian embassy in The Hague with a padlock. He filmed his action. As his reason he cited the Egyptian decision to keep the Rafah border crossing with Gaza closed for Palestinians wishing to flee. This led to a chain reaction in which Egyptians in more countries locked the Egyptian embassy. In a leaked video the Egyptian foreign minister addresses the ambassador to the Netherlands: "If anyone tries to attach a lock or anything else to the embassy, drag him inside and make his life a hell." At the time Habib's padlock action also led to a protest at the Dutch embassy in Cairo, demanding that the Netherlands do more to protect the Egyptian embassy. Habib was questioned by the Dutch police, but was allowed to await the investigation in freedom. Closed until further notice: When the embassy in Egypt will reopen is not yet known. The embassy remains reachable for consular assistance in case of emergency. The <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">Ministerie van Buitenlandse Zaken</entity> says the embassy has been "closed until further notice as a precaution" and that "the safety of our staff always has our highest priority". Regarding the protocols on evacuating the embassy during demonstrations, the ministry, for security reasons, would not say anything.

title: Political flanks capitalise on unrest in France: 'Violence polarises'
lead: Large-scale protests, looting and police violence have gripped France for weeks. The unrest is also further sharpening political tensions, just half a year before the French presidential elections, which will also be of great significance for Europe as a whole. Almost all parties are pointing the accusing finger at the radical-left party La France Insoumise (LFI) as the instigator of the violence. The party is criticised, for example, for failing to distance itself from the anarchist anti-police slogan ACAB (all cops are bastards), which was heard frequently during the demonstrations. Prime Minister Lecornu has called the parliamentary group leaders together to calm tempers. Security around the presidential elections is also central to this. Presidential candidate and LFI leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon has announced that his party will be present, but threatens to disrupt the talks. He wants to show that he will not be summoned by the prime minister. Mélenchon refuses to go along with the view that his party has fuelled the violence. Instead, he accuses <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> of failing to tackle the deep-rooted social and economic problems in the suburbs. According to him, responsibility for the unrest therefore lies with the government and the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>, and other tensions such as the war in the Middle East also play a role. With that frame, he especially appeals to young people. Exhausted and weakened The radical-right party Rassemblement National (RN) is also capitalising on public anger. The unrest strengthens the position of presidential candidate Marine Le Pen, says France expert Niek Pas. For Le Pen, the ongoing unrest is an ideal opportunity to position herself as the champion of order and security against a government that is weakened and exhausted and has lost its grip on the situation. "At the RN party office they are laughing their heads off", Pas says. "Le Pen does not need to do much to win votes, apart from radiating calm." Two rounds That Le Pen has the wind in her sails is also evident from a poll published this week. It shows her not only clearly in front as the favourite for the first round of the presidential elections, but also as the favourite for the second round. She will win it, whoever her opponent is, it seems. France goes to the polls next year on 18 April for the first round of the presidential elections. Two weeks later, on 2 May, the decisive second round follows between the two winners of the first round. NOS op 3 last week made this explainer on the unrest in France: While the political flanks gain support, the social democrats and centre-right are losing ground. Raphaël Glucksmann (Place Publique), Édouard Philippe (Horizons) and Gabriel Attal (Renaissance, the party of President Marcon) are falling in the polls. "Violence polarises", Pas says. "It is precisely the political centre that is struggling to find a convincing response to it. And that uncertainty is worrying. It underlines the deep crisis France is in: a social-societal, financial-economic and political crisis." Reckoning Last Saturday, the violence completely got out of hand. Shops and supermarkets were looted, and symbols of the republic bore the brunt: the town hall of Limoges went up in flames and that of Marseille was stormed. "Le 17 octobre, Saturday, was Macron's reckoning, the evaluation of ten years of presidency", Pas says. "That it is so intense is also because the elections are approaching. Political parties are jumping on this and sharpening their strategies." The parties on the flanks are taking the clearest positions and are fighting each other, says French political scientist and pollster Jérôme Fourquet as well. "They are trying to eliminate all the other political forces that are located in the centre." Fragmentation Amid all this political violence, Macron appears powerless, analyses political journalist Solenn de Royer of Le Monde. According to her, Macron does not understand what is going on in the minds of the rioters. Nor did he, in his televised address after the riots, come up with concrete proposals to calm the unrest. Macron also has little room for manoeuvre: without a majority in the Assemblée Nationale (the French <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">Tweede Kamer</entity>), his hands are largely tied. Since the early parliamentary elections in June 2024, which he himself called, parliament has splintered into three large, irreconcilable blocs. Meanwhile, France is preparing for new protests next Saturday, or act II as the yellow vests call it. Because the police cannot handle it alone, the government also wants to call on the help of the army. On 31 October, act III follows, as the yellow vests have already announced.

title: Safe going out and getting home during ADE: extra measures again this edition
lead: Bike buddies, special hosts at the exit and a place to charge your phone before you leave. These are some examples of the extra safety measures during the <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity> Dance Event (ADE). Yesterday the largest event for electronic music in the world began. Several organisers, such as DGTL and Awakenings, deploy bike buddies at night. That way no one has to cycle alone. "These are two people who continuously cycle back and forth between the event location at NDSM and the ferry," writes the municipality of Amsterdam. "A couple was deliberately chosen so that they too travel together and are not alone on the street during the night." Empty battery At the NDSM site, a physical help post has also been set up for visitors who feel vulnerable or unsafe at night. The Safe Check-In is open daily during ADE from 19.00 to 07.00 hours. Staff are ready to offer help or a listening ear. Visitors who, for example, missed their night bus or have an empty phone can also go there. At Awakenings there is a so-called goodbye host. This host stands at the exit and mainly watches out for people leaving alone. The host can also help with the route, and you can charge your phone with the host. "Handy if you still need to order an Uber or need your phone to share your location with someone." Hajar ADE also took extra measures last year. Then the murder of Lisa, in August near Amsterdam, caused horror and unrest. Now that is the case with the death of Hajar. The body of the 29-year-old woman was found last week in a suitcase in the Amstel in Amsterdam. The municipality of Amsterdam reports that measures have been taken together with ADE. Organisers also receive presentations on safety. And with a special campaign, bystanders learn how to intervene in an unsafe situation. Lisa Shortly before the start of ADE last year, Lisa was murdered in Duivendrecht. The 17-year-old girl was killed with great violence, which caused a wave of horror. The action 'Wij eisen de nacht op' was also launched at that time.

title: Driver under the influence in Amsterdam was transporting pythons in centre console
lead: The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> in Amsterdam made a striking discovery by chance. A 51-year-old driver was found to be transporting two pythons in a storage compartment. He was under the influence. The Amsterdammer was stopped on the A4. When it became clear he was not sober, he was arrested. Goldfish in a bag The police transport team was called to move the car. When officers searched it, they found two live pythons in the centre console. On the back seat was a box of live mice and a goldfish in a bag of water. The animals have been taken to a rescue centre. Ventilation Keeping pythons is not prohibited in the Netherlands. Transporting your own python within a certain number of kilometres does not require a permit. You must, however, comply with welfare requirements. For example, there must be sufficient ventilation, which was definitely not the case here. The police come across exotic animals in the city more often, city broadcaster AT5 writes. Earlier this year, officers also found a dead, mutilated python in a rubbish container.

title: Scorching hot summer leads to record number of heat deaths in European cities
lead: In European cities, many tens of thousands of people died last summer as a result of the extreme heat. Scientists from Imperial College London and the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine arrived at this estimate. New in their study is that they also point to the role of climate change through greenhouse gas emissions: they link a large part of the heat deaths directly to it. The scientists examined data on more than 850 urban areas in 30 European countries, where together about 40 percent of the population lives. Using models, they estimate that there were about 50,000 extra deaths in those regions last summer. For comparison, for the hot summers of 2022 and 2003 they arrived at 29,000 and 28,000 extra deaths respectively. This year thus well exceeds those record years. "The past summer consisted of extreme heatwaves across the whole continent. Since May there have been severe heatwaves every month", looks back climate scientist Clair Barnes of Imperial College. Especially in Western Europe it became unusually hot: on average the summer was about 2.9 degrees Celsius warmer than the average for the period 1991-2020. The difference with earlier years is large: especially the heatwave at the end of June, when code red was declared in the Netherlands, was very deadly. The British scientists estimate that a third of all deaths fell between 17 June and 1 July. The temperature was then about 5 degrees above the average for the period 1991-2020. The health effect was all the greater because few people were yet accustomed to the heat so early in the season. Most heat deaths are among the elderly. Still, around 6,000 people under the age of 65 also died. "It was certainly not limited to the elderly", explains scientist Garyfallos Konstantinoudis of Imperial College. "In the group between 20 and 44 years old, more than 800 people also died." As a rule, young heat deaths often have chronic conditions. "It is shocking, but it is an important point", says heat expert Carolina Pereira Marghidan of the <entity id="org:koninklijk-nederlands-meteorologisch-instituut">KNMI</entity>, who was not involved in the research. "I think not everyone realizes that it also affects young people, and not only the elderly. For the past 20 years, the picture for many people has been that mainly vulnerable elderly are affected. We simply see that this is not the case." In Italy, Spain and France most people died, but Germany and the United Kingdom were also hit hard: Although it is an estimate, the researchers' figures lie remarkably close to the official mortality figures. This was clearly visible because European governments regularly reported mortality figures in connection with the exceptional circumstances. From that data it could immediately be deduced that the extra deaths ran into the tens of thousands. Barnes: "The figures were sometimes published in real time, just to show how intense it was." The <entity id="org:rijksinstituut-voor-volksgezondheid-en-milieu">RIVM</entity> in the Netherlands reported, for example, that during the heatwave at the end of June and beginning of July there were well over 900 more deaths than normal. Pereira Marghidan: "In a way that matches well with what this research shows." For the whole summer the British estimate about 1,300 extra deaths in the Netherlands. "It was a different method and a different time span, but those figures match very well." Climate change Of the 50,000 deaths, 32,000 could be attributed to climate change. The scientists establish this by comparing the measured temperatures with the temperatures that would have been expected without greenhouse gas emissions. That knowledge, combined with medical models of heat mortality, gives an idea of the impact of climate change. "It is good that they estimate climate-related mortality this way", Pereira Marghidan thinks. "That way you see the mortality and they show what part of the mortality can be linked to climate change. That connection is well founded. With other weather phenomena that is harder, but precisely with temperature-related mortality you can make that link well." Silent killer The actual mortality is probably even higher than the 50,000 in the research. "Heat-related death tolls are underreported worldwide", explains researcher Malcom Mistry of the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine. "Heat is also called a silent killer." People do not notice how severely their organs suffer from the heat, and heat deaths often also stay under the radar. This summer shows that Europe must arm itself against that silent killer, the scientists warn. "It is becoming increasingly clear that our cities are not well adapted to the rising heat", says researcher Pierre Masselot.

title: Big money at stake: how Abdul El-Sayed is pulling the Democrats in the US to the left
lead: 'Abdul is cool', reads the T-shirts. Abdul El-Sayed (41) is running for a seat in <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity> and draws packed halls. In the American congressional elections of 3 November, many eyes are on his race in Michigan. In this swing state it will become clear whether the new, progressive wind in the Democratic Party also reaches new voters. Rebecca stood in line for hours before a rally in Flint; the last time, she could not get in because of the crowds. "I am a democratic socialist," she says. "And I like politicians who do not accept money from big companies." El-Sayed takes aim at that money machine in American politics. "A system in which big companies and billionaires can buy politicians is a disease," the candidate in jeans shouts to loud cheers. "Donald Trump is the worst symptom of that disease." 'The big money out of politics, money in your pocket and universal healthcare' is his slogan. If the former health chief of Detroit wins on 3 November, he will be one of the most left-wing candidates ever to win a swing state, and the first Muslim senator of the US. That makes him a sought-after punching bag for the right. Republicans consistently use his full Muslim name, Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed, as Trump and other Republicans did with Barack Hussein Obama. "My name and my faith are not the reason you can no longer pay for petrol and groceries," El-Sayed tells his audience. Rise of democratic socialists Last year Zohran Mamdani (35) already surprised everyone by winning the mayoral election in New York. Mamdani is also a Muslim and a member of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), which wants to restrain capitalism and strives for democratic control over the economy. The organisation is on the rise. Also in the Democratic primaries, which determined who would stand for the party in the congressional elections, far-left candidates did surprisingly well. For example, both Democratic candidates for the House of Representatives in Detroit are DSA members. In a small hall in the industrial city, Ian Mark is recruiting new members. He thinks he can reach floating voters who are fed up with the influence of billionaires and Big Tech on politics, while they themselves barely make ends meet. Bartender Victor Jimenez from Detroit joined last winter. "I have finally found my political home," he says, as he sets out extra chairs. President Trump, who also visits Michigan on Sunday, consistently calls the democratic socialists "communists" and "the greatest threat to the country since the world wars, Pearl Harbor and 9/11". According to Trump, they will destroy the American economy. But communists, unlike democratic socialists, want to achieve their goal through revolution. According to Mark, Trump's framing does not work: "People can no longer be swayed by labels." Still, there is resistance within the Democratic Party as well. Moderate Democrats fear that the radical party members will scare off moderate voters. Democrat Dave Armstrong, who is walking in a No Kings protest in Detroit, shares that fear: "They are a bit too extreme." For example, the DSA wants in the long term to give all migrants a residence status, abolish private rental housing and abolish the police. "Democrats have to fight two wars," says protester Kyla Turner. "Against the far right and against the far left. And that is a difficult struggle." Now that the movement has the wind in its sails, the DSA is holding back its most far-reaching ideas. For now the DSA is aiming for goals resembling those of European social democrats, such as free childcare, stronger trade unions and affordable rent. El-Sayed himself is not a democratic socialist; he calls himself a capitalist. Still, he is regarded as highly progressive, and among the Senate candidates as one of the fiercest critics of Israel and Prime Minister Netanyahu. That goes down well with the large Arab community in the suburbs of Detroit, but within the Democratic Party it remains a sensitive issue. Despite all the headwinds, El-Sayed narrowly leads his Republican opponent. Former president Obama is campaigning with him. DSA figurehead Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez also stands side by side with El-Sayed. For a long time she was regarded as a rebel within the Democratic Party; now she is mentioned as a possible presidential candidate in 2028: a sign of how the party is shifting. In the primaries, pro-Israel and other financiers put around 60 million dollars into a campaign to keep him out of the race. El-Sayed could spend far less, but still won: a signal that big money in the US cannot buy everything.

title: 'MIVD saw on hacked iPhone how Trump's son-in-law received many millions'
lead: The Dutch Military Intelligence and Security Service (MIVD) reportedly monitored the phone of Jared Kushner, son-in-law of US President Trump and his negotiator in the wars in Ukraine, Gaza and Iran, from 2018 onward. That is what US investigative journalist Matthew Cole writes in a new book, an excerpt of which the magazine Vanity Fair has published. According to Cole, the MIVD got in with the help of a defected Russian hacker who worked for the Russian military intelligence service GROe. How long the MIVD ultimately monitored Kushner's phone is not known. The MIVD tells the NOS it does not comment on its working methods, knowledge level or sources. Nieuwsuur, in collaboration with the Volkskrant, conducted extensive research into the claim that the MIVD had access to Jared Kushner's phone and spoke with several people directly involved. No confirmation of the story was found. 750 million dollars Cole writes in the book that the Dutch spies saw through the hack that Kushner logged into a bank account in the United Arab Emirates in Dubai. The account reportedly received hundreds of millions of dollars from a bank in Azerbaijan. Cole writes that this bank account held 750 million dollars, coming from the royal families of Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). The money was reportedly intended to advance political and diplomatic goals in the Middle East. According to Cole, the account was partly managed by Kushner and the Emirati president Mohammed bin Zayed Al Nahyan (MBZ). 'Detour' "Jared was looking for a detour to achieve his diplomatic goals", Cole heard from a source who was aware of the deal between the UAE and Kushner. "Jared promised MBZ that he would look after their interests with Trump if they took part in a fund. Jared wanted normalization of relations with Israel so that trade and investment could flourish." According to Cole, the two families at the time wanted to force a breakthrough in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. This could improve their relations with Israel without losing face. Kushner reportedly agreed to raise the Saudis' plans with his father-in-law. More about Kushner's business interests in Israel and other countries in this video from Nieuwsuur: The affair reportedly came to light when the military intelligence service discovered in 2017 that an employee of the Russian military intelligence service GROe, specialized in stolen bank data, was on his way to the United Kingdom for an espionage assignment. According to Cole, the British detained the man at the request of their Dutch colleagues. The hacker reportedly was given two options: work as an informant for the Dutch government, or face a trial in the United Kingdom with a possible prison sentence of several years. The Russian employee decided to give the Dutch intelligence service access to one of the GROe's most sensitive systems, Cole writes. On a server in the Russian city of Rostov, used by the cyber and hacking team of the Russian military intelligence service, the Dutch found screenshots of Kushner's iPhone during their investigation. According to Cole, the MIVD then managed in early 2018 to gain access to the phone itself, allowing the service to watch the screen whenever Kushner used the device. While the services were monitoring Kushner's phone, they discovered that he used it to log into a bank account in the UAE. By the time the Dutch spies gained sight of the phone, hundreds of millions of dollars had already been deposited into the account. "For the MIVD hackers, the bank account became an intelligence puzzle that had to be solved", Cole writes. 'Crazy' Whether Kushner, as a White House employee, reported the account to US authorities is not known. If he did not, Kushner may have violated US anti-bribery legislation. Kushner denies all allegations on X and calls them "completely crazy". "No bank statements, transfer details, account numbers, transaction data or other details were provided to prove these extraordinary allegations." During Trump's first term, Kushner played an important role in US foreign policy in the Middle East. He was part of the diplomatic team that ultimately led to the 2020 Abraham Accords. These normalized relations between, among others, the United Arab Emirates and Israel. He also plays an important role now as a negotiator for Trump. What do you think of the NOS app and website? title: Albert Heijn customers can have groceries delivered again
lead: Albert Heijn customers can once again have groceries delivered to their homes from today, almost two weeks after the cyberattack that brought the supermarket chain's services to a standstill. In recent days, a limited group of regular customers has been able to place orders, and now everyone can do so. The number of orders that can be delivered has not yet returned to its previous level. The supermarket chain can now handle a third of its normal number of deliveries. On Wednesday the supermarket began restarting its systems, which also made its customer service available again. Last Sunday the website and app were working again too. Daily groceries According to Albert Heijn, the first orders are going out and the outlook for the rest of the day is good. "The first deliveries have been taking place since 7.00 this morning", a spokesperson told ANP. Customers are now ordering daily groceries again. "Milk, yoghurt, plant-based dairy, bread, vegetables, fruit and kitchen roll are popular", the spokesperson said. The range and the number of available delivery slots will be expanded further over the course of the week. Customers whose order was cancelled after an error message will receive a store credit from the supermarket chain. No data stolen Customers were unable to place grocery orders after the cyber incident at Albert Heijn's parent company, Ahold Delhaize. Because of the incident, Ahold took certain systems offline as a precaution. As a result, the website and app of Albert Heijn, as well as those of other Ahold brands such as Etos and Gall & Gall, have been unavailable since Sunday 11 October. The company has since filed a report with the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> about the cyberattack, after the police and the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> called on the company to do so through a public appeal. The internal investigation into the cyberattack is still ongoing. The company says that so far it has no indication that any sensitive customer, employee or partner data has been stolen. title: Man shoots at random in Paris suburb, one dead and four injured
lead: A man has shot at random passers-by near Paris. At least one person died and at least four others were injured. The shooting took place in Trappes, a suburb southwest of Paris, near Versailles. According to Le Parisien, the perpetrator used a machine gun. He fired the weapon from a vehicle, first in Trappes and then in the neighbouring La Verriere, the news broadcaster BFMTV reports. The first images of where the shooting took place: According to the mayor of Trappes, the man seemed to be "shooting randomly around him, with the apparent intention of causing a bloodbath". He calls it a miracle that more people were not hit. Motive not known Among the injured is a 12-year-old girl, according to the mayor of La Verriere. Her condition is reportedly stable. Two men aged 29 and 49 were also injured and taken to hospital. The victim who died was 26 years old. The 38-year-old gunman was later arrested nearby in the village of Coignieres. According to French Prime Minister Lecornu, the shooting is being investigated as an act of terrorism, and he says the National Anti-Terrorist Prosecutor's Office (PNAT) is monitoring the situation. No motive has been made public yet. French Prime Minister Lecornu writes on X that "all resources of the security services have been fully mobilised". 'Our thoughts are with the victims' President Macron writes on X that his thoughts are with the victims, their families and all residents of the area. Minister of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> Nuñez speaks of "a very serious incident". He will arrive on the scene "within a few moments". What do you think of the NOS app and website? What do we do well? What could be better? We are curious about your opinion. Fill in the survey via this link.

title: Thousands of households in France and England without power due to storm Austen
lead: In France and England, storm Austen, which also reaches the Netherlands this afternoon, has caused problems. The storm made landfall in Brittany this morning, where local weather stations measured gusts of up to 160 kilometres per hour. Because of the bad weather, ferry services between the two countries have also been cancelled, such as those between Dover and Calais. More than 161,000 households in French coastal regions such as Brittany, Pays de la Loire and Normandy have lost power. Code orange applies until 20.00 this evening for 23 departments in north-western France. That is the second-highest alert level. Hundreds of firefighters have been deployed to respond to reports, such as fallen trees. Yesterday storm Adam moved across southern France over land. Two people died in the process. They were two women aged 86 and 26 who were found drowned in a cellar in the southern French region of Bouches-du-Rhône. The storm had earlier already claimed four lives in Spain. Images of the storm in south-east England and Normandy: The British weather service, the Met Office, has issued code orange for Cornwall and Devon at England's south-western tip. Storm Austen was accompanied there in the early morning by gusts of up to 130 kilometres per hour. In Cornwall more than 13,500 addresses are without power, including, according to the BBC, 4,600 vulnerable people. During the day, gusts of around 100 kilometres per hour are expected in the south and middle of England. The storm will move eastward along the English Channel coast. Second storm: Weather services on the island of Jersey have issued a warning for shipping around the Channel Islands. In that area gusts of up to 130 kilometres per hour are expected. The authorities there had already received 91 reports of fallen or damaged trees this morning. Because many trees are still fully in leaf, the Met Office warns of more power outages and traffic disruption due to fallen trees and blown-down branches. Along with strong wind, a lot of rain is also expected in many places in England. Later this weekend a second severe storm is expected in the UK, which will bring strong wind and heavy rain mainly in the north of the country. Both countries have taken measures to limit nuisance and problems. In France, train services in parts of Normandy have been halted and speed restrictions apply on other routes. Authorities urged people to postpone non-essential travel due to the risk of falling trees and flying debris. Belgium is also dealing with storm Austen. The Royal Meteorological Institute of Belgium has issued code orange for the west of the country, while yellow is in force in the rest of the country. Code yellow: Storm Austen is moving this afternoon from the south-west across the Netherlands with a lot of rain and wind. The <entity id="org:koninklijk-nederlands-meteorologisch-instituut">KNMI</entity> warns from the end of the afternoon of severe gusts in coastal areas and in the south-east, with gusts between 75 and 90 km per hour. From this afternoon code yellow applies to Zuid-Holland, Zeeland, Noord-Brabant, Limburg, Gelderland and Overijssel. From tomorrow afternoon the KNMI again expects severe gusts in coastal areas and South Limburg. During the course of the night the wind will ease again.

title: 31 suspects acquitted in Belgian drug trial because the proceedings took too long
lead: In Belgium, 31 suspects who stood trial in a large-scale drug case are going free because the procedure took far too long. One of them is Dutch drug criminal John H. In recent years he has been convicted several times for drug crime. The facts date back ten years. According to the judge, there were several periods in which the case file was not worked on for no explainable reason. In total this amounted to more than five years. The court also says the file is not exceptionally complex, and that the suspects did not take any actions that could have delayed the trial. Dropping a conviction is a very exceptional decision. When a trial takes longer, a court is more inclined to reduce the sentence. Over 160 years in prison sentences The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> had requested prison sentences for the 31 suspects totaling more than 160 years. H. faced a prison sentence of eighteen years. This already took into account a sentence reduction because the trial took too long. The OM also wanted to seize 14 million euros. The OM sees H. as one of the leaders of this criminal organization. The organization traded chemicals used to make synthetic drugs. Large quantities of ingredients were ordered through a soap factory in Lommel. The federal prosecutor's office is appealing.

title: Councillor does not have to retract statements about amusement park owner Wim Beelen after all
lead: Rotterdam councillor Kevin van Eikeren does not have to retract his statements about entrepreneur Wim Beelen after all. That is what the court of appeal in <entity id="org:gemeente-s-gravenhage">Den Haag</entity> has ruled in an expedited procedure. The Pro councillor had appealed against the district court's ruling earlier this week. On Tuesday the district court had still ruled that Van Eikeren had to retract several statements about multimillionaire Beelen, including those known from the Rotterdam amusement park Spelen bij Beelen. Van Eikeren had said, among other things on radio with the regional broadcaster Rijnmond, that the entrepreneur with his amusement park "plays the Samaritan" while it is "purely about the money" for him. In addition, Van Eikeren said that Beelen had tried to buy political parties in <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity> by making high donations. The judge assessed the councillor's statements as unlawful and without factual basis. He had to post a message on Instagram and LinkedIn within 72 hours acknowledging that his statements were unlawful. Because Beelen was found to be right, Van Eikeren had to pay the costs of the proceedings. These amount to over 1850 euros. Ruling overturned: But that ruling has now been crossed out. In the appeal, the court of appeal has ruled in a so-called turbo expedited appeal that Van Eikeren does not have to retract his statements. The costs of the proceedings are also awarded to Wim Beelen. Nothing has yet been made public about the court's reasoning. The substantive justification will be published later. During the summary proceedings earlier this month the judge still expressed the hope that the men could sort it out between themselves, but that did not succeed. Therefore the judge issued a ruling. Attempts at reconciliation also continued during the expedited hearing on appeal, according to Rijnmond.

title: Hajar killed on first day of disappearance, suspect also suspected of attempting to kill foster father
lead: The 29-year-old Hajar was killed on the first day of her disappearance. That is what the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> reports. Hajar was last seen on Sunday 4 October near the RAI event complex in <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity>. From there she cycled with the 23-year-old suspect Abdi A. in the direction of the Buitenveldert neighbourhood. According to the OM, there were no indications that the two knew each other. That Sunday morning she sent disturbing messages to an acquaintance. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> cannot say what exactly Hajar sent. De Telegraaf said it had seen WhatsApp messages in which she sent "Help me. Now. He is killing me". The OM reports that research has shown Hajar was killed that same day, early in the afternoon. In the evening the family informed the police about the messages. Hajar's body was found last Friday evening in a suitcase in the water at Amsteldijk in Amsterdam-Zuid. The exact circumstances are still unclear, but the police are certain it was a crime. Vulnerable person: It is now clear that Hajar was a vulnerable person who often left home and was untraceable for long periods. On the weekend she was killed, she left with a suitcase. She did that more often, reports Het Parool. Hajar was also reportedly found at night last May in the porch of a house in the Amsterdam neighbourhood De Pijp.
