In district 1 of North Carolina, where the Republicans at the beginning of this year still expected an easy victory, they have since September bought 20 million dollars' worth of ads in the hope of winning the seat after all. In the 15 districts they redrew themselves, they have hastily spent 150 million dollars in advertising money to rescue their faltering strategy. It is not the case that the Democrats are assured of winning the House of Representatives. Even if the gerrymandering pushed through by Trump fails, it is still possible that the Republicans will pull a stunt in other districts. And in <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity> the race is anything but a foregone conclusion . Polls simply do not tell everything. Erosion of norms Gerrymandering is not new, and certainly not exclusively a method of one of the parties. Already in the 19th century Republicans and Democrats used it. Still, a few things have changed in recent years. One of them is the timing. Normally it always happened right after a census. In the US there is a census every ten years, and the results become available soon after the start of the new decade. This matters for Congress, because the number of residents of a state determines the number of seats in the House of Representatives. What Trump has now done is demand a redrawing of electoral districts at a very different moment, in the middle of a decade. That gives more the impression of manipulation and of a clear attempt to retain power. That impression is reinforced by the fact that in April this year the Supreme Court weakened an important civil rights law , so that voters can no longer legally challenge gerrymandering if they believe they are disadvantaged on the basis of skin colour.

title: Anthropic's stock market papers full of major warnings, but investors are not deterred
lead: The documents Anthropic has submitted to enable a stock market listing are full of warnings. Misuse of AI models can lead to "chemical, biological or other dangerous weapons", the American AI company writes. It also points to its billions in debt and losses. Even so, investment experts expect a lot from the announced stock market listing. The warnings are all in the so-called prospectus, a document of hundreds of pages that for the first time gives a clear picture of the company's financial situation. Traditionally, companies going public also name all conceivable possible risks in it, so that investors, large and small, can make an informed choice. Anthropic is therefore issuing a particularly large number of far-reaching warnings, but despite these self-identified risks, investment experts expect a lot from Anthropic, with its AI model Claude . "This will be a spectacular stock market listing in any case", says Mary Pieterse-Bloem, head of investment strategy at Rabobank. Taking work off hands "With Claude the company has something very special in hand", says Pieterse-Bloem, who also teaches at Erasmus University Rotterdam. "Especially for programming and coding it works well. At the university, but also at the bank, you see that it is used a lot." Competing models such as ChatGPT (from OpenAI) and Co-Pilot (from Microsoft) are less advanced in this, which makes the AI model interesting for companies and organisations, also says Jos Versteeg, investment strategist at InsingerGilissen. "For a consumer an AI model is now handy and perhaps cost-saving, but for organisations this model can really take work off their hands and save costs." Billions in losses The billion-dollar loss does not immediately deter. In 2025 Anthropic still earned 4.6 billion dollars. This year alone, 16.3 billion dollars in revenue was achieved in the first half of the year. But on the other hand, the company suffered a loss of 42 billion dollars last year. "That doesn't say much", says Versteeg, "You can look at billions in losses, but also at gigantic growth." For Pieterse-Bloem it is telling that the company is going public with the prospectus now, despite the tense interim elections in the United States next week and the ongoing violence in the Middle East. Anthropic says it wants to go public before the Thanksgiving holiday, so before 26 November. "You only do that if you have confidence in the success of that stock market listing", says the Rabobank investment strategist. "The business model is apparently embraced by investors. And the company thinks that the stock market climate will remain favourable for the time being." Limited number of customers "There is a significant risk in rapid growth", Anthropic writes in the prospectus. The company points to the limited number of customers who currently pay serious money for its services. Five large customers account for a quarter of revenue. In addition, 250 customers pay more than 10 million dollars a year for Claude. The rest of the customers pay nothing or less. Versteeg of InsingerGilissen also sees this as a risk. "Compare it with Alphabet, the parent company of Google. Such a company has enormous reach. That company also has its own AI model, but in addition data centres and its own chips. Anthropic still plays only a limited role in the entire AI chain." Even so, Versteeg thinks that Anthropic will be carried along by major players such as Alphabet, Amazon and Microsoft. In turn, those companies also invest billions in Anthropic. After the stock market listing, the AI company hopes to be worth around 1,500 billion dollars. "We still need to see about that", says analyst Versteeg. 'Belief is great' "It is very reminiscent of the SpaceX stock market listing", says Pieterse Bloem. "It concerns promising technology that does not yet make a profit." Elon Musk's company went public earlier this year with great interest. The share price peaked quickly at the time, but then also fell again. Versteeg expects high demand for Anthropic's shares. "The belief is great. Moreover, a lot of people believe they cannot afford not to believe in it." That Anthropic describes its own model as mortally dangerous to humanity does not deter Versteeg. That may also be a tactic to stay in the news, we wrote earlier. According to Pieterse-Bloem, it is a good sign that the American company at least shows awareness of the dangers. "And if Anthropic doesn't do it, another company will. Better the devil you know than the devil you don't know."

title: Busiest evening rush hour of the year: over 1,100 kilometres of traffic jams
lead: Today's evening rush hour is the busiest of the year so far. Around 17:30 there were 1,109 kilometres of traffic jams on Dutch roads, the ANWB reports. The previous record dated from Wednesday 13 May, when there were 1,046 kilometres of traffic jams. That congestion was related to Ascension Day and holiday traffic. According to an ANWB spokesperson, rain is mainly playing a role. The weather is bad in many places, and because it gets dark earlier, motorists drive more carefully and slowly. As a result, traffic jams form more quickly. There were no major accidents, but the usual traffic jams are longer than normal. Traffic jams gradually decreasing The biggest delays are on the A2 from Eindhoven to Utrecht, the A4 from Amsterdam to Rotterdam and the A1 between Amsterdam and Apeldoorn. An accident did occur on the A28 from Zwolle to Groningen. The delay there rose to 50 minutes. According to the ANWB, the peak has now been reached. The traffic jams are expected to gradually decrease. Around 19:00 most traffic jams should be cleared again.

title: Restructuring at shipbuilder Damen, 225 jobs cut in the Netherlands
lead: Shipbuilder Damen is going to cut around 225 of its 4000 jobs in the Netherlands. The company wants to make its organisation "simpler and more efficient" with this. The jobs will disappear over the next twelve to eighteen months at the various Damen companies in the Netherlands. This happens both in offices and at the shipyards. It concerns positions at all levels and in all fields, a spokesperson says. The company from Gorinchem, with shipyards all over the world, expects that "a large part" of the restructuring can be absorbed through natural attrition, but does not rule out forced dismissals. 'It hits hard' According to union CNV, the news hits employees hard. "Everyone here is working incredibly hard to keep Damen on course despite changing circumstances. So it hits hard to hear that you may become a victim of an efficiency drive yourself", the union tells news agency ANP. At the end of June, the shipbuilder lost an important order. The German minister of Defence cancelled the order for six frigates, which Damen says was completely unexpected. A spokesperson for the shipbuilder says the restructuring in the Netherlands has nothing to do with this setback. Damen says it has invited the unions to talk about a social plan for the employees who lose their jobs.

title: Flávio Bolsonaro leaves Brazil and is on his way to the US with his family after election defeat
lead: Brazilian senator and former presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro has left the country. He has departed for the United States with his wife and two daughters, two days after his defeat in the Brazilian presidential election, his allies confirm to CNN Brasil. An ally of the senator also confirms the news to news agency Reuters. A US official says that Bolsonaro junior is on his way to the US by plane. On Sunday the radical right-wing Bolsonaro junior lost the presidential election in Brazil. In the second round the victory went to the left-wing incumbent president Lula, who received almost 52 percent of the votes. Bolsonaro refuses to accept his defeat and wants the result declared invalid. 27 years in prison The Brazilian Supreme Court ordered Bolsonaro junior to hand in his passports one day after his loss, in connection with an investigation into money laundering practices. He spoke of a 'outrage' meant to intimidate him, and said he never considered leaving the country. A judge has also instructed the Brazilian police to investigate possible illegal foreign financing of the presidential campaign of Senator Bolsonaro. This includes looking at financing by a group that reportedly has ties to US Vice President JD Vance. His father, Jair Bolsonaro, also fled to the US four years ago after losing the election to Lula. When he returned to Brazil last year, he was sentenced to 27 years in prison for leading a coup attempt after losing the presidential election in 2022. How did Bolsonaro manage to escape? How Bolsonaro junior entered the United States is still unclear. Argentina says it has no indications that he travelled through that country. Argentine media earlier reported that a private jet was to fly early this morning from northern Argentina to the American city of Miami with four passengers on board. This flight was reportedly cancelled a few hours before departure. Why is unclear. The reports about the private flight led to speculation that Bolsonaro tried to travel to the United States via neighbouring Argentina. Miami is familiar territory for the Bolsonaro family. Eduardo Bolsonaro, the third son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, moved to the US last year and now lives in Miami. Following media reports about a private aircraft at the international airport of Iguazú, on the border between Argentina and Brazil, the Argentine authorities checked the plane and crew. According to Argentina, no flight plan linked to the Bolsonaro family was found. Election defeat Father Jair Bolsonaro is still under house arrest. He was president of Brazil from 2019 to 2022. After his election defeat, thousands of supporters of the radical right-wing politician stormed the Brazilian parliament, the presidential palace and the Supreme Court in the capital Brasília on 8 January 2023. That storming was seen as an attack on the country's democratic institutions.

title: Prosecutors demand heavy sentences against staff of illegal medicine website
lead: The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> demands 10 and 6,5 years against two suspects behind Slaappillen.net. The webshop sold, among other things, a counterfeit version of the strong painkiller oxycodone, which in reality contained the highly dangerous substance nitazenes. At least three people appear to have died from it. In total, nitazenes have now been found in the blood in thirteen deaths in the Netherlands. PostNL employee handled the shipping. The two residents of Breda who appeared in The Hague today were not the main persons responsible for Slaappillen.net. One is said to have packed the orders and managed the huge stock of, among other things, 400.000 pills, 6000 XTC tablets and large quantities of amphetamines. The oxycodone alone present in the house of his mother, where he lived and worked, had a value of 135.000 euros according to the OM. The other, a PostNL employee, is said to have ensured that the packages entered that company's shipping system. In addition, the OM suspects him of importing and trading large quantities of cocaine. That is why the demand against him is the highest. 'Multi-million business' Both say they had no idea they were contributing to the supply of contaminated pills to customers. The lawyer of one of them described his client as no more than "a glorified assembly-line worker", who acted solely on the orders of others. Both are not directly held responsible by justice for the deaths of the women, but according to the lawyer the OM, with the "exorbitantly high" demands, acts as if that is the case. The public prosecutor countered that both men were precisely "crucial links" in the "professionally run multi-million business" that Slaappillen.net was. The webshop made the threshold for customers as low as possible, among other things by offering payment with iDeal. Also shipments to other countries "Those customers were drawn into a trade," said the prosecutor, "in which only one thing mattered: making money. Vulnerable people were regarded as a goose that lays the golden eggs." They thought they were ordering painkillers, but got a deadly agent into their home that had ten to a hundred times the effect of oxycodone and in dozens of cases poisoned them or even cost them their lives. At the hearing this afternoon it emerged that the packages were not only sent to Dutch addresses, but also to at least Spain, Denmark and Belgium. Of the total of 5000 orders at Slaappillen.net that the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> was able to bring to light via the laptop of one of the suspects, 550 cases involved oxycodone. Main players now arrested. Further investigation will need to show in the coming time whether more deaths from nitazenes can be linked to Slaappillen.net. Last week the police arrested three men suspected of being the main persons responsible for this website, plus dozens of other websites on which illegal medicines and drugs were sold. The Hague District Court will rule on 17 November.

title: Ebola spreads further in Congo: more than 10,000 people infected
lead: In the Democratic Republic of Congo, more than 10,000 cases of Ebola have now been confirmed, according to official figures from Congolese health authorities. Nearly 4,900 people have died of the infectious disease. The African public health organisation Africa CDC describes it as the fastest growing Ebola outbreak ever. The number of infections stood at 9,964 last Friday. About 48 percent of people infected with the highly contagious Bundibugyo variant of the virus die from it. The actual number of infected people is probably even higher, because not everyone with symptoms seeks medical help immediately or gets tested. Life-threatening Until now, the most severe Ebola outbreak was the one from 2014 to 2016 in West Africa. That claimed more than 11,000 lives, mainly in Sierra Leone, Liberia and Guinea. The current outbreak in Congo is growing much faster. Ebola is a life-threatening disease. The virus is transmitted through physical contact and contact with body fluids, such as vomit, blood or semen. The disease causes a highly contagious form of fever, often accompanied by diarrhoea and bleeding. In Congo, the Bundibugyo variant has been spreading since May. The outbreak is causing great unrest and distrust. For example, armed youths attacked health workers with machetes at the end of last week in eastern Congo. They accused the aid workers of spreading the disease by contaminating water. Ebola has now also spread to other African countries, such as Kenya. There, nine infections and two deaths have been confirmed so far. The infections were discovered after a patient travelled from Congo via Uganda to the capital Nairobi. Ebola has also appeared in West African Nigeria. The patient in Nigeria, the wife of a Swiss diplomat, fell ill after a trip to Uganda. According to health authorities, it is still being investigated exactly where she became infected with the Ebola virus. The woman has been transferred to Switzerland for treatment. Maternal deaths The current outbreak is difficult to bring under control, because there is no specific vaccine or effective treatment yet available for the Bundibugyo variant of the Ebola virus. Research into new vaccines and treatment methods is ongoing, however. In addition, the first symptoms of an infection can easily be mistaken for other diseases, such as malaria. As a result, patients are sometimes isolated or treated too late, allowing the virus to keep spreading. Many pregnant women in Congo also avoid hospitals out of fear of infection. As a result, maternal mortality doubled in some provinces shortly after the outbreak was declared in May. The regular healthcare system in Congo has also been disrupted by the outbreak. For example, vaccination programmes for children have been disrupted and schooling has been interrupted for many children. This is especially problematic in areas where millions of children already do not go to school. In addition, the outbreak has led to stigmatisation of affected families, leaving them socially isolated. Two vaccines Since July, clinical trials have been running into two possible treatment methods for the Bundibugyo variant. Various vaccines are also being tested. Research is also looking into whether the Ebola vaccine Ervebo offers protection against this variant. So far, Ervebo is only approved for use against the Ebola disease caused by the Zaire ebolavirus. According to a WHO representative in Congo, additional studies could start within a few weeks for two vaccines developed specifically for the Bundibugyo variant. There are also rays of hope. More than 2,600 patients have now recovered from the disease. This week a video went viral showing healthcare workers in protective clothing dancing after the last two patients left a treatment centre in Mongbwalu. According to WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, this shows that every patient who survives Ebola is a reason for optimism.

title: Two Britons charged over 'plot' at RAF air base
lead: Two Britons have been charged at a court in London in connection with the events of 27 September at the RAF air base in Fairford. The 24-year-old Mohmed A. has been charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service, presumably from Iran. The equally 24-year-old Nouman E. is accused of entering a prohibited area "for a purpose harmful to the United Kingdom". On 27 September, five Britons were arrested at night at or near the base. Shortly before, they had left three minibuses with barrels of petrol at the edge of the site. The five were initially suspected of preparing a terrorist offence. Prime Minister Burnham said two weeks later that the five were "almost certainly" directed by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard in Iran. That suspicion still stands. Ali Mohmed A. was not part of the group of five. He was only arrested last week. According to the British prosecution service, he was the link between the five and someone called "Ali", who gave the orders. This Ali is said to be staying abroad. After the five had left the minibuses and petrol at the base, they were, according to the prosecution service, called by Ali. He reportedly said there was "a bomb in the cars". One of the five then called the police, the prosecutor said today. This mobilised a large police force, after which the five could quickly be arrested. In addition, the police had been alerted by a farmer's wife living nearby. She and her husband were returning from a party and suddenly saw men in balaclavas scattering in all directions in the glare of their headlights. They did not trust it and called the police. Reconnaissance The 24-year-old Nouman E. was charged today with entering the air base, but not on 27 September; rather on 22 August. He was reportedly conducting reconnaissance there at the time and made video recordings. Mohmed A. has been released on bail. Nouman E. had previously been released on bail, but was arrested again last week. He will remain in custody until the next hearing on 20 November, where Mohmed A. must also appear again. Six other suspects may await the case at liberty, after paying a bail sum. No bomb What the purpose of the minibuses and barrels of petrol was remains unclear. They may have been intended for an attack on the American bombers that carried out bombings on Iran from this base. But the bomb Ali was said to have talked about has never been found. The bombers were removed from there on 5 October, according to American media because new threats from Iran reportedly came in.

title: Mysterious crypto boss and clever AI developer: who are the newcomers to the Quote 500?
lead: The usually fairly predictable Quote 500 list has been shaken up this year by all sorts of tech entrepreneurs, it became known this morning. Striking newcomers are crypto boss Jean-Louis van der Velde and AI developer Pim de Witte. Who are they? Jean-Louis van der Velde It is a striking change. Almost no one knows the new number one, who debuts on the rich list today. The mysterious crypto billionaire Jean-Louis van der Velde dislodges Charlene de Carvalho-Heineken from her seat. The heiress to the beer brand was at the top for a long time. The nationality of the 62-year-old, who now lives in Hong Kong, remained unknown for a long time. But now Quote has finally confirmed that he still holds a Dutch passport. This means he enters the list at the top position in one go. Van der Velde's fortune, born in Arnhem as Ludovicus Jan, is estimated at 26 billion euros. That is twice as much as what De Carvalho-Heineken owns. She is now in second place. Withdrawn life Van der Velde earned his money with cryptocurrencies. He is director of the crypto trading platform Bitfinex and in 2014 founded Tether, the world's first and largest stablecoin. A coin pegged to the US dollar, which hardly changes in value. Van der Velde leads a withdrawn life and almost never appears in public. On X (formerly Twitter) it was even speculated that he no longer existed, until a video of him appeared online in 2022. Many journalists have tried to reach him, but without success. Journalist Zeke Faux is one of the few who have actually spoken to him. In his book he recounts that Van der Velde introduced himself as 'the man who does not exist'. They met in 2022, almost by chance, at a crypto conference in the Bahamas. Faux describes his appearance as that of a captain of a perfectly polished charter yacht. For three hours they sat in a cafe by a casino, where Van der Velde twice repeated that money does not interest him and he would rather not think about money. Remarkable, writes Faux, because his crypto company Tether issues a new form of money. Pim de Witte The youngest billionaire ever is Pim de Witte (31). Last year he founded the AI company General Intuition, which is already worth several billion. With this he is 'exemplary' for the list, according to Jeroen Molenaar, deputy editor-in-chief of Quote, because entrepreneurs in the AI sector can grow unprecedentedly fast. He grew up in Nijmegen and now lives in New York City. Before his AI company, De Witte founded Medal.tv, a platform where gamers share footage of their games. That footage and the underlying data prove to be a goldmine for companies working on the next generation of AI applications. The data namely offers a glimpse into how people behave in a simulated world. Not many AI companies have access to this kind of data, which makes Medal.tv's data unique. 'More fun to do it yourself' OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, was interested in the data behind this platform and offered De Witte 500 million euros for it. But he told Nieuwsuur at the time that he is going to develop it further himself with AI technology. "It's just more fun to do it myself." He taught himself programming and by the age of fourteen had already built the largest private server on RuneScape, an online game. After secondary school he did not go on to study, but immediately started working for Doctors Without Borders in London. There he built MapSwipe, a platform that helps fight Ebola in Africa. With it, aid workers can plan routes in crisis situations using satellite images. Despite his many achievements, he told Quote that he is most proud of building MapSwipe.

title: No clear winner in Israel, Arab parties larger than ever
lead: The parliamentary elections in Israel do not appear to have produced a clear winner. According to the first exit polls, the Likud party of Prime Minister Netanyahu wins 24 seats and thus remains the largest party. That would be a loss of 8 seats. The anti-Netanyahu bloc of former military chief Gadi Eisenkot would have grown larger than the pro-Netanyahu bloc: 52 to 50 seats, according to the exit polls. Neither is enough for a majority in parliament. Netanyahu relied on a coalition of five parties that together held 64 seats in parliament. On X, Eisenkot is already drawing the far-reaching conclusion that this first assessment of the result indicates "a total lack of confidence in Netanyahu and his <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity>". Arab parties The two blocs with Arab parties have together won 18 seats according to the exit polls, a record. As a result, they could play an important role in forming a government without Prime Minister Netanyahu, although Jewish opposition leaders would then have to be willing to work with them. Such cooperation has been especially sensitive since the terrorist attack by Hamas on 7 October 2023. Voting was possible until 21.00 Dutch time this evening. The exit polls are a first assessment of the result. The first official results come in overnight, so a clearer picture will probably emerge tomorrow. The official result follows later. One party never wins a majority The Knesset has 120 seats. A majority government therefore requires 61 seats. It has never happened that one party has won an absolute majority. This means parties must always form a coalition to govern or secure support from outside the government. In recent years, forming a coalition has often failed, which has forced new elections. Referendum on Netanyahu These are the first parliamentary elections since the terrorist attack by Hamas in 2023. As a result, security is the most important issue for many Israelis. Although Israelis do not vote for individuals in the election but for parties, the election is also seen as a referendum on Netanyahu. He is the longest-serving prime minister the country has ever had. Turnout today was very high: by 22.00, the time when polling stations closed, more than 77 percent of eligible voters had voted, the Central Elections Committee reports. That is the highest turnout in decades. Local media report that 70,000 eligible voters traveled to Israel from abroad to cast their vote. Voting from abroad is not possible in Israel.

title: Serial killer Ted Bundy also linked to murder of Melissa Ann (17)
lead: Police in the US state of Utah have once again linked a cold case to the notorious serial killer Ted Bundy (1946-1989). The 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith was last seen on 18 July 1974, after visiting a pizzeria with friends. She walked home on foot but never arrived there. A hunter found her body almost a week later in a nature reserve. She had been raped and had died from blows to the head and possibly also strangulation. Police suspected she had already been murdered a few days before her disappearance. The case was never solved. Her death bore the hallmarks of the way Bundy operated, says the prosecutor who led the investigation: "the pattern, the motive, the method and the opportunity". But conclusive evidence was lacking. That evidence now exists, thanks to another cold case attributed to Bundy. In April of this year, police in Utah obtained evidence that he was responsible for the murder of the equally 17-year-old Laura Ann Aime, also in 1974. She disappeared after a party, and her body was found a month later next to a motorway. This year, using new DNA techniques, it could be shown that nearly decayed DNA material on her body came from Bundy. The same DNA profile has now been found on evidence that was preserved in the Melissa Ann Smith case. Electric chair Bundy sexually abused and killed at least thirty women and girls across several states in the 1970s. He was ultimately sentenced to death in Florida for three cases. Before that happened, he made confessions in several cases, including cases the police did not yet know about. He died on 24 January 1989 in the electric chair at the Florida State Prison in Bradford County.

title: Rare nanotyrannus skeleton sold for 42 million euros
lead: A rare skeleton of a nanotyrannus, the smaller cousin of a tyrannosaurus rex, was sold at an auction in New York for just over 42 million euros. That makes it one of the world's most expensive fossils. The skeleton has been given the name Jodi and is named after the person who found the remains in 2019 in the American state of Montana. Auction house Sotheby's had expected the skeleton to fetch between five and eight million euros, but in a twelve-minute bidding battle it turned out someone was willing to pay many times that. According to the British newspaper The Guardian, six people bid against each other online and by phone. Who the buyer is has not been disclosed. The skeleton is 4.7 meters long from nose to tail and about 2.7 meters high. For comparison; a tyrannosaurus rex could grow to about 13 meters long and 5 meters high. An employee of Sotheby's shows the nanotyrannus: The excavated nanotyrannus consists of about 191 fossil bones. A skeleton this complete is rare. Only three are known. The auction house described the nanotyrannus as a "fast carnivore that lived at the end of the Cretaceous, about 67 million years ago". Initially the nanotyrannus was seen as a young, not yet fully grown T-rex, but further research showed that it is a different species. Criticism of dinosaur auctions A few months ago a tyrannosaurus rex also went under the hammer and fetched 44 million euros. Criticism of this kind of auction, in which major fossil finds go to unknown buyers, comes from the scientific community. A university lecturer at an American university told The Guardian that they are worried that "potentially scientifically important fossils may be lost to research and the public if they are in private hands". He also finds the amount paid disproportionate. "The total cost of excavating and mounting a skeleton like this is probably at most one million dollars."

title: Netanyahu wants a 'strong, right-wing government' after elections, but there is no clear winner yet
lead: Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, in a speech on election night, called for a "strong, national, right-wing" government. According to him, the exit polls show that the right wing has achieved a "large majority" among Israel's "Zionist voters". Netanyahu points out that his Likud party remains the largest party after yesterday's parliamentary elections. At present, his party stands at 27 seats in the exit polls. That is a loss of five seats. The elections have so far not produced a clear winner. The pro-Netanyahu bloc, consisting of Likud and four other parties, stands at 52 seats in the latest exit poll. The anti-Netanyahu bloc of former army chief Gadi Eisenkot stands at 49 seats. In other exit polls the blocs are evenly balanced. In the exit polls, neither has enough seats for a majority in the parliament, which has 120 seats. Arab parties The two blocs with Arab parties have together won 18 or 19 seats according to the exit polls. That would be a record. As a result, they could play an important role in forming a government without Netanyahu, although Jewish opposition leaders would then have to be willing to work with them. Netanyahu warned in his speech against cooperation with the Arab parties and said it would be a "disgrace" for parties to be willing to do so. According to him, Israel is "together with our friend President Trump facing a historic opportunity to eliminate the Iranian threat once and for all. Iran is weaker than ever and Israel is stronger than ever." 'Motion of no confidence' Earlier in the evening Eisenkot said the exit polls show "a lack of confidence" in Netanyahu and that Israelis have voted for change and against Netanyahu. He called on the 77-year-old prime minister to "accept the motion of no confidence from the people" and to leave politics. Eisenkot promised to form a government that should usher in a "new era of hope" for Israelis. The Arab party Ra'am, which stands at 7 seats, has already said it wants to be part of a new coalition. According to the party's number two, Yoav Segalovitz, it is "nonsense" to think that after the Hamas attack of 7 October 2023 it is impossible to work with Arab parties. There is no final result yet. Around 03.00 hours last night about a quarter of the votes had been counted. According to the electoral commission, turnout was 77.7 percent. That is the highest percentage since 1999.

title: Tensions between the US and Cuba lead to argument and shouting at the UN
lead: Representatives of the United States and Cuba have had an argument at the General Assembly of the United Nations. The American ambassador to the UN, Mike Waltz, launched a fierce attack on the Cuban regime in a speech. The Cuban delegation, including Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez, did not appreciate this and began pounding on the tables and shouting. The Cubans asked the chair to intervene, but he said that Waltz could finish his speech. Rodriguez meanwhile walked toward Waltz's lectern to debate with him and shouted: "You are a liar." The American responded: "This is America, my friend. This is the United Nations. This is not your communist dictatorship. You cannot silence me." Waltz: "Mr. Chair, this person must leave this podium. He will not intimidate me in the United States of America the way he does with political prisoners." And then: "Back off. This is not Havana." The exchange went on for minutes. This scuffle full of non-diplomatic language at the UN shows how great the tensions between the two countries are. The United States, under President Trump, is running a harsh campaign against Cuba. At the end of January, Trump announced that he would impose import tariffs on any country that sells or supplies oil to Cuba. That warning led to enormous fuel shortages on the island. The consequences are severe. Communist Cuba faces prolonged power outages every day. The economy has collapsed and hardly any tourists come anymore. Read here about the consequences of the total oil boycott in April 2026, when correspondent Nina Jurna visited the country: Under pressure from American sanctions, Cuba agreed in June to sweeping reforms that would loosen the country's socialist model somewhat. One of the most important changes was that companies, banks and the real estate sector would be privatised, but Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel stressed that the reforms would not mean the end of the socialist state model. Today the United Nations is voting on a resolution condemning the US economic embargo against Cuba. This has been voted on annually for 34 years, and the resolution is always adopted by an overwhelming majority. Last year 165 countries voted in favour and 7 against. There were 12 abstentions at that time. Last year Argentina, Ukraine and Hungary voted against for the first time. The resolution is not binding, but it does reflect how the American economic embargo against Cuba is viewed worldwide.

title: CBS: number of homes allocated to status holders remains the same
lead: The number of housing association homes allocated to status holders barely rose in 2024, according to figures from Statistics Netherlands (CBS). Just over 8 percent of all housing association homes that became vacant in 2024 were allocated to households with one or more status holders. That concerns just over 13,000 homes, roughly the same as a year earlier. Among starters, the share of status holders is considerably higher. In 2024, 21 percent of the starters who moved into a vacated housing association home were status holders. "That share has been constant for a few years," says CBS demographer Ruben van Gaalen. "But compared with longer ago, an increase is visible. In 2018, for example, the percentage was 9, a lot lower." The figures for 2024 are the most recent data. The umbrella organisation of housing associations, Aedes, has more recent figures, but those are estimates. More status holders among starters. The CBS examined both the total group of status holders and the group of status holders among starters. "Those are people who are getting a home in the Netherlands for the first time," says Van Gaalen. "In addition, there are also status holders who move on, from one home to another. They usually leave behind a home that someone else can live in." That group of starters has grown in recent years. In 2024, 67 percent of households with a status holder were starters on the housing market. In 2023 that was 64 percent. How many homes really go to status holders? In politics, there has been regular debate in recent years about how many social rental homes go to status holders. Some political parties cited the CBS figures, while other parties mentioned much higher percentages. That debate about figures mainly revolves around whether you look at all social rental homes that go to status holders or only at 'starter homes'. In this study, the CBS looked at all social rental homes. That there are more status holders among starters on the housing market is, according to Van Gaalen, because backlogs are still being worked through. "In 2015 and 2016 the influx of asylum seekers in the Netherlands was very high. As a result, many status holders had to wait a long time for a home." While waiting, they stayed in a temporary reception location. When they were later allocated a home, they therefore did not leave a home behind. This is also reflected in the CBS figures. For 16 percent of households with a status holder, a home became vacant after their move. For households without status holders, that was just over half. In addition, almost one in five households with a status holder moved out of a home in which other residents remained. Regional differences Most housing association homes in 2024 went to single-person households. Status holders who move into a housing association home also more often live alone. How many housing association homes were allocated to status holders differs by region. In <entity id="org:provincie-flevoland">Flevoland</entity> the share was highest at 12 percent. In the Gooi en Vechtstreek region and in <entity id="org:gemeente-utrecht">Utrecht</entity> too, relatively many housing association homes went to status holders. Whether that also means the waiting list for a housing association home was longer there than in other places, the CBS cannot say. "You cannot calculate exactly how much longer people have to wait with the national figures," says Van Gaalen. "That also depends, for example, on how many housing association homes and home seekers there are in a municipality and to what extent people move on." Too few homes When refugees are granted residence status in the Netherlands, they are also entitled to housing. Municipalities are responsible for arranging those homes. According to professor of the housing market Peter Boelhouwer, they regularly make agreements about this with housing associations. In consultation with the municipality, some housing associations allocate a part of their homes to so-called urgent cases, who then get a home with priority. These are, for example, people who cannot remain in their current home due to illness or people whose home is being demolished. Or status holders, for example. "In recent years, more and more groups have fallen under the urgency category," says Boelhouwer. "Housing associations want at the same time to prevent the priority group from becoming so large that regular home seekers have to wait very long. As a result, municipalities increasingly have to look for housing for status holders themselves." Due to the tight housing market, that does not always succeed, according to Boelhouwer. This means that many people with an official residence status still live in temporary reception locations in the Netherlands. "That increases the pressure on those locations, which are actually meant for people who do not yet have a residence status," says Boelhouwer.

title: Wake-up call 28/10: House debates infrastructure • Court case over desecration of graves in Utrecht
lead: Good morning! The <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">Tweede Kamer</entity> is debating spending on bridges, roads, locks and other infrastructure, and in Utrecht women are appearing in court for holding a seance at children's graves. First, the weather: today there is plenty of sun but also occasional cloud. It stays dry in most places, with highs of 14 or 15 degrees and a moderate south-westerly wind. This evening more cloud, and with the exception of the south, there is a local chance of some rain. The coming days bring quiet autumn weather with sun, clouds and sometimes mist. Are you heading out today? Here you can find the overview of traffic jams and roadworks, and here you can see the situation on the rail network. What can you expect today? What did you miss: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, in a speech on election night, called for a "strong, national, right-wing" <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity>. According to him, the exit polls show that the right wing has won a "large majority" among Israel's "Zionist voters". Nearly 42 percent of all votes have been counted. The pro-Netanyahu bloc, with 57 seats for now, has ten seats more than the bloc of former army chief Gadi Eisenkot. Other news from the night: And finally: a nipple tattoo is often the last step for women after a major period, such as a mastectomy or breast cancer treatment. Mariska de Jong is a medical tattoo artist and may call herself the best in the world. Have a nice day!

title: Bloc around Prime Minister Netanyahu in the lead in Israeli election
lead: With 76,8 percent of the votes counted in Israel's parliamentary election, the Likud party of Prime Minister Netanyahu is in the lead, with 27 seats for now. Combined with the seats of other parties that support him, he comes to 54 seats. That gives the pro-Netanyahu bloc a lead of seven over the anti-Netanyahu bloc (47 seats) in the count. The preliminary results were announced by the Central Elections Committee. The Knesset, Israel's parliament, has 120 seats. A majority government therefore requires 61 seats. It has never happened that one party won an absolute majority. That means parties always have to form a coalition to be able to govern or need toleration support. Windfall for Netanyahu The preliminary result seems more positive for Netanyahu than expected. In the exit polls, the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot was still ahead. In 2022 Netanyahu's Likud party won the election and the Netanyahu bloc won a majority in the Knesset. That the political landscape does not seem really changed in Israel, despite everything that has happened since 2022, shows that security is still the most important theme. There is a lot of criticism of Netanyahu, but voters also see no good alternative. That is why an important part of the population still seems to think that Netanyahu is the best person to protect Israel. In a speech on election night, Netanyahu called for a "strong, national, right-wing" government. According to him, it has become clear that the right wing has won a "large majority" among Israel's "Zionist voters". Both Netanyahu and rival Eisenkot showed themselves ready to fight for their supporters: forming a coalition has often failed in recent years, which is why new elections had to be held. Arab parties The two blocs with Arab parties have 19 seats between them according to the preliminary counts. That means they could play an important role in forming a government without Netanyahu, although the current opposition leaders would then have to be willing to work with them. In his speech, Netanyahu warned against cooperation with the Arab parties and said it would be a "disgrace" for parties that would be willing to do so. It is still an open question whether Jewish opposition parties will break their election promise and work with the Arab parties. If so, a minority government supported from outside by a number of Arab parties could be considered. Another option the president, who appoints a formateur, could steer toward is a unity government in which Eisenkot and Netanyahu cooperate. A third possibility for Netanyahu is that he persuades an opposition party to join him and so forms a coalition. If nobody manages to form a coalition, new elections will have to be held. Turnout for the Israeli parliamentary election was high at 77,7 percent, the highest percentage since 1999. That amounts to 5,69 million of the roughly 7,33 million eligible voters.

title: Zoo sector shocked by fatal panther attack in Beekse Bergen
lead: The news about the keeper of safari park Beekse Bergen who died after a panther attack is a "great shock for the whole zoo world", says the Dutch Association of Zoos. According to the organisation, a fatal attack by an animal keeper is "extremely rare". The keeper of Beekse Bergen was working alone on Saturday in the indoor enclosure of two Persian male panthers when one of the animals attacked her. She suffered serious injuries to her head and neck and died yesterday. "Employees are sad and react in despair", says a spokesperson for Beekse Bergen. Other animal parks sympathise. "Everyone feels how intense this is. This will linger on for a very long time", says Wineke Schoo, director of the Dutch Association of Zoos. Handful of incidents known In the Netherlands only a few incidents of this kind at zoos are known. The last attack on an employee was very likely in 2003, says Schoo. At that time a 36-year-old employee of Beekse Bergen died after an attack by an elephant. Two years earlier a keeper at Ouwehands Dierenpark was seriously injured in an attack by a lion. There are also reports of a bear attack at DierenPark Amersfoort in 1981 and a fatal tiger attack at Diergaarde Blijdorp in 1979. According to the Dutch Association of Zoos, however, those incidents cannot be compared with the recent panther attack. "Zoos were very different back then. Much less was known about animal behaviour and there was less legislation and regulation." Today animal parks must meet very strict safety requirements. They are checked on the layout of enclosures, the care of animals and the safety of people and animals. For dangerous species there are extra checks. The European Association of Zoos and Aquaria (EAZA) inspects the parks, and there is also review by the Dutch industry association. "Accidents happen in every sector, but fortunately they rarely happen in the zoo world", says Schoo. How it could still go wrong is still unclear. According to Beekse Bergen there are no cameras in the enclosure. 'Investigation of great importance' The keeper had a lot of experience. She started at the animal park at seventeen and worked there for almost forty years, eight of them with the panthers. Because of the bad weather the animals were in the indoor enclosure, where the keeper was working. Normally employees are kept out of the same space as predators. "We would very much like to know what happened", says a spokesperson for Beekse Bergen. The park is engaging an external company for independent research into the attack. The Labour Inspectorate has also started an investigation. According to the Dutch Association of Zoos, the investigations are of great importance, also for other zoos. "Everyone wants to know what happened", says Schoo. The outcomes may also provide valuable lessons for other parks. "Now we only know what the consequences are." Panthers remain in the park Safari park Beekse Bergen will remain open, it has been decided after consultation with the family of the deceased keeper. In the park a condolence table will be set up with a book in which visitors can express their sympathy. A special place will also be arranged for employees. The attack has no consequences for the Persian male panthers. "They are predators and they naturally showed their behaviour. As cruel as it is, the animals cannot be blamed for this", says Beekse Bergen. Unless the research shows that something is wrong with the animals, the care of the panthers in Beekse Bergen will therefore continue.

title: PvdD makes a new attempt to ban slaughter without stunning
lead: The Party for the Animals is once again trying to ban slaughter without stunning. The party wants animals always to be stunned beforehand, including in ritual slaughter. The bill, which goes to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> today, contains further measures. "The purpose of the law is to limit animal suffering during slaughter as much as possible," says MP Ouwehand. If it is up to the Party for the Animals, CO2 stunning of pigs and the use of an electric water bath for chickens, ducks and turkeys must also stop. The party also wants highly pregnant animals no longer to be transported to the slaughterhouse. Furthermore, an end must come to tipping ducks, chickens and turkeys out of crates onto a moving conveyor belt without stunning. The party also considers it important not to look only at slaughter. Ouwehand has therefore previously submitted another law, which is meant to ensure that the way animals are treated in intensive livestock farming changes significantly. "With our bills we are making a shift towards animal-friendly livestock farming," she says. Stunning in ritual slaughter too: fifteen years ago the Party for the Animals also tried to ban slaughter without stunning. That bill failed in <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity>, partly because of the freedom of religion of Jews and Muslims in this case. But the Party for the Animals believes animal suffering weighs more heavily. The <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity> recently ruled that there is now also more room to choose that, since a ban already applies in other countries and thinking about animal welfare has changed. Not all ritual slaughter takes place without stunning. <entity id="person:silvio-erkens">Staatssecretaris Erkens</entity> (Agriculture) said earlier this year that two thirds of the animals during the Feast of Sacrifice are already stunned before being slaughtered with a neck cut. Erkens said this month that they are "personally" in favour of a ban on slaughter without stunning. There is in principle also a majority in the House. However, this subject is sensitive, so parties still want to look carefully at the bill text. It is therefore not yet possible to say in advance whether the law will succeed this time.

title: Cruise ship that was to sail 'forever' stranded in Cambodia due to high fuel prices
lead: The luxury cruise ship Villa Vie Odyssey, which was on an "eternal voyage" around the world, has become stranded off the coast of Cambodia. The American cruise line says in a statement that fuel costs in Asia are so high that the company cannot pass them on to passengers. According to the company, the monthly cost per cabin had risen from 1600 euros to 7000 euros. "Fully passing on the increase to the residents is not a realistic solution", the statement says. News agency Bloomberg reports that about two hundred passengers were on board. Afternoon disembarkation: All passengers were told on Monday morning in the Cambodian port town of Sihanoukville that they had to leave the ship that afternoon. According to the cruise line, the decision was not taken lightly: to save fuel, the ship had already been staying in ports for longer and sailing at a lower speed. When the ship set off on its world voyage two years ago, passengers could buy a cabin at prices ranging from 90,000 to 812,000 euros. Renting was also possible: rental prices were around 2200 euros per month. Mainly Americans, Canadians and Britons made use of this. Permanent residents without a home: Because the cruise line had said the ship would sail the world's seas non-stop, calling at 425 ports, 147 countries and 7 continents every 3.5 years, a number of residents live permanently on the Villa Vie Odyssey. They have no home on the mainland. The cruise line has pledged to help these people find replacement housing. The Villa Vie Odyssey is a cruise ship more than 30 years old that has undergone a thorough refurbishment. It left the port of Belfast in October 2024, four months late. There were problems at the time with the rudders and certifying the ship. The cruise line writes that it will examine in the coming months whether a restart is possible.

title: Breda hospital cracks down on its own staff: wheel clamps for illegal parking
lead: Staff of Amphia Ziekenhuis in Breda risk a wheel clamp from 1 November if they park their car outside the parking bays at the staff entrance. Persistent offenders could ultimately lose their parking privileges permanently. The hospital tells Omroep Brabant that it is troubled by illegal parkers. "This creates unsafe situations because the passage for other traffic is restricted." It also sometimes leads to damage to other vehicles, according to a spokesperson. Not enough parking spaces For the approximately 5000 people the hospital employs, there are 1609 parking spaces available at the staff entrance. At some times that is insufficient, the spokesperson admits. Especially in bad weather on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays, and during shift changes between 14.00 and 16.00, it can be busy. When staff cannot find a spot, they must report this to security, which then looks for a solution. Too often staff solve it themselves by parking the car outside the bay, Amphia believes. Stricter measures The hospital has already made several attempts to point staff to the parking policy. For example, staff received a warning card under their windscreen wiper and were personally addressed by security guards. Staff were also pointed to their parking behaviour via the hospital intranet. This did not have the desired effect, so the hospital is moving to stricter measures. Security guards will fit wheel clamps on illegal parkers and register the violation. An official warning will also follow. On a third violation the employee may not park in the car park for a week. Anyone who then makes the mistake again may permanently lose their parking privilege. Small group According to Amphia, the vast majority do comply with the rules. "The measure targets a small group that repeatedly parks outside the bays."

title: Minor boy shot dead in Belgrade after attack on Israeli embassy
lead: A minor boy was shot dead shortly after midnight in the Serbian capital Belgrade after he attacked a member of a special police unit with two knives. The officer was guarding the Israeli embassy. Serbian Minister Dacic of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> speaks of a terrorist attack. The terror threat in the country has been raised to the highest level. There is more police presence at important locations in Serbia. The boy was shot dead by the security guard himself after his knife attack. According to the minister, the security guard acted in self-defence and was slightly injured in the face in the process. He has been taken to hospital. Serbian media report that he will probably be allowed home today. According to Dacic, the young attacker came from the city of Sabac, west of Belgrade. He was on the radar of the national security services and a supporter of Islamic State, the minister said. During the attack he reportedly shouted "Allahoe akbar" and images with IS symbols reportedly appeared on his Instagram account.

title: President Zelensky in The Hague today, visits Jetten and the king
lead: The Ukrainian president Zelensky comes to The Hague today for, among other things, a visit to <entity id="person:willem-alexander">koning Willem-Alexander</entity>. Zelensky will be received at Paleis Huis ten Bosch early in the evening, the <entity id="org:rijksvoorlichtingsdienst">Rijksvoorlichtingsdienst</entity> says. Beforehand he will hold talks with <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity>, Minister Yesilgöz of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-defensie">Defensie</entity> and <entity id="person:tom-berendsen">minister Berendsen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">Buitenlandse Zaken</entity>. The Ukrainian president also speaks with leading figures from the Dutch and Ukrainian business communities. The visit comes on the day that the Netherlands has announced a support package for Ukraine. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> makes 1,2 billion euros in total available in non-military support for the coming three years. <entity id="person:sjoerd-sjoerdsma">Minister Sjoerdsma</entity> is in Kyiv. Minister Sjoerdsma of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-bho">Buitenlandse Handel en Ontwikkelingssamenwerking</entity> announced that this morning during a visit to Kyiv. He is in the Ukrainian capital to talk with representatives of the Ukrainian government and with Dutch companies that are active in Ukraine. Sjoerdsma points to the harsh winter the country is facing. "It is also of great importance for the safety of us all that we keep supporting the Ukrainians so that they can sustain the fight. That is why the cabinet is now taking an extra step." For this year alone, 40 million euros will therefore be transferred to the Ukraine Energy Support Fund, a fund set up by the European Commission and the Ukrainian Ministry of Energy to repair the heavily damaged energy infrastructure in the country. This infrastructure is under heavy fire due to ongoing Russian air attacks. The Ukrainian capital Kyiv is being bombarded with missiles practically day and night, so the power already often goes out even though winter has not even really begun yet. Money for reconstruction The cabinet also makes 55 million euros available so that Ukraine can order parts from Dutch companies that are needed to keep the energy infrastructure running. Furthermore, 136 million goes to companies that want to help with the reconstruction of Ukraine. The cabinet also helps companies that want to export to Ukraine to limit their financial risks. Coen van Oostrom of employers' organisation VNO-NCW, who is travelling with the minister, says the task in Ukraine is enormous. "Dutch companies can play an important role in that. But then we must work closely with the Ukrainian government and remove the obstacles for companies." The support package does not mean that extra money is being set aside for Ukraine. Of the 1,2 billion euros, 878 million euros comes from the coalition agreement, and the 327 million extra was announced on Prinsjesdag. Norway and Finland call Putin The visit by Zelensky to The Hague comes on the eve of possible negotiations to end the war. These are expected to take place somewhere early next month. An exact date for talks between Russian, American and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi has not yet been set. Europe is not at the table, for now. The Finnish president Stubb and the Norwegian prime minister Støre called the Russian president Putin on their own initiative yesterday. They had coordinated this with Ukraine beforehand, but Denmark was not happy about it. The Danish prime minister Frederiksen warns that "solo actions" could put Europe's unity under pressure. In response, Zelensky expressed his support for the action by Norway and Finland. Zelensky may discuss Europe's role with Jetten today as well, along with the role of the International Criminal Court (ICC). After the war, the ICC would have to examine war crimes committed against Ukraine. That Russia is held responsible for this war is an important point for Ukraine, as are security guarantees. Zelensky's visit live on NOS The visit of President Zelensky to Prime Minister Jetten can be watched live on NOS this afternoon. Join live from 13.45 hours, with the press conference at 15.30 hours. You can follow the visit via the livestream in the NOS app and on NOS.nl.

title: Two passenger trains collide in Spain, dozens dead
lead: A collision between two passenger trains in Spain has killed dozens of people. Local authorities have confirmed thirty deaths: 24 in one train and 6 in the other. A number of Spanish media outlets speak of 46 victims. Live blog Follow the latest news on the train collision also in our live blog . The accident happened this morning on the high-speed line between Madrid and Andalusia, between the places Los Yébenes and Urda, south of Madrid. The AVE train of railway company Renfe is said to have rear-ended a stationary train. According to El Mundo, this would have happened at more than 100 kilometres per hour. The stationary train was standing still on the orders of railway manager Adif because of a problem with a signal. El Mundo reports that first research shows the AVE train did not receive that information in time. Footage shows that two carriages derailed and fell down an embankment. Emergency services are on site. Train traffic on the route has been halted. Train traffic will not be resumed for the time being either. According to El País, at least eighty trains were cancelled later in the day. There are fears the death toll may rise, because the rescue teams have not yet been able to reach the bottom of the crashed carriages. The two trains reportedly carried about 550 people. Government sources report that human error may be the cause of the accident. A computerised signalling system is used on the track, but it reportedly failed. During this malfunction, an employee reportedly resumed the timetable, after which the trains collided. El País spoke to a passenger who was in one of the rear carriages of one of the trains. About 40 minutes after departure this passenger felt "a hard blow". To news outlet Onda Cero, a passenger says they were thrown through the train. After the impact, according to this passenger, dead people were lying in the aisle. Another traveller says there were people with broken legs. Blood donations requested Spanish Prime Minister Sánchez says on X that he is "devastated" by the serious train accident. He extends his condolences to all victims and their families. Health Minister García said on national television that all hospitals in the area have been alerted. According to her, hospitals in the region have sufficient intensive care beds available to treat seriously injured travellers. The blood transfusion centre in Madrid has "made an urgent appeal for blood donations". Municipalities near the accident are calling on residents not to go to local health centres for the time being. This leaves as many places as possible available for treating injured travellers. Family taken in Railway company Renfe has opened a telephone number for family members of passengers. At Atocha station in Madrid a room is being set up to receive family members of those on board. Several people have already reported there, including Carlos Larquin. His aunt Silvia was travelling on one of the trains, he tells El País. As soon as he heard about the accident through the media, he tried to call her. "I don't know whether she is still alive or injured, because she isn't answering her phone." Third accident in a year It is the third major train accident on Spanish tracks this year. In January, two serious accidents occurred within three days. In the first accident, near Córdoba, a high-speed train derailed. It ended up on the adjacent track and collided there with another high-speed train. More than forty people died in the collision. Three days later a regional train near Barcelona collided with debris from a collapsed wall along the track. The train's driver died. After the two accidents, the Spanish train drivers' union Semaf announced a three-day strike. The union demanded more safety on the railways. Diego Martín Fernández, secretary-general of Semaf, had already warned that accidents of this kind could happen due to a backlog of maintenance on lines still in heavy use. According to him, much more must be invested in building new railway lines. The strikes were over after one day. The union reached an agreement on additional safety measures.

title: New cold case investigation method is successful and will be used more often
lead: There is a new investigative method for solving serious cold cases. A pilot by the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> and the <entity id="org:nederlands-forensisch-instituut">Nederlands Forensisch Instituut</entity>, which uses private DNA databases, has been successfully completed. This method will therefore be used in more cases. The method makes it possible to compare DNA from the scene of a crime with DNA profiles from databases that have given permission for this. In this way it becomes easier to trace a suspect through (distant) relatives. The method can also help establish the identity of unknown victims. "I am confident that thanks to this method we will solve cases in the future," says Mirjam Warnaar, national public prosecutor for forensic investigation. Only in serious cases The OM currently decides when the new method may be used precisely. This will in any case only happen in murder cases and other serious criminal cases, says Warnaar. "Such as an investigation into a serial rapist." Another condition is that there are no leads left. Permission will also be requested from the investigating judge for each case. Heuvelmoord lead The new method has been used since 2023 in six cases, including the so-called Heuvelmoord case. In two cases new leads were found. The Heuvelmoord case revolves around the death of 68-year-old Sjef Leukel in Berg en Terblijt. An unknown man entered the home of Leukel and his wife in 2004 and attacked them. Sjef Leukel died and his wife was seriously injured. During the pilot, two possible relatives of the perpetrator were found in DNA databases, who live in the United States. To investigate that lead further, a request for legal assistance to the US is now underway.

title: Olympic athlete and former politician Mieke Sterk dies aged 80
lead: Former athlete and former politician Mieke Sterk has died at the age of 80. The Haarlem native was part of the quartet that ran a world record of 43.4 seconds in the heats of the 4x100 metres at the 1968 Olympic Games in Mexico City. In the final the quartet finished fourth. Sterk's time, together with Wilma van den Berg, Truus Hennipman-Cruiming and Corrie Bakker, remained the Dutch record for 44 years. It was only equalled during the 2011 World Athletics Championships in Daegu, South Korea, and a year later the record fell. Sterk was a sprinter, hurdler and multi-event athlete. During her career she won twenty national titles in individual and relay events. Outside the track she also stood out for her (in those years) unconventional behaviour. For example, just before the opening ceremony of the 1968 Summer Games she cut off her skirt, because in her view the garment was "te truttig" (too prim). During her career Sterk was politically engaged. For instance, in 1969 she refused to take part in the European Championships in Athens, in protest against the dictatorial regime that was in power in Greece. After her athletics career Sterk became a politician. At the request of Felix Rottenberg she sat for the Labour Party from 1994 to 1998 in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. She was given a portfolio including sport and care for people with disabilities. Criticism of the PvdA's policy brought an early end to her political career in 1997. After harsh words directed at the party executive, Sterk was placed in an unelectable position, after which she was not re-elected.

title: Dozens of servers seized in Limburg over the distribution of child pornography
lead: The police have seized dozens of servers in an international investigation into a dubious hosting company. The company is suspected of being an accomplice in facilitating cybercrime. According to the police, the hosting company was involved in, among other things, distributing child pornography, phishing activities and ransomware attacks. The servers were seized in a data centre in Limburg. According to the police, the company presented itself as a so-called bulletproof hosting provider (see box). The company advertised, among other things, complete anonymity for users. Bulletproof hosting Bulletproof hosts are called rogue hosting companies. They target specifically a criminal clientele, which for example is involved in phishing, sending spam or storing child pornography. They advertise on underground forums that customers stay out of sight of the authorities and that payment can be made anonymously with cryptocurrencies. Through the seizure, the police now have the data of more than 3000 customers who used the servers for criminal activities. The American security service FBI and the German police were also involved in the investigation. They, among other things, tracked down suspects and seized cryptocurrency.

title: Petrol at the pump slightly cheaper again despite expensive oil
lead: The petrol price has fallen again recently, after it was still at a record high halfway through this month. Right now you pay an average of 2.55 euros. During the peak two weeks ago, United Consumers saw an average of 2.73 euros being asked for a litre of petrol. The diesel price is also slightly lower this week, but it has not fallen as sharply as the petrol price. United Consumers receives the recommended prices of five large petrol chains daily. However, this price is often only used along the motorway. Petrol stations away from the motorway and unstaffed stations are often much cheaper. It is striking that pump prices are falling even though the oil price has risen again in recent weeks. The price of a barrel of oil is now around 115 dollars. Since April it has not been this high. Abnormal times "In normal times the petrol price does what the oil price does. But now you see that three factors determine the petrol and diesel price," says energy expert Jilles van den Beukel. "At the moment the price is determined just as much by transport costs and refining costs." Although the costs of shipping oil around the world have risen sharply recently, these costs were already factored into the pump price several weeks ago. Refineries are currently charging less to process crude oil into petrol and diesel. According to Van den Beukel, this may be because more refined oil products have come onto the market recently. Still, the expectation is not that the petrol and diesel price at the pump will keep falling in the long term. "I think the long term is upward, as long as nothing fundamental changes in the Middle East," says Van den Beukel.

title: Explosives from WWII found at Eindhoven Airport
lead: Two explosives have been found at Eindhoven Airport. They are explosives left over from the Second World War. According to a spokesperson for the Royal Marechaussee, one is a mortar shell and the other is a provisionally unidentified object. The Explosive Ordnance Disposal Service of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-defensie">Defensie</entity> will render the bombs harmless. Air traffic at Eindhoven Airport is not affected by the find. The explosives were discovered during groundwork. This is related to the major renovation of the airport, which begins early next year. WWII newsletter Interested in the Second World War? Then subscribe to our newsletter here.

title: Feminist Aletta Jacobs to get a statue in central The Hague
lead: Aletta Jacobs (1854-1929) will get a statue in the centre of The Hague. The statue of the feminist must be unveiled by the end of 2028 at the latest at the Wijnhaven, close to the The Hague campus of the University of <entity id="org:gemeente-leiden">Leiden</entity>. Already in 2017, former House Speaker and then PvdA municipal councillor Jeltje van Nieuwenhoven proposed the plan to put a woman on a pedestal in The Hague for once. And although Jacobs was born in the Groningen village of Sappemeer, as a champion of women's suffrage and the first female doctor in the Netherlands she was, according to the municipality of The Hague, extremely suitable to get a likeness in the city. Hundredth death anniversary. Originally the plan was to unveil a statue for the celebration of one hundred years of women's suffrage in 2019, but that did not succeed. Now the municipality is trying to place the likeness well before the commemoration of the hundredth death anniversary of Jacobs on 10 August 2029. Meanwhile the intended location has also changed, writes regional broadcaster West. First the statue was to come at the Hofvijver, but according to alderman Van Basten Batenburg that spot is not suitable. "The scale and appearance of the intended statue do not relate well to the green character and the other statues along the Hofvijver", writes the alderman. The newly chosen place close to the campus she does find a "fitting location". First feminist wave. Jacobs was born in 1854 as the eighth of eleven children in a Jewish family. As the first woman in the Netherlands she obtained her university degree and became a doctor. After graduating from the State University of <entity id="org:gemeente-groningen">Groningen</entity> she went to London, where she specialised in paediatrics and as a women's doctor. She became an important figure in the first feminist wave. For example, Jacobs fought for women's suffrage and equality in marriage. She became co-founder and chair of the Vereeniging voor Vrouwenkiesrecht. In September 1919, partly through her efforts, women's suffrage was introduced. At the State University of Groningen a statue of Jacobs already stands. She is also included in the Canon of the Netherlands, the list of the most important themes from the nation's history.

title: 'Cutting civil servants is a nice plan, but it has never worked'
lead: The cabinet's plan to make deep cuts in the number of central government civil servants has the support of almost the entire <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">Tweede Kamer</entity>. At the same time, almost everyone is convinced that it will not succeed. Within nine years, 25,000 of the 160,000 civil servants must have been cut, state secretary <entity id="person:eric-van-der-burg">Eric van der Burg</entity> for Slagvaardige Overheid announced. That would yield an annual saving of 3.5 billion euros. Money that is badly needed to balance the budget. But recent history offers little hope: of the last ten cabinets, eight argued for fewer central government civil servants. None of those eight cabinets ultimately managed it. In fact, in recent years the number of civil servants at ministries rose from 110,000 to 160,000. "It has exploded," says former senior civil servant Roel Bekker. According to him, that is mainly because the number of parliamentary motions is higher than ever. This calendar year there were already well over 4,700. It is a monstrous task for civil servants to examine and answer all of them. Arjan Noorlander: 'Plan is a castle in the air' "This goes down well with voters and MPs, but it is not feasible. It is precisely those MPs who burden civil servants with endless questions and regulations that they have endless work on. The Tweede Kamer currently has a record number of seventeen factions. They all want to arrange something for their own constituency through motions and parliamentary questions. Saying that you are going to shrink the ministries is, according to the <entity id="org:centraal-planbureau">Centraal Planbureau</entity> and the <entity id="org:algemene-rekenkamer">Rekenkamer</entity>, a false promise. You simply won't achieve it. Don't do it, they say to the current <entity id="org:kabinet">kabinet</entity>, once again. Certainly if you have no concrete plan for where the civil servants are supposed to go. And what does the cabinet do? Exactly that: name an amount of 3.5 billion, but no concrete plan. So for now this cabinet is building castles in the air." Bekker also finds it remarkable that the cabinet already links a concrete amount of 3.5 billion to the cut, without it being clear which departments must cut how many jobs. What is clear is that <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> and defence remain untouched. Implementing agencies such as the <entity id="org:zbo-uitvoeringsinstituut-werknemersverzekeringen">UWV</entity>, <entity id="org:immigratie-en-naturalisatiedienst">IND</entity> and the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity> are not excluded in advance. Those organisations are already under considerable pressure and in fact need more staff rather than less. Bekker worked in 2007 at the ministry of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> when he was given the task of shrinking the government by 12,800 fte. With great difficulty he managed, by his own account, to bring about a "dip" in the development of the number of civil servants. But in the years after, tens of thousands of jobs were added again. "Politicians quickly forgot the intention and came up with all sorts of things that cost enormous amounts of staff. More police on the streets, expanding prisons. You then have to box against that." Crises and the whim of the day The number of motions has been rising for years. According to Bekker, that is partly because "the whim of the day" rules. He also sees that parliamentarians increasingly insist on tailor-made solutions and devise complicated regulations. Implementing those places a heavy burden on civil servants. Crises such as corona, the childcare benefits affair and gas extraction in Groningen also led to extra civil servants. "The mood in cabinets was: put more people on it. But somehow it is difficult to put an end to it." MPs themselves also find the number of motions far too high. CDA member Harmen Krul calls it "too bizarre for words" that the figure of 5,000 is likely to be reached this year. "Crazy," says Gidi Markuszower. "A great many motions are not adopted, so why submit them?" BBB MP Caroline van der Plas also thinks parliament should be self-critical, but at the same time she understands that the number of motions is rising. "There are a lot of new MPs.
