That means they have more than enough money to pay out pensions. Earlier this year, ABP, PME and other pension funds were affected by the war in the Persian Gulf. But rising interest rates appear to be sustaining their strong financial position. For example, the funding ratio of ABP, the largest pension fund in the Netherlands, rose from 126.9 percent to 132.2 percent in recent months. That of PME rose from 127.7 percent to 132.8 percent. This is good news for pension recipients, as these pension funds are approaching their transition to the new system. The higher the funding ratio before the transition, the more money there is to distribute. Rising interest rates "The financial markets were turbulent again in the third quarter. The war in the Middle East flared up and interest rates rose sharply due to ever-increasing government debt in, among others, the United States and France", says ABP chair Harmen van Wijnen. A higher interest rate is favourable for pension funds because they then need less capital to pay out all agreed pensions. "As a result, the increase in the funding ratio continued in the third quarter", says Van Wijnen. What is the funding ratio? The funding ratio indicates whether pensions can be paid now and in the future. 100 percent means that for every euro in pension obligations there is also a euro in reserves. Below 100 means a shortfall, and above 100 means there is enough money. If the funding ratio is too low, the pension fund must reduce benefits. If the funding ratio is high enough, pension benefits can be increased. Because the new pension system has a more individual structure, the overall funding ratio is a less relevant figure for funds that have 'moved over'. PME and ABP write that the high funding ratio gives them a good position for the transition to the new pension scheme. Just before the transition, the funds can distribute the extra capital from the funding ratio among their participants. This calculates how much each pension is worth in total and how much money goes into the shared buffer. "If the economy and interest rates do not show major fluctuations, our participants receiving pensions can expect their pensions to increase by 12.6 percent in 2027", says Alae Laghrich, chair of the executive board of PME. How much can be distributed depends on the funding ratio on December 31. New system ABP and PME both switch to the new pension system on January 1 next year. In that new system, participants have individual pension pots. Younger participants are invested with more risk. This can result in losses, but also high profits. The closer a participant gets to retirement age, the less risky the investments become. Funds that have already switched to the new system do not report funding ratios, because these no longer play a major role now that participants have individual pots. Earlier it turned out that the funds that had already switched were also doing well. This was mainly thanks to positive returns on the stock market. Because of these positive figures, pensions are expected to be increased slightly next year.

title: Judge Alvin Hellerstein (92) dies, known for 9/11, Maduro and Trump hush money case
lead: US judge Alvin Hellerstein has died at the age of 92. As a federal judge in Manhattan, he was involved in several high-profile cases, such as the September 11, 2001 attacks, President Trump's hush money affair and, more recently, the charges against former Venezuelan president Maduro. Hellerstein, born in New York and a graduate of Columbia Law School, served in the Judge Advocate General's Corps of the US Army and worked as a trial lawyer in Manhattan. In 1998, President Clinton appointed him as a federal judge. Maduro case Earlier this month, Hellerstein presided over a hearing in which the torture charges against Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores were addressed. During a hearing on October 8, Hellerstein often coughed and at times had difficulty speaking. He told the lawyers: "I have problems with my voice. As long as you can understand me, I will continue." He had planned to preside himself over the trial against Maduro and Flores, which he had scheduled for June. The Maduro case, and other cases that fell under Hellerstein, will be reassigned. Previously, he handled the bulk of the civil lawsuits over the 2001 World Trade Center attacks. These dozens of cases concerning wrongful death, injury and property damage took two decades. According to lawyers, Hellerstein showed great compassion for the victims and their relatives. He spoke with them for hours in his office and rejected settlement proposals that he considered inadequate. Trump hush money In August, Hellerstein again rejected an attempt by Trump to overturn his conviction in the hush money case. "Paying hush money to a porn actress or covering up an embarrassing matter does not fall under presidential immunity", he wrote, referring to the payment of 130,000 dollars to porn actress Stormy Daniels, which is central to the case against Trump. Another notable case of Hellerstein's was the trial against Charlie Javice, who received a prison sentence last year for defrauding the bank JPMorgan Chase of 175 million dollars. In 2024, he convicted hedge fund founder Bill Hwang of market manipulation that cost banks billions of dollars. Hellerstein died on Wednesday morning in the presence of his family. The funeral will be held on Thursday in a chapel in Manhattan.

title: Activist and union leader Dolores Huerta (96) dies, the woman behind Obama's slogan
lead: The influential American union leader and feminist Dolores Huerta died on Wednesday at her home in Bakersfield, California, from the effects of cancer. She was 96 years old. Huerta was known as one of the most influential union leaders, icons of the civil rights movement and feminist activists in the country. Her Spanish-language slogan was "Sí, se puede!", loosely translated as "Yes, it can be done!". A symbol of her conviction that people who take action can actually bring about change. The phrase later became world-famous thanks to Obama's English-language variant "Yes, we can". She received countless honours during her career, including the Presidential Medal of Freedom. President Obama, when presenting this highest American civilian honour in 2012, described her as a tenacious leader. He also said he was glad she let him use her slogan for his 2008 election campaign. "I'm glad she let me get away with it so easily, because you can't pull one over on Dolores." Leader of farm workers Huerta was born in 1930 as Dolores Clara Fernandez in Dawson, New Mexico. Her father was a miner and union activist who managed to win a seat in the state parliament. After her parents' divorce, her mother moved with her and her brothers to California. Through her early commitment to civil rights, Huerta came into contact with César Chávez. In 1962 they founded the National Farm Workers Association, which later grew into the United Farm Workers of America. For many years she was one of the most important leaders and negotiators. The breakthrough for Huerta and Chávez came when they mobilised Filipino pickers for what would become the five-year 'Delano grape strike'. Together they negotiated collective labour agreements and contracts with large agricultural companies. They secured groundbreaking care arrangements and fringe benefits for farm workers. This year Huerta revealed that she was sexually abused by Chávez in the 1960s. Two children resulted from this, who were raised by others. She had kept this secret for sixty years, including long after her abuser died in 1993. After her revelation, Chávez's name was removed from the holiday that had previously been a source of pride for the Spanish-speaking community in several states. A sign at César Chávez Park in Denver was covered with a tarpaulin. Someone placed a handmade sign over it reading "Dolores Huerta Park". Legacy of justice Even well past ninety, Huerta still took part in protests and encouraged activists to keep speaking out on issues such as racism, poverty, and women's and LGBTQ+ rights. "We want to leave our children a legacy of justice. Not jewellery, possessions or money, because those are the only things they'll fight over", she says in the 2025 documentary. "So the most important thing is to pass on to them a love of justice; that, I think, is the most beautiful gift we can leave anyone."

title: North Korea fires ballistic missiles toward the sea
lead: North Korea has fired about ten short-range ballistic missiles toward the sea off the east coast, the South Korean military leadership reports. The missiles were launched around 12:30 from near the coastal town of Wonsan. At least one projectile has landed in the Sea of Japan, outside Japanese waters, confirms the Japanese news agency Kyodo. North Korea has carried out weapons tests at least ten times earlier this year. Two weeks ago, it also fired several ballistic missiles toward the waters east of the country. South Korea tested a projectile a few days before that which can reach at least five times the speed of sound and is designed to evade missile defence systems. Landmines and loudspeakers Tensions between North and South Korea are rising. Last month, three South Korean soldiers were injured in landmine explosions. According to that country, these were placed by North Korea south of the demarcation line, the border in the demilitarised zone between the two countries. Pyongyang denies any involvement. Last week, Kim Yo-jong, the sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, reported that loudspeakers are ready along the entire border for psychological warfare. Previously, they stood on both sides of the demarcation line. South Korea played K-pop music and criticism of Kim Jong-un's regime, while North Korea responded with the sound of gongs and howling animals. Last year, the loudspeakers were in fact switched off to reduce tensions between the countries.

title: Morning briefing 29/10: Verdict on youth violence in Beverwijk • New ECB interest rate decision
lead: Good morning! Today the court in Haarlem will deliver its verdict on the assault of a 17-year-old boy during the youth violence in the region last year. And the European Central Bank will announce whether interest rates will be adjusted. First the weather: sunny periods and clouds alternate. With little wind, the mercury rises to 14 to 16 degrees. Are you going out today? Here you can find the overview of traffic jams and roadworks, and here you can see the situation on the railways. What can you expect today? What you missed: US President Trump wants Mary Peltola, a Democratic Senate candidate for the state of Alaska, to be removed from the ballot. According to The New York Times, Peltola is deliberately trying to sow confusion in the elections on 3 November with a recruited 'spoiler candidate'. Two men on the ballot have almost the same name. The incumbent Republican senator is called Dan S. Sullivan, and Dan J. Sullivan is running as an independent candidate. The latter will most likely not win the election, but he could well siphon off important votes from his namesake. Other news from overnight: And finally, this: Seven months ago, a capybara escaped from Marwell Zoo in the English county of Hampshire, without leaving a trace. But recently surfaced camera footage now shows that the animal is doing fine without caretakers. Since Samba disappeared, search operations have been carried out regularly using drones that detect heat images, but also with search dogs and camera traps. In recent weeks, Marwell staff have installed extra wildlife cameras, which have yielded additional photographic material of Samba. Have a great day!

title: 'Continuing at normal speed': recordings point to human error in Spanish train disaster
lead: Audio fragments that the newspaper El País has in its possession appear to indicate that a human error played a major role in yesterday's Spanish train disaster. It can be heard how the traffic control gives a high-speed train permission to continue at full speed, although that is against protocol. El País posted online three conversations of several minutes each between the train traffic control and the two trains involved in the accident: two in which both trains are given permission to resume the journey after a malfunction, and one in which a driver reports that he cannot yet drive because of a malfunction. A few minutes later the train approaching from behind collided with the stationary train. The problems began around 08:30, when Urda station was hit by a malfunction. Shortly afterwards the first contact takes place with the AVE train that was on its way from Madrid to Seville. The driver reports that he has come to a standstill, but is told by traffic control that he may continue under an alternative safety system. "Disconnect the LZB protection and reconnect it. Then resume the journey at normal speed under protection of the BSL", says the train dispatcher. The driver then asks for confirmation: "At normal speed?", which the traffic controller confirms. This is how it went wrong in Spain: Transport Minister Puente called that decision incomprehensible last night. "It is not decided to drive at adjusted speed. That is a speed at which the driver can still stop the train if there is an obstacle on the track, at most 40 kilometres per hour." The track indeed turns out not to be clear, which the control room learns a few minutes later. The Iryo train that had departed from Madrid to Seville a few minutes before the AVE is still standing on the same route, the driver reports in a conversation at 08:41. "I am standing at the signal at Urda", she reports. She too is instructed to continue the journey at normal speed, but at 08:48 she comes back on the line with the message that the train is still standing. "Restarting the LZB system is not permitted, so I am still standing at the signal." The person she is in contact with does not seem to make the connection between those three conversations. "Understood", is all he reports. "Well, okay, let us know. We will hear about it if you keep having problems." Five minutes later the AVE slams into the Iryo train at high speed. Search continues Spanish police have begun taking statements from everyone who was in the traffic control room at that time. Throughout the night the wreckage was searched for victims. Lit by construction lamps, the twisted steel was searched with heavy equipment. It is not yet clear whether that has yielded anything: The death toll of the train accident stands at 68, and around 60 victims are lying injured in hospital. There were 147 people in the stationary train and 397 in the AVE train. It is not clear how many occupants are still missing. Spain has announced three days of national mourning. Last night a minute's silence was also held in several places for the victims. Public transport was also brought to a standstill in several cities. Protest At the Ministry of Transport, several hundred people gathered last night to demand the resignation of Minister Puente and Prime Minister Sánchez. When bottles and fireworks were thrown, the police dispersed them with tear gas. No one has been arrested. Puente maintains that the Spanish railway is safe: "There are systems, rules, protocols. Mistakes can happen, but I want to emphasise that our railways are just as safe as those in neighbouring countries."

title: Cabinet leaders meet after new demands package from JA21, BBB and SGP
lead: The cabinet leadership has convened to discuss the demands package from JA21, BBB and SGP. <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> (D66) and the deputy prime ministers Van den Brink (CDA) and Yesilgöz (VVD) are present, but so is <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">minister Heinen</entity> (VVD) of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity>. This morning JA21, SGP and BBB announced that they will work together in the negotiations with the minority cabinet on the tax plan. From now on it is "together out, together home", said JA21 <entity id="person:bernard-johannes-eerdmans">leider Eerdmans</entity> to the NOS. In a letter to the cabinet, the three right-wing opposition parties offer their support for the tax plan and a constructive attitude toward all other budgets, in exchange for major changes to the plans of D66, VVD and CDA. The tax plan sets out how the minority cabinet wants to arrange taxes in the coming years. JA21, SGP and BBB want to scrap the tax increase meant to meet the NATO norm, which CDA calls the freedom contribution, and instead want a substantial tax reduction. The major changes to the nitrogen plans that BBB requested earlier, more measures on asylum, which JA21 has consistently advocated, and the SGP demands on medical-ethical issues, including surrogacy and abortion policy, are now joint demands. The three parties want to pay for their plans through cuts in other areas. Asked by the NOS, the parties say that they are reserving the details "for the negotiating table with the cabinet". According to SGP <entity id="person:christiaan-stoffer">leider Stoffer</entity>, everything is "covered down to the last euro" and the focus should mainly be on "cutting government spending". Left or right. Because of the cooperation and the content of the package, the coalition, which is already divided internally, will come under even more pressure. D66 and CDA prefer the left, while the VVD prefers cooperation with right-wing parties. The cabinet says it always wants broad support in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> with a hundred seats. Opposition parties say that this is not possible and that the cabinet must choose. Besides putting this right-wing alliance on edge with the minority coalition, it also becomes clearer that broad support is becoming increasingly difficult: the package contains demands that Pro and Volt will not support. On Monday Prime Minister Jetten still urged parties to judge the tax plan mainly on its content and not to link other matters to it. With this letter SGP, JA21 and BBB are doing exactly that: they emphasise their concerns about the cabinet's plans. Besides adjustments on nitrogen, asylum and medical ethics, they also want major changes to the tax increases. "The Netherlands runs on people who work, run businesses and care for their families", they write, and people deserve "a government that ensures that working and entrepreneurship pay off and that taking responsibility is not punished". Proposed tax reductions by SGP, BBB and JA21 - Scrapping the 'freedom contribution'. - Tackling the tax gap between single-earner and dual-earner households. - Raising the SME profit exemption to relieve entrepreneurs. - Scrapping the VAT increase on ornamental horticulture. Scrapping the tax increase for defence spending is particularly sensitive for CDA. The SGP demands on abortion and surrogacy will be especially hard to swallow for D66, the largest governing party. On the demand that municipalities not be forced to take in asylum seekers, asylum minister Van den Brink (CDA) has said several times that he cannot promise this on paper because it conflicts with the Dispersal Act. The major adjustments to the nitrogen package will also meet resistance. The proposal conflicts with agreements that the cabinet said earlier were necessary to get permits moving again. And if the plans are changed substantially, Pro will withdraw its support. The right-wing opposition parties themselves speak of a "constructive offer", with which the cabinet sees its plans assured of sufficient support in the House and the <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">Eerste Kamer</entity>. An offer that will mainly appeal to the VVD will make the pressure on the already divided minority cabinet even greater than it was.

title: Struggling seal centre gets no extra money from municipality
lead: Zeehondencentrum Pieterburen cannot count on extra money from the municipality to stay afloat. The centre has been struggling with financial problems for some time and previously reported that its survival was at stake if the municipality and province did not step in. In the municipal council of <entity id="org:gemeente-het-hogeland">Het Hogeland</entity>, where the centre is based, a majority voted against extra financial support last night. Last year, the Zeehondencentrum Pieterburen merged into the new Werelderfgoedcentrum Waddenzee (WEC) in Lauwersoog. The new centre was meant to give the outdated seal care a "sustainable future", including by offering more space for education and experience. Building the WEC cost 43,7 million euros, 17,4 million more than budgeted. The doors opened in April 2025, but visitor numbers then fell short. As a result, the WEC's debt rose to around 2,8 million euros, an amount the centre cannot simply pay itself. Revenue from entrance fees and other sources is roughly equal to the costs incurred. Valuable: The future of the centre is therefore uncertain. Last night the municipal council of Het Hogeland discussed the matter publicly for the first time. D66 submitted a motion rejecting extra financial support for the centre. Only Pro voted against, a party that wants the executive to "make maximum efforts to keep the WEC". For that, the centre would have to come up with a new course and a sound plan, and cooperate better with entrepreneurs in the port. Still, that financial support is not coming after all. Most parties are convinced that the seal care is of great value to the region, RTV Noord reported, but believe the WEC should save itself financially. A majority of the council also sees no way to co-finance because of strict rules on state aid and the exceeded construction costs. Het Hogeland does still support the WEC in other ways. The municipality stands as guarantor for a loan of 9 million euros that the WEC has taken out with <entity id="org:zbo-de-nederlandsche-bank">De Nederlandsche Bank</entity>. The municipality also spent a total of around 340.000 euros on advisory costs for the centre's financial and legal matters. This concerns, for example, state aid analyses, financial advice and a marketing strategy. Donors: About ten WEC employees attended the council meeting. They handed the petition 'Red het Zeehondencentrum WEC' to mayor <entity id="person:hans-broekhuizen">Hans Broekhuizen</entity>. It had been signed more than one hundred thousand times. That there is broad support for keeping the seal centre was also shown by a fundraising campaign. According to the organisation, more than 1,25 million euros in donations have already come in to save the almost bankrupt WEC. These range from amounts starting at 5 euros to, for example, a gift of 40.000 euros. Bankruptcy application: This gave the centre's supervisory board reason to postpone the bankruptcy application by one week last week. The financial support gave new opportunities to keep the centre open after all. That week ends tomorrow: by then WEC will decide at the latest whether to apply for bankruptcy.

title: Call of Duty maker under fire in South Korea for using Seoul disaster footage
lead: In South Korea there has been outrage over a clip in the shooting game Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 . It shows footage that appears to come from the deadly Halloween disaster in Seoul in 2022, four years ago today. Survivors of the disaster want the footage removed. The short clips show someone being resuscitated. Rows of bodies lying on the road are also shown, as well as a victim being carried away on a stretcher. The footage, lasting a few seconds, was used for the opening scene of the latest edition of the popular shooter. At the Seoul disaster, party-goers were crushed and trampled in the narrow streets of the nightlife district Itaewon. The crowd was completely trapped in the extreme crush. 158 people died. Later, two more fatalities were added to the total because authorities directly linked their deaths to the disaster. Footage of the crowd: Ahead of Halloween it was already clear that it would be busy that year. After two pandemic years, partygoers were looking forward to going to Itaewon without corona restrictions, where Halloween is celebrated on a grand scale every year. As the evening went on, the mood turned and people got trapped, with all the consequences that entailed. "We are shocked that the chaotic and desperate scenes, in which countless citizens performed resuscitation to save each other and victims lay on the cold street, have been used in exactly this way to create a scene in a game," said the survivors and various citizens' groups in a joint statement, in which they demand that the footage be removed. The survivors say people who took part in the rescue effort or witnessed the disaster still suffer from trauma. Comparisons: Activision Blizzard, the publisher of the game, did not deny to Korean news agency Yonhap that real news footage was used. The company says "part of the actual news footage included in the game's opening scene was used to convey the fictional story in the game". "It was absolutely not our intention to name or trivialise tragic events, including the tragedy in Itaewon," said the company. Gamers in South Korea recognised the clips after the game's release. Korean broadcasters have compared them with footage made on the evening of the mass crush. Especially the resuscitation attempt on someone lying on the ground is recognised as news footage of the tragedy. North Korean invasion: In Modern Warfare 4 you follow a South Korean marine who fights a North Korean invasion on Korean streets. Before the release, the game had already become a political topic in South Korea. Conservative politicians urged President Lee to play the game to better understand the threat they believe emanates from Pyongyang. The South Korean president is pursuing a more conciliatory attitude towards North Korea. Reducing tensions with North Korea was an election promise of Lee.

title: War in Middle East again leads to billions in profit at Shell
lead: Shell's profit rose sharply again last quarter. The oil and gas company made 12.1 billion dollars in profit at the bottom line. Shell itself adjusts for higher oil prices and keeps 10.8 billion in net profit. In the same period last year it was 5.4 billion. The company posted revenue of nearly 93 billion dollars. The good results are mainly due to the ongoing war in the Middle East. Several refineries there have been attacked, which process crude oil into petrol and diesel, among other things. These now produce less, and because fewer products are coming onto the market, purchasing becomes more expensive. Companies like Shell, which sell products such as oil, benefit from this. Revenue from liquefied gas has also increased, the quarterly figures show. The European gas price has now passed 100 euros per megawatt hour, the level of the crisis in 2022. That was when Russia invaded Ukraine. More dividend for shareholders. Prices are also rising because the Strait of Hormuz was completely blocked for a long time. Dozens of tankers are passing through again each day, but not yet as many as before the war in the Middle East. Shareholders of the company are benefiting from the high profits. Shell is going to pay out more money per share, the so-called dividend. Appeal: Do you have a dynamic energy contract or have you recently signed a fixed energy contract? And would you like to take part in a TV and radio report? Then we would be glad to get in touch with you. Send an email to economie@nos.nl and we will contact you. From politics, there was an earlier attempt to tax the high profits of oil and gas companies extra. In spring a majority of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> agreed to a motion on this from Pro and D66. But partly because Shell is no longer a Dutch company, imposing such an extra tax is very difficult. It is still being examined at European level whether there are possibilities.

title: Dramatic quarterly figures for Volkswagen: billions in the red
lead: Volkswagen's problems are far from solved. The German carmaker posted a loss of as much as 5.8 billion euros last quarter, according to the latest figures. In the same period last year it also recorded red figures, nearly 1.1 billion euros. Revenue also fell by 6.3 percent to around 75.3 billion euros. The poor performance in July, August and September is partly due to the prolonged crisis at luxury brand Porsche, part of the Volkswagen Group. Porsche has written off more than 6 billion euros because it expects to make less profit in the coming period. The luxury brand sold far fewer cars in China due to fierce competition from Chinese brands, which have been rising in recent years. In addition, Porsche is also hit by the American import duties on aluminium and steel. Under pressure in China. Not only Porsche is facing these problems; the Volkswagen brand itself has also sold fewer cars worldwide. From July through September, the manufacturer from Wolfsburg delivered nearly 1.9 million vehicles, more than 14 percent fewer than a year earlier. In China in particular, sales fell by 38.5 percent in that period. The entire Volkswagen group, with all brands included and the largest carmaker in Europe, delivered 9 percent fewer cars compared with the same period last year. The deep red quarterly figures are the latest blow for Volkswagen. Last month the group already announced it would cut another 50,000 jobs in the coming years, on top of the 50,000 previously announced. For the problems Volkswagen faces, you can read this article from September: Volkswagen CEO Blume also previously announced changes at four German factories. In Emden, Zwickau, Hannover and Neckarsulm no new models will be built, unless costs can be brought down there. These factories may in future be used for the defence sector.

title: Hackers put data on 41,000 employees of the US Department of Homeland Security online
lead: Activist hackers have put online the data of over 41,000 employees of the American Department of Homeland Security. It concerns names, phone numbers, email addresses and other data of the staff of services such as <entity id="org:douane">douane</entity> and the immigration police ICE, including employees in sensitive positions. "They have our data, so it is only fair that we have theirs", reasons a spokesperson for the activist website Distributed Denial of Secrets, which published the data in a searchable database. The aim is to "replace anonymity with accountability", says co-founder Emma Best of the site. She thinks that a great many official requests for the disclosure of documents can be made with the data. Because the data also includes job descriptions and email groups, the hacker group says it is possible to trace the internal structure of departments within the ministry. "This makes clear who the architects and driving forces behind the policy and its implementation are", Best said. For security reasons, the government provides little information about this. Under fire The Department of Homeland Security was set up in the aftermath of the 9/11 attacks to combat the fragmentation of national security. Various security services, for example for immigration, aviation security and internet security, fall under it. Under President Trump, mainly the immigration police ICE made the news, because of a very active deportation policy and violence when arresting immigrants and protesters. The service was criticised because agents are not in uniform, do not wear identification and are sometimes masked, which according to human rights organisations makes it difficult to hold them accountable. Distributed Denial of Secrets says that by leaking the data it aims to make more oversight and transparency possible. Critics fear that employees will be put at risk as a result: criminals also have access to the data. Agents and their families have been threatened more often in the past. Not informed It is not entirely clear how the hackers obtained the staff data. They themselves say they found a leak in the login system of the Department of Homeland Security. The company behind it denies that security is not in order. A spokesperson for the ministry itself says it is aware of the reports about the hack and says that an investigation is under way. Meanwhile, according to the spokesperson, the department is doing everything it can to guarantee the safety of employees. In connection with the leak, Distributed Denial of Secrets did stress that the data may be incomplete and partly incorrect. Even so, American media were able to contact various employees using data from the database. Some turned out not yet to have been aware that their personal details had been leaked. Third major leak in a short time This is the third time in a short period that the American government has faced a major data leak. In September, the hacker group ShinyHunters reported having an enormous amount of files on FBI employees. That was a retaliation for the FBI's call never to pay extortionists. Shortly afterwards, a suspect was arrested in the Netherlands. Later that month it emerged that someone had had access to the personnel records of the Pentagon for months. Millions of data records of American military personnel were taken in the process.

title: Tensions between the Koreas rise, more and more countries involved
lead: North Korea has fired about ten ballistic missiles toward the Sea of Japan, according to the South Korean military. These launches do not stand alone. Tensions on the Korean peninsula have been rising for months. Pyongyang is modernising its armed forces at a rapid pace and increasingly seeks confrontation with South Korea. Military cooperation with Russia also appears to be giving the country more confidence and new technological knowledge. Earlier this month, North Korea tested several ballistic missiles. According to the country itself, the missiles were part of a hypersonic weapons system, missiles that fly far faster than the speed of sound. Whether this is true cannot be verified. Concerns among experts are growing, however. They warn that North Korea's tests are no longer just shows of force, and that the hypersonic weapons system may well be in the final phase of development. A few days later, South Korea tested its own hypersonic weapon for the first time. South Korean President Lee Jae-myung was present at the launch. According to local media, Lee wanted to give North Korea a warning with his presence. Notable, because until recently Lee seemed to do everything to reduce tensions with North Korea. North Korea responded to this launch again with the launch of missiles. Landmines The missile violence does not stop there. Tension is also rising at the border. Last month three South Korean soldiers were wounded in landmine explosions at the border with North Korea. The soldiers were there to clear a new route for an inspection of possibly illegally placed landmines. The border area between South and North Korea is littered with landmines. A large part of them were placed during and in the years after the Korean War (1950-1953). For a number of years North Korea has been arming the area at a rapid pace. It is estimated that since 2024 the country has laid nearly a million mines, including mines on the South Korean side of the border. Joint research by the South Korean military and the UN Command in Korea shows that the exploded landmine is of North Korean make. Whether the mine was deliberately placed on the South Korean side is unclear. According to experts, the mine may well have ended up on the south side, for example through landslides. Furthermore, because markings are deficient in some places, it is difficult to determine exactly where the border lies. After the incident South Korea immediately demanded apologies and an end to North Korean border fortifications. North Korea denies any involvement, but is not backing down either. In recent months North Korea has begun reinforcing its border with weapons, additional barbed wire barriers and fences. Kim Yo-jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, also reported last week that loudspeakers are ready along the entire border for psychological warfare. A major step back, after the loudspeakers on both sides of the border had been removed this year precisely to reduce tensions. Russia The military confidence of North Korea appears to have taken off since the expansion of military cooperation with Russia. While North Korea supplies soldiers and weapons to fight on the Russian side at the front in Ukraine, it gains combat experience and weapons knowledge. Especially in drone technology North Korea appears to be making big strides. Pyongyang seems to have learned from the war in Ukraine that cheap drones can overwhelm expensive air defence systems. Photos of Kim Jong-un's visit to a drone factory last month indicate that North Korea has begun mass production of drones. In addition, Russia has sent officers to North Korea to train drone operators there, according to NKnews, a news organisation devoted exclusively to North Korea. Combined testing has also begun. During a North Korean military exercise last month, a swarm of drones attacked an island target while cruise missiles and ballistic missiles struck simultaneously from different directions. If North Korea succeeds in producing large quantities of drones, that will have major consequences for the air defence of South Korea and the American troops stationed there. South Korea's response to the rapid drone development still lags behind. The country's drone division is currently undergoing a reorganisation and is subject to budget cuts. However, the defence minister announced last year that he wants to train half a million 'dronewarriors'.

title: Flevoland invests millions in new harbour near Urk, 'up to 750 jobs added'
lead: Twelve years after the first plans were put on the table, the decision has now been made: a service harbour is to be built outside the dike near Urk. The project is meant to considerably strengthen shipbuilding and the maritime sector in Urk and the <entity id="org:gemeente-noordoostpolder">Noordoostpolder</entity> in the coming decades. The province of Flevoland will invest tens of millions of euros in it. A majority of the Provincial States has agreed to that college proposal. According to the college, existing maritime companies can keep growing thanks to the project, and there will be more room for new economic activities. The harbour is to create 550 to 750 jobs. To realise the harbour, the province will have to borrow quite a lot of money. The exact amount has been declared secret. What is known: the project will be profitable after 45 years and all loans and investments will be repaid after 73 years, Omroep Flevoland reports. This happens thanks to entrepreneurs from Urk and the Noordoostpolder who commit to the project for the long term. They are willing to pay the province annual ground lease fees over the coming decades, with which the loans will ultimately be repaid. Risk versus nerve. A too-large financial risk, opponents said, including Pro, the Party for the Animals and also coalition party VVD. They argue that it takes far too long before the investment is earned back. "We have always been in favour of developing the harbour and we still are," said VVD parliamentary group leader Francho Achtien. But the current proposal, in his view, saddles the province with too heavy burdens. "Paying back the loans takes a lifetime." Moreover, the province cannot spend the borrowed money that is tied up for the harbour in those years on anything else. "We have a big problem with bus transport," says Kjell van de Wijlandt of the Party for the Animals. "With this money we can pay for that." BBB parliamentary group leader Andrea van Veen instead pointed to the nerve this project shows. "You are not only voting for the harbour, but also on whether you have a vision for Flevoland. The harbour will contribute to the growth of the province." According to the ChristenUnie, the maritime sector is "booming," said parliamentary group leader Ria Visser-Kapitein. "We need to provide room for this. We urgently need the employment and entrepreneurship." Ground lease. Entrepreneurs from Urk and the Noordoostpolder seem to have confidence in it, at least. According to entrepreneur and harbour initiator Henk Kapitein, eleven companies want to take part and fifteen more are on the waiting list. The proposed investment credit for the harbour was already raised several times due to higher costs for energy, building materials and personnel. Several factions asked whether that amount will not rise even further in the coming time than foreseen. The college will therefore inform the States every six months about the harbour's progress, it was decided last night. Ready in 5 years. Soon the province will start a European tendering procedure to find a contractor. According to executive member Sjaak Simonse, that procedure takes about nine months. Construction of the harbour must start in 2028 and be finished in 2031. The service harbour is intended, among other things, for shipbuilding, ship maintenance, maritime services and sustainability.

title: Anoma van der Veere new NOS correspondent for Southeast Asia
lead: Anoma van der Veere will become the new Southeast Asia correspondent for the NOS. He replaces Mustafa Marghadi, who after five years is leaving his correspondent post in Jakarta. For the NOS, Van der Veere was already correspondent in Japan. He will keep that region under his remit and so expands his area to include Southeast Asia. In time he will move from Tokyo to the Thai capital Bangkok. Van der Veere is looking forward to his new region. "It is an area full of contrasts, where the great stories of our time are unfolding: the power struggle between China and the United States, the pressure on democracy and the consequences of climate change." Connection with Thailand. We all feel that in the Netherlands too, he says. "Through the things in our homes and the trade routes we depend on, our prosperity and security are directly connected to Southeast Asia. I look forward to making those connections visible, through the stories of the people who live there." Because of his Thai background he also has a personal bond with the area. The 37-year-old Van der Veere has now lived in Japan for eight years. He has worked for the NOS since 2021. He is also a researcher and lecturer at the Leiden Asia Centre and University College in Maastricht. He previously also taught at educational institutions in Japan.

title: Nature targets for peat areas not met, 'environment too fragmented'
lead: The hundreds of millions invested in peat areas have not yet led to the nature targets being met there. That is the conclusion of the <entity id="org:algemene-rekenkamer">Rekenkamer</entity> in the report Nature policy for peat: a bog? The researchers looked at the 173 peat areas spread across the Netherlands, wet nature areas with a soil type made up of plant remains. Not only do many animals and plants that occur nowhere else live there, the peat also helps hold tons of CO2 in the soil. Because of this importance, <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> has released two billion euros between 2021 and 2030 to strengthen the areas. According to the Rekenkamer, this currently succeeds sufficiently in only 18 of the 173 cases. The Netherlands Court of Audit examines whether government spending is lawful and effective. 'Administrative bog' Peat areas are threatened by drying out, nitrogen, invasive exotic species and deteriorating water quality. To counter all of that, improvements in the areas themselves are not enough on their own; buffer zones must also be built around them. That is where it goes wrong, according to the Rekenkamer. In the peat areas the provinces have the say, but in the buffer zones a web of authorities holds control, from municipalities and water boards to the national government and private parties. The direction there is often unclear, and dependence on others leads to long, sluggish processes, "a bog of administrative decision-making". Conflicting interests are often at play around the peat, the Rekenkamer observes. For example, farmers want to be able to use pesticides and keep the water level low, while that is bad for the peat. Recreation, new housing and road building also put pressure on and fragment the areas. The Rekenkamer believes that <entity id="person:jaimi-van-essen">minister Van Essen</entity> of Nature (D66) "plays only a limited role". He can push policy through, but according to the report he does too little of it. "If the minister does not do this, the targets for peat areas but also for other nature areas are in danger," the Rekenkamer warns. 'Delay is decline' The ministry of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-landbouw-visserij-voedselzekerheid-en-natuur">Landbouw, Visserij, Voedselzekerheid en Natuur</entity> states in a response that the monitoring and steering of nature policy is organised decentrally and lies primarily with the provinces. It also sees the need to gain more direction on the file. It is discussing this with the provinces, among others. "The findings show that we cannot wait with nature restoration. Delay is decline, and we must move forward."

title: Booing at Berlin opera: Wagner adaptation about Israel divides audience
lead: An adaptation of the well-known Wagner opera The Flying Dutchman stirs up a lot in Germany. At the Deutsche Oper in Berlin, the redemption story of a wandering captain is linked to the German approach to Israel and guilt for the Holocaust. A bold choice, which for many goes too far or is inappropriate. The premiere was accompanied by booing, and outside there was police protection. With one exception, the German reviews were devastating. Ranging from " disastrous " to "failure". "Wagner as Hamas would like to see him", headlined the Austrian newspaper Die Presse . "Both Wagner and the historical facts are being slaughtered", according to the Jüdische Allgemeine. At the second performance last night, booing was heard again. After the intermission a considerable part of the audience did not return. When the Palestinian suffering was touched upon, both cheering and jeering could be heard, an atypical setting for an opera. Clinging to guilt: The original story of Der Fliegende Holländer from 1843 is about a captain who wanders at sea and may go ashore once every seven years. If he then meets a woman who swears loyalty to him, his curse is broken. In this interpretation the ship must represent Germany, which carries the historical guilt of the Holocaust on its shoulders. Israel embodies the rescuer Senta, Palestine her discarded love Erik. The singing parts alternate with images of Israel, historical information and staged scenes of German-Israeli history. With this adaptation the director, the Swiss Milo Rau, wants to spark a discussion in Germany about how to deal with Israel. By clinging to the feeling of guilt about the past, the country would be unable to see what is happening in Gaza. Criticism of Israel is very sensitive in Germany. Artists and media makers therefore mostly stay away from the theme, out of fear of accusations of antisemitism or of losing subsidies. Artists and artistic directors state that they can no longer perform their work freely. The UN rapporteur for freedom of expression recently criticized Germany this summer. The room for criticism of Israel is too small and is criminalized, was the conclusion. It has led to self-censorship in the arts, said opera director Rau in an interview. He deplores that "in the perpetrator countries Germany and Austria it is chosen to remain silent" about the situation in Gaza. With this opera Rau wants to do what art should do: push boundaries. Provocative it certainly was, as audience reactions showed. "This cannot be", was heard when 'stop with your guilt' was projected on a screen. Wrong end of the stick: "In Germany people dare to do more with opera than in the Netherlands, including political staging", says opera expert Hein van Eekert of NPO Klassiek and the German counterpart WDR3. But in this case he thinks Rau wanted to put too much into the opera. Rau chose to perform Wagner in Israel. That counts as a taboo, because of the composer's antisemitic views. Images of this appear during the opera. "It goes beyond a reinterpretation, it is almost a different story. That will have hit the average opera-goer the wrong way", continues Van Eekert. That may explain the booing: "It does not necessarily have to be political, the opera-goer simply wants to see his opera." Rau clearly wants to provoke the opera lover. "Art is confrontation", he said. "It has to explode in your face. That is why I do it." At the end of the performance the German spectator is called upon to take 'responsibility'. What that exactly means remains unclear. When the curtain fell last night, visitors left the hall while still discussing. The opera stirs the tongues, that much is clear.

title: Fear and anger reign in Spain, day after another major train disaster
lead: A day after the serious train accident in Spain, anger and fear prevail among residents. It was the third fatal accident this year, and Spaniards are asking themselves: how could this happen again? Yesterday morning a high-speed train collided at full speed with a stationary train near the village of Urda, about 140 kilometres south of Madrid. At least 69 people died and dozens were injured. Spanish Minister of Transport Óscar Puente attributed the accident yesterday to human error. Yet further analysis shows that the accident cannot be attributed to that alone. Several system failures also occurred before the accident. Increase in accidents Some Spaniards are now asking whether they can still travel safely by train. The number of serious accidents on the Spanish railways has indeed increased over the past ten years, with the most fatal accidents in recent history in the past four years, according to reports from the Railway Safety Agency. In 2025 there were 69 serious accidents. This year, two fatal accidents together killed more than a hundred people. Besides yesterday's accident, 46 people died in January. Then a high-speed train derailed near Córdoba. The train ended up on the adjacent track and collided with another high-speed train. The derailment was probably caused by an already existing break in the rails. Concerns for longer The concerns about the state of the Spanish railways have existed for longer: in 2025 the train drivers' union Semaf already urgently asked the government to revise the maintenance protocol, the union chairman told broadcaster RTVE. Semaf reportedly proposed lowering the maximum speed and carrying out more preventive maintenance. With nearly 4,000 kilometres of track for high-speed trains, Spain has, after China, the most kilometres in the world. And the railway is heavily used: in 2025, 44.5 million passengers used the high-speed network. Figures from the European Commission show, however, that between 2018 and 2022 Spain spent only 16 percent of its total rail spending on maintaining existing systems. France and Germany spend about a third of their total spending on maintenance, renewal and improvement of existing lines. The Madrid-Seville line, where both accidents occurred, uses an outdated system. A replacement had been planned for the first quarter of next year, a source tells the newspaper El País. Union strike After the fatal accident in January, Semaf announced a three-day strike for more safety on the railways. On the first day the union already reached an agreement with the government: 1.8 billion euros would be invested in maintenance. Today the train drivers are striking again over the structural improvement of railway safety. The strike was already planned, but has become extra urgent because of this accident, the union said. The union does call on people to "remain cautious" about speculation on the cause of the accident until more details are made public. The other rail union, CSIF, wants transport minister Puente to "take his responsibility" and resign. Puente attributed the accident to human error by an employee. The union calls that "inappropriate", and according to CSIF the employee is being used as a "scapegoat". "The minister has evaded all responsibility, despite the initial malfunction in the computer system that set the events in motion", CSIF writes. Political campaign kicks off With 31 days to go until the Spanish elections on 29 November, it is also immediately clear that politicians are seizing on the railway problems for their campaigns. Several candidates appeared near the accident to express their support: the anger Spain feels already echoed in their speeches yesterday. Thus far-right leader Santiago Abascal called transport minister Puente the "minister of death". "This government has truly destroyed everything, including the infrastructure", he added. Alberto Núñez Feijóo, prime ministerial candidate for the largest opposition party, said residents have "the right" to know the "state of the railways and safety systems, what warnings were received, what measures were taken and what actions were undertaken". Prime Minister Sánchez promised an investigation and improvements to the railways. The king and queen are visiting the injured in hospital in Toledo today. At the site of the accident, searches for victims are still ongoing, but the authorities do not expect any more bodies to be under the rubble.

title: Paris attacker admits racist and Islamophobic motive: 'No regret'
lead: The suspect in last week's terrorist attack in the Paris suburb of Trappes has admitted he had a racist and Islamophobic motive. Kevin T. says he chose Trappes because it would be a "haven for Islamists". He says he has no regret. "He admits that he specifically targeted "Muslims and people of African or North African origin", the public prosecutor announced today. T. reportedly also admitted during his interrogation that he had prepared the attack. The 39-year-old opened fire from his car with a machine gun on passersby last Friday morning. In about twenty minutes he first made victims in Trappes and then a little further on also in La Verrière, after which he was rammed around 10:20 and arrested in the town of Coignières. He reportedly fired 128 bullets, Le Monde writes. During the arrest, police found the machine gun, tear gas grenades and gloves in his car. The attack was almost immediately described by President Macron as a terrorist act with a possible racist motive. 'No regret' In the attack the 26-year-old Pengo Bossio Wangi was killed. Seven other people were also injured, including an 11-year-old girl. The child was hit eight times. In his confession T. reportedly denied that he wanted to hit children. The suspect says he may have "misjudged her body size", but stresses that he has no regret. The girl was wearing a headscarf when she was shot. "Maybe that is why he attacked her", her mother said earlier. "She is a child born in France, in Trappes. She has the right to build her life here." Hiding behind a car The girl's parents tell RTL that she is now doing better. Last Wednesday a silent march was held for the victims of the attack, during which her mother gave a speech. "Do you want to know where they found my child's body? I will show you. She ran to a car to take cover there, and that saved her", the mother said in an emotional speech. "That little girl absolutely did not deserve this." Three of the injured are still in hospital, one of them still in critical condition. Terrorism During a house search the authorities found, among other things, weapons and ammunition, the prosecutor said. Books were also found in his house, including a Quran, a Bible and a copy of Hitler's Mein Kampf. From the preliminary investigation it appears that T. had already started preparing his attack on 3 September. Among other things he bought parts for a machine gun and reportedly paid off his debts. He also reportedly deleted his social media a few days before the attack, sold his laptop and hid his phone. The last two were found and seized last Tuesday and still need to be analysed. The attack is being investigated by the authorities, among other things, as a terrorist act under paragraph 1 of Article 421-1 of the criminal code, the prosecutor said. The suspect denies having terrorist intent, but regards his act as "lawful".

title: 2 years in prison for severe assault on Haarlemmer (17) in Beverwijk
lead: Two men from <entity id="org:gemeente-heemskerk">Heemskerk</entity> and Beverwijk have been convicted of the severe assault of a 17-year-old boy from <entity id="org:gemeente-haarlem">Haarlem</entity>. They were sentenced to two years in prison. A third suspect was acquitted. The three suspects, aged 22, 24 and 25, stood trial for attempted manslaughter and robbery with violence. The court found the first charge proven for two of them. Fouad B. (24) and Adam E. B. (22) were each sentenced to two years in prison, six months of which are suspended. They must also pay damages of over 41,000 euros and are subject to a no-contact order with the victim. Inadmissible The third suspect, the 25-year-old Mourad L., denied using violence during the assault. Nevertheless, he can be seen in footage of the incident, together with a fourth suspect. That suspect is said to have filmed the incident and pulled down the victim's trousers. But this suspect was not prosecuted. Therefore the court declares the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> (OM) inadmissible for the third suspect. A judge can decide this if the OM has not met formal requirements, or if the investigation and prosecution were not carried out properly, writes NH . The trio was not present at the verdict. Social media The assault took place on 6 September last year. The violence probably arose from a quarrel between two rival groups of youths from Heemskerk and Beverwijk, and Haarlem. On that day the victim had eaten with friends in Beverwijk, and when he left the restaurant he was asked by a group of boys where he was from. As soon as it became clear the answer was Haarlem, he was surrounded by about twenty boys with machetes and baseball bats, according to the victim statement. Footage shown in court shows the victim being stripped, beaten and kicked several times in the head, including when he was unconscious. He broke his hand, got bumps on his head and temple, and had to abandon his studies. The assault was filmed and the footage spread on social media. It caused great unrest in the region. Several secondary schools in Beverwijk and Heemskerk closed their doors for a day, and sports clubs stayed closed. Mayors took emergency measures, and the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> was allowed to carry out preventive searches in certain places.

title: No AI for children in primary school, says House of Representatives
lead: The use of generative AI in the classroom should be banned for children in primary school. A majority in the House of Representatives supports a proposal on this from Volt and the CDA. "We must not make the same mistake as when social media were embraced uncritically", says <entity id="person:laurens-antonius-josephus-maria-dassen">Kamerlid Dassen</entity> of Volt. CDA MP Armut: "As far as we are concerned, generative AI adds nothing for primary school pupils." Generative AI is artificial intelligence that, based on instructions, is itself capable of generating text, audio, video or images, such as ChatGPT, Claude and Copilot. According to the parties, young pupils in primary education develop to a large extent "their critical thinking, creativity and imagination". The use of generative AI poses a risk to this, they think. Critical thinking Children must first learn well to read, write and think critically, including about AI, before they start working with AI themselves, Dassen believes. "I believe in the opportunities AI offers us, but at the same time generative AI increases learning gaps. We need to act on that now." As far as the CDA is concerned, learning from books remains the foundation. For children, digital literacy is also important, says MP Armut, but AI must then be used purely to support learning. The parties that want a ban are Volt, CDA, Pro, D66, PvdD, Denk, SP, 50plus, ChristenUnie and JA21. Together they hold 88 of the 150 seats. <entity id="person:judith-tielen">Staatssecretaris Tielen</entity> understands the concerns of the House of Representatives, but she is not in favour of banning AI for primary school pupils right now. She is working on a plan on digitalisation in education and says she wants to be careful. "I simply need a bit more time for that." Too little learning about AI The PO-raad, the sector association for primary education, welcomes the proposal. "Initial research shows that learning yield declines when pupils make frequent use of generative AI, so we understand the concerns politicians have about the use of generative AI in education. Above all, it is extremely important that pupils learn how to analyse a source and that they can think critically themselves." "At the same time, a possible total ban for primary education comes out of the blue. We are open to making good agreements about this with the ministry and experts, because it is clear that something needs to be done", the PO-raad adds. Educationalist and group 8 teacher Barend Last understands the concerns among politicians. "I can follow the reasoning that children should not have unrestricted access to generative AI systems." Even so, he fears that such a ban would cause children to learn too little about AI and then miss valuable lessons about preparing for society. "The core objectives state that pupils must learn to use AI responsibly. So you should not ban all use of generative AI", he says. According to him, there are plenty of examples of it being used in an educational way. Barend Last fears that the House of Representatives will formulate a statutory ban too broadly. "Educational chatbots can for example be instructed not to give the answers but, for instance, to think along with the pupil according to didactic principles. Educational publishers are also experimenting with AI chatbots."

title: Polls: coalition loses dozens of seats, a year after elections
lead: Exactly one year after the last elections for <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>, the coalition parties are facing sharp losses in voter favour. In the most recent Peilingwijzer, D66 of <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity>, which won the most votes at the elections a year ago, now stands at 13 to 17 seats in the House of Representatives. That is 11 fewer than it currently holds in the House. The VVD keeps 14 to 18 seats in this weighted average of the polls by Ipsos I&O and Verian/EenVandaag, a loss of 6. Meanwhile the CDA also falls by 4, to 12 to 16. As a result the minority coalition is around 45 seats, less than a third of the seats in the House. By far the largest party in the Peilingwijzer remains opposition party PRO, at 25 to 31 seats. The party of Jesse Klaver still reaps, according to research by Ipsos I&O and Verian/EenVandaag, the fruits of the discontent of many progressive voters over the 'right-wing' government policy that D66 signed up for. Lowest rating for Yesilgöz: Mirror image, the VVD is reproached by its voters from last year for having moved too far to the left. According to Verian/EenVandaag there is an important difference between the situation at D66 and at the VVD: whereas confidence in Jetten among his base is still fairly high, only 28 percent of VVD voters think leader Dilan Yesilgöz should again be lead candidate at the next elections. Ipsos I&O sees the same. Yesilgöz, who recently said he wanted to remain leader through the next elections, receives the lowest rating from voters of the main political leaders. Expressed as a grade, it is a 3.7. No more than 8 percent of VVD voters say they vote VVD because of the leader. PVV also loses: Notably, it is not the PVV that benefits from the further diminished appeal of the VVD. The party of <entity id="person:geert-wilders">Geert Wilders</entity> is also down, at 18 to 23 seats. Switchers from VVD and PVV mainly cause JA21 (15-19) and Forum voor Democratie (10-14) to grow. Ipsos I&O sees in the underlying research great volatility among voters. On the one hand, the coalition parties are held against them for failing to achieve enough, and many people are therefore looking elsewhere at the moment. On the other hand, about three quarters of opposition voters think their party must hold firmly to its own principles, "even if <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> fails to get the budget done". Those budget talks with the opposition are being held these days. BBB nearly disappears: Among the smaller parties, three stand at 4 to 6 seats in the Peilingwijzer: 50Plus, the Partij voor de Dieren and the SP. Roughly the same size is the ChristenUnie, with 3 to 5, followed by the SGP and Volt with 2 to 4 and Denk with 1 to 3. Of BBB little remains in the current Peilingwijzer, at 0 to 2. Maurice de Hond. Political scientist Tom Louwerse, the maker of the Peilingwijzer, stresses that seat polls outside election time have little predictive value for the next result, according to available research. "On the other hand, parties do respond to them. You saw that recently, for example, when the poll by Maurice de Hond, which is not included in the Peilingwijzer, came out at 12 seats for the VVD. That led to many newspaper pieces and critical questions at party meetings." "Another effect," said Louwerse, "is that it puts more pressure on these parties to bring concrete matters into negotiations in which their own profile stands out well. Compromises then become even harder. That makes budget negotiations like those currently being held not easy." About the Peilingwijzer: De NOS regularly publishes the Peilingwijzer, which combines seat polls by Ipsos I&O and Verian/EenVandaag. More about the method behind it can be found on the website of its maker, political scientist Tom Louwerse of Leiden University.

title: Vulnerable Afghan farmers are producing more opium again, despite Taliban ban
lead: Farmers in Afghanistan are producing significantly more opium again, despite a ban on the lucrative drug cultivation that the Taliban introduced four years ago. That is what the United Nations (UN) reports. The figures show the vulnerability of Afghan farmers, who can barely make ends meet due to the struggling economy. Within a year, the area used for Afghan opium production has nearly quadrupled to about 43,000 hectares. That is still significantly less than before the ban in 2022. In that year, 200,000 hectares were used for poppy cultivation. Poppy is used to produce drugs such as opium and heroin. Although production has certainly not returned to the level from before the cultivation ban, farmers can, due to the persistent demand from Europe among others, earn considerably more from a kilogram of dried opium. Before the ban, a kilo brought in about 100 dollars; today it quickly amounts to more than 500 dollars, the UN states. Secret cultivation Farmers try to keep their production as far under the radar as possible. In large grain fields, only small patches of land are used to grow poppies. Other production sites are surrounded by walls. This shows the desperation among Afghan farmers. It is strictly forbidden for them to make opium. The Taliban crack down hard on production, because according to the rulers it does not fit their strict Islamic doctrine and because the regime strives for international recognition. A few years ago the Taliban took a very different stance on this; the group earned significant income from exporting opium during their war with the US and NATO. Opium export intact Despite the dangers, farmers turn to opium production because it is more profitable than other forms of agriculture, but also because the illegal export routes are still largely intact. This does not apply to the export of legal products, such as grain, cotton and watermelons. For some time there has been unrest along the border between Afghanistan and Pakistan, due to an armed conflict between those countries. The Taliban say that the estimated increase in opium production is greatly overestimated by the UN. According to the Afghan rulers, the actual cultivation in 2026 is twice as low as the estimate by UN agency UNODC. What they base this on is unclear.

title: Public Prosecution Service drops case against trainee officer over fatal 2023 arrest
lead: The <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> is dropping the case against an officer over a fatal arrest in 2023 in Rotterdam. On 9 June of that year a 32-year-old Rotterdam man died when officers were holding him under control. Research reportedly showed that the officers involved violated the use-of-force instructions applicable to them, which caused the suspect to die . The OM now reports that an eighth officer, who had previously been named as one of the suspects, was still in training. He followed instructions from colleagues with a higher rank. After investigation by the national investigation service, the OM concludes that he did not take action on his own initiative that contributed to the man's death. The case against the other seven officers will be heard in January and February 2027 in a special court in Utrecht. That court handles cases against investigating officers. Never before in the Netherlands have so many officers had to appear before the judge at the same time. Traffic incident In February 2024 the Public Prosecution Service announced that it would prosecute eight officers for their involvement in the death of the arrestee. On 9 June 2023 two officers responded to a report about a traffic incident. The arrestee reportedly had collided with a car on his bicycle and kept going. The man was chased by the officers, first in a police van and later on foot, the Public Prosecution Service writes. The suspect did not follow the officers' instructions, after which he was tasered. More officers arrived to assist. Because the man kept resisting, several officers held him face down. The man became unwell and was resuscitated. He eventually died in hospital. A few months later suspicion arose that the way the man had been restrained may have played a role in his death. Alfredo Goeloe The case of the 32-year-old victim recalls the arrest of 51-year-old Rotterdam resident Alfredo Goeloe . He was checked by officers last 12 September after a report about a stolen fatbike. When Goeloe could not show proof of identity, he ran away. Afterwards it turned out he had drugs on him. After a chase, officers finally detained him. While officers held him down on the ground, he lost consciousness. Footage of the arrest captures Goeloe calling for help and saying he had diabetes. Resuscitation was unsuccessful and he died. Editor's note An earlier version of this article framed the story as the OM prosecuting the seven officers. That had been known for some time and is therefore not the news. The article has been rewritten.

title: Thousands of THC candies seized, destined for the Netherlands
lead: French customs intercepted thousands of packages of THC candies intended for the Dutch market. THC is the main active substance in marijuana. According to the European anti-fraud office OLAF, the candies and packaging closely resembled products of a well-known European brand. This infringed trademark rights, but OLAF also warns that children could easily confuse the THC candies with ordinary sweets. And that can be dangerous. The anti-fraud office also warns that such food products do not comply with European rules. Due to the packaging, users get the impression that it is a normal and safe product. In total, 3560 packages were seized and destroyed. They had been sent from the United States and were to be forwarded to the Netherlands. Children ill The office also has websites and shops on its radar that sell such candy. Incidentally, all of them are in France. According to OLAF, the authorities there are taking appropriate measures. There are regular incidents with THC candies. This summer, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> in Utrecht already warned about unsafe candies that had made children ill. They had found the candy in a schoolyard. Last year, Haribo candies were recalled by the <entity id="org:nederlandse-voedsel-en-warenautoriteit">NVWA</entity> after THC was found in them. Several people had become unwell. One child had even fallen into a coma. But it later turned out that the recalled candy did not contain any THC after all, the <entity id="org:nederlands-forensisch-instituut">Nederlands Forensisch Instituut</entity> concluded after investigation.

title: Cabinet to talk with various opposition combinations tomorrow
lead: The cabinet will continue talks tomorrow with various combinations of opposition parties. That is the outcome of consultations between the cabinet's leadership. The coalition of D66, VVD and CDA is still looking for support for the tax plan and other budgets. <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> and <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">minister Heinen</entity> and <entity id="person:eelco-eerenberg">staatssecretaris Eerenberg</entity> (both <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity>) will first talk with the ChristenUnie and 50Plus tomorrow, then with JA21, BBB and SGP, and finally with Pro and Volt. Most of these parties also already held talks earlier this week. Three routes The three talk groupings stand for three routes the cabinet has to find a majority for its plans. CU and 50Plus, together with the seats of Groep Markuszower, can secure a majority in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. Markuszower, who spoke with Heinen this week, said earlier that he makes few demands. For him, it is mainly important that Pro does not come to power, said the former PVV member of the House of Representatives. Freedom contribution JA21, BBB and SGP together form 'the route on the right'. The three opposition parties announced this morning that they will now work together in negotiations with the minority cabinet. Jetten, deputy prime ministers Van den Brink (CDA) and Yesilgöz (VVD) and minister Heinen held talks this afternoon about the package of demands. The three right-wing parties offer their support for the tax plan and other budgets in exchange for adjustments to the coalition's plans. JA21, SGP and BBB want the tax increase to meet the NATO norm, called the freedom contribution by CDA, taken off the table, and a substantial reduction in the tax burden. The trio also wants adjustments to the nitrogen plans that BBB requested earlier, and more asylum measures, which JA21 consistently advocates. The SGP's demands on surrogacy and abortion policy have also become joint demands. Broad support The cabinet has so far consistently said it wants to pursue broad support in the Tweede Kamer with a hundred seats. Opposition parties consistently say that is not possible and that the cabinet must choose. The package from the right-wing alliance underlines this again, because it contains demands that Pro and Volt, who together form 'the option on the left', will not support. Pro-<entity id="person:jesse-feras-klaver">leider Klaver</entity> stressed in recent days that he is willing to compromise. Due to the cooperation on the right and the content of the package, the coalition, which is already internally divided, will come under even more pressure. D66 and CDA prefer the left, the VVD prefers cooperation with right-wing parties. Incidentally, the cabinet's leadership will meet again this evening at Jetten's ministry to discuss how to proceed.

title: World summit on combating racism and discrimination kicks off in The Hague
lead: About 1500 people from more than 80 countries are visiting The Hague today and tomorrow for the Unesco Global Forum against Racism and Discrimination summit. Prime Minister <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Rob Jetten</entity> gave the opening speech at the World Forum today, and <entity id="person:willem-alexander">koning Willem-Alexander</entity> was also present. "Millions of people face discrimination and racism in their daily lives", Jetten writes on Instagram. "A harsh climate prevails for everyone who stands up for equal rights, and institutions set up to protect all of us are under great pressure." The king spoke with several guests from different countries about the specific challenges in combating racism and discrimination worldwide. The forum is the only international summit focused specifically on the global approach to racism and discrimination. "Worldwide, tensions are rising. Discrimination, racism and incitement to hatred are increasingly visible in societies", writes Unesco. The UN agency for education, science and culture has been fighting racism since its founding in 1945. In 1978 it adopted the Declaration on Race and Racial Prejudice. In it, it is reaffirmed that "all human beings belong to a single species and are descended from a common origin. They are born equal in dignity and rights and all form an integral part of humanity." Change and taking responsibility are central at the summit this year. "Treaties have been concluded on racism and discrimination, declarations drawn up, action programmes developed and promises made. That has been important. But what have all those agreements actually delivered?", according to Unesco. In The Hague, among other things, strategy and policy on combating racism and discrimination will be discussed. The Hague: The event is being held in The Hague because it is worldwide the international city of peace and justice. For example, the International Court of Justice (ICJ) and the International Criminal Court (ICC) are seated in the city. The latter is under heavy pressure from the United States. "Combating racism and discrimination is at its core a fight for human rights and human dignity", says National Coordinator against Discrimination and Racism Rabin Baldewsingh. "There is therefore no better place imaginable to bring the world together precisely on this issue." "For the Netherlands this is a unique opportunity to take international responsibility", according to Baldewsingh. He emphasises that he does not think the Netherlands has a monopoly on wisdom, but "because we are convinced that countries can learn a lot from each other". 'Change possible' Baldewsingh calls it an honour that the Netherlands was chosen by Unesco to co-organise the summit. "The Netherlands has taken important steps in recent years, including by establishing an independent National Coordinator, strengthening the national approach to discrimination and racism, and the social dialogue about our colonial and slavery past. We are bringing those experiences to this Forum." Earlier editions took place in France, Mexico, Brazil and Spain.

title: Commotion around Tax Plan could lead to chaos in tax assessments
lead: If <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity> rejects the Tax Plan 2027 of the minority cabinet at the end of this year, chaos could arise for millions of taxpayers. That is connected to the deadline that applies to the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity>.
