On 20 November at 12.00 noon, all changes to income tax must truly be in, because after that the provisional assessments are made, which are sent from December onwards. If the Eerste Kamer rejects the Tax Plan after 20 November or forces changes through a novelle, the provisional assessments will no longer be correct. This must then be corrected later, in the final assessment one and a half years later. That means back-claims or refunds. The phrase "that will become a second Childcare Benefits Scandal but even bigger" is already being used in the corridors. Not far-fetched. ChristenUnie MP Grinwis raised the topic last Monday in the House debate on the Tax Plan. He asked the <entity id="pos:staatssecretaris-van-financien">staatssecretaris van Financiën</entity> Eerenberg: "What if <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> says yes by majority to the Tax Plan, but the Eerste Kamer does not?" That option is certainly not far-fetched. The minority cabinet is still engaged in difficult negotiations with the opposition over support for the Tax Plan. Whether that will succeed with parties that can provide a majority in both the Tweede and Eerste Kamer is uncertain. Eerenberg therefore said in the debate in answer to Grinwis that this is "the scenario we really should not want with each other or make appealing, because it is not". How does the provisional assessment work? Anyone can request a provisional assessment from the Belastingdienst for the following year from early December. You do that, for example, if you want to receive the mortgage interest deduction monthly, instead of in one lump sum at the end of the tax year. The Belastingdienst determines the following year what the final assessment is. Then it becomes clear to what extent the provisional assessment was correct, and thus whether you must pay an additional amount or get money back. To set the provisional assessment, the Belastingdienst assumes the tax rules that apply then. If the Eerste Kamer changes those at the last moment, the final assessment is likely to turn out differently. The enormous implementation problem that looms will change the discussion for senators of the opposition parties. Their possible vote against could cause uncertainty about income tax and thus the disposable income of millions of Dutch people. That is why the minority cabinet may ultimately settle for only a majority for the Tax Plan in the Tweede Kamer. Opposition parties in the Eerste Kamer will then probably never dare to vote it down. Gamble. So far <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> keeps saying this route is certainly not desirable. But the minority cabinet is still undecided, due to internal disagreements, whether it wants to do business 'from the left' with Pro and Volt or 'from the right' with JA21, SGP and BBB. If this process goes completely wrong, they can take a gamble: rely on CU, 50Plus and Groep Markuszower in the Tweede Kamer, and count on nobody in the Eerste Kamer wanting to be responsible for chaos with income tax. ChristenUnie MP Grinwis responds that there is a "great responsibility" resting on the House and cabinet to get out of this regarding the Tax Plan. "It would surely be irresponsible if we gamble with the tax assessments and benefits of millions of Dutch people by presenting them with the bill afterwards."

title: Herman Brood included in state art collection: 'Like winning gold at the Olympic Games'
lead: An untitled painting by singer and artist Herman Brood, who died in 2001, has been included in the state art collection. The curators of the <entity id="org:rijksdienst-voor-het-cultureel-erfgoed">Rijksdienst voor het Cultureel Erfgoed</entity> (RCE) say they reached this decision because "we believe Herman Brood, as an icon of the twentieth century, deserves more recognition as an artist". This is the first time an artwork by Brood has been included in the Rijkscollectie, an enormous collection of more than 120,000 artworks and historical objects owned by the Dutch state. Brood, who scored big hits as a singer with songs such as Never Be Clever and Saturday Night , thus joins a list that includes 17th-century masters such as Rembrandt van Rijn and his pupils Govert Flinck and Ferdinand Bol, but also modernists such as Piet Mondriaan, Karel Appel and Armando. On the wall at the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity> The acrylic work, which shows two men holding a pistol, until recently hung on the wall at the headquarters of the Belastingdienst in The Hague. Because many fake works and forged certificates of Brood are in circulation, the RCE says it has spent a lot of time in recent months establishing the authenticity of the work. To do so, it worked with the Stichting Valsbrood, a team of three old friends of Brood who specialise in recognising forgeries. The Rijksdienst writes that after research it was established that the work is authentic and dates from the early 1990s. 'A junkie who painted' One of the friends is 76-year-old Rob Dupre. He says Brood would "come to life spontaneously" if he heard this news. "During his lifetime he was seen as a rock 'n roll singer who earned extra money as an artist. Others called him a junkie who painted. As if anyone could do what he did. This news is like winning gold at the Olympic Games." Dupre says he is certain the painting is genuine. "Brood himself said he could not paint, but that his art was his handwriting. If you have looked over his shoulder for so long, you know when something is real or not." The two friends got to know each other in 1990 when Brood walked into Dupre's discotheque in the centre of Amsterdam. "Every Tuesday he performed for us. In return he asked us to help him sell his paintings." About eight months ago, the auction house Sotheby's approached Stichting Valsbrood with the question of whether they could take a look at Brood's untitled work on behalf of the RCE. According to Dupre, the team often sees immediately whether something is a forgery or not. "Herman's work is not as detailed as that of Rembrandt. We therefore have to look at the use of colour, because Herman was colour blind. We check whether the colour combinations fit and what kind of paint has been used. And whether the linen the paint is on is old enough. We of course examined this work extra carefully. We could not allow a forgery into the Rijkscollectie." A deal over tax debt Dupre estimates the value of the work at 15,000 euros. It is unclear whether Brood himself ever received money for the painting. Dupre does not rule out that it ended up with the Belastingdienst through a deal over a possible tax debt of Brood's. "He did not do receipts and that kind of bourgeois stuff. He painted five paintings and then spent them on drink, drugs and women. He was not businesslike at all." That a painting by Brood has been included in the state art collection, Dupre sees as the ultimate recognition of his craftsmanship. "People often said: 'My little daughter can do that too.' But what he did was incredibly difficult. If he took longer than 30 minutes over an artwork, we worried. Almost nobody can work that fast." The curators of the RCE acknowledge his distinctive style. "Especially his early work is creative and original, because he experimented with all kinds of techniques, but in which the hand of the artist is clearly recognisable", says a statement. The use of primary colours is mentioned, as is the fact that he often used syringes to apply paint to the artworks. "It was his own version of action painting. Or perhaps we can better speak of 'rock 'n roll' on canvas."

title: It will be a dry weekend with little wind, but not always sunny
lead: The difference with last weekend can hardly be greater. Then storms Austen and Boelo brought a lot of wind and rain. This weekend it is sometimes almost windless and stays dry. Calm autumn weather, although it remains to be seen how much the sun will shine. Mist gives way to sun On Friday many places start with mist. In the course of the morning the greyness disappears and the sun comes out. In one place this happens faster than in another. The sun will probably break through first in the south. In the north, if luck is against us, it may stay grey for much of the day. The temperature lies between 12 and 14 degrees. Saturday too will be a mix of the mist dissolving and the sun breaking through. The chance of stubborn mist becomes smaller on Sunday, but instead there will be quite a lot of clouds through which the sun struggles to break. How warm it gets depends strongly on how long the sun shines. If the sun shines for a longer period, it is lovely autumn weather and very pleasant outdoors because there is hardly any wind. Colder after the weekend On Monday a very small amount of rain may fall and after that colder air comes towards the Netherlands with a north-easterly wind. It cools gradually in the days after the weekend. At night the chance of frost increases.

title: Italy allows personalised number plates, plan met with mockery
lead: TI-104MO (Ti Amo), AM-013RE (Amore) or MA-771EO (Matteo). From next year, Italians will be able to personalise the number plate of their vehicle. The Italian government wants to use this to bring in extra money. Prime Minister Meloni announced the plan when presenting the budget for 2027, the last before the parliamentary elections. She encourages Italians to be creative above all with the number plates. Personalising a plate for a car is expected to cost 600 euros. For a motorcycle it is 360 euros. An Italian number plate currently consists of a combination of two letters, three digits followed by two more letters. It is not known to what extent Italians may deviate from this format. Meloni mocked The plan by Meloni has led to hilarity on social media. For example, memes (humorous internet images) appeared of Meloni as Marie Antoinette with the text: "Your Majesty, the people are starving!" to which Meloni replies: "Give them personalised number plates". This refers to the famous saying of the French queen who is said to have said "then let them eat cake" when she was told that the people had no bread to eat. The government would do better first to do something about, among other things, the rising cost of living, is the criticism on social media. Italy's national debt currently stands at around 139 percent of gross domestic product (GDP). Within the European Union, the country has one of the largest debt burdens. Taxi drivers Taxi drivers, among others, are pleased with the personalised number plates because approved providers can be easily recognised by them. Others fear that the personalised number plates will contain offensive texts. The government does not want to say how much money the plan is expected to bring in.

title: Japan and Germany become 'premium partners', but clash over protection of cars
lead: With smiles, bows and agreements on closer cooperation, Japanese prime minister Sanae Takaichi receives German chancellor Friedrich Merz in Tokyo. The leaders shake hands and even call each other "premium partners", as if they had taken out a trade subscription without ads. But open criticism can be heard amid the courtesies. European protection of the car industry, which Germany is championing, threatens to hit Japanese manufacturers hard too. Japan thinks that must change. Clumsily and bending, Merz walks on Thursday through a packed research facility in Tokyo, followed by Japanese diplomats above whom he towers. During his visit many things are discussed: defence cooperation, cyber security and the energy supply of the future. But there is one subject Merz does not openly want to say too much about: the car industry. "We are seriously concerned", says Minister of Economy Ryosei Akazawa on Wednesday during a meeting between the chancellor and Japanese companies. Merz listens with an impassive face. "We are above all partners who, as like-minded countries, must precisely act together against overproduction by certain countries", he says, referring to China. The EU wants to favour electric cars produced within the union in subsidies and government purchases. According to the German business newspaper Handelsblatt, there are plans to also bring cars from Japan under this 'Buy European' programme, as well as from the UK and South Korea. No decision has been made yet. New blow Germany, as an exporting country, was for a long time reluctant to introduce trade restrictions, but Berlin is no longer opposing this. The car industry among others is suffering heavily from Chinese competition, which is rapidly gaining ground with cheap and subsidised models. Action was therefore called for. That became clear again today with the presentation of deep-red quarterly figures at Volkswagen. On Thursday morning Toyota director Kenta Kon also personally asks the chancellor to treat cars from Japan the same as European-produced vehicles. In his view that is "best for customers, the car industry and car culture". How Merz responds Toyota does not disclose. But that the company takes the request directly to the press makes clear that the criticism is not staying behind closed doors. For Japan, yet another economic blow threatens. Toyota sold a quarter fewer cars in China from April to September than a year earlier, the lowest number for that period in nine years. Demand is weak and Chinese manufacturers are luring customers away with cheap electric models. Chinese competition is also growing in Southeast Asia, for years a stronghold of Japanese car manufacturers. Meanwhile, import duties from Donald Trump are weighing on exports to the United States. And now Europe also threatens to make things harder for Japanese manufacturers: with advantages for its own industry for which their cars produced in Japan are not eligible. That while Japan and Germany both say they want to become less dependent on China and protect their companies against Chinese competition. Middle powers Merz is very keen to win over his hostess. His plan is to form a global alliance between middle-sized countries as a counterweight to both China and the US. As the third and fourth economies in the world, Germany and Japan, with help from other countries, can form a powerful bloc, the chancellor said. "Then the question is not whether we are on the menu or sitting at the table, because then we own the whole restaurant." The countries plan, among other things, cooperation on AI development and defence. Germany also wants to join the development of a Japanese-British-Italian fighter aircraft. Both countries have decades of military restraint behind them as a result of the Second World War. The two now declare they are "willing to take greater responsibility for peace and stability". In other words: invest heavily in defence. Merz leaves Japan with dozens of trade deals and investment plans between the two countries. That is what the "premium partnership" should radiate. If the Japanese car industry nevertheless suffers damage from the European measures, that friendship will once again take a significant scratch.

title: After earlier acquittal, 11-year prison sentence for man who killed girlfriend in 2016
lead: A 48-year-old man from Harderwijk has been sentenced on appeal to eleven years in prison for killing his girlfriend in 2016. The district court had earlier acquitted the man due to lack of evidence. According to the court of appeal, it can only be that Robert L. killed his partner, the court said. Despite "highly incriminating circumstances", he has left important questions unanswered, according to the court. L. reported the woman missing at the start of 2016. She was said to have left their home in Amsterdam-West in the night of 7 to 8 January 2016, in a drunken state, after an argument. On 29 March of that year, a hiker found her body in the Zandenbos near Nunspeet. After investigation it became clear that she had died by strangulation. Her boyfriend was quickly named as a suspect. Out of the house The woman wanted Robert L. to move out of the house. Their relationship was therefore very bad, but the man never said exactly where he was on the day of her disappearance. The court assumes that in those hours he drove from Amsterdam to Nunspeet. He was well acquainted with the place where her body was found. The court speaks of "a place that is not easy for others to find". He has always denied that he did anything to his girlfriend and remained silent during the trial. According to the court, it was L. who last saw the 51-year-old woman alive. A few weeks after his girlfriend went missing, L. lived in the home with another woman. The court holds L. heavily responsible for having killed the woman "in a very gross manner", reported her missing and refusing to answer questions about what happened, writes Omroep Gelderland. For example, he has told nothing about what the argument they supposedly had was about. Last year L. was acquitted in the district court in Amsterdam, after prosecutors had demanded fourteen years in prison. The judge ruled at that time that there were indications pointing to Robert L., but that hard evidence was lacking. The public prosecution service appealed.

title: Fixed, variable or dynamic? Households search for the right energy contract
lead: For months, prices for oil and gas have been rising because of the war in the Middle East. Large energy companies are not suffering from this, today's figures show. While companies are making high profits, energy tariffs for consumers keep climbing. And that raises the question: is it best to take out a fixed, variable or still dynamic contract? Several energy companies announced the sky-high profits they made over the past three months. Shell and Vattenfall, for example, saw their profits double due to high oil and gas prices. Meanwhile, the gas price for a megawatt hour rose above 100 euros yesterday for the first time since autumn 2022. The rising gas bill is raising questions at the Consumentenbond. "A lot of questions from people about what they should do. It is really alive." says Joyce Donat of the Consumentenbond. Consumer collective United Consumers also sees that customers are looking for answers and certainty. Still, there is no ready-made answer. Fixed contract "Until recently it paid to take out a fixed contract just before summer. Normally prices are lower then. But that was not the case this year because of the war in Iran," says Donat. The Consumentenbond advises people to mainly look at what feels most comfortable. A fixed contract for three years now means a lower price, but it can also mean that you pay a higher amount for a longer period if the gas price falls again. Some households the NOS spoke to choose certainty instead by taking out a fixed contract, even though it may cost more. Freerk Twijnstra is one of them. "We are moving this week, so we had to take out a new contract. It's just like investing: you don't really know how things will go. So we locked it in for three years." Anyone with a fixed contract that expires automatically gets a variable contract, whose prices are adjusted several times a year. For some people a fixed contract is not an option. For example, a fixed contract for the detached house of Harm in De Meern is so expensive that he chose a dynamic contract. With that contract type the price changes every day or sometimes every hour. Harm now pays just over 300 euros per month for energy. "I'm now above 2 euros per cubic metre. A year ago it was something like 1.10 euros." Even with a dynamic contract there is still an option to limit excessive costs. For example, when taking out his contract, Ibrahim Faydali from Enschede chose a cap on the gas tariff. "I pay a few euros extra per month for that. I'm very glad I did." A household's energy bill consists of the costs of gas and electricity themselves, but also of grid operator charges and an energy tax from the government. Minister Stientje van Veldhoven of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-kgg">Klimaat en Groene Groei</entity> says in a response to the NOS that she can well understand that households are worried about the rising gas price. "The cabinet is choosing measures to support precisely the households that need the most help." She is referring to the Noodfonds Energie and various subsidies for insulation. Not only gas. The high gas price is not only felt by people who use gas to heat their homes, because the electricity price is also linked to the gas price. Although much electricity is generated using wind and solar energy, still just over a third of electricity is generated in gas power plants. Marian Stevens runs a pottery workshop in Venray. Over the past years she has made it sustainable and she is fully off gas. Recently she had to take out a new energy contract. "I was quite shocked by what I saw: I have to pay a lot more. Given the investments we made to get off gas, I had thought we would not be spending so much on energy costs." The unrest in the Middle East persists for now. That also means that in the coming months the energy companies will probably continue to make large profits. In a response, Shell says: "We acknowledge that high energy prices can be problematic for vulnerable citizens and businesses, and that governments are also facing difficult choices." Voices in politics are being raised about imposing extra taxes on profits at companies like Shell. The company itself says it already bears a considerable tax burden worldwide. At this DIY store in Den Hoorn, they notice that mainly stoves and draught excluders are selling very well:

title: Military helicopter from Italy crashes in Bosnia and Herzegovina, four dead
lead: An Italian Chinook crashed in Bosnia and Herzegovina around 4 p.m. local time. That is what the Italian Ministry of Defence reports. The crash occurred near the city of Brcko, close to the border with Croatia. Local media report four dead and 11 injured. Earlier, a local Bosnian mayor spoke of three dead and twelve injured, one of whom was in critical condition. A fourth person has therefore now died. Nothing is yet known about the nationality of the victims. The Italian Ministry of Defence reports that it cannot yet provide further details "pending more precise information, particularly on the health condition of the persons involved". The cause of the crash is being investigated. The crash was captured by a bystander: The military helicopter was flying in Bosnia for the EU peacekeeping force EUFOR Althea, which aims to safeguard and promote the security and stability of that country. Dutch military personnel also take part in EUFOR Althea. Last week, around 175 military personnel of the 11 Air Assault Brigade, officers and support staff, returned from Bosnia and Herzegovina. In April 2025 it became known that the Netherlands would contribute to the peacekeeping mission. The military personnel stayed a few weeks longer in the Balkan country in connection with elections. The Dutch military personnel worked in Bosnia together with colleagues from, among others, Greece, Hungary, Italy, and Romania. The home base of the military personnel was Camp Butmir in the Bosnian capital Sarajevo, the headquarters of EUFOR Althea.

title: With a fat cat, French AI company Mistral says: take a look at us too
lead: With a reference to a fat cat, the French AI company is launching its newest AI model on the market: le chonk . The nickname refers to an internet joke about the weight of cats. The fatter the cat, the more 'chonk' the little beast is. The new AI model is officially called Large 4 and, according to Mistral, is the biggest and most powerful AI model the company has released so far: chonk, then. Mistral is seen as the only serious European answer to the American and Chinese AI companies, says Eric Postma. He is professor of artificial intelligence at Tilburg University. "The company is trying to compete with the American models, with the idea that you are not dependent on the United States for AI technology." It is difficult to compare different AI models well with each other, but experts see that the AI companies Anthropic and OpenAI remain the providers of the most powerful AI models. "Mistral is trying to develop the same type of product as these companies", says Jelle Zuidema, lecturer in artificial intelligence at the University of Amsterdam. "But they are always a few months ahead and it is just a little bit less." Much more investment in America But we should not let ourselves be too distracted by this 'race', Zuidema thinks. "The Americans are very much busy with that: who has the very best AI model? That is partly also to make a great impression." "They partly do that to raise money from investors", says Postma of Tilburg University. "That is deeply embedded in the culture of the United States: it is a ruthless struggle to raise as much money as possible. As a result, the American AI companies have a great deal of money at their disposal." Since its founding in 2023, Mistral has raised more than 6.6 billion euros, according to data from market analyst Crunchbase. By comparison: roughly 181 billion euros have been invested in OpenAI and 153 billion euros in Anthropic. "Because investors put such incredibly large amounts of money into Anthropic and OpenAI, these companies can offer their AI services far below cost", says Zuidema. "You can take out a subscription for 200 euros, but use thousands of euros' worth of AI computing power. The strategy: get people used to AI technology now, and raise prices later." Because Mistral cannot compete with that, the company has to look for something else that sets it apart from the competition, says Paul Verhagen. He is an AI and geopolitics analyst at The Hague Centre for Strategic Studies (HCSS). He thinks Mistral can benefit by emphatically presenting itself as a European company. "Mistral is not necessarily better than the AI models developed in the United States or China. And competing on price is difficult." Independent of the United States "But in Europe there can be another reason to still choose Mistral: you are then not dependent on other countries. We have seen in recent months that the American government is willing to block access to American technology. If that really happens, you do have a problem." "You do not want another country to be able to decide whether you have access to this technology", says Postma. Because AI is used in so many places, that could bring our entire economy to a standstill, says Zuidema. "We cannot assume that a good relationship with the US will always persist. If things go further in the wrong direction, Europe still wants to have access to good AI technology." Verhagen thinks European governments and important organisations should look seriously at Mistral from that perspective. "Think of Defence, but also the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity> and energy such as gas and electricity. That is important for our security. It is good to use AI models from Europe there." "Mistral needs that support to become a successful company, he thinks. "The government does not necessarily have to look at the cheapest option, but can choose to consider independence more important. With the money Mistral earns that way, the company can keep developing its AI models and also help other companies with its knowledge. Mistral does not necessarily have to make the very best AI models, but it does have to be good enough to keep up."

title: CDA and D66 not happy with JA21, BBB and SGP's list of demands: 'Doesn't make it any easier'
lead: Coalition parties D66 and CDA are not happy with the list of demands that JA21, BBB and SGP presented this morning. "This has not made it any easier", says CDA-<entity id="person:hendrik-bontenbal">leider Bontenbal</entity> this evening. "Is this really what you want?", asks D66-<entity id="person:jan-maarten-paternotte">fractievoorzitter Paternotte</entity>, addressing the three. The three right-wing opposition parties announced this morning that from now on they will work together in the negotiations with the minority cabinet. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> is still looking for support for the tax plan and other budgets. The three are offering their support in exchange for adjustments to the plans of D66, VVD and CDA. JA21, SGP and BBB want the tax increase to meet the NATO norm, called the freedom contribution by CDA, scrapped, and a substantial tax cut. Medical ethics as bargaining chip. In addition, the trio want adjustments to the nitrogen plans, which BBB has long asked for, and more measures on asylum, which JA21 consistently advocates. The SGP demands on surrogacy and abortion policy have also become joint demands. Especially the latter irks Paternotte. "We are not going to trade fundamental rights of women for a budget," he says. "Medical ethics as a bargaining chip, that is crazy." Bontenbal does not go into the substance of the package from JA21, SGP and BBB, but does say that it has become more complicated to get out of it. "Because they have taken over each other's demands together." He does think the cabinet should keep talking with them. "Also to hear how firm the demands are." Showing colours. This evening the top of the cabinet is meeting together at the ministry of <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity> to discuss how to proceed. Earlier today the premier, the deputy prime ministers and the <entity id="pos:minister-van-financien">minister van Financiën</entity> already discussed this here as well. Tomorrow morning the cabinet will speak with different combinations of opposition parties: first with the ChristenUnie and 50Plus, then with JA21, BBB and SGP, and finally with Pro and Volt. After that it is time for the cabinet to show its colours, says Bontenbal. "My patience is starting to run out." The three discussion combinations of tomorrow stand for three routes the cabinet has to find a majority for its plans. CU and 50Plus can together with the seats of Groep Markuszower secure a majority in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. JA21, BBB and SGP together form 'the route on the right'. Pro and Volt also hold on to each other and are 'the option on the left'. Pro-<entity id="person:jesse-feras-klaver">leider Klaver</entity> stressed in recent days that he is willing to compromise.

title: Sharp share price drop for Google's parent company, one of the biggest share price falls ever
lead: The share price of Alphabet fell by more than 12 percent on the New York stock exchange. The parent company of Google thereby lost nearly 500 billion dollars in value in one go. That makes it one of the biggest share price falls ever. This happened after the company published its quarterly figures. The general mood on the American stock exchanges was not something to write home about. The Dow Jones index closed 0.3 percent down, the S&P 500 index was 0.3 percent lower, and the technology index Nasdaq fell 1.4 percent. AI investments The unrest among investors about Alphabet is mainly due to the negative cash flow. The difference between income and expenditure fell to minus 9.1 billion dollars over the past three months. It is only the second quarter with a negative cash flow since Google went public in 2004. This is partly caused by falling advertising revenue from the search engine. At the same time, a lot of money is being invested in developing artificial intelligence (AI). According to analysts, tech companies that invest heavily in AI must increasingly do their best to convince investors that spending on data centres, computing power and chips will be earned back. Cannibalising the search page With the rise of chatbots, such as ChatGPT from OpenAI, analysts warn that Google is at risk of losing market share. Many users who previously mainly consulted the search engine for answers to their questions are now increasingly turning to chatbots. Those users therefore use Google less, so the company is missing out on advertising revenue. In addition, Google also provides its own users with AI results in the search engine. But in doing so Google is in fact fuelling competition between its own services. The AI results come at the expense of the traditional search page, so users click on advertisements less as a result. Last year Alphabet still booked record revenue and the company's market value was estimated at more than 4000 billion dollars.

title: French houses seized in investigation into former Ukrainian official
lead: In a Ukrainian corruption investigation, property in France has been seized. The case concerns large-scale fraud in the purchase of bulletproof vests for the Ukrainian army. That is what the EU judicial body Eurojust announced. A former official of the Ukrainian ministry of Defence is suspected of corruption and money laundering. He is said to have played a key role in the purchase of 67,000 bulletproof vests, which turned out to be of worthless quality. The Ukrainian state is estimated to have been defrauded of 53 million euros. Houses in Nice The suspect is said to have been bribed by the seller of the military equipment. This money is said to have been invested in French property via a contact person. Among other things, houses in the port city of Nice are said to have been bought. These homes have been searched and seizures have subsequently been made, as well as of bank balances. It is unclear whether any arrests have been made. It has also not been announced how many people are suspected of involvement in the corruption case. The police operation is a cooperation between the French and Ukrainian authorities. Eurojust, which is based in The Hague, has played a coordinating role. Paid in advance The contract for the tens of thousands of bulletproof vests was signed in March 2022. At that moment Russia had just been a week into its large-scale invasion of Ukraine. The vests were paid for in advance. Only upon delivery did it become clear that they were of poor quality. Corruption is a persistent problem in Ukraine. On the one hand, the country has in recent years taken big steps to tackle and prevent bribery within government, the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) concluded last summer in a report. On the other hand, high officials are regularly arrested on suspicion of corruption. Thus last month the country's highest prosecutor resigned due to a corruption investigation. In August, among others the deputy chief of staff of President Zelensky was charged.

title: Drenthe family receives posthumous Yad Vashem honour: 'Extraordinary people'
lead: Four members of the Brouwer family from the Drenthe village of Gasselternijveenschemond have posthumously received a Yad Vashem award. The four helped Jews, including Amsterdammer Aby de Lange, go into hiding during the Second World War. For son Job de Lange, the honour brings the circle full. "Thanks to those people I exist," he says to RTV Drenthe. The four receive the honorary title Righteous Among the Nations, which is intended for non-Jews who during the war risked their own lives to help Jews. The surviving relatives were handed the award this afternoon by the Israeli embassy. "Today we honour extraordinary people," said ambassador Zvi Aviner Vapni in the village church. "Ordinary people who made exceptional choices." Thie Brouwer (1902-1988), his wife Watsina (1904-1991), mother Jantina (1864-1962) and sister Aaltje (1904-1988) helped Jews and non-Jews find hiding addresses, including in the border region of Drenthe and Groningen. For example, the Jewish Aby de Lange from Amsterdam was given shelter by the family in Stadskanaal. Resistance Thie Brouwer in particular played an important role in the resistance, both within and outside Drenthe. In the early war years he worked in Assen, where he was dismissed because he did not want to cooperate with the German occupier. Later he worked in The Hague, where he was dismissed for similar reasons. There he was also involved in distributing the resistance newspaper Trouw and helped people go into hiding. The family members: Thie Brouwer later returned to Drenthe to help the resistance there. He got help from his wife, who for example hid weapons in the pram to deliver them afterwards. Thie's mother Jantina lived in Stadskanaal, where throughout the Second World War she offered shelter to people in the home where she lived with her daughter Aaltje. Among them was therefore the Jewish Amsterdammer Aby de Lange. Application Historical researcher Jan-Willem van de Kolk submitted the application for the honour several years ago to the institute in Jerusalem. Thie Brouwer's son died in 2022 at the age of 92 and still had many documents, letters and reports from the Second World War in his possession. Van de Kolk therefore had good hope that the Brouwer family would receive the honour. "Moreover, the Shoah Foundation recorded a testimony from Aby de Lange years ago. Those are all important documents that support the application," he said earlier to RTV Drenthe. In the end it was up to the committee to make a final judgement. Almost 6000 Yad Vashem awards have been presented in the Netherlands. Yad Vashem means 'a memorial and a name'. The idea behind it is that people are remembered permanently. WWII newsletter Interested in the Second World War? Subscribe to our newsletter here.

title: British actor Patrick Stewart (86) dies, known among other things from Star Trek
lead: British actor Patrick Stewart died yesterday at the age of 86. This was announced on his social media. Stewart was a classically trained actor who mastered the Shakespeare repertoire. To the wider public he was mainly known for his role in the science fiction series Star Trek: The Next Generation and the superhero films from the X-Men series. Stewart died in his home in Los Angeles after a short illness, in the presence of family and friends and "surrounded by live music, prayer, tears and laughter", as it is described. He suffered from Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia. Stewart was born on 13 July 1940 in Mirfield in England. The New York Times writes that he overcame a gloomy youth in an English coal mining area before he went to drama school. He had worked as a furniture maker to save money for the training. He first performed when he was 19 years old. Shakespeare A few years later, in 1966, he began at the Royal Shakespeare Company in the United Kingdom. He stayed there for fourteen years. Speaking to news agency AP he said: "People who were not in the company said to me: 'Take a break. Why don't you go somewhere else?' And I'd say: 'To do what?' Television?'" In 1971 was his Broadway debut; he played a tinker in A Midsummer Night's Dream. A selection of Stewart's appearances in the series Star Trek: After a long theatre career Stewart played in many films and series, although the real fame took a while longer. He became best known as Captain Jean-Luc Picard from the Star Trek franchise. He first appeared in it in 1987. His deep voice characterised him, as did the catchphrase "Make it so". He is also known for his role as Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men trilogy. He appeared in three films between 2000 and 2006. Later he was seen in four more films, before Professor X died in Logan from 2017. He made his return in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness in 2022. Divorces Stewart married choreographer Sheila Falconer in 1966, with whom he had two children. His later marriage to Wendy Neuss, an American producer, also ended in divorce. The reason for both divorces, as he admitted in his memoirs, was an affair with a younger woman. "In a life full of joy and success, my two failed marriages are my greatest regret," he wrote. In 2013 he married Sunny Ozell, an American singer who was 38 years younger than him.

title: Cabinet wants smoking banned in places where many children are
lead: Smoking in places where many children are will be banned, if the cabinet has its way. People would no longer be allowed to light a cigarette at farms with animals for children or, for example, on the outdoor grounds of childcare centers. A proposal to ban this is expected to be discussed tomorrow in <entity id="org:ministerraad">de ministerraad</entity>, sources told the NOS. Through the legislative change, managers of such places would be obliged to introduce a smoking ban. In principle, they would then also have to enforce that no smoking takes place. Many of those places, such as squares at after-school care and supervised playgrounds, have already been declared smoke-free by their managers. They want visitors not to smoke there. Yet at a small part of the places this is not yet the case. For those last places, the cabinet therefore wants a mandatory smoking ban after all. The <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">Tweede Kamer</entity> has also asked for this, although parliament actually went further. Broad support: The Tweede Kamer initially also considered a smoking ban at other places where many children come, such as zoos and amusement parks. But the cabinet is first focusing on places that are entirely aimed at children, such as supervised playgrounds and childcare, because that would be easier to arrange given the broad support for it. Later, unsupervised playgrounds and places such as outdoor swimming pools could be considered. Smoke-free generation in 2040: The cabinet is aiming for a smoke-free generation by 2040, and this plan is part of that. Other measures have already been taken for this, such as a display ban, neutral packaging and fewer points of sale. The Adviescollege toetsing regeldruk (ATR) was already critical when the cabinet submitted this plan for advice, and the college also noted that earlier plans to have a smoke-free generation by 2040 did not appear to be effective.

title: Agent tasers parcel delivery driver after illegal parking in Amsterdam, bystanders outraged
lead: A parcel delivery driver in Amsterdam was tasered during his arrest yesterday afternoon. According to the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>, the driver blocked the road while loading and unloading and the situation escalated. Bystanders filmed the incident. The incident happened around 3:30 p.m. in the Runstraat in the city centre. Footage in the hands of city broadcaster AT5 shows the driver has several parcels on the ground behind a white van. Behind that is a motorcycle. Watch the footage here, which a bystander filmed: The clip starts a few seconds before the man is tasered. A motorcycle officer and the driver are in discussion and the driver asks: "Why am I being arrested?", while stretching his hands out to the side. The driver is then tasered from close range. The driver falls to the ground. The footage makes clear that several bystanders express their outrage. For example, a woman shouts: "You can't just taser someone. Have you gone completely mad?" Situation escalated. A police spokesperson tells AT5 that the man had parked his van in a place where that was not allowed. The officer then spoke to him about it. The officer reportedly then asked the man to move the van so traffic could pass. The driver reportedly refused. A police spokesperson stresses to NOS that the footage is only a fraction of the bigger picture and that the officer was forced to use the taser. According to the police, the officer wanted to arrest the man but the man did not cooperate. He then used his electroshock weapon because the situation had reportedly escalated. The police spokesperson says the escalation may have taken place before the start of the video. Incident under investigation. The spokesperson stresses that officers must always report when they use force. Every use of force incident is investigated. "That should show whether this was proportionate," said the spokesperson. After his arrest the man was taken to the police station. He received several fines there. He has since been released.

title: Deaths after rock formation collapses in Turkish tourist region of Cappadocia
lead: In Turkey at least three people have died after a rock formation collapsed in Cappadocia. Five others were also injured. The collapse occurred at the entrance to an open-air museum in Göreme. According to Turkish media, the victims are a Turkish couple and a French tourist. The collapse was presumably caused by a landslide as a result of heavy rainfall. A rescue team has been deployed to search for more victims under the rubble. The Minister of Justice has launched an investigation into the incident. World Heritage List: Cappadocia is a popular tourist attraction and is known for its special and unique rock formations and centuries-old underground cities. The region is one of the most visited places in the country. Many hot air balloon rides are also made there. Cappadocia is on the Unesco World Heritage List.

title: Meteorite found in Mali turns out to be 4.1 billion years old
lead: A Martian meteorite found in September 2022 in the Sahara desert in Mali has, after research, been shown to be at least 4.1 billion years old. The meteorite is therefore one of the three oldest Martian meteorites found on Earth. That is the conclusion of researchers from NASA in an article in the scientific journal Science. The 800-gram piece of red rock, named Teghaza 001, is according to scientist Yang Liu "truly unique". According to him, it offers more insights than the two other pieces of Martian meteorite. Teghaza 001 was found in 2022 in eight fragments in the desert, about 34 kilometers from the village of Bir Shali. The largest fragment was as big as a tennis ball. The most important minerals researchers found in it are feldspar and pyroxene, important rock-forming minerals that are common in the Earth's crust. Water The rock also contained zircon crystals with uranium. Furthermore, the chemical composition of Teghaza 001 indicates that water flowed past it. This sets it apart from the two earlier finds. According to the NASA scientists, Teghaza 001 has a unique composition of solidification and volcanic minerals. The roughly equally old meteorite ALH84001 consists almost entirely of one mineral, and the meteorite called Black Beauty, about 2.1 billion years old, is again much smaller. Teghaza 001 probably comes from the southern highlands of Mars. "This is really the first piece of Martian crust we have found in a part of Mars where we have never had a sample before", said Lee Saper, the second author of the article. According to the scientist, the find suggests that there was water on the Martian surface more than 4.1 billion years ago. Life on Mars The find, however, does not answer the all-encompassing question of whether there was ever life on Mars. Saper: "The findings support the idea that early Mars had the necessary ingredients and conditions to harbor life, but do not directly answer the question of whether there has been life on Mars."

title: Heavy fighting in Yemen, Houthis accused of causing famine
lead: Heavy fighting and bombardments are taking place in various places in Yemen. In the besieged city of Taiz alone, thirteen deaths are reported, mainly women and children. The local authorities accuse the Houthis, who have surrounded the city, of causing a famine in the city. "The city is not on the edge of a famine, but in a famine", says governor Nabil Shamsan. The southwestern city has been cut off from the supply of water, food, medicine and fuel. Since the start of the heavy offensive earlier this month, almost 300 people reportedly have been killed in fighting. Possible war crime There is a deliberately caused humanitarian crisis in Taiz, says Human Rights Watch in a statement. According to the human rights organization, the Houthis may even be guilty of a war crime. People in Taiz recently told the NOS that there is systemic starvation . In the city, nine civilians have been killed by Houthi fighters in two days, a local human rights organization states. Eleven civilians reportedly have been kidnapped. According to the Houthis' ministry of Public Health, thirteen people were killed today by a Saudi bombardment. These were reportedly mainly civilian casualties. Denial Houthi leader Abdul Malik al-Houthi claimed today in a televised speech that humanitarian aid is indeed being allowed into Taiz. He stated that only weapons deliveries to pro-Saudi militias are being blocked. The Houthis have occupied large parts of Yemen for years and are fighting against the Saudi Arabia-backed <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity>. The Yemeni armed forces claim that in 24 hours they have killed or wounded more than 300 Houthi fighters. Hundreds of attacks reportedly were carried out within one day. Positions of Houthi fighters in the west of Taiz in particular have been fired upon, according to the army leadership. Missile attack on Saudi Arabia The Houthis have claimed a series of air attacks on Saudi Arabia. Among the targets were two international airports and several oil refineries. According to the Saudi authorities, several missiles were intercepted. A Saudi citizen in the capital Riyadh was injured by falling debris. A house was also damaged.

title: George Michael guitar from Faith video brings in 215,000 euros
lead: A guitar of the late British singer George Michael fetched 180,000 pounds (215,000 euros) at an auction, the BBC reports. The guitar was used in the video for the 1987 hit Faith. More than thirty memorabilia items of the singer went under the hammer at the British auction house Sworders. The personal items, including signed photos and albums, brought in a total of 238,000 pounds (285,000 euros). George Michael broke through in the early 1980s with Wham!, a popular pop duo he formed with Andrew Ridgeley. In 1986 the duo split up, and a year later Michael scored an enormous hit with the song Faith from his eponymous first solo album. George Michael died in 2016 at the age of 53 from a combination of heart and liver problems. The video for Faith: The auction was preceded by a row. The items were owned by Siobhan Bailey, for years the personal assistant of Michael. Bailey died in 2014 and after her death her husband Ian Belcher, from whom she was separating, inherited the collection. That Belcher decided to sell the collection went down badly with Bailey's brother. Gerard Bailey told the BBC that his sister "would have been appalled at the thought of an auction held in her name and of personal, dear possessions being sold to the highest bidder". The chairman of auction house Sworders said that contact with Belcher over the past 2.5 years had been "very pleasant". "You can look at it in two ways: as a way to make money or as a kind of commemoration and tribute to Siobhan, and that is how we have approached it."

title: Convicted Australian mushroom murderer loses appeal, will never be released
lead: The woman sentenced in Australia to life imprisonment for the murder of three people by poisoning with mushrooms has lost her appeal in the case. That means Erin Patterson has no chance of early release. Patterson (52) was sentenced at the end of last year to three life terms, with the possibility of early release after 33 years. The Office of Public Prosecutions appealed against that ruling. Justice found that, because of the seriousness of the criminal offences committed, the woman was not entitled to early release. The Court of Appeal of the state of Victoria agrees. "This offence was extraordinarily cold and calculating and deserves the most severe sentence possible", said one of the judges. The three judges of the court also rejected Patterson's appeal against her convictions. Poisonous mushrooms Patterson maintains that during a family lunch in July 2023 in Leongatha she accidentally added death caps, highly poisonous mushrooms, to the meal. The parents and aunt of her ex-husband died from the effects of the poisoning. The uncle of her ex survived the lunch but lay in a coma for weeks. Her ex-husband had also been invited to the lunch but cancelled at the last minute. Patterson can still challenge the Court of Appeal's ruling before the Australian High Court. That is her last opportunity to appeal her conviction. The case caused great upheaval in Australia and received much (inter)national media attention. A prison sentence with no prospect of early release is very rare in Australia.

title: Crypto platform Binance hacked, possibly billions stolen
lead: Binance, the world's largest crypto platform, has become the victim of a hack. According to the company, an estimated 6.3 billion dollars in crypto assets was affected by the attack, roughly more than 5.6 billion euros. The company says that about 3 billion dollars in assets has been recovered and frozen, so they cannot fall into the wrong hands. What has happened to the remaining more than 3 billion, Binance does not say. The company does note that "all user funds are safe". Co-founder Yi He says the company "will compensate all losses from hacks". According to its own account, the platform has a bitcoin fund to cover users' balances in case of a hack. Binance tells financial news agency Bloomberg that an investigation has started. In an initial statement the company says hackers may have entered the systems via a developer's laptop. It hopes users can access their balances within 48 hours, once the necessary security scans have been done. In a newer statement the company speaks of a complex attack and multiple points where security was breached. Because Binance does not have a license from the Dutch regulator <entity id="org:zbo-de-nederlandsche-bank">DNB</entity>, it has not been active on the Dutch market since 2023. It also received a fine of over 3 million euros because it was still active in the Netherlands without that license. Prices fell. The news about the security problems immediately led to sharp drops in cryptocurrency prices. Bitcoin fell to around 77,500 dollars, its lowest point in six weeks, and ether dropped below 2,200 dollars, its lowest point in months. The providers of crypto tokens Tether and Circle said that in response to the incident they have frozen balances. Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino reported that his company has frozen more than 1.5 billion dollars in assets. Jeremy Allaire, co-founder and CEO of Circle, said that his company, "in coordination with investigative services", has frozen more than 800 million dollars in balances. Both companies issue so-called stablecoins, digital coins whose value is pegged to the US dollar. Binance was founded in 2017 by Changpeng Zhao. He stepped down as CEO in 2023 as part of a settlement with the US Department of Justice after he failed to prevent money laundering on the platform. In 2024 he was sentenced to a prison term, but in 2025 President Trump granted him a pardon.

title: All votes counted in Israel: no majority for political blocs in parliament
lead: In the Israeli election, neither political bloc has won a majority in parliament after all votes were counted. The Central Elections Committee has announced this. Neither the governing coalition of Prime Minister Netanyahu nor the opposition bloc of Gadi Eisenkot reached at least 61 seats. The election result confirms that Netanyahu's Likud party has become the largest, with 27 seats. His coalition of right-wing conservative, far-right and religious parties won 53 seats and thus falls 8 short of a majority in the 120-seat Knesset. In the 2022 elections, the coalition still reached 64 seats. Netanyahu's rival, former army chief Gadi Eisenkot, won 21 seats with his party Yashar, founded last year, and thus came second. His opposition bloc remained stuck at 48 seats. It was already clear that the election result had led to a deadlock in Israeli politics. The formation of a new government is likely to take a long time. Arab parties, the winners of these elections, may play a key role. The Arab parties Ra'am and the Joint List together won 19 seats, against 10 seats in 2022. To obtain a majority, Eisenkot needs the support of these parties. Still, it is questionable whether the Jewish opposition will cooperate with the Arab parties. Recognising Hamas as a terrorist organization that must be dismantled is one of the demands Eisenkot makes. Turnout in the election was 77.9 percent, the highest percentage in decades. Just over 5.7 million people cast their vote. On Wednesday 4 November the seat distribution will be finalized. President Herzog will then ask whoever in his view has the best chance of a majority to form a government. Parties have until 18 November to file complaints or take legal steps.

title: Mega operation in Vught: monumental station building is lifted and moved
lead: This is no ordinary move: the monumental station building in Vught is being lifted in its entirety today and moved 13.6 meters. Weighing 720 tons, the building from 1868, including its historic basement, will be moved east over the course of seven hours. Watch a time-lapse of the first hour here: The operation began this morning at around 08:00. By mid-afternoon, the building, 28 meters long and 9.5 meters wide, must be standing in its new place. Livestream The move of the station building can be followed live at NOS. The station building has to make way for a fourth track. From 2030 onward, more trains must run between Meteren and Boxtel. That fourth track will be laid in a trench between Den Bosch and Vught, exactly where the station building now stands. That is why the building must be moved. Leaving the building in place and building around it, or demolishing and rebuilding it, were not options. The station building is a national monument, and by moving the building in its entirety, including the basement, its monumental value is preserved. The move is part of the High-Frequency Rail Transport Programme, an initiative of the ministry of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-infrastructuur-en-waterstaat">Infrastructuur en Waterstaat</entity> that has been running since 2010. The goal is to run more trains on busy routes. On some routes, this must result in a "metro-like" frequency of six trains per hour. Currently, most routes have only two to four per hour. Concrete structure as a tray To move the national monument, it is first lifted. A concrete structure will then be placed beneath the building to serve as a kind of tray. A sliding track will be installed under that structure, with which the building will be slid to its new location in steps of 40 centimeters. In total, 34 steps are needed; exactly 13.6 meters. The building will ultimately sit 32 centimeters lower than it does now. Taco Bresser, director of the company responsible for the move, told the Brabant regional broadcaster DTV Nieuws that the chance of something going wrong is small. The building is in good condition and the distance is relatively short. The building will nevertheless be continuously monitored with measuring equipment during the operation. If anything deviates or weather conditions are unfavorable, the move can be postponed. Place with a wartime past The fact that the station building is a national monument is related to the major role it played in the Second World War. The station was at that time a place for the transports of thousands of Jews and other prisoners to and from Camp Vught. Het Brabants Dagblad writes how station master Willem Jooren, who lived above the station, helped prisoners who were deported via Vught. He provided them with food, tobacco, warm clothing, and helped some escape. The station's basement played an important role in this. Jooren hid people there and thus helped them stay out of the hands of the Germans. Granddaughters Ageeth, Gerdie and Marianne looked into their grandfather's story and are glad that the station building, including the basement, will be preserved. In 1984, Jooren was posthumously awarded the Verzetsherdenkingskruis, a decoration for resistance fighters from the Second World War.

title: 'Ukraine pauses attacks on Russian oil refineries under pressure from Trump'
lead: Ukraine has temporarily stopped carrying out air strikes on Russian oil refineries after weeks of pressure from US President Trump. The Wall Street Journal reports this, based on sources familiar with the military operations. The decision has not been officially announced. The pause has been in effect since the start of last week and is expected to last until after the midterm elections in the United States or even longer. Relations between Ukraine and the US have sunk to a low point. Earlier this month Trump said it was time Ukraine got a new leader. A day before that, the US president announced he had reached an agreement with Russian President Putin on suspending sanctions and the supply of diesel. Starlink, the American satellite service of Elon Musk, also limited the speed of drones. Ukraine urgently needs the military version of Starlink, Starshield, to defend its territory. According to Musk, the Ukrainian army had violated the terms of use, but President Zelensky denied this. Russia and Ukraine have for months been attacking each other's energy supplies. Trump claimed earlier this month that Russia and Ukraine had agreed not to attack each other's energy targets for the time being. A few days later Ukraine resumed the attacks because, according to President Zelensky, Russia had not kept to the agreements. Deaths in Russian attacks: Last night one person died in Russian missile attacks in Kyiv. The attacks damaged buildings and caused fires, Mayor Klitschko reports. Earlier that day the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) reported that an employee of the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant had been killed in a Russian drone attack. IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi repeated his call for military restraint in the area around the nuclear facility.

title: 'Unworkable' and 'unfeasible', experts say of demands from right-wing parties
lead: <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> still cannot choose between left and right, so the opposition is putting pressure on the cabinet. JA21, SGP and BBB are putting demands on the table in exchange for support for the cabinet's tax plan. The most important demands concern migration, nitrogen and taxes. What exactly does the new alliance want, and are the demands feasible? Migration Unlike the previous cabinet, the Jetten cabinet wants to maintain the dispersal act, which distributes asylum seekers more evenly across municipalities. JA21, SGP and BBB believe that act should not be enforced: municipalities should be able to refuse an asylum seeker centre (azc) or reception facility. The parties also want the temporary status of Syrian refugees to be reassessed sooner, so that they can be sent back. And they want to see "concrete steps" in the short term on housing asylum seekers outside Europe, so that they can await the procedure there. "Many of the things written here seem practically unworkable," says associate professor of migration law Mark Klaassen (University of <entity id="org:gemeente-leiden">Leiden</entity>) about the parties' proposal. "The <entity id="org:immigratie-en-naturalisatiedienst">IND</entity> is already buried under a large mountain of applications and is currently not at all able to actively reassess Syrians. Then they would have to redo the entire procedure for these people." Not enforcing the dispersal act is in principle possible, says Klaassen. "But that will undermine municipalities' willingness to carry out the dispersal act. The minister does not have to apply administrative enforcement, but having no means of doing so at all will make municipalities less willing to comply with the obligation." Focusing on waiting for the asylum procedure abroad is already cabinet policy, Klaassen adds. "Whether that plan succeeds depends on the cooperation of countries outside Europe." Nitrogen The cabinet wants the agricultural sector to emit 42 to 46 percent less nitrogen in 2035 compared with 2019. This means, among other things, that dairy farmers may keep no more than 2.6 cows per hectare. JA21, SGP and BBB want to scrap this measure. The parties also want to raise the arithmetic lower limit, which concerns how much nitrogen may end up in nature, to 1 mol. That is 200 times higher than the current lower limit. "I assume these parties endorse the nitrogen targets, so that the country can get out of the lock," says Jan-Willem Erisman, professor of environment and sustainability (Leiden University). "But they are taking elements out of the plan without coming up with an alternative. With these proposals we will not get out of the nitrogen crisis." Taxes The parties want to get rid of the "freedom contribution", the extra tax on citizens to pay for investments in defence. In addition, they want tax relief for small and medium-sized enterprises in the Netherlands (MKB), and they want to address the tax gap between single-earner and dual-earner households. The parties do not explain where the money should come from. "What is in this letter is not concrete enough," says Bas Jacobs, professor of economics and public finance (Vrije Universiteit). "Correcting the tax burden for single-earner and dual-earner households involves many billions. The freedom contribution could also amount to an X number of billions. Tax relief for entrepreneurs in SMEs: hundreds of millions, if not billions as well." In general terms, the professor states that the parties are only concerned with serving their own constituencies. "Nobody feels responsible for the collective, for the treasury. That is becoming a problem, and the only way to solve it is to dare to take on pain too, and not just keep asking."

title: Incriminating material possibly shredded in Serbia as anti-corruption hunt begins
lead: It was already clear that Serbia's incoming leaders will have a tough time prosecuting their predecessors for corruption. But it may become even harder now that there are indications that government bodies are sending documents through the shredder. The country's highest prosecutor orders that the destruction must stop. In a statement she calls on prosecutors across the country to ensure that the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> intervenes and reports such practices. The destruction is punishable and she calls for any attempt to do so to be recorded. Her instruction is "urgent", she writes in capital letters. Evidently there is a rush: the prosecutor points to "findings and information" that documents are going through the shredder at state institutions, banks, security services and other important institutions. Party mood In recent days photos have surfaced of bags full of paper shreds, taken by employees of public services. It is not certain whether these really are remnants of sensitive documents. The claim that large sums of money are disappearing at a state bank has also not been proven. But concerns that <entity id="org:regering">de regering</entity> of former president Vucic is trying to clean up its act as much as possible while it still can are not coming out of nowhere. It is precisely the fight against corruption and cronyism, and the promise to prosecute those who have been guilty of it, that gave the Student List a resounding victory in Serbia's parliamentary elections on Sunday. Serbia is still in a mood of relief and celebration, but the students are not yet in power, and that will take a while. First of all, the elections in 53 polling stations spread across the country must be rerun because of irregularities. Voters can cast their votes again there on Sunday. The final result will be determined on that basis. After that, the president has thirty days to convene the new parliament. That president is Ana Brnabic, a loyal follower of Vucic who is temporarily holding the post after he resigned in September to be able to run in the parliamentary elections. She can drag things out by taking the full thirty days. After that a government must be in place within ninety days. Brnabic must also call presidential elections, which by law must take place before the end of the year. Editors-in-chief dismissed Meanwhile the old government remains in office, albeit in a caretaker capacity. The civil servants at the ministries are also still in their posts, as are the municipal authorities, which without exception are in the hands of Vucic's party. The country is thus in a kind of power vacuum, where it is clear which direction it is heading in, but not exactly when. Footage is circulating of citizens removing portraits of Vucic from government buildings and throwing them into rubbish containers. Some officials are choosing to get ahead of events. The director of public broadcaster <entity id="org:zbo-registratiecommissie-tandheelkundige-specialismen">RTS</entity> resigned, after first sacking the editors-in-chief and heads of various programmes. RTS had under Vucic turned into a state broadcaster. Yesterday, the main TV news bulletin paid no attention to Vucic for the first time in a long time. Today the presenter, on behalf of the broadcaster, apologised on air. "Dear viewers, these are the first steps towards, we hope, the recovery of RTS. This is the first apology for everything we have failed to do in recent times. We still have to work on the content of the programme. We want to restore your trust." Misconduct The students want the regulator to take steps against commercial broadcasters close to Vucic. They are said to have systematically broken the law. Presenters of news programmes there have suddenly disappeared without a trace. As a result, gaps are appearing in the programming. The students also call on media, government and state-owned company employees to report misconduct via a special email address. As whistleblowers they will enjoy legal protection, the students promise. There is good news for festival-goers: the Exit Festival, also popular among Dutch people, is returning to Serbia. This year it has for the first time moved to various locations abroad. The organisers were under political pressure because they openly supported the student protests in the country. In July it will take place again as it used to in the city of Novi Sad.

title: Wake-up call 30/10: Cabinet continues talks on budget • Vught station building moved
lead: Good morning! Today the Cabinet continues talks with various opposition combinations on the budget, and the Vught station building is being moved. First the weather: this morning it is at first grey with mist or low cloud in many places. This afternoon, mainly in the southern half of the country, there will also be regular sunshine, while further north it remains cloudy and misty for some time. Maximum temperatures are between 11 and 14 degrees with a moderate easterly wind at most. Are you going out today? Here you can find the overview of traffic jams and roadworks, and here you can see the situation on the railways. What can you expect today? What did you miss: In the elections in Israel, neither political bloc has won a majority in parliament after counting all the votes. The Central Elections Committee has announced this. Neither the governing coalition of Prime Minister Netanyahu nor the opposition bloc of Gadi Eisenkot reached at least 61 seats. The election result confirms that Netanyahu's Likud party has become the largest, with 27 seats. His coalition of right-conservative, far-right and religious parties won 53 seats and so falls 8 short of a majority in the 120-seat Knesset. In the 2022 elections the coalition still reached 64 seats. Netanyahu's rival, former army chief Gadi Eisenkot, won 21 seats with his party Yashar, founded last year, and so took second place. His opposition bloc stalled at 48 seats. Other news from the night: And then just this: British actor Patrick Stewart died yesterday at the age of 86. Stewart was a classically trained actor who made the Shakespeare repertoire his own. To the wider public he was mainly known for his role in the science fiction series Star Trek: The Next Generation and the superhero films of the X-Men series. A selection of Stewart's appearances in the Star Trek series: Have a nice day!

title: US tech companies seek money in Europe, risk for European companies
lead: Quarterly figures from American tech companies this week show that they need even more money to develop artificial intelligence (AI). They increasingly raise that money by issuing loans, first in dollars but now also in euros. That also brings a risk for European companies. Building data centres in particular costs a lot of money. Previously these hyperscalers, as the large American tech companies are also called, mainly used their own profits, but that is no longer sufficient. That is why they issue many bonds. These are loans with interest and an end date on which the total amount lent is repaid. And these technology companies are doing this increasingly in euros instead of dollars. This allows them to reach a new group of investors. Alphabet, the parent company of Google, was the first hyperscaler last year and issued two loans that together amounted to more than 13 billion euros, and another 9 billion euros this year. And this year Amazon also followed with the largest corporate bond ever issued in euros: 14.5 billion euros. That was reason for the European Central Bank to keep a close eye on this development. Crowding out. Companies react differently to this development than before, says Oana Furtuna, financial markets analyst at the European Central Bank. "For example, there are European companies that postpone issuing a loan when an American tech company does so, in order to avoid direct competition." In addition, it may be that investors buy these new bonds and can buy fewer from other lenders. That could lead to crowding out of European corporate bonds, ECB economists including Furtuna write. Companies would then have to offer a higher interest rate on a loan, and it becomes more expensive for them to raise money. Economist Tyrone Gunther of <entity id="org:zbo-de-nederlandsche-bank">De Nederlandsche Bank</entity> also sees this risk. "When a lot of debt suddenly comes to the market, you see investors asking for more interest when they lend money. So it becomes more expensive for companies to borrow." Both economists do stress that this is not yet an issue in Europe. But in the US it is a different story. Chair of the American central bank Kevin Warsh recently expressed concerns about tech companies issuing loans. According to him, the rapid increase is one of the factors behind higher interest rates in the US. Debt mountain. Still, Furtuna thinks the arrival of these euro bonds may also bring advantages. In the European Union there are still only few technology companies issuing bonds on this scale. And these are often loans with a very long term. The choice for investors thus becomes greater. "In general, investors are certainly pleased with that", says chief strategist at Achmea Investment Management, Thomas van Galen. The arrival of these euro bonds also has another advantage, according to him. Many large European investors use bonds issued in euros to reduce certain interest rate risks. "The pond of bonds that investors fish in is thus better stocked", says Van Galen. The wave of debt that hyperscalers are now issuing comes at a time when governments face high financing costs. Interest rates on government bonds of the US, but also France, Germany and the United Kingdom, are rising to levels not seen in 25 years. That also affects investors' choices. "If you have the choice between a French government bond or a bond from a hyperscaler, then it is no longer a given that the government loan is the safer investment", says Van Galen. Now that AI companies increasingly issue long-term loans, the question arises whether investors will swap their government bonds for bonds from tech companies. Then it would become more expensive for governments to borrow. Although some analysts on Wall Street claim this, there is as yet no clear evidence for it.

title: Number of first asylum applications falls in third quarter
lead: The number of first asylum applications in the third quarter of 2026 fell by 13 percent compared with the same period a year earlier. That is what the <entity id="org:zbo-centraal-bureau-voor-de-statistiek">Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek</entity> (CBS) reports, based on provisional figures from the <entity id="org:immigratie-en-naturalisatiedienst">Immigratie- en Naturalisatiedienst</entity> (IND). In the third quarter, which runs from 1 July through 30 September, almost 5900 people applied for asylum for the first time. That is 850 fewer than in 2025. Mainly Eritreans and Syrians made fewer applications. They accounted for 480 applications from Eritreans and 470 from Syrians, about half as many as a year earlier. Even so, the number of first asylum applications in the first nine months of 2026 is still 8 percent higher than in the same period of 2025. European Asylum and Migration Pact Since 12 June the European Asylum and Migration Pact applies, with as its main aim to reduce the number of migrants who enter the EU illegally and to gain more control over the asylum influx. The third quarter is therefore the first full quarter since the pact was introduced. The IND has also changed the way it works. Staff must now process asylum applications within six months, whereas that procedure often took about two years before. To make this possible, the procedure has been simplified. Vluchtelingenwerk Nederland and asylum lawyers warned that the procedure is indeed faster, but that this comes at the expense of care and quality . Especially vulnerable asylum seekers run risks as a result. Fewer family reunification migrants According to the CBS figures, in the third quarter 3200 family members of status holders came to the Netherlands. That is considerably fewer than in the third quarter of 2025, when 4700 family reunification migrants came to the Netherlands. About 70 percent of them came from Syria. The number of family reunification migrants over the whole of 2026 is almost equal to last year. Separately from the European Asylum and Migration Pact, the two-status system was also introduced on 12 June of this year, which aims to relieve the Dutch asylum chain and reduce the inflow of asylum seekers and family reunification migrants. A and B status That system distinguishes between refugees with an A status and people with a B status, for example people who fled war. Asylum seekers without a fixed refugee status (who have B status) may now only bring their family over after two years. Under the new rules they also must first have housing, have enough money to support their family, and family reunification is limited to the core family. Whether the decline in the number of asylum applications is related to the introduction of the new rules is unclear. Neither the CBS nor the IND can confirm that link, news agency ANP reports.

title: Two cats abandoned in neighbourhood cupboard: 'I'm sorry I did it this way'
lead: In a neighbourhood cupboard in Leusden, no food or hygiene products were left, but two cats. A handwritten note from the former owner was enclosed. In it, the person states that they do not have the money to pay the medical costs and see no other way out. It concerns two animals from the same litter. "I hope they can stay together. I'm sorry I did it this way." The cats are called Mikasa and Ashoka, the owner further writes, and they are not microchipped or neutered.
