There have also been talks with creditors and, according to the board, there is a prospect of an agreement. More clarity on this is likely within two weeks. "An agreement is a condition for being able to continue working on the future," the WEC said. The construction of the WEC cost 43.7 million euros at the time, 17.4 million more than budgeted. The doors opened in April 2025, but visitor numbers subsequently disappointed. As a result, the WEC's debt rose to around 2.8 million euros, an amount the centre cannot simply scrape together itself. The income from, among other things, entrance fees is roughly equal to the costs incurred. Great support from society The seal centre announced on 12 October that its survival was at stake and that it risked going bankrupt within two weeks. The WEC had placed all its hopes on financial support from the municipality of <entity id="org:gemeente-het-hogeland">Het Hogeland</entity> and the <entity id="org:provincie-groningen">provincie Groningen</entity>, but they let it be known they would not give money. Since the cry for help, supporters of keeping the centre are taking action. Donations are pouring in and there are many fundraising and sponsorship campaigns. Partners of the centre also want it to stay open, writes RTV Noord. Among others, WWF-NL, Visit Wadden, the University of Groningen and seal wardens sent letters of support to the municipality and province. The WEC says today that it is "deeply moved" by the support it has received so far, and says it will put "all its time and energy" into finding a solution.

title: Ten years on, more darkness in the Wadden area, but the battle is not yet won
lead: It is ten years this week since dozens of organisations agreed to better protect the darkness in the Wadden area. In that time a lot of steps have been taken, experts say, but there is still much to be gained. In October 2016, 43 parties, ranging from the central government and <entity id="org:zbo-staatsbosbeheer">Staatsbosbeheer</entity> to all kinds of nature organisations, signed a letter of intent called Dark Sky Werelderfgoed Waddengebied. Since then the partnership has worked to combat light pollution in the Wadden area and to preserve the darkness. This concerns 'excess' artificial light: outdoor lighting, advertising, illuminated logos and light in offices. According to ecologists, light pollution can disrupt the biorhythm of animals and plants. In addition, excess light makes the stars and planets less visible. Steps taken An de Wrede of the Friese Milieu Federatie, an umbrella organisation working for Frisian nature, sees that along various parts of the coast lighting is being used more consciously. "I'm thinking for example of the harbour in <entity id="org:gemeente-harlingen">Harlingen</entity>, or of the islands where green lampposts stand," she tells Omrop <entity id="org:provincie-fryslan">Fryslân</entity>. But according to De Wrede, it could be much better. One of the biggest problems is the growing number of business parks, she explains. New buildings, car parks, advertising and outdoor lighting also mean new light sources. Room for improvement That there is still room for improvement is also the view of Jorian Moree, a cultural geographer specialising in climate adaptation. He has been involved in projects aimed at reducing light pollution in recent years. According to Moree, habit and convenience play an important role. It is easier to switch on all the lights at once than to investigate for each building or site how many lamps are really needed. "There is still much to be gained there." One of the places in the Wadden area where a lot of excess light was found at night was the harbour in Lauwersoog. Researchers looked at how many lampposts, floodlights and illuminated buildings there actually were in the harbour area. That produced striking examples. Quays where no ship was moored at night were fully lit. In restaurants or buildings by the fish auction that had been closed for hours, all the lights were still on. In 2023 the entrepreneurs decided to do something about the light pollution in the harbour. With the so-called Donkerte masterplan, they want to cut light emissions by 50 percent within three years. A dark harbour would also have positive effects for the Lauwersmeer National Park right nearby. Lighting was adjusted or made dimmable. In other places, motion sensors were installed, so lamps only come on when someone is actually present. Milky Way visible During the Nacht van de Nacht, a yearly campaign in 2024 in which municipalities, businesses and households switch off their lights at night to draw attention to light pollution, it became clear how much effect the changes in Lauwersoog had. <entity id="org:rijkswaterstaat">Rijkswaterstaat</entity> and shipping company Wagenborg were asked to switch off as much lighting in the harbour as possible for one hour. "When the cloud cover cleared, the Milky Way became visible above Lauwersoog," says project leader Klaas Laansma of the Donkerte plan. "Measurements by researchers at the University of <entity id="org:gemeente-groningen">Groningen</entity> show that there is now less light."

title: The Hague braces itself: shopkeepers board up their shops out of fear of riots
lead: Out of fear of what tomorrow may bring, a considerable number of Hague shopkeepers began boarding up their shop fronts today. They are playing it safe and do not seem willing to wait and see whether the disturbing reports circulating on social media become reality. Via platforms such as Snapchat, Telegram and Instagram, calls have been made to take to the streets in various Dutch cities to protest. There are fears this will escalate into riots and looting, although it is unclear who or which organisation is behind the calls. It is also difficult to estimate how many people will turn out. Apple store already empty That no protest has been registered with the municipality of The Hague does not seem to concern the entrepreneurs there. In France, Belgium and Italy, demonstrations recently escalated into large-scale riots, in which many shops were vandalised and looted. The fear after all the reports on social media is that The Hague is next. Anyone walking through the city centre immediately sees all the precautionary measures taken. Among others, the Tommy Hilfiger shop, the Lego store, a branch of fashion brand Guess, a Kruidvat outlet, a jeweller and the local kitchenware shop have been barricaded. Some shopkeepers have even announced they will stay closed so their staff can stay home. The Hague Apple store has chosen to clear out the premises in advance. Images show there is no phone or laptop left anywhere in the store. A group of carpenters is busy with the preparations. That The Hague shopkeepers are choosing to board up their premises seems to earn understanding from the shopping public who were in the centre today. "It is something you don't expect in the Netherlands. It is un-Dutch," says a woman to Omroep West. "If I were a shopkeeper here, I would rather spend a few thousand euros on preparation than later face tens of thousands in damage and have my shop looted," her husband adds. The chairman of the shopkeepers' association says several entrepreneurs have been threatened by phone. "They were told their shop would be cleaned out tomorrow." 'It can happen quickly' A carpenter who is boarding up a perfumery explains how he goes about building the barricade. The skirting boards in front of the shop fronts have been removed, wooden posts have been placed, and then plenty of wood has been screwed against the shop front. Whether this keeps potential rioters out? "They get through everywhere, but we're trying to stop them." Meanwhile there is still hope that all the precautionary measures will turn out to have been unnecessary after all. One shopkeeper says: "Hopefully nothing at all will happen tomorrow, but with social media it can happen very quickly."

title: German media: arrest of former intelligence chief puts cooperation with US under pressure
lead: US intelligence services have warned Germany's foreign intelligence service BND that cooperation could be revised. That is according to research by German broadcasters WDR, NDR and daily SZ. The warning followed the arrest of former BND head August Hanning. Within the BND, the warning is causing great concern and unrest. Managers have reportedly been instructed to report any changes in the cooperation immediately. The US is Germany's most important intelligence partner. The US says it will still continue to provide information in urgent cases, such as terrorist attacks. It is unclear which information is no longer being provided. Several BND employees have told German media that they have the impression the Americans are sharing less information and that its quality has declined. According to sources within the German government, cooperation is still proceeding normally. According to the German broadcasters, the BND and the American embassy do not wish to respond on substance. Arrests Hanning and his chief of staff Manfred D. were arrested separately on 6 October. The 80-year-old Hanning headed the BND from 1998 to 2005. He is suspected, among other things, of espionage, obtaining state secrets and treason. D. was still working for the German secret service until this spring. Hanning reportedly had access to the service's secret documents for years with D.'s help and used them to draw up a security analysis for a foreign intelligence service. D. is suspected of complicity in treason. He allegedly helped Hanning for years to gather secret information. D. worked as personal assistant to four BND heads and therefore had close ties to the top of the service. He may therefore have been checked less strictly. House search According to German media, police reportedly seized hundreds of additional documents at Hanning's home. An earlier house search had already found 2000 secret documents. These reportedly included reports on Iran's nuclear programme and the Russian army. The additional documents are now being examined. Witnesses are also being questioned. The BND is conducting an internal investigation into how the alleged espionage could take place for years. Hanning denies the accusations.

title: Group photo at G20 summit cancelled, countries do not want to be photographed with Russia
lead: The traditional group photo at the G20 summit in the United States did not go ahead because of the presence of Russian minister Lavrov of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-buitenlandse-zaken">Buitenlandse Zaken</entity>. The American government decided to drop the photo moment because other attendees threatened a boycott. Delegations from a number of countries that support Ukraine, including Canada and Australia, did not want to be in the 'family photo' with Sergei Lavrov in Atlanta, the photo with all participants of a summit. A number of delegations even threatened to walk away, writes the American news channel CNN. European officials still thought that two separate photos might be made, one with Lavrov and one without him. When that proved not to be the case, the American Secretary of State decided to forego it, because he did not want the summit to be overshadowed by a photo row, say involved American diplomats to news agency AP. Chance to talk Lavrov responded calmly to the controversy. "If it is mainly important to you how you stand in the photo and who you stand next to, then that says enough." He repeated the Russian position that it is mainly European hostility towards Russia that stands in the way of peace negotiations. German minister Wadephul acknowledged that Lavrov's visit to the summit was controversial, but also called it an opportunity to keep pressing for peace in Ukraine. "It is really time to end hostilities and discuss how this conflict can be resolved." Whether agreement will be reached on that is still an open question: analysts fear that, because of mutual disagreement on important issues, not even agreement on a joint closing statement will be reached. Besides Ukraine, the agenda also included, among other things, the American war with Iran and China's influence in Asia. Putin invitation Minister Lavrov warned that the recent rapprochement between the US and his country does not mean the air has cleared. Trump may have scrapped diesel sanctions because of high fuel prices, but other sanctions are still in force. "The underlying questions have not been resolved", Lavrov believes. "No real steps have been taken in the relationship with the US. Don't harbour any illusions about the diesel deal.' The G20 consists of the nineteen countries with the largest economies, the European Union and the African Union. This summit was a preparation for a meeting of heads of government next month in Florida. President Trump has also invited his Russian counterpart Putin to that, but it is not yet clear whether he will come. Lavrov said afterwards that he had had a pleasant conversation with American minister Rubio. Only briefly, "because as host he also had other commitments", the Russian said.

title: Leo XIV first pope to vote in American elections
lead: Pope Leo has voted by letter in the American elections. As far as is known, this is the first time a pope has cast a vote in a country's elections. Leo describes this in a statement as an important civic duty. "The Holy Father considers it important to underline the right and duty of every citizen to take part in the democratic process", the Vatican said in a statement. "In line with his long habit of active citizenship, he voted by mail in Chicago." The 71-year-old Robert Francis Prevost, as the pope was called before his election, was born in the US. He still holds American citizenship and, after years of mission work in South America, also has a Peruvian passport. Not lost That he is head of state of another nation as pope is not necessarily a problem for voting. The US Department of State says that by accepting such a position a person does not automatically lose US citizenship, although it may be "actively examined" if someone accepts a position as head of state, head of government or minister. Leo cast his vote in his birth state of Illinois. Among other things, the future of Democratic governor Pritzker is at stake there, and a successor is being sought for Democratic senator Durbin. 'Right and duty' As far as is known, this is the first time a pope has voted in an election in his country of birth. It has never been reported that John Paul II, Benedict XVI and Francis voted in their countries of birth, respectively Poland, Germany and Argentina. Nor is it known that the Italian popes who came before them in the centuries before contributed to secular elections. A spokesperson did not want to say whom Leo voted for. In the past Prevost did switch parties now and then: he voted in the Democratic primaries in 2008 and 2010, but requested a ballot for the Republican primaries in 2012, 2014 and 2016. According to the Vatican, he "as an American citizen has always voted when he was entitled to do so". Leo has a strained relationship with the leader of his birth country. Donald Trump criticised him after he called for peace in the Middle East. The president then called the first American pope a weakling and a radical leftist. It cannot have cost him Leo's vote in next Tuesday's elections, because no presidential election is being held. Listen to our podcasts about the midterms in the US In the run-up to the midterms on 3 November, the NOS colleagues at Bureau Washington are making new episodes of the podcast Amerika Kiest. Listen to them via NPO Luister or via another audio platform

title: Call of Duty removes real footage of Korean disaster from game
lead: Game maker Activision is removing footage of a Korean disaster from the game Call of Duty . Relatives were shocked that real footage of a deadly crush had been used for the game. It concerned short clips of an incident in 2022 in the Itaewon district of Seoul. There, 160 people were crushed to death in a crowd during a Halloween party. After the long coronavirus lockdowns, partygoers had flocked there in large numbers, which in narrow streets led to the tragedy. The footage was used by Activision to set the atmosphere in the game Modern Warfare 4 . It centres on a North Korean invasion of South Korea. Apologies Activision takes the criticism to heart and says it will remove the footage with the next update of the game, on 12 November. The company says it never wanted to make a connection with the Itaewon disaster and also did not want to trivialise the suffering there. The game maker says it apologises to aggrieved relatives. A victims' group says it has not yet had direct contact with Activision. In South Korea there is also broader criticism of the game, from people who find a fictional war with North Korea distasteful at a time when relations with the country are so bad.

title: Evacuees from Olesjky arrive in Crimea: 'Finally peace, we were starving'
lead: The convoy meant to bring residents of the Ukrainian city of Olesjky to safety has arrived in Crimea, which Russia occupies. Footage showed late in the afternoon the column of buses driving across the peninsula towards Russia. Russia and Ukraine had agreed, after mediation by Pope Leo and the American first lady Melania Trump, on a ceasefire of several days to make the evacuation possible. Emotional, residents of the city received the buses and ambulances that make their departure possible this morning: 'Yesterday my daughter said: Don't you dare change your mind!' 'No, no,' I replied, 'my bags are already packed, I am leaving', said a woman whose children had already fled the city earlier. 'I am leaving because I have missed them so much.' Rare cooperation Olesjky, in the south of Ukraine, was already occupied on the first day of the Russian invasion in 2022 and has since been under heavy fire as a front-line city. Fighting continues daily, snipers, mines and drones threaten the population. Of the originally 20,000 residents, an estimated only about 2,000 remained behind. The convoy of 25 buses and 9 ambulances could take about 750 of them. It is not clear how many people actually left; on the Ukrainian side, several hundred are mentioned. For those who stayed behind, the convoy left food, medicine and fuel. Notably, representatives of Russia and Ukraine cooperated in this, a very unusual sight in the war. Two people died 'Finally peace, we were starving', said a resident with tears in his eyes when the buses with aid arrived yesterday morning. 'We had only courgette, tomatoes and wild greens, nothing else at all.' A young man who was taken away in an ambulance said yesterday that he had been seriously wounded by a landmine. 'We had not seen it, because of my father's poor eyesight. My legs could be saved, but my father died.' According to the spokesperson for the Kremlin, two people died during the evacuation, including a Russian sapper who removed mines on the routes towards the evacuation point. The convoy left Olesjky heading south, towards Crimea, which Russia has occupied since 2014. From there it continues to the Russian city of Anapa. People may choose to stay there, or they can board a flight to Belarus, to travel from there to northern Ukraine. The total journey is then 1,500 kilometres, while the front lies a stone's throw from Olesjky. On Russian state television a conversation was broadcast with someone from Olesjky who plans to stay in Russia. 'I want peace and quiet. Somewhere you can live as a human being again, not the way we lived these past years.' Another, on the other hand, says he wants to travel on to Ukraine, speaking to Ukrainian TV. 'My family is in Ukraine, children and grandchildren. I have not seen them for five years and I miss them so much. They are waiting for me, they are counting the hours until I arrive.' Some of those left behind distrusted the detour the convoy takes through Russia. 'People are scared, scared of Russia.' Simply crossing the river would have been better, she said. 'I want to go to Ukraine, my children are waiting there. But I am staying with my husband. He cannot fly.' Another said she did not want to leave her birthplace, although she called life in the city a nightmare. 'My parents were born here, my grandparents, great-grandparents, everyone.' 'It is their own choice, but we will do what we can to provide humanitarian aid', responded the Ukrainian escort to the reports from those left behind. His Russian counterpart later said that the convoy's journey had gone without problems. The Kremlin did, however, warn against too much optimism about this successful cooperation. 'This is a standalone situation that you cannot simply translate to the broader process at this moment.' The war in the rest of the country therefore continued unabated. In a drone attack on a train platform in Dnipro, at least fifteen people were killed and several others were injured. Elsewhere too, people were again killed and wounded in the past day.

title: Endangered French zoo monkeys recovered after theft
lead: In France eleven monkeys have been found that were taken a few days ago during a break-in at a zoo. Two other animals have not yet been found. They are marmosets and several pinché tamarins, a species threatened with extinction. In the night from Monday to Tuesday they were stolen from the zoo in Lescar, in the south-west of France. The thieves forced doors open with a chisel and smashed a window with a crowbar. Although the animal park has night watchmen and camera surveillance, the theft was only discovered the next morning. Even so, the police quickly got onto several suspects. Three people have been arrested. The suspicion is that they wanted to sell the animals on the black market for a lot of money. The animals had once been placed in the park after being seized from animal smugglers. Good health The zoo says it is happy with the return of the monkeys. 'They are a bit traumatised, but otherwise in good health', the park writes. 'Feel free to come and see them.' The park hopes that the last two animals will also be found thanks to the police investigation.

title: Ebola death toll in Congo rises to over 5,000
lead: The Ebola outbreak in Congo has now claimed the lives of 5,000 people, health services in the country report. Earlier this week it was already reported that the disease has been officially confirmed in just over 10,000 people. The outbreak, first noticed in May, is the second deadliest outbreak of the virus ever. Only in Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone did more people die between 2014 and 2016, about 11,000 of the 28,600 people who became infected. Experts this week still did not dare to make a prediction about how this epidemic will develop. The good news is that the number of cases is not increasing exponentially: in recent weeks a stable number of 400 to 500 infections has been recorded. "That is a plateau", says research physician Boghuma Titanji to news agency AP. "But a high plateau." She also considers it worrying that the figures are not yet declining. Out of sight In addition, the figures on new infections show that only a quarter of the new cases come from people found through contact tracing of other patients. This means that by far the largest part of new patients became infected through people who were not yet known to healthcare workers. Ebola can spread through contact with infected body fluids, such as blood, saliva or sweat. No vaccine is yet available against this variant. Experts hope one will be available next year so the outbreak can then be brought under control. Infections have now been confirmed in four countries: in addition to Congo, also neighbouring Kenya and Uganda, and Nigeria in West Africa. Efforts to combat the disease are hampered by the inadequate healthcare there, but also by distrust of healthcare workers and conflicts in the region.

title: British prime minister open to discussing apology for slavery, but rules out reparations
lead: British Prime Minister Burnham is open to a conversation about apologies for the history of slavery, but he does not support reparations. He writes this in an opinion piece in The Guardian. The subject is once again prominent on the agenda during King Charles's current tour of the Caribbean. Labour Prime Minister Burnham writes that "for years there has been a call for a sincere conversation about the legacy of slavery" within the Commonwealth. Many of the 56 states in that association were formerly colonies of the United Kingdom where slavery was permitted. Burnham believes that "we have damaged the functioning of the Commonwealth by burying our heads in the sand". "That is why we are going to engage in structured talks with those affected by the trans-Atlantic slave trade. Attention to the call for apologies on behalf of the British state will be an important part of that, and I am open to it." Tightening ties That commitment goes further than the British government has been willing to go so far. Although then prime minister Blair expressed deep sorrow and regret in 2007, full apologies on behalf of the British government never came. Conservative prime minister Sunak said in 2023 that "reviewing our history is no way forward", and Burnham's party colleague and direct predecessor Starmer also said that "history cannot be changed". Burnham now acknowledges that the consequences of slavery "still influence our world". He thinks the relationship with other countries within the Commonwealth suffers because of the issue, but that by engaging in the "difficult conversation" about it, the mutual bond can be strengthened. However, he still rejects reparations. "That does not seem to me to be the right answer. I do not believe the British people of today can be held responsible for historical wrongs, however serious, that occurred in another time with other laws." Looking into debts He does want to look into whether something can be done about the debts under which many of the countries are struggling. He is thinking of a longer term or a lower interest rate. He has asked former prime minister Gordon Brown to focus on that. Prime Minister Mia Mottley of Commonwealth country Barbados welcomes dialogue, but sticks to the demand for reparations. "Conversations are important because we do not yet think the same about everything, especially when it comes to reparations. We will keep saying that clearly and respectfully, but a sincere disagreement on some themes should not stand in the way of progress on others." Execution site The British gesture comes at a time when King Charles is undertaking a sensitive trip through several Commonwealth countries in the Caribbean. From tomorrow he will attend the Commonwealth conference together with Burnham, where the legacy of slavery is also on the agenda. Yesterday in Guyana Charles visited the site where a slave uprising in 1823 was brutally suppressed by British plantation owners. The king, among other things, took a look at the place where dozens of defeated freedom fighters were executed. He did not publicly speak about his impressions there. Such remarks would also be sensitive because of ministerial responsibility. According to the BBC, at other visits later in the day there was "a small but loud group of protesters" who wanted to draw attention to apologies and reparations.

title: Podcast De Dag: tons of subsidy for a film that never reached the big screen
lead: A star cast with Oscar winners Dustin Hoffman and Helen Hunt, beautiful footage in palazzos in the Italian town of Lucca, and all of it under the direction of the respected and well-known director Peter Greenaway; the film Lucca Mortis has it all. The <entity id="org:zbo-stichting-nederlands-fonds-voor-de-film">Nederlands Filmfonds</entity> puts in more than five tons in subsidy, to help Dutch makers involved in the film. Listen here: You can listen to this episode of De Dag via <entity id="org:zbo-nederlandse-publieke-omroep">NPO</entity> Luister and all other podcast apps . Do you like it? Then don't forget to subscribe. But a few years after filming, the film has ended in a tragedy. Nieuwsuur reporter Fleur Damen looked into it and made a reconstruction together with NRC. Shooting days did not go ahead because the actors and crew were not paid, post-production is on hold because invoices were not transferred, and director Greenaway is no longer involved in the film. The Filmfonds says it knows nothing about this and maintains confidence that Lucca Mortis will appear on the big screen. What does that say about making these kinds of films with subsidies? Reactions: email to dedag@nos.nl Presentation & editing: Marco Geijtenbeek Editorial: Marco Geijtenbeek & Judith van de Hulsbeek

title: Wake-up call 31/10: Anti-government protests in several countries • Five Eredivisie matches, including Ajax-AZ
lead: Good morning! In several countries people are demonstrating again today against the policy of the national <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity>. People have also been called to protest in the Netherlands on social media. Football is also being played today: five matches are on the programme in the Eredivisie. Leaders Feyenoord play Fortuna Sittard, and number 2 Ajax host number 5 AZ. First the weather: cloudy and somewhat misty. In the south there will be sun now and then this afternoon. It will be around 12 degrees. Are you going out today? Here you can find the overview of traffic jams and roadworks, and here you can see the situation on the railways. What can you expect today? What did you miss: An evacuation convoy from the Ukrainian city of Olejsky has safely reached the Crimea, which is occupied by Russia. Residents of the besieged front-line city were brought to safety by buses and ambulances. Most residents there had already fled earlier, but an estimated 2000 were still left behind. The residents were living in dire conditions, with almost no supplies and a constant threat from drones, mines and snipers. Russia and Ukraine had agreed a ceasefire to make the evacuation possible, after mediation by Pope Leo and the American first lady Melania Trump. According to Ukraine, several hundred people made use of it. Other news from the night: And finally this: In the Zeeland capital Middelburg as many as 42,000 little lights are hanging on a house for Halloween. The light spectacle by Bob Rijnaard is a great success. It started out as a bit of fun, but it has now grown into a real happening with lights, lasers and sound effects. The whole neighbourhood helps, and children in particular are wildly enthusiastic. Have a great day!

title: Terminally ill professor Jan Rotmans has an 'AI twin' made of himself
lead: Giving lectures and answering questions, even when he is no longer there. That is what a digital version of professor Jan Rotmans (65) should be able to do one day. The terminally ill scientist is having a "digital twin" built with artificial intelligence. In this way his knowledge of social change is to be passed on to future generations. There is criticism too. Rotmans says he is the first Dutch professor to have such a "digital twin" built. He is having his avatar built by studio The Synths, which previously developed a digital likeness of Ruud Gullit. The professor is regarded as a pioneer in the field of climate models and system change. His dozens of books, hundreds of scientific publications and lectures will form the basis of his avatar. "Last week everything about me was recorded: sound, image, voice and facial expressions. In the coming months a version that looks very lifelike will be made," Rotmans tells the NOS. The first version should be available online by the end of the year. Later a hologram is to follow as well, which can walk across a stage. "That way I can still be in places where I am no longer." Metastatic prostate cancer A factor here: Rotmans has had metastatic prostate cancer for almost two years. In 2024 doctors still gave him five years. Under the circumstances he is doing well. "I am very active. The outlook is better than a few years ago and the most recent tests were encouraging." Rotmans hopes in the time ahead to be able to learn from his "AI clone". In this way he wants to talk with his digital likeness about problems he has been warning about for some time. What if the internet went down for two weeks, for example? "I don't rule out that my avatar will offer solutions that I myself do not have." AI professor on the plan: 'Very undesirable' Iris van Rooij, AI professor at Radboud University, calls it "a very undesirable development". She calls the application "a direct consequence of the AI hype, a form of dehumanisation". A static model of text and images is not a human being, she stresses. "The model itself is inherently meaningless: it is whatever the reader or listener attributes to it. People attribute all sorts of things to bots, such as intelligence, thinking and emotions, or social relationships. But a digital conversation partner is nothing more than a scam." Van Rooij says she understands, in her own words, the wish to leave behind knowledge and insights, and to want to inspire future generations. "But we already have media for that, with books, articles, videos, et cetera. And exactly those media are being used to build statistical models. Why should a machine made of AI slop (mass-produced digital junk, ed.) be put between them by a commercial company? I would very much like it, when I am no longer here, for people to read my articles and books. For people to do that on the basis of my own words, which I chose carefully, in the zeitgeist and context in which I wrote them, and on that basis try to understand my insights and ideas." Rotmans stresses that this is not yet the case. "The AI I use now is all logical and mostly based on things I have done and said before. Above all I hope that soon things will come out that also surprise me." His avatar could give answers that are not correct, make claims Rotmans does not stand behind, or spread disinformation. "That is why we are testing it extensively to remove mistakes," he says. Rotmans wants to assess new insights that his digital twin gains himself first. And when that is no longer possible, he trusts that other people will do so. "The way Wikipedia works, for example, where people correct each other." He is not afraid of misuse. "Climate deniers have already misused my insights and articles and used my knowledge in a way that undermines authority. I would rather be a frontrunner, because then I still have it in my own hands. And if this goes wrong, I can warn people. I accept the risk attached to it." Not a replacement Rotmans says his AI twin should explicitly not become a personal replacement. "My wife also says: I am not going to sleep next to such an AI avatar. The digital twin is being trained so that it will not answer strange questions, or say anything about things I have nothing sensible to say about." He expects other scientists to quickly follow his example and that within 25 years almost everyone will have such a digital twin. "Almost no one is enthusiastic. For me that is a good sign. If I try something new and everyone is enthusiastic, then I start to doubt, because it probably isn't innovative enough. When many people are sceptical, I know I am on the right track." title: Hebron largely sealed off for more than a week, thousands of Palestinians expelled
lead: The city of Hebron in the occupied West Bank has been largely sealed off by the Israeli army for more than a week. Thousands of Palestinians have been expelled and the army is demolishing homes there. It is a response to the shooting at a checkpoint near the city in which two Israeli soldiers were killed last week. "Some residents are staying with friends or family, others have become homeless," says Palestinian human rights activist Issa Amro on the phone. He lives in Hebron. "Some people have tried to go back home over the past days, for example to fetch warm clothes because of the rain. But the army has refused that." It concerns partly children, pregnant women, elderly people and the sick, he stresses. The Israeli army has kept the access roads to and from Hebron closed since last Friday and has since been besieging two neighbourhoods in the city. According to the Hebron municipality, around 5000 Palestinians are trapped in their homes or have been forced to leave their homes. Shooting at checkpoint Last week two Palestinian men opened fire at a military checkpoint west of the city of Hebron. Two Israeli soldiers were killed and three others were injured. The two shooters were shot dead by the Israeli army during the firefight. According to the army, the shooters planned to carry out a larger attack on Israeli civilians on a nearby motorway. When that did not succeed, they reportedly opened fire at the checkpoint. The Israeli army's account has not been independently confirmed. Homes demolished Prime Minister Netanyahu announced that same day a large-scale attack by the Israeli army. "We will take action to destroy this place, to completely change it," he said, referring to the neighbourhoods where the shooters lived. He also refers to the refugee camps in the north of the occupied West Bank. There, the Israeli army carried out large-scale attacks with ground troops and airstrikes at the beginning of 2025. Homes and roads were then destroyed and tens of thousands of Palestinians were displaced. "The army has demolished several homes and shops in the neighbourhoods it is currently besieging over the past week," says activist Amro. "Other buildings are being marked in preparation for demolition." News agency Reuters shared footage last week showing the army demolishing buildings in Hebron with bulldozers. In addition, the Israeli army itself released footage yesterday of the destruction of two homes with explosives. According to the army, these are the homes of the attackers. Olive harvest season Meanwhile, the terror by settlers continues. The olive harvest season is in full swing, a period in which settler attacks increase every year. According to human rights organisations, the army often does not do enough to stop the attacks. Amro had just returned from the Tel Rumeida neighbourhood during the phone interview, where a group of settlers attacked a Palestinian family. "They were picking olives together when they were beaten up by settlers." He says three of the five victims were injured so badly that they were taken to hospital. Attacks by settlers also took place in other locations in the occupied West Bank in recent days, including near Ramallah, Nablus and Bethlehem. Israeli elections In Israel, parliamentary elections were held on Tuesday. While the situation in the West Bank and the fate of the Palestinians was not an important election theme, Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu's main challenger, promises that he wants to tackle settler violence. Eisenkot spoke two weeks ago of "Jewish terror" after European diplomats were attacked by settlers. The elections have not produced a clear winner, so it is still an open question whether Eisenkot can become prime minister. Still, Amro thinks it makes little difference who comes to power. "It may change the tactics or the timing, but the suffering of the Palestinians will continue." According to him, Israeli policy is aimed at making the situation in the West Bank so unbearable that Palestinians leave. According to Amro, only serious sanctions and intervention by other countries can actually move the Israeli government to change course.

title: France braces for 'Halloween' protests
lead: In France, the ongoing protests are further sharpening the already deep rift between radical left and radical right. As the country prepares today for the third major protest weekend in a row, the dynamics of the demonstrations are changing. Alongside dissatisfaction over education and the rising cost of living, for some protesters there is a new reason to take to the streets: resistance to racism and the far right. This is entirely linked to the racist terrorist attack in the Paris suburb of Trappes last Friday. In it, 26-year-old Pengo Bossio Wangi was killed and seven others were injured, including an 11-year-old girl. Suspect Kevin T. this week acknowledged having had a racist and Islamophobic motive. A special anti-terrorism prosecutor's office has started a judicial investigation. Last week there were already various commemorative gatherings and demonstrations in and around Paris. According to critics, the attack was the result of a breeding ground for racism that is fuelled by radical right parties and news channels. This theme is expected to come up often at today's protests. "There are political movements that are ensuring that far-right ideas are increasingly gaining ground," President Macron also said this week in an interview with the HugoDécrypte news medium, which is popular among young people. Macron cited as an example the Rassemblement National, the radical right party whose leader Marine Le Pen is at the top of the polls to succeed him. The French president also expressed criticism of the party on the other side of the political spectrum: the radical left La France Insoumise (LFI). The party supported the pupils' protests of recent weeks and received much criticism for this. Macron said he deplored that some LFI party members condone the use of violence. LFI members had joined a demonstration against a conference by activist group Objectif Remigration. In far-right circles, remigration is a euphemism for the mass expulsion of foreigners. The controversial conference was due to take place today in a Paris suburb, but has been banned out of fear of disturbances. The counter-demonstration at the congress centre is also not allowed to go ahead. Another demonstration by Objectif Remigration itself, planned for tomorrow, is also banned. Meanwhile, both LFI and the Rassemblement National are profiting from the protests that have got out of hand. While these two parties are gaining ground in the polls on the flanks, the traditional centre parties are coming under increasing pressure. That the unrest in France has still not disappeared is also evident from posts on social media. Inspired by the elections in Brazil, the action On bloque l'extrême droite (We block the far right) was launched this week, in which accounts and posts from far-right accounts on social media are blocked. In this way the initiators hope to influence the algorithm such that the visibility and spread of posts with far-right ideas on social media decreases. In this way they hope to exert influence on the political debate leading up to the presidential elections. It is still unclear to what extent the online campaigns and the recent attack in Trappes may affect the protests on the street. Just as last weekend, demonstrations in central Paris are banned. Both the march of various trade unions and that of the gilets jaunes movement have been moved to a route between Porte de Bagnolet and Porte de Charenton, on the edge of the city. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez meanwhile warns of calls circulating on social media to gather tonight, under the guise of Halloween, for a 'revolution'. The minister described the risk of urban violence as "very heightened". Just as a week ago, 70,000 officers are therefore being deployed today.

title: Deadlock over UN peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara: Russia and US veto each other's proposal
lead: Russia and the United States have each vetoed the other's resolution on extending the UN peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara. This threatens to end the presence of UN military personnel and observers in the area. The mandate for the mission officially expires today. Normally the mission was extended quite routinely since 1991, but this time the vote in the UN Security Council went differently. The US had submitted a resolution stating that the mission would be extended by one year and that, in doing so, Morocco's autonomy plan for the area would be the only basis for negotiations. It also stated that there would be fewer UN military personnel in the area. Russia voted down that proposal. Voted down Russia then also put forward a resolution to extend the mission by one year, but without the changes proposed by the United States. The United States then voted down that proposal. If the Security Council does not succeed in reaching agreement, the mandate of MINURSO will expire. That means the future of the 35-year-old peacekeeping mission is highly uncertain. Western Sahara Morocco entered Western Sahara in 1975. It was a colony of Spain, which withdrew definitively in 1976. Morocco now controls the largest part of the area, which lies on the North African coast between Morocco, Mauritania and Algeria. Oil is said to lie off the coast, and the area is rich in raw materials. The annexation led to a conflict with the Polisario movement, which is supported in its desire for its own state by Algeria. The Polisario Front, founded in 1973, initially fought against the Spanish occupation and since 1975 against the presence of Morocco. A ceasefire was reached in 1991. The UN initially wanted a referendum in which the inhabitants of Western Sahara would express themselves on self-determination, but this has still not taken place. In recent years the UN in general has called for "a mutually acceptable solution". Polisario took up arms again in 2020, which ended the ceasefire. In 2023 the 50th anniversary was celebrated, including with a military parade. The Moroccan royal palace reacted with satisfaction to the failure of the extension. It states that all troops and equipment must leave the area in the coming days. The representative of the Polisario Front, Sidi Omar, says he is grateful that Russia blocked the US proposal because, in his view, that proposal "would torpedo the foundations of the UN peace process". One letter was the problem Last year the Security Council changed course by supporting Morocco's autonomy plan as the basis for negotiations. That was a diplomatic boost for Morocco. But that did not mean the UN had formally approved the plan or dropped the right to self-determination. However, the US proposal went further: the mission would be renamed from MINURSO to MINUSO, so without the R, which refers to a referendum in the mission's name. After the vote, US Ambassador Mike Waltz pointed out that a referendum has never taken place, due to persistent disagreements over who is eligible to vote. "Unfortunately, some members of this Security Council have used their veto to keep the letter 'R' for referendum in the name of the mission, while the United Nations has not been preparing for holding such a vote for decades," he added. 'Too far' According to Russia, the US proposal went too far in supporting Morocco in the disputed area. "The Security Council must not approve such a unilateral approach," stated Russian UN ambassador Nebenzia. "That is why we felt compelled to block the adoption of the proposal." Although Morocco says it respects the ceasefire in the area, the organisation Oxfam fears deterioration in the region. "The loss of MINURSO's monitoring and de-escalation tasks threatens to undermine security and stability, with serious consequences for civilians and the prospects for a peaceful solution," the organisation says.

title: Rubber boat with dozens of migrants pulled from sea near Breskens
lead: Emergency services this morning pulled a rubber boat with 38 people from the sea near Breskens. The boat was towed to a marina in Cadzand, Omroep Zeeland reports. In Cadzand it turned out, according to the military police, that there were 36 Afghan migrants on board and two suspected people smugglers from Sudan. Those last two have been arrested. The other occupants are being taken care of. "Around 06:00 we received a report of a suspicious situation on the North Sea, off the Zeeland-Flemish coast," says a spokesperson for the military police. "When we arrived we saw the rubber boat with refugees drifting." See the footage of the boat at sea here: The military police decided to start a rescue operation immediately together with the Coast Guard. "It involved a small vessel with a very large number of people," the spokesperson said. "That created dangerous conditions. There were no life jackets. It was harrowing to see how closely they were packed together on a small vessel." The spokesperson also points out that the little boat had become unmanageable. "The engine was gone." In the harbour of Cadzand the occupants were received by ambulances and an emergency team of the Red Cross: The spokesperson of the military police cannot yet say anything about the health condition of the occupants. It is also still unclear where the boat came from. The Zwin As far as is known, it is the first time a boat with migrants has been seen off the Dutch coast. However, in April a group of 28 migrants was found in the dune area Het Zwin, just over the border in Belgium. That group had a large black rubber boat with an outboard motor and life jackets with them. The suspicion was that they wanted to sail toward Great Britain. Far more often, rubber dinghies on which migrants attempt the crossing to Great Britain are found off the Belgian, but especially the French coast. Smugglers are often involved. Station wagons full Data from the military police shows that the necessary boats, life jackets and outboard motors are partly transported by road via the Netherlands. "In the Netherlands we mainly deal with the transit of the equipment," the military police said earlier. "At the end of 2021 we came across the first transports in the Netherlands. We saw SUVs, vans and station wagons crammed full of rubber boats, outboard motors and life jackets." Nieuwsuur reported last week that the military police and the Public Prosecution Service have recently been seeing more of this kind of rubber boat appear in the Netherlands. It concerns the same type of boat that was used in Breskens.

title: Cabinet continues talks with opposition as deadline approaches fast
lead: The cabinet is continuing talks today at the Catshuis with the opposition about the tax plan. So far it has not succeeded in securing sufficient support for it, while the deadline is fast approaching. This morning there was an internal meeting between <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity>, the deputy prime ministers Yesilgöz and Van den Brink and <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">minister Heinen</entity> and <entity id="person:eelco-eerenberg">staatssecretaris Eerenberg</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity>. Afterwards the party leaders Bikker (ChristenUnie) and Struijs (50Plus) will drop by. Together with the Groep Markuszower, with which no official negotiations have yet taken place, they could help the minority cabinet in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> reach a majority. Digital conversation Afterwards there is a digital conversation with party leaders Eerdmans (JA21), Vermeer (BBB) and Stoffer (SGP). This 'little alliance' of right-wing parties is not visiting The Hague, at its own request. The three gave a lukewarm response yesterday regarding their offer to support the tax plan, provided a number of conditions are met. These concern, among other things, asylum, nitrogen and abortion and surrogacy. The coalition parties D66 and CDA have great difficulty with that. This afternoon Pro and Volt will come to the Catshuis. They are also working together. These parties could together secure a majority in the Tweede and <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">Eerste Kamer</entity>, but the VVD in particular sees little in a cooperation 'over the left'. Deadline approaching The deadline for the tax plan is getting closer. Normally it is settled by August, but now, on the last day of October, nothing is clear yet. By Tuesday at the latest the cabinet wants to send the bill to the Tweede Kamer, which will vote on it a week later. Afterwards it will still go to the Eerste Kamer. Most measures in the tax plan must take effect on 1 January.

title: Evacuated Ukrainians from Olesjky back in Ukraine via a detour
lead: The people evacuated from the South Ukrainian city of Olesjky have arrived back in Ukraine via a detour. President Zelensky reports this on social media. The residents of Olesjky were trapped in their city. It was occupied on the first day of the Russian invasion in 2022 and has been under heavy fire ever since. Of the originally 20,000 residents, an estimated 2,000 were still in the city. Escaping was nearly impossible for them due to, among other things, the daily attacks and the mines lying there. Recently the situation became unbearable: because of Russian mines, no car could enter or leave the city. In addition to the loss of water, electricity and heating, a chronic shortage of food and medicine also arose. Residents of the town were completely worn out. On Tuesday a multi-day ceasefire went into effect to evacuate residents. Yesterday people who wanted to leave Olesjky were taken by bus via Crimea to the Russian city of Anapa. From there some of the people flew to Belarus, where they arrived this morning. They were received by medical teams and aid workers. Evacuees could also choose to stay in Russia or to remain in Olesjky itself with new food supplies. According to Zelensky, those evacuated to Belarus have since crossed the border back into the Chernihiv region, which borders Belarus. Ukrainian MP Arachamia said this morning that the repatriation would take place with four aircraft. It is not known how many people have been evacuated. The American first lady Melania Trump, who was also involved in the ceasefire, wrote on X that it concerns more than 750 people. Meanwhile the attacks continue back and forth. Yesterday two people were killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on the Russian region of Bryansk. Five people were also injured. That is what the local Russian authorities say. In the Ukrainian capital Kyiv, an important water network was hit by a Russian attack last night, leaving part of the residents without water overnight. The water and sewage systems are now working again. According to President Zelensky, power plants have also been hit again by Russian drone attacks. As a result, 280,000 people in Dnipro and Kyiv are without electricity, he writes on Telegram.

title: Police clear centre of Zoetermeer, ten people arrested
lead: Police intervened last night in fights in the centre of Zoetermeer. The ME cleared the area. Ten people have been arrested. According to Omroep West, unrest arose during or after a Halloween party in the Stadshart. There were several fights between groups of young people. When the police wanted to intervene, fireworks were thrown at officers. Subsequently dozens of young people fled. Some of them ran into car parks. Others fled along the shops. Pursuit While dozens of police officers launched the pursuit, the mobile unit cordoned off the centre. Everyone still walking around there was sent away. A number of arrestees are still in custody. It has not been announced what they are suspected of.

title: Intellectually disabled man abducted and abused after date arranged on dating app
lead: A group of people in their twenties is suspected of abusing and humiliating at least two people they approached via a dating app. One of the victims was also abducted. The abducted victim is a 61-year-old man from Schiedam. Last month he was taken from his home and held overnight in Amsterdam. He was also abused there. His hair and eyebrows were partly shaved off. His nephew speaks on behalf of the victim and says he is a very vulnerable man. "My uncle has a mild intellectual disability," says nephew Jerry. "He often ends up in situations where people take advantage of his good nature, but this surpasses everything." Date In the night of Saturday 19 to Sunday 20 September, the man from Schiedam thought he had a date with another man. They had made contact via a dating app. The victim's family suspects he was lured into a trap. The man agreed to meet at home in Schiedam and was then taken against his will by two men to Amsterdam-West. There he was abused and a video was made of him. A third man is said to have been involved as well. Images on Snapchat Footage of the victim was subsequently posted on Snapchat. The video also shows a young man who says with a laugh: "Listen, today I cut someone's hair for the first time in my life." "My stomach turned when I saw that," says Jerry. "What was done here is degrading." The video also shows the victim looking dazed, receiving slaps to the head and having fingers poked into his eye. "Treating vulnerable people like that, I have no words for it." Jerry thinks his uncle was drugged and is a victim of homophobia. The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> is investigating the motive. Two arrests In the case, two men from Amsterdam aged 21 and 23 have meanwhile been arrested. The police also suspect them of a similar incident in Hilversum. There, someone was abused in June, also after a date arranged via a dating app. A third suspect, a 21-year-old man from Haarlem, is in custody for that incident. All three are suspected of coercion and assault. The third suspect who was involved in the abuse of the man from Schiedam has not yet been identified. The intellectually disabled victim from Schiedam was eventually released the next morning. The men took him outside and left him alone. The man rang the doorbell of a house nearby and the residents alerted the police. Officers searched the house where the victim had been held that same morning, but no one was home at the time. The suspects were arrested later, the second one last week. In intensive care The man from Schiedam, according to his family, spent a few days in the hospital's intensive care unit after the abduction. "He had several kinds of drugs in his blood," says Jerry. He thinks the drugs were administered to him. The police are investigating this. In the meantime his uncle is doing better. He lives in a different place. "He doesn't dare be at home anymore, because that's where it all started," says Jerry. The victim's family hopes that attention to this case can help prevent similar incidents. According to the police, dates arranged via dating apps more often end in a crime. "Think of people who are robbed or fall victim to sexual violence," says a spokesperson. Out of shame or fear, victims do not always dare to go to the police. The police emphasise that such an incident is never the victim's fault and that they are always taken seriously by the police.

title: Lufthansa crew member dies after electrocution in a swimming pool in India
lead: A 57-year-old crew member of German airline Lufthansa died yesterday after being electrocuted in a hotel swimming pool in the Indian city of Bengaluru. A second person also lost their life. At around 5:30 p.m. local time, the pool on the third floor of the Conrad Hotel became electrified. The exact cause is still being investigated. Anonymous sources tell German newspaper Bild that it happened when the underwater lighting of the pool came on. Lifeguard injured. The other victim is, according to the Hindustan Times, a 45-year-old Slovak who works for technology company IBM. In addition, an American tourist and an Indian lifeguard were injured when they tried to rescue the victims. They are in hospital and, according to the newspaper, are out of mortal danger. Lufthansa has confirmed the death of the 57-year-old employee and states in a statement that it is "deeply saddened". "We extend our deepest sympathy to the family, relatives and friends of the deceased crew member. We ask for your understanding that, out of respect for the privacy of those involved, we cannot provide further information about the accident or the deceased." KLM. The hotel is used by airlines to let staff rest after flights. KLM also uses the hotel. The airline confirms to NOS that KLM crew members were also in the hotel at the time of the accident. They were not injured. The staff have since left the hotel and flown back to the Netherlands.

title: Rain forecast for part of Gelderland uncertain because there are (possibly) bats
lead: Quickly checking the app to see whether it will rain is of little use for now in parts of Gelderland. The weather forecast for the area is highly uncertain because the signal from the <entity id="org:koninklijk-nederlands-meteorologisch-instituut">KNMI</entity> radar in the Betuwe is disrupted by a row of poplars. For now, it is not allowed to prune or fell those trees. First it must be investigated whether there are bats, reports Omroep Gelderland . The Netherlands has two precipitation radars, one of which is in the Betuwe, specifically in Herwijnen. The KNMI uses the data from those radars for the weather forecast in apps such as Buienradar. But the fast-growing tall poplars near the radar turn out to affect precipitation forecasts in part of Gelderland: much more or much less rain falls than the radar indicates. Pulses blocked: That is because the trees block the pulses sent out by the radar. It concerns a strip from Herwijnen towards Germany, running between <entity id="org:gemeente-arnhem">Arnhem</entity> and <entity id="org:gemeente-nijmegen">Nijmegen</entity> and across <entity id="org:gemeente-doetinchem">Doetinchem</entity>. The problem has been going on for some time. At the end of last year the KNMI asked the <entity id="org:gemeente-west-betuwe">gemeente West Betuwe</entity> for permission to prune the trees. But the municipality has not yet granted permission. "We cannot intervene directly," says a spokesperson for the West Betuwe municipality. He points to nature protection legislation. The poplars may be part of a foraging area or flight route of bats. "These areas and routes are protected," says the spokesperson. Next steps: Ecological research has in the meantime been carried out into what role the trees play precisely for bats and what consequences a possible "intervention" would have. The results are expected soon. Based on the outcome, the next steps will be determined, says the municipal spokesperson. Meanwhile the KNMI is applying corrections to compensate for disturbances in the radar image. To do so, the weather institute uses radar scans at greater height, which as it were look over the trees. Data from other radars in the Netherlands, Belgium and Germany are also used. In the corrections, the radar scans of the area behind the row of trees are not included in the forecasts, says a KNMI spokesperson. "But it remains desirable to have as few disturbances as possible."

title: Strange situation in Poland: president pushes his way into the Constitutional Court
lead: Judges tried overnight to stop the president of Poland from entering the Constitutional Court. The unprecedented situation arose when President Nawrocki wanted to go inside the court building in Warsaw. A scuffle broke out at the entrance, in which judges also tried to push the president back outside. In the end Nawrocki managed to get inside with a small group of people. This brought a long-running conflict over the appointment of new judges to a climax. Watch here how the president was stopped: The judges concerned were recently appointed by the Tusk government. It is trying to reform the court and to undo changes made by the previous conservative government, including the appointment of conservative judges. Protest and confrontations Last evening unrest broke out at the court and there were confrontations between police and protesters. Objects were reportedly thrown. Three people were arrested. The conflict began years ago when the conservative-nationalist party PiS appointed its own judges in a controversial manner. The cause of yesterday's unrest was the suspension of the court's chairman Swieczkowski, who was appointed by the PiS government. He is obstructing the current prime minister Tusk and his government in their plans to reform the rule of law. Appointments blocked This led to a problem for the Tusk government in appointing new judges to replace the PiS judges whose terms had expired. When the government nominated new candidates, right-conservative President Nawrocki refused to have them take the oath. This led to the remarkable situation that the new judges were in the court building but were not allowed to work by chairman Swieczkowski, because they had not taken the oath. It was then decided to suspend the conservative chairman and the vice-chairman, in the hope of breaking the deadlock. This met with resistance outside the court walls last evening, where demonstrators gathered and PiS leader Kaczynski was also present. President Nawrocki, who was on his way to Senegal, also hurried back. Opposition speaks of a coup "The people must defend the Constitutional Court, because without the constitution there is nothing. Then lawlessness reigns," said a demonstrator wearing a camouflage cap. "They want to appoint their own people and govern as they please, but we must not allow that." The conservative opposition led by Kaczynski speaks of a coup. Another protester, a man carrying the Polish flag, finds the situation unreal. "Never before has anyone taken such a brutal action against the Constitutional Court. Letting the police and other authorities in, secretly taking documents, that was not an issue until now." The police say that officers were present at the judges' request, to guarantee safety. According to Prime Minister Tusk there was no other way to achieve the reforms and decisive action was necessary. The Constitutional Court of Poland reviews whether new laws are in line with the constitution. The judges therefore have a great deal of power and can effectively determine whether new laws get through, which makes a big difference to the government's ability to act. Due to all the political interference, by the PiS party but now also by Tusk's party, fewer and fewer Polish citizens trust the institution. At the end of the restless night, President Nawrocki called for urgent consultations. He too spoke of a "violation of the constitutional order of Poland" and wants talks to "stabilise the political situation". Today there will be another demonstration in front of the entrance to the court building in Warsaw.

title: Porn on hacked billboards along highway in Egypt
lead: Hackers this week showed pornographic footage on digital billboards along a major highway in the Egyptian city of Giza, a suburb of Cairo. The footage has since been taken offline. The billboards originally displayed advertisements for an international company, writes the Egyptian ministry of <entity id="org:tweede-kamer-commissie-biza">Binnenlandse Zaken</entity> . However, the website of that international company was hacked, allowing the hackers to broadcast the pornographic footage. The company was able to restore the website and has also taken the footage offline. The authorities say they have taken legal steps in response to the incident. Footage of the incident is circulating on social media. Drivers on the highway in question are filming from their cars or from the side of the road. The pornographic footage carried the text "Leaked by: Ch, 19ylegal never and nivex" and the name of the Telegram account Leakersgov . That channel shares, among other things, photos of the billboards and articles about the hack. 'Dictatorship' "Egypt is still a dictatorship", the hacker group writes on the channel. "The government maintains its power through repression, while the country struggles to move forward." The group calls on the government to "change its priorities and commit to the population". In 2013 army chief Sisi seized power through a military coup. Under him the country has become an authoritarian state, according to Freedom House among others. There is almost no room for opposition or criticism of the government. Demonstrating is also almost impossible. Although the Egyptian constitution guarantees press freedom in the country, this is far from reality. This week the critical, independent news site Mada Masr was banned by a judge. 'Digital security is a joke' Little is known about the hacker group. The group says it created the Telegram channel to show that digital security is "a total joke worldwide". "The media want to portray this attack as a very sophisticated, state-sponsored cyberattack", the group writes. "But the truth is that your digital infrastructure is shameful, wherever you are." The group says it will share more footage of hacks worldwide, and the reactions to them, in the group. It is unclear what exactly is meant by this. "Welcome, the show is international."

title: Dozens of arrests in The Hague, no major demonstrations in the Netherlands
lead: The Hague is quiet again after a turbulent day. Although the looting that was feared has not materialised, 34 arrests were made on and around the Malieveld. People were arrested for wearing face coverings or for possessing illegal fireworks, a police spokesperson said. <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> was out in force in the city because of possible youth protests. In various places people were searched and had to show identification. This happened on and around the Malieveld, near Centraal Station, at the Spui and on the Grote Marktstraat, among other places. An emergency order is in force in that area, which earlier in the day applied only to the shopping district. 'Manageable' The police urged people not to come to the city centre. According to the police, the number of people in the city did increase during the day. Earlier in the day the municipality had described the situation as "manageable". It mainly concerned small groups of young people, reporter Edwin van den Berg observed: Dozens of people had gathered on the Plein to protest. Some demonstrators carried a Prinsenvlag. The orange-white-blue flag was used by the NSB among others and is now a symbol of the far right. The hard core of football club ADO Den Haag was also present on the Plein. Yesterday it announced that it would protect the city and local businesses. On social media, supporters wrote: "We are not against violence; in fact, it is our hobby. What we do not tolerate, however, is the looting of our city, the destruction of cultural heritage or any other form of vandalism." Shops boarded up As a precaution, many shopkeepers boarded up their façades and kept their shops closed. Although it remained fairly quiet in a large part of the city centre, businesspeople in The Hague estimate the damage will likely run into the many thousands of euros, mainly due to lost income. On the Korte Voorhout it was briefly tense: On the Korte Voorhout the Mobiele Eenheid intervened to prevent a confrontation between ADO supporters and a group of young people. The supporters were sent back to the Plein by the ME. Good-natured in <entity id="org:gemeente-maastricht">Maastricht</entity> In Maastricht too, account was taken of violent demonstrations and there was a large police presence. There too, a number of shopkeepers had boarded up their façades as a precaution. The day passed in Maastricht without incident, a police spokesperson said. No arrests were made and the atmosphere on the Vrijthof was good-natured. In <entity id="org:gemeente-amsterdam">Amsterdam</entity>, <entity id="org:gemeente-utrecht">Utrecht</entity> and <entity id="org:gemeente-rotterdam">Rotterdam</entity> demonstrations were also expected. No large groups of people have gathered there either.

title: Mexico challenges Panama Canal with railway across narrowest part of Mexico
lead: A new overland trade route in Mexico is nearly finished. A railway line in the south of the country is meant to serve as an alternative to the Panama Canal, the most popular trade route through Latin America. Like a huge brown snake, a train stands along a quay in the south of Mexico, while a strong sea wind from the Pacific Ocean relentlessly lashes against the carriages. In the background, an enormous hangar is being built from the ground up. Next to the train stand machines operated by men in white helmets and orange vests, pouring concrete over a large sandy plain. Today the train is not running, but it stands on the construction site as if to remind everyone of the reason this port is being expanded. Corredor Interoceánico The Mexican city of Salina Cruz is the starting point of this train, which every day will carry goods from container ships coming from Asia to the other side of Mexico, to the port city of Coatzacoalcos on the Atlantic Ocean. From there, container ships can take the goods to the east coast of the United States or even further, to Europe. The project is called the Corredor Interoceánico. Over the coming years it is meant to grow into a trade route of global scale. It should also serve as a solution to logistical problems that transport companies between Asia and Europe, among others, are facing. The narrowest part of Mexico The route crosses the narrowest part of Mexico, an isthmus of 200 kilometers, in the economically less developed southeast of the country. A first test already showed the speed and efficiency of the project: 900 cars from Hyundai's South Korean car factory were transported by train to the Atlantic Ocean within a day last month. Had the ship moored off the coast of Panama to take the Panama Canal, it would have taken much longer. That canal is still the most popular trade route through Latin America, but its locks are struggling to handle the huge numbers of container ships. 'Dry canal' In addition, the Panama Canal has been hit by drought in recent years. The water level fell so low that fewer container ships could pass and shipments faced delays of several weeks. The authorities in Mexico call their alternative trade route a 'dry canal', which offers transport companies the same passage through Latin America, from one ocean to the other, but without the vulnerability of the Panama Canal. European interest There is already interest from Europe. "We have already concluded an agreement with Portugal for the use of this route, and we want to extend that to the rest of the European Union," says Pascual Rosario Sepúlveda Soto, one of the coordinators of the project. A benefit for Dutch companies too? The Dutch trade organization Evofenedex calls the railway in Mexico an interesting alternative to the Panama Canal. In addition to the drought, the American president's wish to control the canal also plays a role. "That creates uncertainty," says policy adviser Elmar Otten. An alternative is therefore "certainly welcome". Whether Dutch entrepreneurs will actually use the Mexican railway depends on factors such as price, reliability, capacity and the suitability of the seaports. "If all of that is in order, it is an attractive alternative," said Otten. Apart from the train and the ports at both ends, the <entity id="org:regering">regering</entity> wants villages and towns along the route to benefit as well. Ten industrial parks are to be established so that companies can load and unload goods along the way, for example to get closer to the sales market in the United States. It is a huge economic boost for a region that is much less developed than northern Mexico. Investments needed Although the train is running and the ports are being expanded quickly, the remaining infrastructure still needs to be improved, emphasizes Daniel Méndez Sosa, mayor of Salina Cruz. He points out that the federal government mainly puts its money into the ports and shows little concern for the towns. "This project can only work if all authorities cooperate. As a municipality, we do not have the money for large investments, for example in roads. If those investments do not come, the project will not get very far," says the critical mayor from his office on the square of Salina Cruz. Nevertheless, he has no doubt about the enormous potential of the project for his city. "Salina Cruz will become one of the most important cities in Mexico and the whole world with this project," he says confidently. "With this route we save time and offer companies economic benefits, also close to the US. And one of the poorest regions of Mexico can benefit from the industry that will grow here."

title: Rotterdam builds unusual bridge, of value to cancer patients
lead: A new pedestrian bridge was installed today at the Erasmus MC in Rotterdam. It is a striking bridge about one hundred meters long, partly clad in wood, which is of great value to cancer patients. The bridge directly connects the Daniel den Hoed Family House with the cancer ward of the Erasmus hospital. This means cancer patients and their families will no longer have to cross a busy road. "This has been long awaited," says Heidi Leeuwangh of the family house, enthusiastically, to broadcaster Rijnmond. "It's hugely important. Our guests are very involved with it." 'Faster and more comfortable' Construction of the bridge began last September. "Family members can get from one side of the road to the other much faster and more comfortably," said alderman Pascal Lansink (VVD) at the time. "Imagine your loved one is in hospital and is very ill. Then you really want to be there in time, for example to say goodbye." The family house offers a temporary 'second home' for family members of cancer patients. This way they can be close to each other during treatments. Patients can also stay overnight in the house. Like the family house, the bridge is named after Daniël den Hoed, the doctor who was one of the pioneers of radiotherapy in the Netherlands in the late 1930s. In use in December The bridge has been partly financed by KWF Kankerbestrijding. The foundation has donated 1.1 million euros. A large part of that amount was raised during the Rotterdam Marathon in 2023. The municipality, together with the Daniel den Hoed foundation and the Erasmus MC, is paying the rest. The bridge cannot be used immediately. Over the coming weeks the bridge will be fitted out. "The expectation is that the bridge will open in mid-December," the municipality reports.

title: Protests in dozens of French and German cities, riots in Paris and Frankfurt
lead: In dozens of French cities there was a demonstration for the third weekend in a row. By far the largest rally was in Paris, with around 70,000 participants according to the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. In various cities, riots broke out in the course of the afternoon and early evening. The police deployed tear gas and arrested people. In addition, there were youth protest marches in at least thirty German cities. Across Germany there were tens of thousands of participants. In Berlin and Cologne around 5,000 demonstrators, says the German police. 'Infiltrated by extremists' After the demonstrations ended, rioters took over in several cities. They reportedly deliberately mingled with the demonstrators, writes the German Tagesschau. Things got out of hand especially in Frankfurt. There, shop windows were smashed, shops were looted and officers were injured. Around midnight the police reported having made thirty arrests. Officers were present in large numbers in the city centre until deep into the night. In Cologne too, officers intervened after the demonstration, when riots broke out around the cathedral and the central station in the evening.
