As an analyst she was previously involved in election campaigns of Joe Biden and Kamala Harris, both Democrats. "What I have learned from that is that it is very important to formulate a message that appeals to different groups. We often see Latino voters as one group, but there is an enormous amount of diversity." Whether the Republicans will pull off another surprise tomorrow remains to be seen. The promised economic prosperity has failed to materialise, and in addition there is a lot of discontent among Latinos about the harsh actions of the immigration agency ICE. From 93 to 57 percent approval That disappointment is also visible in the polls. Approval among Latino voters who voted for Trump in the previous presidential elections has plummeted. Where at the start of his presidential term 93 percent were still positive about his performance, that figure is now only 57 percent. And although Trump himself will not be on the ballot this time, Latino voters view that differently. More than half of registered Latino voters say they see these congressional elections as an opportunity to vote against President Trump. Joaquin Castro, a prominent Latino politician of the Democrats who has represented Texas in the American Congress for nearly fourteen years, recognises this. This weekend he is in Austin to motivate campaign volunteers for the final sprint. Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico has a chance of winning in the traditionally Republican state. "I think Latino voters now feel betrayed," Castro says. "They feel the president had promised to go after criminal immigrants. But instead he is also targeting American citizens and undocumented people who have been living here for twenty or thirty years and are important members of the community. They feel the community has been given a target on its back. And they are fed up with it." The Democrat is hopeful that deep-red Texas will turn blue for the first time in decades tomorrow. "This could well be the year." Latinos as kingmakers Whether the Democrats' hope comes true depends, according to Professor Gutierrez, on the support of Latinos. "Texas has traditionally been a predominantly Republican state. The Republicans have held power here continuously since 1992. The fact that we are now seeing such exciting neck-and-neck races means that in the end it comes down to how Latinos vote." Election night at the NOS The NOS is reporting the results live in a livestream on the night of Tuesday to Wednesday. From 03:00 hours, reporter Arjen van der Horst will comment on all developments. At 07:00 hours he hands over to Mark Visser, who will connect with studio guests and our correspondents and reporters in the United States. From 09:00 to 09:30 hours we will address viewer questions. Want to know something? Email vraag@nos.nl.

title: British adventurer completes 28-year round-the-world trek on foot: 'I did not do this alone'
lead: He crossed the notorious Darién Gap, walked across the Bering Strait between Alaska and Russia, and swam the English Channel and the Caspian Sea. After a 28-year journey on foot around the world, British adventurer Karl Bushby is home today. The now 57-year-old Brit set off in 1998 from Punta Arenas, in southern Chile, on his so-called Goliath expedition with 500 dollars in his pocket. He had served for twelve years in the British Parachute Regiment, where he was extremely bored because it was peacetime. Bushby suffered from anxiety disorders and was afraid of death, he said this month to The Guardian. The idea of a years-long walk would not let him go, he wanted to achieve something. The twenty-something set himself two goals: he was not allowed to use any motorised transport and had to reach his British birthplace of Hull on foot. By doing so, he also chose not to watch his then 8-year-old son Adam grow up. Adam stayed with Bushy's ex-wife in Northern Ireland. Still, according to him, the bond with his son is good. Today Bushby's expedition of about 58,000 kilometres came to an end, during which he is estimated to have taken 75 million steps. In Hull, the former soldier was welcomed festively by family, friends, the mayor and hundreds of onlookers: With a fully loaded cart he walked into the city. To the crowd, Bushby said that "the whole world was needed to get me back here today". However, he did not make the journey alone. "It was a worldwide effort." During his trek, which recalls the wanderings of the Greek hero Odysseus, he had a variety of adventures. For example, he swam among crocodiles to escape a guerrilla war in Colombia, came face to face with a polar bear, and passed through marshy primeval forests, jungles and deserts. Together with a French adventurer, he crossed the treacherous sea ice of the Bering Strait from Alaska to reach Siberia. Only a few people had attempted this before them. Remarkably, neither of the men had any experience with Arctic expeditions. Initially Bushby estimated that his world journey would last five years. "After that you get a heavy dose of reality," he said. "I thought it would take at least twelve years, plus some extra time." His trek took him through thirty countries on four continents: North America, South America, Asia and Europe. For the last part of his journey he wanted to walk to England through the Channel Tunnel, but access was refused to him. He therefore ended up swimming to Dover. The crossing lasted twenty hours, spread over three days. No country cost him more time than Russia. Because of visa problems and severe weather conditions, Bushby took almost ten years, with interruptions, to cross that country. He was detained there and threatened with expulsion because he had entered Russia illegally after crossing the Bering Strait. Because of the harsh climate, he could only stay in the country for a few months each year. He was also regularly confronted with bureaucratic obstacles. When Russia refused him a visa in 2012, he walked 5,600 kilometres from Los Angeles to the Russian embassy in Washington in protest. In the end he did receive the required documents after all. Bushby also lived in Mexico for two years out of necessity. This was mainly for financial reasons. After the financial crisis of 2008 he lost his sponsors and had to temporarily halt his journey. He also tried to enter Mongolia, but was held by Chinese authorities because they thought he was a spy. In addition, the coronavirus pandemic caused him major delays. Poorest of the poor Besides sponsors, writing a book and giving lectures, it was the countless strangers who kept him going during the journey. He slept in huts made of car parts, was looked after by the family of a Peruvian doctor when he suffered from a serious stomach infection, and was served countless meals consisting of nothing more than rice and water. "I was welcomed by the poorest of the poor," he said. "I have met 99.9999% of the very best of humanity. In every culture, in every country, the reaction was exactly the same." Bushby fell in love twice during his journey. He had a seven-year relationship with a woman from Colombia and a three-year one with a woman from Japan. But the relationships could not withstand the heavy toll that travelling demanded. Mixed feelings When geopolitical conflicts made it impossible to travel through Russia and Iran, Bushby decided in 2024 to cross the Caspian Sea, the largest inland body of water in the world. That crossing lasted 31 days. For that crossing he used a technique he calls floatimming, a combination of floating and swimming. Wearing a buoyancy vest and wetsuit, he moved backwards by beating the water with his arms, because, by his own account, he is not a good swimmer. Bushby views the future with mixed feelings. Speaking to news agency AP yesterday, he said he was uncertain about what would come after his expedition. "My life's purpose and the reason I live are about to end. It will be difficult to fit back into a society that you no longer really know."

title: German doctor confesses to abusing dozens of children aged 2 to 20
lead: In Germany a paediatrician has confessed to abusing dozens of children and young people, German media report. The man was due to appear in court today on suspicion of abusing seventy victims. He is said to have assaulted them between 2013 and 2025 while working in hospitals in Nauen and Rathenow, west of Berlin. The indictment shows that the alleged victims are between 2 and 20 years old. The 46-year-old doctor is suspected of 130 criminal offences related to child abuse. The judge took almost three hours to read out the entire indictment. He has confessed to almost all of the offences he is suspected of. In a statement the doctor said he hoped the victims would one day be able to move on with their lives after what happened. Images The doctor is said to have mainly sought out boys in their patient rooms, where he abused them. This happened under the pretext of research. He is also accused of making photos and videos of the abuse. He is also said to have assaulted four children at a day nursery in Brandenburg. The doctor was there on assignment from the German GGD to carry out medical examinations of the children. There too he is said to have made photos and videos of the abuse. In 2023 the doctor is said to have met more often with a patient aged 15 and later 16. The doctor is said to have performed sexual acts with the victim and again made images of it. In addition to the abuse in the patient rooms, the paediatrician is also suspected of sexual offences at his home. Complaint by mother The case came to light when the mother of one of the children filed a complaint in November last year, suspecting abuse. The doctor was subsequently arrested. When his electronic devices were searched, images were found pointing to further possible misconduct. The court in Potsdam is hearing the case, which is expected to last until December. A verdict is expected halfway through that month. In response to the allegations, the hospital group where the doctor worked has revised its child protection procedures. "Nowadays, examinations and nursing procedures in sensitive situations are always checked by two people," the care institution says.

title: Outrage over Martha Stewart dressing up as a homeless person: 'Ongevoelig'
lead: American businesswoman and television presenter Martha Stewart has apologised for her Halloween costume. On Saturday Stewart shared a photo of herself dressed as someone who is homeless. This drew quite a lot of criticism. In the photo, since removed, Stewart had smudges on her face and wore torn clothing and a beanie. She also held up a sign in the photo reading "Ik heb honger. Help me!" Many critical reactions came in about the costume. "Waarom denk je dat mensen die langs de weg liggen te sterven, een kostuum zijn?", someone wrote under the Instagram post. "Kijk eens om je heen, Martha. Mensen hebben het moeilijk hier", was the response from another. Stewart reacted yesterday in People Magazine to the outrage. The 85-year-old media personality and cookbook author said she is upset that her costume, which was "juist bedoeld was om meer aandacht te vragen voor het zeer ernstige onderwerp dakloosheid", has offended people. "Dat was nooit mijn bedoeling." Between 2013 and 2025, homelessness in the United States increased by 27 percent, official figures show. An estimated over 700,000 homeless people live in the country. "Dakloosheid blijft een van de grootste uitdagingen en lopende crises van de Verenigde Staten", continues the businesswoman. She explains that she has often worked to tackle homelessness, including by supporting charities. "Ik wil ook blijven helpen een verschil te maken." In the first statement Stewart did not apologise, but an apology followed a few hours later. On her own Instagram account she shared a brief second response. "Het is moeilijk om toe te geven als je het echt hebt verprutst. Mijn vorige verklaring was niet voldoende." Stewart goes on to say she knows many people are having a hard time financially. "Een kostuum dragen, zoals ik deed, is ongevoelig en niet grappig. Het spijt me heel erg." Stewart has built a lifestyle empire over the past decades. Her big breakthrough came in 1982 with the cookbook Entertaining. In the 1990s she launched her own magazine and appeared in several successful TV programmes. In 1999 she became the first female self-made billionaire in the US, after having founded her media company Martha Stewart Living Omnimedia (MSLO) a year earlier. In 2013 she sold MSLO for over 350 million dollars. In 2004 Stewart was convicted of, among other things, conspiracy, in a case about the sale of shares in another company. Despite her five-month prison sentence, Stewart remained successful. The multimillionaire has since written more than a hundred books.

title: Following Spanish example, House of Representatives calls for media code on femicide
lead: Dutch media could do better to think about their reporting on femicide and gender-based violence, a majority of the House of Representatives believes. D66, VVD, PRO, SP, JA21 and BBB want <entity id="person:rianne-letschert">minister Letschert</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-onderwijs-cultuur-en-wetenschap">Onderwijs, Cultuur en Wetenschap</entity> to enter into discussion with media organisations about a voluntary media code on femicide, as already exists in Spain. The request was submitted by Hanneke van der Werf (D66). Last month she, together with other parliamentarians, visited Spain. There, policy to combat gender-based violence has been pursued since 2004. "In Spain, active work is being done in many different domains to combat femicide," says Van der Werf. "And the media play an active role there, especially in raising awareness of the subject." <entity id="org:regering">De regering</entity> cannot impose anything on media organisations, but can enter into discussion with them. "For example, it is important to talk about language use. That you are as clear as possible about who the victim is and who the perpetrator is. Labels such as family drama do not do justice to what happens in a relationship behind closed doors", states the House of Representatives member. She is also considering providing more context in the form of a referral for more information, as is currently done for 113 suicide prevention. How it works in Spain. In Spain there is no official guideline that journalists must follow. However, two laws mention the responsibility of the media. Based on those laws and the experiences of specialised journalists, media have drawn up their own rules. Laura De Grado Alonso works for the Spanish news agency EFE and is one of the journalists there who specialise in the subject. In general she is satisfied with the Spanish approach. De Grado describes how it began in Spain, with the story of Ana Orantes. For forty years she was together with José Parejo. Throughout their entire marriage he abused her. Domestic violence was not taken seriously by the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>. In 1996 she was finally able to divorce him. A year later, on 4 December 1997, she told her story on television. That was unprecedented at the time. Less than two weeks later she was murdered by her ex-husband. "This was a major event because the case received enormous media attention. Until then, violence against women was often regarded as a private matter, a family issue or simply the problem of an individual. But this case changed everything", says De Grado. In Spain awareness grew that change was needed to curb violence against women. A few years later, in 2004, under the socialist government of Prime Minister Zapatero, the first step was taken toward a law against gender violence. In the following years Spanish media developed their own frameworks for their reporting. Agreements on paper. EFE also has agreements on paper, says De Grado. "First, we never present gender-related violence as a standalone incident or a conflict between two individuals. In our reporting we explain the broader context of gender inequality and violence against women. To make clear that this is a societal problem". This starting point also meant media adjusted their language. "If femicide is involved, we explicitly name it. Where possible we avoid euphemistic terms such as deceased", says De Grado. In addition, they avoid phrasing that places responsibility on the victim. They also try not to reduce victims to numbers, but to give each victim a face. In Spain figures on femicide and gender violence have been kept nationally since 2003. Since 2022 a distinction has also been made between the different types of murders. In the Netherlands that does not happen. De Grado considers the figures certainly important: "We always state how many women were murdered that year and how many since the start of counting in 2003". But in her view it should not stop there. As a final important point she mentions that journalists must be aware of their role. For example, by not only reporting when it is too late and someone has been murdered. But also more often reporting on gender violence in itself. Whether Dutch media are open to discussing similar agreements remains to be seen. D66 member of the House of Representatives Van der Werf does hope to have taken a first step. "Hopefully society can become more aware of the warning signs in advance. And that people more quickly recognise the signals".

title: Prison sentence sought against Eindhoven man who 'went hunting' for cats with a crossbow
lead: Nine months in prison has been demanded against a 26-year-old resident of Eindhoven, because he shot cats with a crossbow. One of the five cats attacked was hit in its eye and did not survive. The shootings caused a lot of unrest in the neighbourhood, according to the Public Prosecution Service. Between November 2025 and May of this year, four cats were hit by an arrow. The suspect "really went hunting for cats in the neighbourhood in a targeted way. He did not take into account the impact that had on the owners and other people in the neighbourhood," says the public prosecutor. Suspect Yihui L. initially denied that he had shot at cats. Later he admitted it and L. stated that he had been angry, partly because a cat had scratched him. Stepped in cat poop The man said that on the street he had tried to take a cat home for his girlfriend. He tried to lure the animals with cat food. He eventually got scratched by a cat he had tried to pick up. His anger was further fuelled after he stepped in cat poop in the forest. A disorder within the autism spectrum has been identified in the suspect. At the time of the shootings, according to experts, he had diminished criminal responsibility. L. expressed regret for his actions during the interrogations and hearings. According to the OM, L. has now almost entirely repaid the veterinary costs that cat owners incurred for their injured animals. With the help of doorbell cameras, the police tried to track down the shooter. The suspect was eventually caught by neighbourhood residents on 19 May and handed over to officers. L. has been in custody since then. To China The OM finds it worrying that the man "shot at cats with a crossbow for such a minor reason". An unconditional prison sentence has been demanded, because the suspect indicated that he will return to China after serving his sentence. L. is of Chinese descent and studied and worked in Eindhoven. The court will give its ruling in two weeks.

title: Over one million euros collected for restoration of burned Limoges town hall
lead: For the restoration of the town hall of Limoges in France, more than 9,000 donors have collected over 1 million euros in less than two weeks. The historic building partly went up in flames during the night of 17 to 18 October after masked rioters entered the town hall and set it on fire. Images of the collapsed building went around the world and led to outraged reactions from French politicians. The fundraising campaign comes from the French heritage foundation Fondation du patrimoine. The town hall had been in use since 1883 and has been on the French list of monuments since 1975. Images of the fire: The town hall has great historical value for the Limousin region and is regarded as one of the symbols of Limoges, a medium-sized city at the foot of the Massif Central. During the Second World War, the town hall served as a refuge for Belgian parliamentarians in exile, after Belgium had surrendered to Nazi Germany. Under the supervision of the regional heritage service, work has now begun to protect and secure the parts of the building that were not destroyed. The restoration itself is due to begin in 2028 and, according to a provisional forecast by the Ministry of Culture, should be completed between 2030 and 2031. How much the full restoration will cost has not been announced. The aim of the fundraising is to raise at least 2 million euros. Tax deduction The fire started on 17 October during large-scale riots across France. The roof and bell tower of the town hall largely collapsed. A few days later, a 34-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of arson. According to the French news agency AFP, the suspect has ties to extreme left-wing circles and is known to the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity>, because he previously used violence against officers. Prime Minister Lecornu came to Limoges after the fire and promised that the town hall would be rebuilt 'identically'. The French government also decided to extend the monument status of the building, so that the restoration can receive extra financial support, on top of the money from public and private financiers. To encourage donations for the restoration, the French <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">Tweede Kamer</entity> agreed at the end of October to a budget amendment for 2027. As a result, donations to the reconstruction now receive an increased tax deduction of 75 percent, up to a maximum of 1,000 euros. The social unrest in France of recent weeks is not over for now. Today, after a short holiday, pupils have resumed their protests at secondary schools in Paris, Marseille and Rennes, broadcaster BFMTV reports. Although things remained relatively quiet today, student organisations have announced that they will step up the actions in the coming days. New blockades and demonstrations are planned for tomorrow, a general strike day follows on Thursday, and on Friday and Saturday the yellow vests are also expected to join the protests again.

title: Another attack on shop cooling across Europe: 'Companies have been sleeping'
lead: The first reports came in around 02:00 at night at Danfoss, says the supplier of cooling and freezing systems: the temperature in installations rose. In several European countries, from Ireland to Estonia, cooling systems turned out to have been attacked digitally. In the Netherlands too, the freezing and cooling systems of at least seventeen companies were disrupted overnight. "Companies have really been sleeping here", says ethical hacker Sijmen Ruwhof. In hundreds of shops in France, the temperature in cooling systems rose in October when malicious actors broke into the computer systems. How could this happen? The attack today, as far as is known, took place on devices of two companies: Denmark's Danfoss and America's Copeland. They supply boxes that allow a freezer or cooling compartment in a shop to be connected to the internet. This way, the installer can, for example, see remotely that there is a fault. For both brands, it has been known for months that there are vulnerabilities in the devices. After the attack in France, Danfoss sent a letter to its customers to point this out. The message: disconnect the cooling from the internet and "restore access to the units only via a secure network". Apparently not everyone has done so. As a result, it is easy for hackers to find out which devices are connected to the internet and can be attacked, says cybersecurity expert Ruwhof. Waiting for an attack "A stupidity", Ruwhof calls connecting cooling installations directly to the internet. "And especially after the hack at the French freezers, the installations should have been taken off the internet long ago. You can set your clock by it that such a system will be attacked." This Belgian butcher was hit by the cyberattack: Companies could have taken measures to prevent the attack. The freezing and cooling systems can, for example, be connected to the internet through a secure network. It is then still possible to check faults, for example, but the devices are then not visible to all hackers. It is unclear who is or are behind the attacks. "That is still a bit early", says Ruwhof. What is noticeable is that the systems have not been digitally 'held hostage', he says. Digitally locking computers and then demanding ransom is a popular method of cybercriminals who want to make money. It is also striking that all kinds of different supermarkets and supermarket chains have been attacked, says Ruwhof. "That indicates that the attackers, for example, are not specifically after one company." There is also no evidence of a link between the attacks on the cooling systems and the attack on Albert Heijn last month. Tens of thousands of euros in damage Shops where the cooling was attacked had to throw away part of their products. It is still unclear how great the damage precisely is. At the Belgian butcher's shop De Laet & Van Haver, a number of cooling units were attacked overnight. "We were there fairly quickly and were able to cool back part of the products in time", says co-owner Luc De Laet. "But there are also products for which that no longer succeeded." These are now piled up in a cold room that is working again. "It is all still nicely packaged, but it has become too warm. We do not want to take that risk, so we are going to destroy it. It will be about ten to fifteen thousand euros in damage." At the affected Belgian supermarkets too, much has to be destroyed. The Belgian public broadcaster VRT reports that the Delhaize in Eeklo has tens of thousands of euros in damage. At another branch in Hoepertingen, at least sixty thousand euros worth of food has to be thrown away.

title: De Dag podcast: how the Democrats are trying to win the elections (now and later)
lead: After two years on the sidelines, the Democrats hope to turn the tide tomorrow in the midterm elections in America. The outcome is important not only for the political balance in Congress, but also for the Democrats' course ahead of the presidential elections of 2028. America expert Casper Thomas highlights three states in this podcast where the Democrats are running prominent candidates: Texas, Kansas and Michigan. What and who works for the Democrats? Reactions? Email dedag@nos.nl Presentation and editing: Elisabeth Steinz Editorial team: Wouter Sloekers

title: Ceasefire in Ukrainian city of Olesjky expires: what does that mean for the war?
lead: Last night the ceasefire in the southern Ukrainian city of Olesjky ended. The six-day truce was one of the first times fighting between Russia and Ukraine was halted since the start of the Russian invasion in 2022. Residents of Olesjky could therefore be evacuated. It was an unusual situation that fighting between the two countries stopped for so long. What does it mean for the war going forward? Was this a turning point or only a one-off? The most important questions, laid out. Why a ceasefire? The southern Ukrainian city of Olesjky has been under fire since the start of the war. Most people had already fled, but about 1,700 people were still in the city. Before the truce began, famine threatened them. This was partly because Russians had placed landmines on the access roads, making resupply impossible. It was also almost impossible to flee the city. Besides a shortage of food and medicine, the city lacked electricity, heating and running water. How did the truce come about? The truce was announced on 23 October and took effect on 27 October. The White House claims the ceasefire came about partly thanks to the help of American first lady Melania Trump. Pope Leo XIV also called for a ceasefire in Olesjky. In a phone call with President Putin, he expressed his concern about the humanitarian situation and called for a truce. The six-day truce consisted of three phases: first a ceasefire, then delivery of humanitarian aid and finally the evacuation of civilians who wanted to leave the city. According to Melania, almost 800 people have been evacuated in total. Some of them have since returned to Ukrainian territory. The evacuees travelled through the Russian-occupied Crimean peninsula and the Russian city of Anapa to Belarus. Some stayed in Anapa. A few hundred people remained in Olesjky, possibly because they were afraid to travel through Russia. Are there more places like Olesjky? According to Daria Rabinovitsch, co-director of Helping to Leave, a charity that helps civilians leave occupied areas, there are at least three other areas isolated in the same way, where civilians are trapped with no help able to reach them. "It is difficult to estimate exactly how many people are currently cut off; because of the lack of mobile coverage and internet, neither the people trapped there nor their family members can report the situation," Rabinovitsch tells the NOS. These include the Kinburn spit, close to Kherson, which is cut off from the rest of the peninsula, and settlements near Polohy, which lies between Zaporizhzhia and Mariupol. "Although there are people who want to evacuate, it is almost impossible to find a driver willing to drive there to pick them up," says Rabinovitsch. The town of Enerhodar, south of Zaporizhzhia, is also gradually being cut off by heavy Russian shelling of the roads. Areas often become isolated when the front line shifts and Russia gains more territory, says Rabinovitsch. Will there be ceasefires in those places too? For now, no plans have been made for a ceasefire in other areas, a Kremlin spokesperson told the Russian state broadcaster TASS. Ukraine reportedly offered to extend the ceasefire, but Russia reportedly rejected this, another anonymous source told AFP. Generals on both the Russian and Ukrainian sides say the armies used the ceasefire to reinforce personnel and supplies. An anonymous Ukrainian army officer told news agency AFP that he fears the fighting could become "worse than before". What now? The truce over Olesjky was not by chance timed just before the American midterm elections, which take place tomorrow. According to experts, it was a good moment for Russia to present itself as a peace-loving party. With winter approaching, another attempt is being made to reach a peace agreement. A meeting is scheduled for 10 November in Abu Dhabi, where negotiating teams from Russia and Ukraine will speak with American officials about the possibilities for an agreement.

title: Zelensky: Russians carry out bloodbath with bombing of aid post
lead: According to Ukrainian president Zelensky, Russia has caused a bloodbath with airstrikes on a village near Zaporizja. At least 26 people have been killed. Five people were injured and about twenty people are missing. The Russians reportedly bombed a former school in Komysjoevacha where aid goods were being distributed. The school was also used as a shelter. Komysjoevacha is right near the front. According to Zelensky, Russia carried out two attacks in quick succession, to make as many victims as possible. After the first bomb on the school, rescue workers and police officers arrived at the scene, after which nine more bombs followed. He calls it "a downright gruesome attack". Russia has not yet responded to the attack. In images that Zelensky shares on social media, a large crater can be seen: According to the Ukrainian president, the Russians must have known that aid goods were being distributed every week at the school to the remaining villagers. "This is once again proof that Russia does not want to de-escalate", says Zelensky. He adds that after the evacuations in Olesjki this weekend there was a moment when next steps could be taken to show that peace is possible. "But with this massacre, the Russians are sending the opposite signal: they are going for more bloodbaths." The attack on Komysjoevacha was not the only fatal Russian attack today. According to the Ukrainian emergency service, one person was killed in Soemy and in Slovjansk. At least eight people were injured.

title: Breda pub crawl during Elfde van de Elfde cancelled due to expected crowds
lead: The pub crawl in Breda during the kickoff of the carnival season on 11 November will not go ahead. The municipality fears it will become too busy in the city centre. "An organised pub crawl conflicts with the measures aimed at controlling and spreading visitor flows", is the statement. So next Wednesday at exactly 18:11 there will be no crowd at the Breda Nachthoreca Kroegentocht. Officially, the municipality could not ban it: no permit had been applied for, so it could not be refused either. But after a conversation with the organisation, the organisation itself decided to cancel the event. The pub crawl has existed since 2022, and since then dozens of cafés have taken part each year. This year was going to be the same, but although the programme for the next edition was already finalised before it was called off, the organisation says. Stamp cards had been printed, flyers handed out and posters hung up around the city. "That makes it disappointing, because we have been organising this for years." The municipality says it contacted the organisation directly as soon as the plans became known via social media. 'Really an event' Despite the disappointment, the organisation does understand the municipality's request. Just like carnival itself, the celebration of the Elfde van de Elfde is also attracting ever larger crowds. "In recent years we have seen that it has really become an event", says a spokesperson for Breda speaking to Omroep Brabant. "With activities, stages and many visitors." The municipality is taking measures to better spread the crowds across the city. For example, the Grote Markt will have two stages this year instead of one. The municipality is also doing crowd control. With measures such as closing streets, softer music or diversions, the municipality wants to ensure that the flow of revellers runs smoothly. Busier and busier: 11 November is the traditional start of the carnival season, and it is celebrated on a grand scale mainly in <entity id="org:provincie-noord-brabant">Noord-Brabant</entity> and Limburg. The season is kicked off at 11:11 sharp. Two years ago the Elfde van de Elfde was celebrated in Brabant and Limburg in this way. Carnival itself begins next year on Sunday 7 February. That event is also well attended every year. In recent years, according to NS figures, 200,000 people travelled by train to carnival cities south of the big rivers on Saturday and Sunday. Last year the <entity id="org:gemeente-breda">gemeente Breda</entity> called on revellers not to come to the city centre because of the crowds. This prompted the municipality of Den Bosch to decide this summer to abolish carnival Thursday. The festivities drew too many visitors, which led to nuisance. The Thursday before carnival is officially not a carnival day, but in Oeteldonk, the name the city takes on during carnival, celebrations normally already take place on that day. Up in the air: In <entity id="org:gemeente-tilburg">Tilburg</entity> the entire future of the festivities on 11 November is up in the air. Local hospitality businesses and the municipality of Tilburg clash over whether minors are always welcome on that day. The municipality considers it a party for everyone, including minors, and wants the hospitality sector to sign a contract stating that everyone is welcome on the party squares. The hospitality sector calls teenagers a vulnerable group. Entrepreneurs want to keep the option to refuse them if it is too busy or if they are drunk. So far the municipality and Tilburg hospitality have not reached a solution. This week they will sit down together again.

title: '2 million for golden tip Bolle Jos' is buzzing in Sierra Leone, will he be betrayed?
lead: He reportedly earns tens of millions of euros a month from drug trafficking, has been sentenced in several court cases in the Netherlands and Belgium to a total of 103 years in prison, and reportedly stays in Sierra Leone. After earlier attempts to arrest Jos Leijdekkers, alias Bolle Jos, the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> (OM) today took a new step in the hunt for the drug criminal. The OM announced that the reward for the tip that leads to his arrest is being increased tenfold, from 200,000 euros to two million euros. Moreover, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> is launching a social media campaign in Sierra Leone and neighbouring countries. In it, people who know something about Leijdekkers' whereabouts or travel details are called on to come forward. Justice Minister Van Weel says that "we want to make the temptation greater for the golden tip". It is an open question whether Leijdekkers, who is known to spend part of his fortune on a high-tech team that protects him, is impressed by this. Disbelief over the amount. It is certain that two million euros is a lot of money in Sierra Leone. For comparison: a teacher earns sixty leones per day, which comes to 2.30 euros. And for residents of the poverty-stricken country, such a teacher's salary is already a high amount that many of them do not even earn. Today the news that the million-euro sum has been offered for the golden tip about Bolle Jos was already buzzing among residents of Sierra Leone. Sources at the NOS reacted with disbelief to the news. They can hardly imagine the amount, and in theory it could therefore lead to tips from Sierra Leoneans about the travel or residence details of the convicted drug criminal. Enormous risk. However, it must be noted that very few people have this kind of information about Leijdekkers: even people at high levels do not know where he is and how he moves. For those who do know, such as a pilot of a plane or a captain of a ship he travels on, sharing that information is an enormous risk. If they did, and that tip leads to Leijdekkers' arrest, the tipster risks having Leijdekkers' vast criminal network after them. He or she would then have to leave home and hearth behind, because going unnoticed with two million euros is a challenge in West Africa. NOS op 3 made this video about Sierra Leone in October: That Leijdekkers still walks free has everything to do with the high circles he moves in. The convicted drug criminal reportedly associates with President Bio of Sierra Leone, is said to be married to his daughter, and has ties with the head of the country's immigration service and the head of the anti-drug brigade. Van Weel hopes that people from the criminal's close circle will be stimulated by the increased tip amount. But it is a question whether this is interesting for these people; his circle is not large and those who deal closely with Leijdekkers have become wealthy thanks to him. And they too run an enormous risk if they snitch (klikken). In October the European Commission suspended payments of budget support to Sierra Leone, to put the country under pressure. But for the ordinary Sierra Leonean, who is affected by such measures, it is dangerous to rise up, and all the more so to say anything about Leijdekkers. Earlier, criminal law professor Sven Brinkhoff told the NOS that offering a high reward for a tip can create so much unrest around a suspect that it leads to evidence. It is clear that pressure around Leijdekkers is being increased, especially in combination with intercepted shipments linked to him. Now that more attention is being drawn to him partly because of the increased tip money, it becomes harder to work with him. That is why the question is how comfortable Leijdekkers feels in the country and whether he can still trust the people around him.

title: Coalition parties agree among themselves on tax plan and box 3, extra Council of Ministers this morning
lead: The coalition parties D66, VVD and CDA have reached agreement on adjusting the tax plan for next year and introducing a capital gains tax in box 3. According to insiders, the new form of wealth tax will be postponed by one year. Furthermore, the coalition parties are not choosing between the left-wing or right-wing opposition to achieve a majority. This morning <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity> will meet in an additional Council of Ministers meeting, after which the proposals will be sent to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. On Wednesday evening there is a debate on the tax plan. On Monday the top of the coalition discussed the matter for hours. Until now the minority cabinet tried to secure a majority in advance by seeking an agreement with opposition parties. But over the weekend, talks with both left-wing and right-wing parties again did not lead to a breakthrough. The left-wing bloc of Pro and Volt wants investors to pay more tax and workers less. But the VVD did not want that. The right-wing bloc of JA21, SGP and BBB wants to abolish the obligation for municipalities to accommodate asylum seekers and wants changes in the area of nitrogen and the liberal abortion practice. And those demands went too far for D66 in particular. Offers In the letter with adjustments that goes to the Chamber tomorrow, the cabinet will make offers to the opposition. That mainly concerns some extra tax relief for citizens. But that does not mean a choice is made for left or right. The coalition is charting its own course. With that, <entity id="person:rob-jetten">premier Jetten</entity>, unlike he initially wanted, is letting it come to the debate on Wednesday. In the dynamics of that debate, a package could still emerge that can gather approval from a majority. Parties can also propose amendments during the debate itself. The government parties might embrace those. But entering the debate without prospects of a majority is risky for the cabinet. If the tax plan is voted down, that has major consequences for both taxpaying citizens and the treasury of the Kingdom. Haste Today finding a majority became even harder due to an advice from the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity>. It judges harshly the haste the cabinet has in introducing the tax on gains from wealth in box 3. That change would be introduced in 2028, but according to the Raad van State that is not feasible. More than 250 extra civil servants are needed for that at the <entity id="org:belastingdienst">Belastingdienst</entity>, and the banks are also not yet able to supply the data on their clients' wealth gains to the tax authorities. Therefore the Raad van State calls on the cabinet to postpone the plans until at least 2030. But the cabinet therefore does not want to go beyond a one-year postponement for now.

title: Two arrests for violent robbery of 93-year-old woman in Amsterdam
lead: The <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> has arrested a 16-year-old boy and a 30-year-old man on suspicion of robbing a very elderly woman in Amsterdam last week. The 93-year-old woman broke her back in the process, but is doing as well as can be expected under the circumstances. On Tuesday last, the woman was walking with her rollator under the gallery of a flat on Comeniusstraat in the West district when a man suddenly struck her. She was hit so hard that she fell to the ground and broke her back. He then robbed her of her bag, which hung from the handlebar of the rollator. Neighbours rushed to help as soon as they heard the woman screaming. "She was extremely confused," a neighbourhood resident said after the incident to city broadcaster AT5. "It's so sad." A police spokesperson spoke of an "incomprehensible, cowardly act". Rummikub game The woman was on her way to a friend to play a game of Rummikub, regional broadcaster NH reports. After her fall she was taken to hospital. The victim's family calls the robbery incomprehensible. "We can barely comprehend that anyone is capable of such a cowardly act," says her son. "The eventual loot: three tenners and a box of Rummikub tiles." He lets it be known that his family is "extremely grateful" to the neighbours who came to help. Investigating judge The 16-year-old boy who was arrested remains a suspect in the case, but is no longer in custody. The 30-year-old man is. Tomorrow the investigating judge will decide whether he remains in custody.

title: Dead and seriously injured in shooting in car in residential area of Rotterdam-Oost
lead: A driver of a vehicle died tonight in a shooting in a car in a residential area in Rotterdam-Oost. In a press release, the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> reports that the deceased is a 36-year-old man from Dordrecht. Another man was seriously injured in the shooting, the police write on X. The shooting took place shortly after 20.00 hours on the Evenaar in the Oosterflank neighborhood. Because it is not yet clear how this could happen, the other three occupants have been named as suspects and arrested. The seriously injured man is one of the arrestees. He has been taken to hospital. Footage shows that several ambulances are present: A trauma helicopter was also called out. Investigators worked at the scene of the shooting for a long time.

title: Privately owned jet that crashed in Florida may have lost parts in the air
lead: The private plane that crashed almost vertically in Florida overnight appears to have already lost parts in the air. "We have indications that the plane broke apart before impact", U.S. media quote Tom Chapman of the NTSB, the agency that investigates aviation accidents in the US. Chapman announced new details about the fatal accident at a press conference. Parts of the plane presumably landed well away from the crater. Investigators are still in the dark about the cause of the accident. 'Rocket strike' All nine occupants died. The private jet came down at high speed and crashed right next to a trailer park. Governor Ron DeSantis described it as a rocket strike. None of the 77 residents of the trailer park died, but people still may not return to their homes. The moment of impact was filmed from the ground: The co-pilot has been identified as 20-year-old Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras. Her identity was made public by her mother. A family with two young children and the nanny also died in the crash. Two other passengers have also been identified. The identity of the pilot has not yet been made public. "We are going to crash", the pilot said shortly before the plane hit the ground. "We have no time left", were the last words from the cockpit, as can be heard in publicly released recordings. The plane had run into trouble shortly after pilots reported ice forming on the aircraft.

title: Gelderland partly locked for new grid connections: 'Bitter pill'
lead: Some municipalities in Gelderland are being locked for new connections to the electricity grid. That is what the ministry of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-economische-zaken-en-klimaat">Economische Zaken en Klimaat</entity> (EZK) announced this evening. New applications will have to wait from next year until capacity becomes available. The municipalities concerned are sixteen, writes Omroep Gelderland, including <entity id="org:gemeente-doetinchem">Doetinchem</entity>, <entity id="org:gemeente-lochem">Lochem</entity> and <entity id="org:gemeente-zutphen">Zutphen</entity>. "This is a bitter pill for the region," says deputy Ans Mol-van de Camp. Because new applications have to wait for a connection, "important social tasks" will be put on hold for the time being, she says. "Housing construction, economic development and sustainability require speed and cannot afford delay." Applications with social priority, such as a school or a hospital, will still be approved. Applications for housing construction that have already been submitted also have room. New homes or plans for them will have to wait. The connection stop applies in any case until 1 July 2027, the regional broadcaster reports. In the course of that year it will be assessed whether the measures are sufficiently effective to start granting applications again. Pressing In February, grid operators sounded the alarm because the situation in <entity id="org:provincie-flevoland">Flevoland</entity>, Gelderland and <entity id="org:gemeente-utrecht">Utrecht</entity> was pressing, and much more serious than assumed. In part of Gelderland the grid is now indeed full. For the rest of the province, "unremitting effort" is needed to prevent a complete connection stop, the province says. Gelderland is not the first province to take its own measures due to overloading of the electricity grid. In part of Utrecht, a complete stop on new or heavier connections was announced in April. The shortage of space there has decreased, but is not yet sufficient for new connections. Housing construction can continue. Since 1 July of this year, national priority rules have applied to the grid. All applications for power supplies go to grid operators, who decide who gets priority. These include basic facilities such as hospitals and projects that spare the grid (such as companies that store energy), as well as, for example, someone who wants to install a charging point. Since summer, unused space on the grid is no longer reserved for households either. Across almost the whole country there is a waiting list for new or heavier connections. The waiting time differs by region. Last month it became clear that the number of companies and organisations waiting for a connection to use (more) electricity has increased further. According to Netbeheer Nederland, the cooperative organisation of grid operators, there were about 15,500 people waiting in the first half of the year. The problems with the overfull grid are causing companies to postpone investments and sustainability efforts.

title: US announces Ukraine-Russia talks in Abu Dhabi
lead: Led by US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, talks will be held in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November on ending the war in Ukraine. Steve Witkoff announced this on X. According to the Americans, delegations from both Ukraine and Russia will be present. A US official told news agency Reuters on Monday that the talks between the three countries would cover security guarantees for the period after the war and de-escalation. The American negotiators want to force a breakthrough in the war between the two countries before winter sets in. The Americans' previous attempt to reach an agreement dates from February, before the United States and Israel began a war against Iran. Ukraine has not yet responded to the proposed talks. Russian president Putin reportedly agreed two weeks ago after a meeting with envoy Witkoff in Saint Petersburg. Also talks in Brussels. According to a US official, there are also talks with various European countries in Brussels this week. Representatives from France, Germany, the United Kingdom, the European Union and NATO are reportedly to be at the table. Topics would include, among other things, security guarantees for Ukraine, security in Europe, and economic support for and reconstruction of Ukraine. Russia and Ukraine are still far apart on the conditions of a possible peace agreement. Trump has recently been increasing pressure on Ukraine. The American president wants Ukraine to stop air strikes on Russian oil refineries. Meanwhile Russia continues its attacks on Ukraine, and civilian casualties occur almost daily. Yesterday 26 people were killed in air strikes on a village near Zaporizja. The Russians reportedly bombed a former school in Komysjoevacha where aid goods were being distributed. President Zelensky called the attack "utterly gruesome".

title: Hotel in Amsterdam evacuated due to major fire
lead: During a major fire at a hotel in Amsterdam, 140 guests were evacuated overnight. The fire possibly started because of an appliance that caught fire. The fire brigade quickly had the fire under control. Several hotel guests were checked by ambulance personnel. Two of them had to go to hospital for a check-up because they had inhaled smoke. The fire at the hotel on Johan Cruijff Boulevard broke out at 23:45 on Monday evening. Because many calls came in to the emergency services and because of the smoke, the fire brigade escalated to 'major fire'. Since there were around 140 hotel guests present, the fire brigade searched the building several times to make sure all people were out of the hotel in time. The evacuated hotel guests were initially taken in at the concourse of Bijlmer Arena station. Later in the night they were housed in hotels nearby.

title: North Korea denies being behind the Binance hack
lead: North Korea has for the first time responded to the American accusations that it is behind the theft of billions of euros from crypto platform Binance. Kim Yo-jong, the influential sister of leader Kim Jong-un, now denies that the country is behind the hack and calls the accusation "absurd rhetoric". The FBI announced last weekend that North Korea is responsible for the theft of more than 5.6 billion euros in virtual assets from Binance, the largest crypto platform in the world. It would be the largest financial heist ever. According to the American security service, a hacker unit directed by North Korea converted the stolen bitcoins into ethereum, another cryptocurrency, and "further laundering stages" may follow to erase traces. Kim Yo-jong calls the American accusations a "serious political provocation". "The US is misleading international public opinion by suggesting that all cybercrime in the world is our work", Kim responded. She is referring to an earlier hack at the beginning of this year. Then too, the FBI named a North Korean hacker group as the perpetrator after a hack at the popular crypto exchange ByBit. In that case 1.5 billion dollars in digital money was stolen. That heist was then considered the largest ever in the crypto world. Binance has announced that most of the crypto assets stolen from the platform have since been reimbursed.

title: Two million retirees, including former civil servants, can expect a significantly higher pension
lead: For some 2 million retired Dutch people, 2027 looks set to start off financially very well. This is shown by a calculation by pension adviser Aon at the request of NOS. Pension funds that switch to the new pension system on 1 January are in a very good position right now. If that is still the case in two months, their members will benefit considerably. An increase of between 12 and 25 percent is very possible. It concerns 37 funds with 7.7 million members, of whom 2 million are retired. These include retired civil servants, shop workers, transport workers, bank employees and metal workers. Distributing reserves In the new pension system, the collective pot of money is divided into individual pension pots. Into that personal pot goes what you have built up during your working life. In addition, funds also distribute their reserves, the remaining money in the bank after all obligations to members have been met. The larger that reserve, the more there is to distribute. Part of that reserve is needed as a buffer to still top up retirees' payments in case of poorer stock market results. And part is needed for pension compensation. What is left over is distributed among retirees and workers. This is sometimes also called the sailing-in bonus. Workers receive that one-off increase in their pot too, but that money continues to be invested. Retirees see the effect of that amount directly in their monthly payment. 2 million retirees Pension adviser Aon looked at the ten largest pension funds that are now making the switch to the new system. Those funds account for 95 percent of all Dutch people who will be transferred in 2027. Retirees of those funds are on average set to gain 17 percent. This differs per fund. The final increase may also differ by age. In general, the increase for older retirees will be somewhat lower than for younger retirees. The increase applies from 1 January, but retirees will have to wait for the final calculation in the new year. Once everything has been correctly calculated, retirees will see that increase in their monthly payment. The increase for the first months of 2027 will be paid to them with retroactive effect. "The outlook is rosy for members of pension funds that switch to the new system on 1 January", says Corine Reedijk of Aon. "The last two months of the year will remain tense, but if the situation stays stable, members of these funds will also have a good start in the new system". Civil servants With more than 3 million members, of whom one million are pensioners, civil servants' pension fund ABP is by far the largest fund now making the switch. The most recent figures, from the end of September, show that ABP has invested assets of 543 billion and a coverage ratio of 132 percent. That means that even after paying out all accrued pensions (100 percent), it still has money in the bank (32 percent). If not too much changes in the coming two months, there will be a lot of money left to distribute among members. ABP does not wish to make forecasts itself. "How much it will be for individual members cannot be directly linked to the coverage ratio, but also depends on their personal situation", says the spokesperson. The pension fund points out that at ABP more personal factors count towards the final pension increase. One example is that at ABP some members receive a higher compensation if they missed indexation in the past. Wait and see It is still a matter of waiting and seeing for the pension funds and their 7.7 million members. For instance, a falling interest rate can lead to a lower coverage ratio, leaving less money to distribute. Earlier this year interest rates rose, but in recent months they have fallen again somewhat. Setbacks on the stock market can also affect the pension funds. For example, tech company share prices are extremely high, but they have been fluctuating quite a lot recently. The funds that made the switch last year were also able to raise pensions considerably thanks to the sailing-in bonus. That concerned 1.5 million retired workers from healthcare, technology, construction, hospitality and temp agency sectors. The windfall is one-off. Whether their pensions rise again this year depends on how well their funds have invested.

title: Wake-up call 3/11: Americans head to the polls • Verdict in Woudenberg sex offence suspects case
lead: Good morning! In the United States it is election day today. American voters are voting for Congress, their parliament. And the former couple from Woudenberg suspected of abusing children they babysat is hearing the verdict. First the weather: This morning locally some sun, but from the east also a lot of cloud, from which here and there some rain may fall. This afternoon from Germany more sunny spells and gradually dry. With a moderate northeasterly wind, maxima range between 9 and 12 degrees. The coming days relatively quiet and dry autumn weather with maxima around 10 degrees. A look back at the weather of October and the forecast for the coming days can be seen in this video: Are you going out today? Here you find the overview of traffic jams and roadworks, and here you can see the situation on the railways. What can you expect today? What did you miss? North Korea has responded to American accusations that the country is behind the billion-euro theft from crypto platform Binance. Kim Yo-jong, the influential sister of leader Kim Jong-un, denies this and calls the accusation "absurd rhetoric". The FBI said last weekend that North Korea must be responsible for the theft of over 5.6 billion euros in virtual assets from Binance, the largest crypto platform in the world. It would be the largest financial heist ever. Kim Yo-jong calls the American accusations a "serious political provocation". "The US is misleading international public opinion by suggesting that all cybercrime in the world is our work," Kim responded. Other news from the night: And then also this: Researchers from the University of Pisa have observed a very unusual friendship in Africa between two male animals. On the highlands of Ethiopia they saw a bull and a donkey repeatedly moving towards each other. The animals licked and cuddled each other, and the bull regularly climbed onto the donkey in an excited state. Homosexuality is not unusual in the animal kingdom, but what is very exceptional is that it occurs between different animal species. The researchers published about it this week in the scientific journal Current Biology . Have a nice day!

title: Surinamese internationals still lose Dutch nationality despite change in law
lead: Surinamese-Dutch footballers still live in great uncertainty because of the passport issue. The players can still lose their Dutch nationality if they choose a Surinamese international career. Suriname hoped that a change in the law would put an end to all the problems that arose at the beginning of this year for several players. They had lost their Dutch nationality by operation of law, because they had voluntarily acquired another nationality. In September, the Surinamese parliament adopted a law stating that footballers from the diaspora with another nationality can now obtain Surinamese nationality "by operation of law". What is the passport issue again? The passport issue came to light in March when NAC Breda requested that the 6-0 defeat to Go Ahead Eagles be replayed, because according to the Brabant club Dean James was not eligible to play. The right-back obtained his Indonesian nationality in 2025 so that he could play for that country's national team. Unknowingly, under Dutch law he had automatically lost his Dutch nationality, because he had voluntarily acquired another nationality. As a result, suddenly quite a few players from the Eredivisie and the first division playing for Indonesia, Suriname and also Cape Verde were classified as 'foreigners' from outside the European Union. The president effectively grants the athletes Surinamese citizenship. "They do not have to submit an application themselves, sign anything, or take an oath or make a declaration", according to the Surinamese newspaper De Ware Tijd. But this arrangement does not seem to offer enough certainty. "The consequences of the Surinamese arrangement for Dutch nationality are assessed on a case-by-case basis under Dutch nationality law. The mere fact that Surinamese nationality is obtained by operation of law is not sufficient to fall within one of the legal exception categories", according to a spokesperson for the Dutch <entity id="org:ministerie-van-justitie-en-veiligheid">Justitie en Veiligheid</entity> ministry. "The <entity id="org:immigratie-en-naturalisatiedienst">IND</entity> (Immigration and Naturalisation Service) and the Ministry of Justice and Security were not involved in the preparation of this change in the law", the spokesperson writes. "When I read the ministry's response like this, it is quite clear that the passport issue has not been resolved", says sports law attorney Dolf Segaar. Attorney Hermie de Voer, who specialises in nationality law, is also not at ease. "Suppose a player decides to play football for Suriname, and that passport has indeed been issued by Suriname, but in the meantime you also want to renew your Dutch passport... I can easily imagine the Dutch ministry then saying very firmly: you have another passport, so you are no longer a Dutch national. Then a player will still have to go to court to have Dutch nationality established." "This is a very bad situation", says Surinamese head coach Henk Fraser. "Both countries should work together and provide clarity. You are simply dealing with people who follow their hearts, who want to play football for Suriname, but who now do not know where they stand. They are being mercilessly punished in this way. I find that truly incomprehensible." Several Surinamese players decided not to play for 'de Natio' during the last international break because of the uncertainty, Fraser admits. Players such as Danilho Doekhi (Lazio), Milan van Ewijk (Coventry City) and Jayden Oosterwolde (Fenerbahçe) have also put the choice for Suriname on hold. Voluntarily giving up nationality Jean-Paul Boëtius was also not involved in September. But the clubless winger was simply not called up, he says by telephone. However, he too has automatically lost his Dutch nationality, after he first played for Suriname in 2025, and thereby, without knowing it, voluntarily gave up his Dutch nationality. Boëtius is by no means the only one. Among others, Tjaronn Chery (NEC) and Virgil Misidjan (RKC <entity id="org:gemeente-waalwijk">Waalwijk</entity>) are in the process of trying to regain their Dutch nationality. That could take a year, Chery said at the start of this season in conversation with the NOS. Recently Boëtius received a letter from the Rotterdam municipality. "It stated that within the next two weeks I must hand in my Dutch passport. Under the so-called huppelepup law, you have lost your Dutch nationality. Yet just before all this began I had renewed my Dutch passport. It is still valid until 2036." "I now have a sticker in my Surinamese passport, which gives me a residence permit to live in the Netherlands. But yes, that is also only for a year. Yes, this is a very annoying situation. I simply want to become Dutch again. I was born and raised here." "The Dutch passport is also simply stronger than the Surinamese one", Boëtius continues. "If I want to fly somewhere, east, west, north, south, wherever... With a Dutch passport that always works. But with a Surinamese passport you often have to apply for a visa." "You know, I am super proud that I was allowed to play, and still am allowed to play, for Suriname. But it is a pity that it has turned out this way. I and other players feel rather misled, by people who, incidentally, no longer work for the Surinamese federation." Boëtius: "I just want to say that I am now receiving very good support from the federation, there are lawyers who are working out every detail for us. But their predecessors came up with the so-called sports passport. Only... that did not exist at all."

title: Dead and injured after two helicopters collide on Mount Everest
lead: Two helicopters collided and crashed on Mount Everest. One person died and two people were injured. Mount Everest lies on the border between Nepal and China and is the highest mountain in the world. There are no roads on the mountain, so helicopters are the only way to bring sick or exhausted hikers down. The helicopters crashed in the village of Pheriche, which lies at about 4,200 metres altitude. Rainy season over. A 47-year-old tourist from India died in the accident, news agency AP reports. A traveller from New Zealand and one of the helicopter pilots were also injured. It is not clear how many people were in the helicopters. Autumn is a popular season to climb Mount Everest, because the rainy season is over and it is less cold than in the winter months. But the trek is also very popular with hikers in the rest of the year. So popular that the Nepalese government has in the past taken measures to curb the number of climbers, but without a clear effect.

title: Prime Minister Jetten asks opposition: take responsibility
lead: Prime Minister Jetten calls on the opposition in <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity> to take their responsibility and give sufficient support to the tax plan. He points out that extra investments are being made in purchasing power and safety. According to him, there are now very nice elements "for left and right" in it. Jetten said this after an extra <entity id="org:ministerraad">ministerraad</entity>, in which new adjustments to the tax plan and Box 3 were formally adopted. The plan now goes to the Tweede Kamer, which will debate it tomorrow. Once the letter has been sent, more will become known about the content. At the last minute: <entity id="org:kabinet">het kabinet</entity>'s top agreed last night on changes to the tax plan. According to Jetten, this is now the third time the cabinet has made concessions to the opposition. The minority cabinet does not want to choose the bloc on the right (JA21, SGP and BBB) or the bloc on the left (Pro and Volt), and is therefore not assured of a majority in advance. Still, Jetten is optimistic. He said there have been many "constructive talks" and that he also feels the need, together with the opposition, to enter 2027 with a good tax plan. Ahead of this morning's consultation, Jetten said he has every confidence that it will turn out well. "I am convinced we can bring the Chamber over the line to support these plans." Jetten pointed out that a number of opposition parties are positive about the adjustments. This concerns in any case the small centre parties ChristenUnie and 50Plus. Those two cannot together help the cabinet to a majority, but with the support of the Groep Markuszower, which split off from the PVV, it does add up sufficiently. According to Jetten, it should also succeed in <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Eerste Kamer</entity>. "Together here in The Hague we bear the responsibility to do good things. And a good tax plan with many improvements for citizens and businesses is part of that." 'Tough process' <entity id="person:eelco-heinen">Minister Heinen</entity> of <entity id="org:ministerie-van-financien">Financiën</entity> called making a tax plan with a minority cabinet that has insufficient support in the Tweede and Eerste Kamer "a tough process". He said he will keep puzzling until the last vote. "I keep presenting proposals. We cannot let this slip from our hands." He too expects the plan to be adopted in the Tweede Kamer in any case. About the Eerste Kamer he says: "We are doing it step by step, and this whole route is full of risks, but I keep puzzling, and every time we come one step closer."

title: Tax plan 2027: purchasing power up slightly, VAT increase on ornamental horticulture postponed
lead: The higher VAT on flowers has been postponed by a few months and the freedom contribution, a tax on labour, will not go ahead next year. That is apparent from the revised tax plan, which was approved this morning by <entity id="org:ministerraad">de ministerraad</entity>. The document has just been sent to <entity id="org:tweede-kamer">de Tweede Kamer</entity>. New in the plan is that the higher VAT on ornamental horticulture will only be introduced in the course of 2028, instead of at the start of that year. It was a major wish of BBB to change this plan. Furthermore, it becomes clear that the freedom contribution, a plan of the CDA to levy extra tax on labour and spend that money on defence, is off the table for next year. That concerns 347 million euros. The tax would place too much on the plate of 'ordinary, hard-working people', several opposition parties felt. <entity id="org:kabinet">Het kabinet</entity> wants to cover that by scrapping tax benefits for companies and individuals, but still wants to consult the Tweede Kamer on which benefits these should be. Purchasing power improvement <entity id="person:rob-jetten">Premier Jetten</entity> said this morning in an explanation that there will be 1.5 billion in purchasing power improvement compared with Prinsjesdag. Several commitments have been made since then, including not raising the excise duty on fuel. The deduction for specific care costs remains, but will be more targeted at people who really need it. That was a major wish of ChristenUnie and 50Plus. In addition, a total of 95 million will become available for security in the coming years, among others the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> and the <entity id="org:openbaar-ministerie">Openbaar Ministerie</entity> will benefit from that. That was mainly at the request of Groep Markuszower, which together with ChristenUnie and 50Plus can secure a majority in the Tweede Kamer. How exactly this amount will be spent will be made clear later. The new wealth tax in box 3 will, after criticism from the <entity id="org:raad-van-state">Raad van State</entity>, be postponed by one year from 2028 to 2029. Only "if that is feasible" can the cabinet possibly still let the plans take effect in 2028. The change is partly 'covered' by temporarily further lowering the low rate for entrepreneurs in box 2. The hope is that they will use this benefit to withdraw more capital from the business, which would then ultimately yield tax money for the state coffers. This coverage therefore for now exists only on paper. Furthermore, 3.1 billion comes from a pot that was ready to compensate wealthy people who have paid too much tax in recent years. CO2 storage The plans also state that the cabinet saves almost 170 million euros by postponing money for 'Aramis' to 2032. Aramis is a project to store CO2, originating from industry, in an empty gas field under the North Sea. What this postponement means for the climate goals is not clear. The Tweede Kamer debates the package of tax measures tomorrow. Premier Jetten called on the opposition in the Tweede Kamer today to take responsibility and give sufficient support. In the letter, the cabinet already responds positively to an amendment (a proposal for a change in legislation) from ChristenUnie and 50Plus to lower income tax for the two lowest income groups. To pay for that, the increase in the labour tax credit that the cabinet had proposed would be scrapped. That means the tax reduction will apply to a larger group of citizens than only employees. ChristenUnie wanted people with a disability benefit to benefit from it too.

title: Americans to the ballot box, here is where the difference is made
lead: In America it is Election Day , and the results of the Congressional elections will trickle in tonight. In these midterm elections, the Republican majorities in Congress are at stake. All seats in the House of Representatives are being elected again, and in <entity id="org:eerste-kamer">de Senaat</entity> it concerns 35 of the 100 seats. The elections are important for President Trump and his Republican party to firmly keep power in Washington. The Democrats see an opportunity to curb Trump's extensive power. Although Trump remains unpredictable, Congress at least has influence over budgets. That can also be important, for example, for American support for Ukraine or the introduction of sanctions packages. Both the House and the Senate are currently in Republican hands. According to Cook Political Report , an independent American polling website, the Democratic party is on course to win a majority in the House of Representatives. In the Senate, the task is harder. That is because Democrats must take several seats from the Republicans, in states that were won by more than 10 percentage points two years ago. Still, a shift is not unthinkable. How exciting is the Senate election? Of some of the 35 seats in the Senate being decided today, it is already virtually certain who will win them. In fifteen states, according to Cook Political Report, the race is not yet over; in six states, it could really still go either way. In North Carolina, one of the fifteen states mentioned, the Democrats hope to take a seat from the Republicans fairly easily. That would be an early boost for the party in the evening. It is important, though, that the Republicans do not take a seat from the Democrats in New Hampshire, Minnesota or Michigan . In that last state, a hard campaign was fought and it could go either way, but Cook now considers the chance greater that the Democrats will keep their seat there. Nieuwsblad The Economist is more cautious than American polls when it comes to the Democrats' chances. The chance that they gain control of the Senate is, according to them, 53 percent. How exciting is the House of Representatives election? That the Democrats could win the House of Representatives is therefore not unthinkable. For that they need 218 seats. Cook Political Report considers the chance already present that the Democrats could take fifteen seats from the Republicans. That could already be more than enough for a majority. Eighteen elections could still go either way. In swing states such as Michigan and Pennsylvania, red could easily turn blue again. If the Democrats manage to gain a majority, the speaker of the House of Representatives will be a Democrat. For now, that is still the Republican Mike Johnson, an important figure in American politics. Election night at the NOS The NOS will broadcast the results live tonight in a livestream . From 03.00 hours, Arjen van der Horst will provide commentary on all developments. At 07.00 hours he will hand over to Mark Visser, who will connect with studio guests and our correspondents and reporters in the United States. From 09.00 to 09.30 hours we will address viewer questions. Want to know something? Email vraag@nos.nl . When will we know the result? It is likely that we will know the day after the elections who gets the majority in the House of Representatives. The Senate may take longer. Four years ago, it was only clear on Sunday who got the Senate. Each state has its own counting system, so in some states it takes longer. The political sensitivity surrounding the counting of votes may also cause certain results to take longer to become known. The Trump administration openly questions the system. Donald Trump is already pursuing several lawsuits to steer results that he does not like in his favour. So it could still be a turbulent night. Want to know more about the elections? In the video, our correspondent explains what is at stake:

title: Woman in Tilburg home died as a result of a crime
lead: The woman found dead last Sunday in her home in Tilburg died as a result of a crime. That is what the <entity id="org:politie">politie</entity> reports. The body of the 54-year-old woman was discovered Sunday morning in the home on Berkenrodelaan. What exactly happened has not been made public. A day later, the police still reported that there were suspicions of a crime but that multiple scenarios were being taken into account. According to Omroep Brabant, a great deal is still unclear. Who is responsible for the woman's death is not yet known. No suspect has been arrested yet. After the body was found, the police conducted an investigation in the home, among other things. A team spoke with neighbours. Screaming According to the Brabants Dagblad, the woman lived alone and neighbours heard screaming on Sunday. Her body was then reportedly discovered by family members.

title: Fireworks dealers can apply for compensation, entrepreneurs dissatisfied
lead: Shopkeepers who sell fireworks can register from today for a compensation scheme, because they are missing out on income at the coming New Year's Eve. This New Year's Eve there is a fireworks ban, and private individuals may not set off fireworks. There are a number of conditions fireworks dealers must meet to claim the compensation. For example, shopkeepers must show that around New Year's Eve from 2025 to 2026 they sold fireworks intended for New Year's.
